reviews.review_title: Elite Magnetic TKL Keyboard With Precision Control
reviews.review_description:
The Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Tenkeyless is engineered as a competitive‑grade keyboard built around Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, offering adjustable actuation from 0.1 mm to 4.0 mm and a 100‑million keystroke lifespan (). This switch architecture eliminates debounce delay entirely, enabling instantaneous actuation and reset behavior that mechanical switches simply cannot match. The magnetic sensing provides exceptionally consistent input recognition, and the keyboard’s internal calibration system compensates for magnetic interference to maintain stable performance over time. Combined with the TKL layout, which frees up desk space for low‑sensitivity mouse movement, the Huntsman V3 HE is clearly designed for players who rely on precision micro‑adjustments and rapid directional changes.

One of the most defining features is Rapid Trigger, which allows keys to reset the moment they begin to rise rather than waiting for a fixed reset point. This dramatically increases responsiveness in FPS titles, enabling faster counter‑strafes, smoother movement corrections, and more reliable repeated inputs. Esports.gg’s testing highlights how Rapid Trigger transforms WASD control, making movement feel “snappy, predictable, and extremely responsive” — a sentiment that aligns with real‑world gameplay impressions. The keyboard also supports Dynamic Keystroke, allowing up to four actions on a single key at different actuation depths, and Snap Flex, which assigns one action on press and another on release. These features give competitive players granular control over movement, utility activation, and complex keybind setups, especially in games like Valorant, CS2, and Apex Legends ().

The Huntsman V3 HE’s 8000 Hz HyperPolling is another major technical advantage. With true 8000 Hz performance, the keyboard sends input data to the PC eight times more frequently than standard 1000 Hz keyboards, reducing average latency to 0.60 ms — roughly 8% faster than competing high‑end boards (). In fast‑paced shooters, this reduction in input delay contributes to more immediate movement and firing responses. Esports.gg’s analysis notes that the keyboard feels “instantaneous,” with no perceptible delay between keypress and on‑screen action. For competitive players who rely on tight timing windows, this level of responsiveness provides a measurable advantage.

Build quality is another strong point. The keyboard uses a 5052 aluminum alloy top case, which gives it a rigid, premium feel while keeping weight manageable for LAN events. The switches are factory‑lubricated, and a dense internal foam layer improves acoustics, reducing hollow resonance and delivering a smoother, more muted sound profile. The doubleshot PBT keycaps resist shine and wear, maintaining texture even under heavy daily use. The detachable USB‑C cable and hybrid onboard storage for up to six profiles add practical flexibility, especially for players who switch between systems or travel frequently ().

Razer’s software approach is also noteworthy. The Huntsman V3 HE supports Synapse for Web, allowing users to adjust actuation, Rapid Trigger sensitivity, polling rate, lighting, and keybinds directly through a browser without installing software — ideal for tournament environments or shared PCs. The keyboard’s Chroma RGB is bright and evenly diffused, and while lighting is not the focus of this model, it integrates cleanly with competitive setups. Real‑world impressions consistently highlight the keyboard’s stability, predictable actuation behavior, and the immediate improvement in movement control during gameplay.

Overall, the Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Tenkeyless delivers exceptional responsiveness, deep customization, durable construction, and esports‑grade precision. Its combination of Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, Rapid Trigger, Dynamic Keystroke, Snap Tap, and true 8000 Hz HyperPolling makes it one of the most technically advanced competitive keyboards available. For players who prioritize movement accuracy, instant input recognition, and customizable actuation, this keyboard offers a genuine performance advantage that is immediately noticeable in high‑speed FPS environments.

So this listing is for the v3 ten key less Hunstman v3 8K HE keyboard specifically designed for gaming with hall effect switches and snap tap actions. The keyboard has an 8000 Hz polling rate and has onboard memory to store profiles.

I have both the v1 and v2 version of this exact keyboard so comparing all three of these keyboards, they all have the exact same solid build quality and sound quality which is a quite thocky experience. The keyboards are solidly built and made of premium material which leads to a very comfortable typing experience. The keyboard is constructed of a solid plastic and metal material which makes them feel premium. The keyboard is about 14" x 5" x 2" high and weighs in with a heft and weight that allows it to sit solidly on your desk.

I have been using this keyboard exclusively for nearly two weeks now and it is now my daily driver. I am thoroughly impressed by the HE switches and how very comfortable it is to type on. The software is the one short area as the Synapse software really does not effectively work on Mac but it does sort of work on Windows but don't expect much. The keyboard itself is highly customizable and allows for full customization in color along with key press. Also there is no Linux support either but you can use SignalRGB to control lighting. Also Synapse itself really bogs down your PC and slowly causes a memory leak which means you need to regularly reboot your PC.

That being said, the level of customization is something to behold. You can customize everything from tap throw distances to macro's and feature sets. The keyboard can literally be customized by key for color if you want to go through and do that - all though I just keep them one solid color purple for my keyboard. The elevators on the back of the keyboard also help make the keyboard much more comfortable to type on at an angle. The keyboard's compact size really makes it ideal for someone who is limited in space.

The price for this keyboard is a premium and is not always the best value for the money but that is not why you are buying this keyboard. This keyboard is designed for someone already in the ecosystem for this keyboard and for the enthusiast who wants the latest and greatest product from the company. Overall I'm very happy with my purchase

My first introduction to magenetic switches and adjustable actuation is was the Steelseries Apex Pro and since then, I have become fond of keyboards that have the feature. I have tried many Razer keyboards and I can say this one is pretty nice.

So to start out with, I have abnormal Raynauds disease which impacts my hands and feet. Often times, my fingers are numb which has caused keyboards to wear out faster due to the fact that I would bottom out the keys so I knew it was being pressed which obviously will wear out the switch faster. Adjustable actuation helps with this as you dont need to press it as hard for it to register.

I don't really like TKL keyboards, I like my numpad but Razer tends not to make full sized keyboards anymore. But as I also don't have a lot of desk space... it is probably better for me to have.

This keyboard is actually pretty okay, the RGB syncs with all my other Razer products that support chroma which are my mouse (Naga Pro), and headset (Kraken), and microphone. Synapse (Razer's software) as usual, has a learning curve when using new features and some may find it frustrating as the interface tends not to be on the beginner friendly end.

Once I was able to fine tune it to my preference though, it was nice to use. The high pooling rate is beneficial as it means that it registers the inputs quicker. The keyboard itself isn't bulky by any means and the snap tap feature is responsive.

I do wish they made full sized keyboards more often though as I still found myself trying to use a numpad that isn't there... but that is a me problem.

Overall, I like this keyboard and recommend it to anyone who is looking for the ability to customize their key presses for functionality.

reviews.review_title: Great for both work and gaming
reviews.review_description:
I bought this keyboard after spending some time looking for a wireless mechanical keyboard that I could use for both work and gaming, and I’m really happy with my purchase.

What I like most is the feel of the keys when typing and the sound. It has that characteristic mechanical keyboard sound that is very satisfying without becoming annoying when I’m working for several hours. I also think the 75% size is perfect: it takes up much less space on my desk without sacrificing the keys I actually use.

I also really like the way it looks. It feels stylish, solid, and much more polished than I expected. The wireless connection has worked very well, and being able to switch between devices is really convenient.

I mainly use it for work and do a lot of typing, so it was important to me that it be comfortable as well as nice-looking, and so far it has completely met my expectations.

When I bought it, I didn’t realize that the letters were printed on the front of the keycaps rather than on top. It only took me a few hours to get used to it, though, and now I actually like it because I think the lettering may wear off more slowly.

The only thing I didn’t like is that it doesn’t have a dedicated “Home” key. It has an “End” key, but not “Home.” That said, the software makes it incredibly easy to remap keys and customize their functions, so it works perfectly for me anyway.

I also like that you can choose from several colorful lighting effects, although I usually keep the lights turned off because I find them a little distracting while working. The keyboard is somewhat heavy, so I would consider it more of a desk keyboard than something you would want to carry around, which is completely fine for my use.

The AULA F75 Pro isn’t just a keyboard — it’s a life upgrade. From the moment I unboxed it, I knew this thing was built different. The build quality feels premium in a way that makes everything else on my desk feel insecure. The weight, the finish, the layout — chef’s kiss.

But the sound? Oh man… pure mechanical ASMR. Every keystroke is a buttery, creamy “thock” that makes typing feel less like a task and more like a treat. It’s so smooth and satisfying I found myself typing things I didn’t even need to type — emails, notes, grocery lists, lorem ipsum paragraphs — just to hear it sing.

Key layout & switch orientation: One thing I absolutely love is how the keys are south-facing, sitting slightly inward instead of pointing outward toward you. It gives the whole board a cleaner, sleeker look and makes the RGB shine through in a softer, more premium way.

Wireless performance: flawless. Zero lag, zero hiccups, zero drama. It connects instantly and stays rock-solid whether I’m gaming, working, or just vibing on YouTube comments.

Battery life: absurdly good. I swear this thing runs on wizard energy because I keep checking the percentage and it keeps refusing to go down.

RGB: The lighting is vibrant without being over-the-top, and the multi-function knob makes switching effects, brightness, and colors stupidly satisfying. One smooth twist and you can go from a calm ambient glow to full-on gamer neon. It’s intuitive, responsive, and makes controlling the RGB feel extra premium without the need of a software which is a plus.

Overall? This keyboard is elite. Legendary. A masterpiece of clicky, thocky engineering. If you want something that feels incredible, sounds incredible, and looks incredible, the AULA F75 Pro is the one. I absolutely, genuinely loved this product.

There are many different LED modes as well, which is nice, as well as the fact that you can set these modes without having to install some sort of app to control them.

While I primarily use the 2.4 connection, I do like the fact that it supports 3 bt devices. The response rate is very good and on par with the Corsair. You will have to get used to the arrow key layout with end, pg up, pg dn, and delete being in one single vertical row.

Probably the most intriguing thing that made me want to even look at it was the front etched keys, which were perfect for my use case. I usually rest the keyboard on a shelf slightly higher than my shoulder when I sit so the keyboard is closer to my eye level than my hands. These keys make it easier to quickly see and press some custom commands I have instead of having to pick up the keyboard, sit it on my lap or tray, and then use my commands.

The key presses are also very muted from the cherry mx switches, which is a plus and slightly more satisfying.

Overall, I'm Impressed.

reviews.review_title: Bought both keyboards so I could compare
reviews.review_description:
(TLDR): The “LED” one (less expensive) works/sounds just as fine, the only real difference is the “QWERTY” one has brighter and more vibrant backlighting.

If you just care about functionality/affordability, get the cheaper one. If you care more about aesthetics, spend a lil more!

- - - - -

I have two fellow gamer friends who desperately needed new keyboards, and since I already bought them keycaps, I decided to look for affordable mechanical keyboards for them. Amazon recommended these, reviews seemed promising, but I had another issue.. what’s the difference?? Why is one $10-15 more?? Nothing really explains the difference here and Google couldn’t help me with wtf LED vs QWERTY was (I thought they both were?? 🤨 Idk still learning about keyboards, bear with me here) A few reviews said one was brighter than the other, but other than that, I was unsure why one cost more.

One friend only cared about functionality as they work from home, but the other friend very much cares about aesthetics and has a nice gamer setup. So figured, I’ll just get both!

So here’s a breakdown of all the notable but pretty settle differences:

RBG LED (White Logo)

On Box: Sindri Red Dragon

Price: Cheapest Option (great for what you pay for, best affordable option)

Sound: Red Switches, not “silent” imo but not too loud either (I think this one sounded SLIGHTLY clackier, but friends couldn’t tell difference, maybe I just watch a lot of keyboard videos to notice lol)

Base: Black “Metallic” appearance (bottom keyboard in light pic) Felt slightly lighter, not all that noticeable though

Lighting: Not nearly AS vibrant, but still bright enough (top keyboard in dark pic) When you first plug in, the light is stagnant.

Functionality: No lag so far, smooth typing, perfect for casual gamers or work use

RGB QWERTY (Red Logo)

On Box: Rudra Red Dragon

Price: Slightly Pricier (still great for what you pay for tbh)

Sound: Red Switches, same, not “silent” imo but not too loud either

Base: Black Plastic appearance (top keyboard in light pic) Felt slightly heavier.

Lighting: Much more vibrant (bottom keyboard in dark pic, pic doesn’t do justice, it was significantly brighter) When you first plugin, the light is flowing.

Functionality: No lag so far, smooth typing, perfect for gamers and work use

- - - - -

My review is already long af, but I’ll have my friends update me on overall usage overtime. The “aesthetics” friend plays way more games on their PC, so I’ll be able to tell heavy gamer use for the QWERTY one. While the “functional” friend will be using it for work, as they work from home, so I’ll tell more daily use for the LED one. 👍 I’ll ask more about the settings as well as time goes on, for now, they’re just happy with their new keyboards!

reviews.review_title: Decent for a deal, but could be more durable.
reviews.review_description:
I wouldn't buy this keyboard for more than thirty dollars, but it goes on sale enough that I believe it's worth buying for the twenty or so dollars the bring the price down to. I've had this keyboard for over a year, and it's worked flawlessly for most of that time. There's not much to say about it, functionally. It's a standard full-sized mechanical keyboard. It's not quiet, but I like how clicky it is, personally.

Now, for the reason I don't recommend you buy this for full price. About nine or ten months into owning this item, the keys started to behave finicky. The 'R' key no longer lights up and the 'A' key has a problem with double inputs. I'll give the keyboard this, I use it a lot. I'm a writer and a gamer, so I've really put it through its paces. I'm also not as anal about maintenance as I probably should be. If you regularly dust and clean under the keycaps, it would probably last you a good deal longer.

If your like me, someone who puts your keyboard through heavy use, I would go with something more durable. If you only intend to game with it, it should be fine for about a year, which for twenty dollars is a fine deal.

title: Logitech G413 SE Full-Size Mechanical Gaming Keyboard - Black
description: Upgrade your gameplay experience with the Logitech G413 SE Full-Size Mechanical Gaming Keyboard. It delivers a gaming-grade mechanical switch experience. It’s designed to help serious players perform at a higher level and push themselves even further. The G413 SE features tactile mechanical switches; PBT keycaps, 6-key rollover anti-ghosting performance; a black-brushed aluminum top case with white LED lighting; 12 function key media controls; and reliable USB-corded technology. A compact, tenkeyless option is available. In short, the gaming-first features you need to put more perfect performance within reach. A keyboard engineered to perform. A keyboard that’s Made for Play.

reviews.review_title: Light, bright, responsive, and with a wonderful profile layout
reviews.review_description: Best keyboard I've ever owned. Sturdy case, sleek profile, the layout makes this keyboard incredibly easy to clean without the need to dismantle the keys in the process. The White LEDs are bright and easy to see in the dark, unlike many backlit keyboards that can make it harder to read the keys. The responsiveness both in typing and in the tactile feel of every key clacking on release is a delight. I was skeptical when the sale brought the price below $35, but I could not be more impressed with the quality upon arrival. As a friend has been using a slightly different G4 model for 5 years, I have every expectation that I will be using this keyboard for years to come. Very happy customer.

reviews.review_title: Worth 60 bucks easy, on sale it's an absolute bargain.
reviews.review_description:
I ordered one of these after my place of employment got tired of keyboards failing constantly. After several months of outright abusive use by my co-workers, they still performed flawlessly with a lovely sense of tactile feedback, soda spills aside. One failed only after half a thermos of coffee was spilled into it, but that's to be expected from anything not waterproof rated.

After ordering one for myself to use at home, I LOVE typing on it. It's my first true mechanical keyboard, and it's pleasant to just tap away, typing whatever I feel like. Each key feels like it's got two levels of depression (almost like me): First a clear 'catch' when the key activates and types, and then another more firm one when you reach the bottom of the key well. I've yet to have it double-type anything even when my clumsy fingers wanted to, although it hasn't saved me from butterfingering my keystrokes in games.

As far as gaming goes, it's not PERFECT. It does make an audible noise when typing, so when you are frantically spamming the strafe or jump keys, it's going to sound like clicking the mouse over and over, but it's really no worse than your average mouse. If you're wearing headphones and blasting your speakers, you won't notice it. If you're in a silent small room, you can't avoid hearing it. Find your medium.

Its clearly more meant for office work, but I find it good for gaming, and it's sturdy and heavy enough it doesn't move around at all or feel like it'll die if I drop my phone on it.

reviews.review_title: Great Mechanical Keyboard for gaming or surfing the web.
reviews.review_description: Satisfying but quiet clicks, decent lighting, solid construction, and amazing responsiveness give this keyboard a 5 ⭐ from me. I game pretty much everyday and Logitech is the only keyboard/mouse company I find worthwhile AND affordable. As a major plus, it's also very ergonomic and easy to use for long periods of time.

reviews.review_title: Perfect for me. Really like it.
reviews.review_description:
Just got it so not a complete review. But so far, I really like it. I'm not a gamer, but just needed a keyboard upgrade and this is perfect. So far :)

Note: True, there are no painted letters/numbers on the keys. Once usb plugged in, everything is seen with the backlight on the keys. I figured out the reason: painted letters and numbers wear off after a while. This see-through letters/numbers (presumably) will always remain. You don't use the keys unless plugged in anyhoo! So, I see no problem!

It's very nicely weighted and has a nice feel on the keys. Great for the $35 price I paid!

reviews.review_title: Not the best choice for Mac; satisfying click but not for quiet environments
reviews.review_description:
I can't tell you how well this works for gaming, but if you're looking to buy this as a Mac keyboard for standard daily use, definitely read on.

This keyboard is far better for a PC. It doesn't have matching keys for a Mac keyboard, so you'll have reduced functionality with key commands. These are differences I've come across so far:

- Instead of a CMD key on both sides of the space bar, this keyboard has only one on the left of the spacebar that functions that way, and it's not in the position of the usual Mac CMD key. (see my pic)

- There's no volume control on this keyboard, so you'll have to have your Mac keyboard available to change volume unless you keep volume control visible on your menu bar.

- Screen dimming requires holding this keyboard's fn key and then using F1 or F2.

- Some special function keys on this keyboard don't do anything on a Mac.

Here's what I do like about the keyboard:

- Satisfying click. The keys are like old school keyboards with large keys that actually had feel to them. The volume of the click is kind of loud though, so if you need to maintain a quieter environment this keyboard won't do.

- The attached 10 key is nice to have.

- It's corded so no batteries required.

- The keyboard is sturdy feeling with just-right weight to it

- The key backlighting is adjustable

- No quick trigger keys means no accidental double lettering

- Because the keyboard rises high off your desktop compared to modern keyboards, make sure you have a seating position that lets you keep your hands lower than normal.

Overall this keyboard is probably great for gaming or for PC users who don't have to keep it down while using it. If you're a Mac user, especially one who needs a quiet environment, you should look at different models.

reviews.review_title: Great keyboard with backlight with mechanical keys.
reviews.review_description: This is a mechanical keyboard. That means it is noisy where it has the traditional keyboard sound. I personally love it! The key are far more responsive than the soft-touch keyboards that are mostly used today. The clicking of the keys could be distracting to someone sharing an office, however, if you work in a private office, this keyboard is great. Also, the keyboard is backlit which makes it that much more useful when working late nights in a darker environment. It is constructed of metal and has a slip resistant base that stays put on my keyboard slide.

I've been very happy with this keyboard for everyday work use. The mechanical keys have a great feel and make typing much more enjoyable, especially during long periods of writing and data entry. The build quality feels solid, and the keyboard has a clean, professional look that fits well in an office setup.

I am not impressed, compared to an old and cheap Steelseries Apex 100 (Fuhlen rubber dome) I've had since the late 2010s. This keyboard has taught me that I really dislike backlit keyboards. Even on its lowest backlight setting, it is distracting, and the keycaps are not visible with it off. I haven't used a good mechanical keyboard in quite some time but I did not enjoy the typing feel of this one. The keys are subjectively spongy and stiff. Sadly, it is boxed up for return and was not meant to be. I will still give it three stars as the build quality seems solid and I think it would work well for someone who is not bothered by bright backlighting and enjoys the distinctive feel of these keys.

reviews.review_title: Never thought I'd love a keyboard so much...
reviews.review_description:
It's taking a little getting used to the slightly different arrangement of some keys but man... overall, this keyboard KICKS TAIL!!! I love how it lights up, I'm always working in low light or the dark and my eyes aren't what they used to be so I just can't tell you how much of a difference it makes. I also feel like the key symbols won't/can't wear out because they're backlit. Typical keyboards have letter and words wear off over time, but I don't see how that's possible with this keyboard. It's not a "gamer keyboard" it's just a great basic keyboard with all the functions you need. Keystrokes feel amazing! Not sure how to describe but when you're typing it just feels really nice. A real quality built product and worth every penny. I'm considering buying another before they don't make them anymore... LOL Oh, the battery lasts forever on this thing too. You can turn it OFF when you're done for the day and you can set the keyboard to pair/work with multiple computers (even have keys configured differently if you like). The backlight shuts off when you remove your hands from the keyboard or stop typing for about 5 seconds, but its got this really cool "motion detection" feature that once you put your hands over the keys again or start typing it lights right back up! I'm telling you if you're in the market for a new BLUETOOTH keyboard and are willing to pay a little more for a NICE one... this is the board to have!!! I really love it. I'll give you the 1 thing I didn't like about it as I began using it... The FUNCTION ROW of keys has no space above the NUMBERS or Number pad, etc. So it's super easy to hit the wrong keys sometimes. I'll often go to use the "home" key and end up hitting the key to switch between machines, or the biggest one is the "lock" key the farthest top right key over the number pad's "minus/dash" key. I often go to hit the "minus/dash" key and end up locking my windows (having to sign in again). HOWEVER, using the Logitech software that is used to configure the keyboard I was able to just disable that lock key. I don't need a KEY for that anyway. When I want to lock my Windows session (log out) without shutting down, I'll just do it the normal way with my mouse (Start > Power > Lock). No big, been doing that forever anyway. Anyway, this keyboard is awesome. Especially, once you get used to it. Most times I get a new keyboard and have to get used to the key arrangements and different spacing anyway. Might as well do it with a great keyboard. 😊👍🏻 P.S. I have always been a Microsoft keyboard/mouse kinda guy. I didn't think much of Logitech until I got the MX Master 2 Mouse, which is now also my favorite ever. This keyboard goes with that mouse it's sold in bundles they're of the same product set.

I love this keyboard. I use the same monitor for my gaming PC and for my work Surface Pro. I had a wired keyboard which I had to unplug from the gaming PC and plug into the docking station every morning and then do the reverse after my work hours. It became tedious after a while, so I decided to upgrade to a wireless keyboard that can switch between multiple devices without having me crawl under my desk to do so.

This one seemed not too expensive, had full width, and reviews were decent. I'm very pleased. Switching between devices is handled with 3 dedicated buttons for this specific purpose, no crawling required. I used the dongle to pair it with the gaming PC, and Bluetooth to pair it with my work computer. Now I can work from the kitchen or the yard if I want to.

It's slightly louder than I expected, but is by no means clickety like some others I've used. Typing is now completely satisfying. The texture of the buttons is soft and the feedback is addictive and makes me want to type forever.

As an unexpected bonus, I was able to connect the keyboard to my phone and type in mobile apps with a full keyboard!! What a novel and refreshing experience.

The only complaint from my daughter is that it doesn't have colored backlight. It's just plain white.

If you need a keyboard that fits in a crowded desktop or you just like a clean and neat desk looks, and if you work with applications that require precision on what you type, coding, CAD, the feel and precision of a mechanical keyboard is what you need. Love it. I've heard it's great for games too, but I don't play games at all, so I can't tell, but I bet durability required for games is similar to software coding, tons of strokes per minute. Games are certainly more rough, due to adrenaline, that can be hard on a keyboard. Not my thing, I need precision, and compact format.

So I just received and began to use this keyboard today. I am pretty blown away by how nice it looks, how good it feels, and just the experience overall. Compared to my previous keyboard, I already like this a fair amount more. For reference, I was using the Corsair k57 RGB wireless. Also a quite nice keyboard, but this has a much more premium feel. It's also much more professional looking, which is why I chose it as I plan to use this in an office environment. Some thoughts below.

-The clicks are super nice, I've never used a "clicky" switch with feedback like this before and I quite enjoy it. Probably my favorite feedback I've had from just typing on a keyboard. The various corsair boards I've used in the past I typically chose a quiet and/or a linear switch.

-Overall a very nice, professional look. I wouldn't expect any weird looks with a keyboard like this in a professional environment.

-Pairing was easy, plugged in the receiver and it instantly connected; no other input needed. Even the sister product to this never did that for me, the MX master 3S mouse. I had a bit of a struggle trying to get that to pair using the included receiver, as I recall. (Otherwise one of my favorite mice, also coming from a mostly corsair brand background). There is also bluetooth pairing, if preferred. (or if the receiver refuses to work, like my MX master 3S.)

One minor negative is the backlight. The first problem was even getting the keyboard to light up at all. The keys for the keyboard backlight simply did not seem to function at all, no matter if I had the FN key held or not. Puzzled, I installed logitech's software and looked for options there. No luck. A bit annoyed at this point. Luckily, their software offered me access to an upcoming beta version of their software, "Logitech Options", so I downloaded that to poke around and see if there were more settings there. As it turns out there were. Oddly, they didn't work though. The keyboard refused to light up, the keys meant to dim or brighten it doing nothing at all. As I began a search to see if this was a common issue, the backlight finally came on. No idea what changed. Pretty standard white LED backlights. Lots of pissed off customers on forums about it though. Apparently, Logitech has been pretty silent about the issue. I'd be pissed too, if my $200 keyboard didn't have a functioning backlight due to software issues.

With that rambling anecdote, the backlight itself is just fine, about what I expected for a professional keyboard like this. Just clean white LEDs.

In summary, a very nice looking, nice feeling premium keyboard. Pretty unassuming in a professional environment. Easy setup. Quite happy with it.

Edit: The backlight does not seem to remember brightness settings between use sessions, so if you will get super annoyed or angry about having to hit brightness up each time you use, that's something to consider. Most annoyingly, if the room is deemed "too bright" by the sensor, the backlight will not turn on at all. Understandable, but I'd still like the option.

I replaced a Logitech 860 with the MX, the quality and feel of the MX is very good. I love the feel of the keys. The key setup is more tighter than the 860, but after a couple days I’ve became accustomed to it and I like it. The difference in the feel and quality is significantly better than the 860.

I was very disappointed when I started using this overpriced keyboard.

First of all, the build quality is inexcusable for a $150+ keyboard, especially from a brand like Logitech. The space bar and the backspace keys squeak horribly every time I press them. I understand that can be fixed by applying some white silicone grease, but I shouldn't have to do that with an expensive keyboard right out of the box. In addition, the rubber foot across the back of the keyboard has already started to peel off.

I purchased the tactile (quiet typing) version, and while it isn't the loudest keyboard I have ever typed on, "quiet" is not at all how I would describe it. Someone in the next room or cubicle would definitely be able to hear you typing on this. I wonder how loud the "clicky" version is...

And now, to address the backlight issue: Several reviews have mentioned problems with the backlight. It seems to function "as intended", but the design choices really make me scratch my head. The backlight will turn off just a few seconds after you stop typing, and doesn't turn on again until you press a key. That means that if you aren't constantly typing, the backlight will be turning on and off in a way that is very visually distracting at the bottom of your vision. If you take your hands away from the keyboard, you will not have the keys illuminated to help orient your hands when you start typing again. In a dark room that means you can't see anything on the keys. Even the timing of the backlight is inconsistent. Sometimes it turns off while I am still typing, sometimes it stays on for a minute or two with no input, like it got stuck.

At first I thought I just had to adjust the timeout settings on the Logi Options+ app. Nope! No options! Just a couple of annoying, distracting backlight animations (like, random keys illuminating, why would anyone want that?!). I'm not sure who signed-off on the design for this thing or what they were thinking.

Furthermore, the caps lock key has a distracting blinking whenever it is on, especially annoying if you are gaming and caps lock is set to something like toggle run/walk.

The keyboard is Bluetooth only, which seems to work fine. But I would have liked to have the option to plug it in like a normal USB keyboard. As far as I know the USB plug is only for charging, but also leaves an always illuminated and fairly bright "charging" LED, very obnoxious if your computer is in your bedroom.

In short: Don't waste your money on this. I will be returning mine.

I just finished my first long work session with this keyboard. I'm glad I bought it. It's very easy to type on. It's my first mechanical keyboard of any kind. I went with the quieter version. You still get the clicking sounds, just not super loud. I finally understand what people mean when they say typing on a mechanical keyboard feels more satisfying compared to non-mechanical ones. Highly recommend this keyboard if you're looking to get into mechanical keyboards. Definitely won't be my last.

Original review: It's a keyboard an it works

After hearing people rave about mechanical keyboards, I decided to get myself one. I am not sure how representative of mechanical keyboards this one is, but I find it to be very similar to everything I have used before. The keys don't feel "clicky" at all. In fact, I am constantly running into an issue of resting my hands on the keyboard, and "mushing down" a key by mistake (in other words, "wwwwwwwwwwwwwwwww" because my finger pressed a key without me even noticing).

I think I can get used to pulling my hands away from the keyboard to keep that from happening, but I find it weird that I now have to do this. I assumed the keys would be harder to press, not mushier than the cheap-o keyboards I have had.

Another issue I have had is that the keyboard is not flat. I have tested it on multiple surfaces, including a glass table. I ended having to prop one side up with some paper. Not too happy about that.

For whatever reason, this does not have a print screen key. Luckily you can remap it using the Logi Options+ software.

Honestly, at this price, I am not sure I would recommend this keyboard. Ok, so why 4 stars? It does have some positive points. First, it looks pretty sharp. Second, aside from not sitting flat, it feels solid / well-built / quality. It is small, yet it is heavier than most keyboards. I am used to keyboards lasting "forever", so I will update here if/when I run into issues. Third, switching between different machines works flawlessly. Fourth, it allows me to bring my settings to all computers (e.g. remapping the screen capture key). Fifth, it has a rechargeable battery and it lasts long enough that I never have to worry. I do have a charging cable right on my desk, so every once in a while I just leave it plugged in, so I have never seen it go below 85%. What else can I say, it is a keyboard and it works.

-----

Updated review: beware the USB dongles.

Logitech mouses and keyboards (e.g. "MX Mechanical", "MX Master 3s", "MX Anywhere 3") connect either via Bluetooth, or via a USB dongle. However, the USB dongles are not all the same. For example, the "MX mechanical" keyboard only connects to a "bolt" dongle; and the "MX Anywhere 3" mouse only connects to a "unifying" dongle. Unfortunately, there is no clear guide / summary for which devices go together. You just have to check each device before buying to see what dongle it uses. Devices in the same generation are *not* guaranteed to use the same type of dongle.

Here is my experience: I setup for myself a MX mechanical keyboard + MX Master 3s mouse and everything works fine. Both devices connect to a "bolt" dongle, so I have a "bolt" dongle on my laptop, and another "bolt" dongle on a desktop computer. I can switch between laptop and desktop with a press of a button. The keyboard/mouse itself is fine, the review can be seen above.

My wife saw my setup and wanted the same, but she didn't want the MX Master 3s mouse ("it is too big"), so I got her a this same "MX Mechanical" keyboard and a pink "MX Anywhere 3". As it turns out, the mouse does not come with a "bolt" dongle, it comes with a "unifying" dongle. So now I have one "bolt" dongle which connects only to the keyboard, and one "unifying" dongle which connects only to the mouse. Thus, to "fix" this situation, I either need to use Bluetooth for everything (which I was trying to avoid to begin with), or I need to purchase 1 extra bolt dongle and 1 extra unifying dongle, so that each computer has both a "unifying" and a "bolt" dongle. Let's hope I have enough USB ports, or I will also need a USB hub.

Even if you are aware that different dongles exist, you still need to be careful. If you buy a "MX Anywhere 3", you get a "unifying" dongle, but if you buy a "MX Anywhere 3 for business", then it has a "bolt" dongle. This is, by the way, how I ended up with a "unifying" dongle - while browsing the products, I opened up two tabs, one with a black MX Anywhere 3, and one with a pink MX Anywhere 3, except one of them was "for business" and the other was not.

You might think this mess would warrant giant disclaimers ("DOES NOT HAVE A BOLT CONNECTOR"), or some kind of guide for which devices go together, but nope. For extra hilarity, Amazon bundles a "MX mechanical mini" (bolt) with a "MX Anywhere 3" (unifying). The whole thing is confusing, misleading, and just terrible user/customer experience. If I could start over, I would just get something else.

reviews.review_description:

reviews.review_title: Perfect for work and the sound is ohh so goood!!!
reviews.review_description: I LOVE this keyboard!! After spending two weeks researching I decided on the Aula F99 and I am so happy with my decision. reviews.review_title: First mechanical keyboard ever - love it!
reviews.review_description:
Perfect right out of the box. Set up was effortless. I love the simple and minimalist look and layout of it. I decided to swap my old HP wireless keyboard that I use for work out for this one and while it's a tad bit louder than I expected for snall office settings, I still love the sound and feel of it. reviews.review_title: Bought it for my husband and now it's mine
reviews.review_description:
First I want to say that I initially bought this for my husband as he had bought a walmart clicky brand keyboard and was finally growing tired of the clicky sound lol. Well as the keyboard enthusiast I suggested this one as it was simple and a few of the review videos had sounded promising.

When it arrived the first thing I noticed was the heft, this was made with durable material and not light weight at all, which put some ease to my mind that it wasn't just made of cheap plastic. The size was just perfect, I couldn't be happier, and when I typed for the first time the creamy and thocky sound just itched the right place in my brain. I could not get enough of it.

I love that there are 3 types of way that you can connect, BT; Dongle or wired. I always prefer wired.

The keycaps are nice, although I prefer rounded keycaps to the sharp square ones, I did replace the factory keycaps and I just fell in love with this more. The switches sound nice and deep and honestly, this is almost perfect for me, I'll be playing around with this keyboard especially since it's hot swappable and I might try other switches.

For those just starting out with interest in the keyboard area, this is a great first start with a not too expensive price point! I did end up having to buy another keyboard for my husband since I stole this one, it was definitely worth it though! Can't wait to mod this one a little more!

Coming up on almost a year of owning this keyboard. It was just what I needed. I love the feel of the keys, the sound, the 3 different options to connect, the weight and the number pad. The battery life wireless is okay. I wish there was a power button. Sometimes you accidentally touch a key after turning off the computer and the keyboard feels like it stays on forever lol. The Aula F99 is a "96%" mechanical keyboard that comes in around the $90 price point normally, but can get as low as $60 on sale. That form factor means that it does have a numpad and arrow keys as well as home, delete and page up/down keys, but those keys are moved up in-line with the function keys and the numpad/arrow keys are squished up closer to the main keys with the arrow keys set a little further down to make space. Having a numpad was a must for me because I like to play games that often use the numpad for important functions, and I also prefer typing numbers on a numpad when the occasion arises. At this price point, this is probably one of the best options for people who want a numpad and/or arrow keys but still want a keyboard that looks and sounds more like a custom keyboard you see in YouTube shorts of people doing sound tests.

It has linear switches meaning there's no "bump" or clickiness to them, I'm not 100% sure what exact switches they are because there is some conflicting information online. I think mine has "Star Vector" switches? Regardless, the switches are quite light on force and very quiet, which brings us to the sound. This keyboard sounds great for the price. It's a little on the clacky side, but the switches have no scratchiness to them and are obviously pre-lubed, and there appears to be some kind of sound-deadening material inside the case as there is none of that hollow pinginess you get from something like a cheap Logitech mechanical. Overall it is a massive improvement from the Logitech keyboard I had previously to this one.

The case is plastic but seems to be fairly high quality. The keyboard is surprisingly heavy which is very confidence inspiring and gives you a very stable feeling typing experience. It also has RGB lighting on all of the keys but the keycaps are not shine-through meaning the lettering doesn't light up. If that's a big deal to you, I'm sure you could swap them out for something else later as it does come with a keycap and switch puller, which also means you can change the switches if you want. It also has 3 different connection modes: "Wired" which uses a USB-C port on the board for connection (and it does come with a USB-C to A cable in the box), "2.4 GHz" which uses a little wireless dongle that sits in a little slot on the top edge of the board when not in use, and it's also able to connect via bluetooth. I haven't tested the battery life as I use this keyboard at my desktop computer with the wired connection, but having the different modes and a physical switch to change between them means you could have this board connected to multiple different devices and switch between them whenver you want which is cool and useful if you need that.

I'm fairly new to the world of mechanical keyboards, this is only the second one I've ever owned, the first being a Logitech board that didn't sound or feel nearly as good as this one. As I type this review out on this very keyboard, I find myself liking the sound and feeling more and more. I'm sure there are things about it that someone with more knowledge and experience could pick apart and criticize, but overall I am very happy with this keyboard and would definitely recommend it to anyone who's not an expert and is looking for something better than the offerings from companies like Logitech and Razer.

reviews.review_title: SteelSeries Apex 5 – Almost a 5-Star Keyboard, but Not Quite (4.76 on My Scale)
reviews.review_description:
The SteelSeries Apex 5 left a strong impression. It’s a well-built keyboard with some excellent features and clever design choices. The cable is thick, long, and even has a nice touch — the SteelSeries logo on the USB plug. The RGB effects are top-notch, with smooth transitions both on keypress and when idle. I was genuinely excited about all of this... until I noticed what was missing. And for me, that’s a big deal.

Let’s break it down.😁

### What Makes It (Almost) 5 Stars – The Good:😃

- Excellent Media Controls: The volume wheel is fantastic: easy to reach, smooth to use, and includes a click-to-mute function. The menu button also works similarly to the playback controls found on many headsets with built-in microphones or hands-free kits. Super convenient.

- Onboard Controls – No Software Needed: You can manage brightness, RGB colors, effects, profiles, and more — all from the keyboard itself. No software required. Only macros can’t be directly viewed or edited in menu, which is a small detail worth noting.

- Smart OLED Display: It shows the status of Num Lock, Caps Lock, Scroll Lock, and whether the Windows key is disabled. Very handy (though there’s a small catch — more on that below).

- Customization & Visual Feedback: Besides full per-key RGB customization and reactive effects, pressing the “Fn” key (the SteelSeries logo key) lights up related function keys in red for quick reference. It’s super helpful… but again, not perfect (you can’t change the color — more on that too).

- Profile Memory Built-In: You can save up to 5 profiles directly on the keyboard and toggle them on/off without cycling through all of them. I personally use just two: one for gaming and one for productivity.

### The Not-So-Good – My Gripes😒:

- No Dedicated Context Menu Key: This is my biggest issue. A full-size keyboard should include the dedicated menu key (the "right-click menu" key). SteelSeries replaced it with their custom “Fn” key, which really disrupted my usual workflow. I ended up switching to Shift + F10 to keep things consistent across devices.

- Fn Key Can’t Be Reassigned: The SteelSeries logo key, which replaces the context menu key, is fixed — it can’t be remapped. Personally, I’d have preferred having the Windows key only on the left, and using the right one for Fn, keeping the menu key in its usual place.

- OLED Button Always Lit: The brightness of the button next to the OLED screen cannot be dimmed or turned off. If you’re working in a dark room or watching movies, this little light will keep shining at you — kind of annoying.

- OLED Icons Overlap Custom Logos: If you upload a custom image to the OLED screen, the status icons for Num Lock, Caps, etc. may overlap your logo. Not a dealbreaker, but it limits how creative you can get with personalization.

- No Visual Feedback When Windows Key Is Locked: Unlike other lock states (like Caps Lock), there’s no lighting change or visual indicator on the keyboard itself when the Windows key is disabled — just a small icon on the OLED. Feels inconsistent.

- Function Key Highlight Color Can’t Be Changed: When pressing “Fn,” the related keys light up red — but that red is not customizable. If your RGB theme is red, this effect becomes basically invisible.

- Slight Input Delay: There’s a small delay in key activation. I don’t notice it while typing or working, but for competitive gaming, it might matter. Rtings.com confirmed this in their testing too.

- Non-Replaceable Hybrid Switches This is the most serious issue. The switches aren’t standard and can’t be replaced by the user. If a key fails, you’re stuck with relying on warranty, support… or scavenging another board. Not great.

### Neutral Points – Might Be Good or Bad Depending on You🤷🏻‍♂️:

- Actuation Distance: I switched from a keyboard with ultra-light 0.8 mm actuation, and I kept typing extra characters. The Apex 5 feels much more precise and helped reduce typos — a big plus for me.

- Key Feel & Keycaps: The keycaps aren’t made from premium material, but they feel decent. Coming from linear switches, the tactile feel took a bit of getting used to — but I adjusted quickly.

- Magnetic Wrist Rest: I don’t use it much, but the magnets are strong and hold it firmly in place.

- Macro Labeling (M1, M2, etc.): Some keys are labeled as macro keys (M1, M2...), which can be confusing at first — but you’ll get used to it.

- Customization Without Software: You can change basic RGB effects and profiles directly from the keyboard. The software adds more depth, but it’s nice that you’re not forced to use it.

- USB Plug with Logo: A small but smart touch: the SteelSeries logo on the USB plug helps you spot which device you’re plugging in.

- No Physical Lock LEDs: The lock indicators (Num Lock, Caps, Scroll) have been moved to the OLED screen, and you can set those keys to change color when active. Some might miss the old-school LED lights, but I’m fine with it.

### Final Verdict 💸😇

 The SteelSeries Apex 5 is a well-built, visually polished keyboard with great RGB, useful media controls, and a solid set of features for gamers and professionals alike. Still, a few oversights — especially the missing context menu key and the non-replaceable switches — keep it from being a perfect 5-star device in my eyes.

If those flaws don’t bother you, then this keyboard is an easy recommendation. Just know what you're getting — and what you're not

reviews.review_title: Nice keyboard - Amazon Refurbished just sucks
reviews.review_description:
I have only had this keyboard for a few days at the time of this review, but from what I can tell it is a solidly built keyboard with a nice feel and decently responsive keys.

I did have to knock off a star though as the keyboard I received was in poor condition with two of the keys having keypress detection issues. This however was NOT the fault of SteelSeries as I bought this one from Amazon Refurbished.

Do NOT buy this keyboard from Amazon Refurbished. They do only the bare minimum to make the keyboard presentable, and do not open it to check the internals before shipping it. Or else they would have seen the gunk inside that was causing the key press detection issue.

Thankfully, user maintenance was easy. Simple matter of taking off the key caps, taking out the cover screws, and the mainboard screws. Then I was able to clean it with a little alcohol and reassemble it. Works like it was new. Just didn't expect that I would have to be the one doing the refurbishing on day one. But that's why I gave it 4 stars, pretty easy to perform user maintenance on it to ensure that it continues to function. Which boggles me why Amazon didn't do that.

Ok, so after spending a couple weeks with this board I can tell you-

A couple of things I wasn't really aware of-

2) How much I relied on outside esc and ctrl keys for orientation

These keys are very sensitive compared to the old BW I've used for years. I've been accidentally entering a lot of keystrokes at rest. They are very quiet and soft stroking compared to the green switches in the older Black Widow I've retired. So if you want clicks, feedback or resistance look elsewhere. I pulled up all those caps on that row and replaced with wider pudding caps for brighter distinction. Programed those keys to mirror their neighbors, esc ,Ctrl etc so that when an erroneous keystroke is made it should at least still be the function I was looking for, albeit orientation may be off from wasd. So anyway I'm having to look down a lot more at the keyboard and retraining my mind to orient off the *F key

reviews.review_title: Durable and well built. Survived a liquid disaster.
reviews.review_description:
I have the green switch version.

Durable and Chroma lighting is excellent. Put O rings in the keys to dampen slightly. Key feeling and clicks are a matter of personal preference.

Spilled coffee on this one twice. I thought the keyboard was toast after the last disaster spill. Keys weren't functioning and the leds were out. I took it apart and rinsed it out the affected areas heavily with alcohol. Blew the liquid out with compressed air/compressor. Works fine now.

After taking it apart I could see how good the quality was. Keyboard backplate is actually solid metal.

2 screws under the top two rubber foot pads. Careful, the pads tear easily.

18+- screws under the keys. Remove the keys to find them all.

Had it for a bit over a week now and it's been great. I originally had the Razer blackwidow V1 with the green clicks switches and it was great the thing finally crapped out on me a few weeks ago. The thing lasted me forever, was super durable and felt very responsive. My biggest complaint was it was hard to clean. So I decided to go with the newest version and try the Yellow switches. I didn't like the softer yellow switches at first but have come to like them and this keyboard solved the cleaning issue. My biggest problem was actually the Macro keys on the left hand side. With my old keyboard I used the edge of they keyboard to orient my hand without looking when gaming, this makes it hard to do that because my fingers end up on the macro keys. I've started to retrain myself to position properly but it wasn't easy. Other than that this keyboard is fantastic.
Awesome keyboard!

Fun RGB lighting, fully customizable colors within the Razer lighting program. Lighting program is easy to use with plenty of tutorials on installation. Can customize individual keys for different lighting when pressed. Extra macro buttons on the left will take some getting used to, but just imagine what all you can assign them as. Solid keyboard in terms of weight, back wings to lift up to have it at a slight angle. Keycaps nice and solid quality. These are soft and bubbly sounding in my opinion, not sharp and clicky. In prior experience with Razer, the price is a bit up there, but I would wager its worth it. Received on September 28th, 2025; will check back after a while to update review if needed.

Before I got this keyboard, I was using the 2016 edition razer blackwidow ultimate. That keyboard still works perfectly, and the only problem I had with it was that the keyboard was LOUD as heck.

Enter the blackwidow v4 x with yellow switches. At first i was extremely happy with the look, feel, and materials of the keyboard, it felt very premium, and the keys were MUCH quieter.

I bought it in December of 2023. By March 2024 I noticed an issue with the "P" key being unresponsive. Meaning when you press the key, there was a chance of it not registering the keypress. So if you press the key 10 times, it may only display about 5 or 6 times. Not that bad for gaming since the "P" key is hardly used. However when typing it could get very annoying. I attached a video showing me trying to press the button 3 times, followed by a space, then the button 3 times, then a space etc. You can clearly see it does not register the keypress quite often.

Eventually I decided that since I paid $100+ I was going to get a working product. My RMA process started on April 20, 2024, and after many days of back and forth emails with razer trying to convince them it was a hardware, not software, issue they gave me a shipping label to send out on April 26, 2024. I received the replacement about 3 weeks later on May 17, 2024.

Today on May 18, 2024 I noticed the same unresponsive key issue with the "2" key above the "W" key. This IS a big deal for gaming since it is used very often.

I dont want to go through the RMA process again, and im pretty sure I cant get a refund from amazon after 4 months so this keyboard will likely just be tossed in the garbage where it belongs. A lot of time and money wasted on a sub-par product.

Been using Razer keyboards and mice since about 2012 but its probably time to try a different brand to try since their quality seems to have gone down. Shame.

You still have all of your Home, End, PgUp, PgDn, Insert, Delete, and Print Screen and Pause/Break keys. The only key missing is the Scroll Lock key which is never used anyway so this is perfect.

It has nice RGB that lights up under and around the keys. Also comes with some extra switches and even a decent keycap and switch puller tool. Even comes a thin, cheap, plastic dust cover which I appreciate.

My only complaint whatsoever about this keyboard is that I'm not too crazy about the switches, but that's really a personal preference thing. reviews.review_title: The best value for a budget keyboard, hands down.
reviews.review_description:
This keyboard has been an absolute dream, and the price cannot be beat. It uses bsun switches (I'm honestly not sure which, I've done some digging but can't find them), of which I got the linear version. These switches are nice, there is no noticeable scratch, a crisp bottom out, and the stabilizers are actually silent with no rattle or ticking. There is a variety of foam included, but they leave a bit of room in the case which keeps the board from sounding muted. There are NO SCREWS, so modding this thing is a breeze (might need a small flathead tho) and you have a lot of options straight out of the box. It also comes with a hotswap board, so you can lube the switches (already lubed, but do what you want) or change them out entirely. There are also FLIPPY FEET (2 STAGE!!) so you can adjust your typing angle. I have heard people complain about the software that comes with the board, but it turns out it is fully compatible with the Signal RGB app. Now I can assign any pattern I want, even outside of the presets! The lighting is very prominent since the LEDs are south-facing. 3 of the lights do not work in the software, but they are on the edge of the board with the modifier keys so they are not noticeable.

My ONLY gripe is that the keycaps are not very durable. I have been using mine for a few months now and the tops of the WASD keys are starting to become shiny and smoother. These are likely not PBT, but they are a very thick ABS so the sound stays deeper and fuller. However, a PBT set from a name brand manufacturer costs more than this entire keyboard, so this is an incredibly minor complaint.

reviews.review_description:
Just received my RisoPhy RGB Mechanical Gaming Keyboard and I'm already impressed! Unboxing was smooth — everything was well packaged and arrived in perfect condition.

Right out of the gate, the mechanical switches feel fantastic — satisfying and responsive with great tactile feedback. Typing this review on it now and it already feels way better than my old membrane keyboard.

The RGB lighting looks amazing — all 104 keys are individually backlit with tons of color and lighting mode options. Instantly upgraded the look of my desk setup.

Build quality feels solid and premium — no flex, no creaking, and the keycaps have a nice, smooth texture. It's a standard full-size layout with number pad, so it was easy to jump right in with no learning curve.

Can't speak to long-term durability yet, but based on first impressions, this keyboard seems like an excellent value. Will update if anything changes, but so far I'm very happy

Bought this keyboard for my office, as a replacement for a wireless, membrane based keyboard that was starting to show its age.

The value of this keyboard is excellent. Based on the feel, it seems to be a true mechanical keyboard with switches, and not a simulated one using a membrane contact with a clicky mechanism. The feel is great and the pressure is just right to prevent most accidental touches to adjacent keys from inserting extra letters. Nice and clicky, maybe not the best for noise if you're in an office with other people, but the feel is great and if you work in a private office like I do the noise won't matter much. I had thought the RGB colors would be distracting, especially for an office, but actually they are fairly subdued and actually seem to help with positioning (I am a fast hunt-and-peck 3 finger typist, so this actually matters a lot to me).

I have a much more expensive Razer mechanical gaming keyboard at home, and the main difference I see between them, other than cosmetic differences, is that the Razer keys seem like they have a hair trigger and require very little motion to produce keystrokes, while this keyboard is a bit stiffer and requires the keys to be depressed a little harder in order to produce a keystroke. So if you are relying on a hair trigger response for gaming, this maybe is not the best choice, although for a casual gamer like me it's more than adequate. But for actually getting work done, the hair-trigger of the Razer keyboard makes it really hard not to make typos, and this keyboard is a lot better in that regard.

One minor nitpick is that the font used to label the keys is a little odd, and the "6" really, really looks like a "G", which can be a little off-putting at first. But that's just a minor quibble.

Final verdict: Definitely worth buying, unless you're an absolutely elite hardcore gamer.

reviews.review_title: Great build quality and wonderful switches and key caps.
reviews.review_description: Can’t beat it for the money. The switches feel great to type on and have a wonderful thock sound to them. In my initial typing test I found the keys to be accurate with minimal accidental activation to the adjacent keys at all. The build quality is much better than I anticipated, and the keyboard had no issues connecting to my PC right out of the box. My only gripe is the software. It is difficult to find the correct download on their website, and although I understand the mini screen is customizable I was unable to find the software version that allows customization.

I love this keyboard. It was kinda difficult to figure out how to add the gif I wanted. But figured it out and it’s so cute. I added my own switches just for the sound preference. It’s worth the price, the quality is great. It has so many rgb light options

A lot to unpack here but bear with me as I may be able to help with setting up the gif feature. So the instructions are absolutely no help, and for all the other features aside from choosing your RGB light set up manually from the display screen you need to install a driver to connect it to. Keyboard comes with none of that info on where to download. After watching countless videos I found a tutorial for a different ajazz keyboard explaining there’s two websites.. confusing. My husband is a computer nerd and he helped me through this (he hated it). Go to a-jazz.com (translate to English). On the menu option look for “drivers” search the keyboard model number to download the driver for this keyboard “AK-980 v2” I couldn’t find it so I used the 970. I chose the “wired” option since I had my keyboard plugged in via USB wire and make sure you are on usb mode not “BT”. I did not use the dongle either (usb receiver/chip thingy). Run the driver and the program-app will open. What you want is the monitor icon on the left side where the settings are. If you don’t see it, you may have downloaded the wrong driver. We did that the first time around. Once you have that, you can “import” a gif. Make sure you copy and save the gif of your choice from google or wherever in the “gif” folder of the ajazz program beforehand so you can find it easily. Once you import you can save it and “upload to keyboard” takes a few minutes. Before actually uploading, if the frames at the bottom still appear black after importing your gif, then it will not upload correctly. Check to make sure you are uploading the correct gif as the primary default one cannot be deleted and shows black frames also and that’s okay you can have more than one saved. If you have the correct driver, once importing the gif you will see about 135 frames of the new gif in color (not black) and this is what you want. For any other help definitely check YouTube/reddit.

Finally, this is an excellent keyboard - my honest opinion. It is good quality but I took off a star because seller provides no immediate resources out of the box not even the website to download the driver. The gif is the main attraction for many (me) yet impossible to do if you’re not that computer savvy, you’ll get stuck.

Furthermore, I believe mine was returned and maybe because of the difficulty of the gif feature idk .. I don’t think they were able to figure that out. It’s brand new yet the box was a bit raggedy, looked like it sat at someone’s home for a bit! So far I think I’ll keep it because I finally set it up to my preference, my husband spend two hours figuring it out for me, and I love the typing sound, weight, and quality. Still unsure about battery life, I plan to keep it plugged in via usb wire at work so I can’t say on wireless use.

The only thing I can't speak to is the software for remapping the keys. This can be downloaded from the Cherry site. But it doesn't run on my Linux system so I can't make use of it. However I really see no need to remap any of the keys, and if I really need to do that, there are other ways.

reviews.review_title: I can't believe the improvement over other switches. It's crazy!
reviews.review_description:
If you thought other companies made good key switches, then you are in for a surprise with this keyboard. Cherry absolutely nailed it with these new MX2A switches. I purchased the version with the Cherry MX2A Silent Red switches. Now, I basically hate linear switches. Really, I usually can't stand them, but these new silents reds are the smoothest, and most buttery feeling switches I have ever felt. I have been using mechanical keyboards my entire life. Since before the patent ran out on the Cherry MX switches and the only mechanical keyboards you could buy had Cherry switches. Now, everyone makes their own switches, with all kinds of "features" like hall effect, rapid trigger, analog, adjustable actuation, magnets, etc.. Here's the issue with all of those though, they feel like crap to type on and are super loud. I have spent thousands on keyboards over the years. I still have over 15 mechanical keyboards sitting in storage that I stopped using. I am not exaggerating either. To give you an idea of where I'm coming from, my favorite switches used to be Cherry MX Brown. Now they are Cherry MX2A Silent Reds. I haven't even mentioned how quiet they are too. Unbelievably quiet for a mechanical keyboard. It's definitely the quietest mech keyboard I have ever used, which is saying a lot. Some people may think the keyboard is fairly basic, and in all reality, it is. It doesn't require software, doesn't have RGB or any lights (besides the led for caps lock and such), it doesn't have a removeable cable, or a super high polling rate over 1000Hz. Visually and functionally speaking, the keyboard is simple. But that a huge positive in my book. It does have full N-key rollover, so if you do use it for gaming, there won't be any issues there. I don't need to install any bloat to use the keyboard. I don't need to configure anything. It's just plug and play. It's fairly compact for a full-sized keyboard too, so be aware of the slightly more compact layout. My only real complaint is that it does not have 4 rubber feet on the bottom to keep it from sliding around. There are 2 rubber feet on the bottom front, but on the bottom rear, the feet are hard plastic, so it doesn't stay in place super well. There are rubber pads on the bottom rear feet that fold out, but I don't use a keyboard angled, so they are useless for me. Other than that, one thing, this keyboard is perfect for me. Am I going to use it for my hardcore gaming sessions? No. I actually purchased it for office work, and it's going to be perfect for that. However, will I be purchasing another keyboard with these same exact switches for my gaming pc? 100% YES! Look, you may not like the design of this keyboard, or its simplicity, but do not sleep on these new Cherry switches. Cherry is back with a vengeance, and if you're looking for a new keyboard, get one with these new Cherry switches. Whether it be this keyboard or not. The switch is king, and Cherry is back on top.

Update: I now own 3 of these keyboards, lol, all with the Cherry MX2A Silent Red switches. One for the gaming pc, one for the work office, and one for the home office. They can't be beaten when it comes to typing quality. No regrets.

reviews.review_title: Budget HE keyboard that gives you all you need...
reviews.review_description:
AULA WIN68 HE is my first ever HE keyboard, after years of being in the world of mechanical keyboards and exclusively favoring the brown switch (tactile) I always watched many videos and people praising HE keyboards and the edge they give to you in gaming primarily. We all know of the famed Wooting 60 HE which started this trend in gaming world both the price and being only 60% give's it only a small and competitive market for a few individuals that can afford it or need it for professional e-Sports. As primarily a single-player gamer I was blow away with how much HE switches changes your experience of playing and gives you for the first time ever something that gamepads had over keyboards, and that is you don't need to push the key all the way for it work, both only a slight push fulfils the given command that you want (MMOs and racing games benefit from this the most). The web software is one of the best features of this keyboard and it allows you to customize every single key however you want it, every key supports rapid trigger as well as customizing the dead zone as well as primarily the sensitivity of the keys. reviews.review_title: nice key board for cheap price
reviews.review_description: I am extremely happy with this purchase. The product worked exactly as expected and exceeded my expectations in both quality and performance. It was easy to use, well-made, and delivered excellent results. Everything arrived in great condition, and it has performed flawlessly since I started using it. I would definitely recommend this product to others and would not hesitate to purchase it again

This is a very good full keyboard, with inverted T arrow navigation keys, numeric keypad, home/end/pgup/pgdown/delete/insert grouping, and 12 function keys. It's also backlit with a good variety of lighting modes. So far I'm really happy with it. Could it be better? Sure; it lacks a wrist rest, ergonomic layout like a Microsoft Natural, and doesn't have dedicated media control keys (although this last point isn't a big deal for me since this keyboard is for use with a computer that won't be used for multimedia).

However, keyboards are a very personal thing and a big deal these days, so here are some more details to help you understand this keyboard's features.

Weight: It's not as heavy as the dedicated gaming mechanical keyboards that seem popular now with gamers and programmers. But it's not flimsy either. Light enough to not be much hassle if you're going to be traveling with it.

Key feel: This keyboard is not one of the loud clicky ones. It does feel more tactile than a typical membrane keyboard, and the keys have a nice travel when you press them, but the click sound is very soft. These are regular-style keys, not chicklet keys.

Lighting: I wasn't too worried about have top RGB features, but sometimes if it's darker in the room I do like some backlighting. This keyboard is a nice compromise between keyboards that have only white backlight, and keyboards that have a full software control app that let you customize everything. There is no software with this keyboard, it has several modes all configured using the function keys. Here are the lighting modes:

- Lighting off/on

- Neon mode: multiple colors light up three static zones on the keyboard. There are a few combinations you can select. The colors stay the same in the zones and don't change.

- Spectrum mode: 7 colors rotate and fill the entire keyboard continuously. So it'll be lit red, then fade into purple, then blue, then green, etc.

- Static mode: You cycle through and pick the color you want of the 7 supported colors, and it will stay lit continuously with just that one color.

There are brightness and breathing effects that you can configure for each of the modes.

I only use static mode, but gamers might like the other ones. I saw more expensive boards that only did spectrum or only had one color.

Key visibility: The keys are not painted so they're a little hard to read in poor lighting if you don't use the backlight. However, I did like that the symbol keys had the correct placement for lower/upper case characters. I have seen many expensive keyboards from Razer, Corsair, Alienware, etc., that often invert the upper/lower case labeling for symbol keys and number keys. If you're an experienced typist, you'll work around that, but it bugs me when I see it. I found out later that this is an intentional design decision so that the more commonly used lower case symbol is more visible when backlit (the lighting doesn't cover the entire key and ends up emphasizing whatever character is in the upper case position). But you won't have to worry about that with the ReDragon.

Key layout: After looking at the huge variety of keyboards on Amazon, you'll notice that some smaller keyboards don't have the numeric keypad or the six-key navigation group. Or that some have that ANSI style keyboard with the bigger Enter key but then put the slash key somewhere else. Or some that have compressed distance between keys or even smaller keys to make it more compact.

This keyboard has an ISO keyboard layout with 104 full-sized keys. The key spacing is about a quarter-inch, which is similar to other full-size keyboards I've used.

For the price, I think this is a great peripheral. Longevity would be my only concern, and I'll update this review later if I run across any issues.
