reviews.review_title: DO NOT Buy! Failed within 15 days; Support SUCKS! Overpriced, Go Watch 7
reviews.review_description:
BOTTOM LINE: if you don't need the 3 Labs - Advanced Glycation End (AGE) product index, the Antioxidant index (does not work anyway), or the Vascular Load, ***Go With the WATCH 7!*** If you do get a watch 8, return it to Amazon as soon as it screws up!

Watch 8 #2 is now "inching up" on its O2 measurements. At first, it was 2% points over my Innovo FDA-Approved O2 device. That's okay, because as long as it was consistent, I could deal with it. Now, it is 3% over my Innovo -- My Watch 8 #1 and Watch 7 did the same. I hope this is not a harbinger of failure. It also must be tightened down painfully snug at night.

Oct 14, 2025. Bought new watch 8, now Watch 8 #2

I am riddled with inflammation, so pursue antioxidants. I take 3 supplements twice a day. Yet the Antioxidant index stays low. Farce.

****************************** Below is the Watch 8 #1

Oct 10, 2025 - Samsung refunded cost

Sent it in a second time. Kept checking (two weeks) and nothing. Finally, Samsung offered a refund. Not for the tax, of course. Awaiting refund.

Sep 26, 2025 Already Failing with Same Errors

Was on the phone forever with Samsung, being fobbed off on every department imaginable. I bought a Brand-New Watch for $350, and they "repaired it" only to have the same problems!

I am so mad I could chew a horseshoe and spit nails. I wish I'd never bought this thing! If you are stupid enough to buy it, return it to Amazon at the first fail! It is not YOU! The sensor array is P-poor and it fails. I miss my Watch 4.

Sep 25, 2025 Samsung repaired the watch under warranty. It wiped out all trending in the app.

"New" watch still has "blanks" in its monitoring (picture). Samsung says, "wear snugly". It is already so snug it hurts (picture). Furthermore, the "O2" monitoring is 5% MORE than my commercial O2 monitor. I guess I have to go back to wearing five different monitors that are correct.

Sep 15, 2025. The watch has become worse. I will contact Samsung under the warranty.

Anytime I get sweaty, the watch stops tracking on the wrist! I'm skinny - BMI 20.2. It's a fitness watch, for God's Sake! One expects it to work when you are sweaty! But no - it stops tracking the heart rate and the oxygen level. This is not at all what one wants in a Fitness tracker!

Aug 31, 2025. The watch has developed issues with tracking heart rate.

I was walking - spanking pace - and the watch stopped tracking my heart rate. I stopped for a directed measure. It said "put your watch on". I took the watch off and cleaned it, and had same result. I finally rebooted the watch and it worked again. I DID NOT have this problem with the Watch 4.

Aug 5th, 2025. Anti-oxidant scan doesn't work right.

The scan kept saying low - eat a carrot. Three days of carrots and it is still low.

Also, I tried to take another scan and the software kept saying "Put your watch back on." - but the watch WAS on. Too many bugs.

Aug 2nd, 2025 My initial review wasn't accepted; I am unsure why.

I hemmed and hawed about Watch7 and Watch8. I went for this Watch 8 due to features. I am very disappointed.

First, I have many Samsung-branded chargers. I was very disappointed that the Watch8 band would not allow the Watch 8 to work on the flat chargers. I guess you could put a weight on the watch, like 2 lbs (!) to press it down, but I believe Samsung should have designed their Watch8 to be compatible with its supporting chargers. See first pic.

Second, this is a 40mm watch. I compare it to the Watch4 and the Watch 7, the only others with which I have familiarity. The Watch8 face measures 40mm, but the display is smaller by 2mm, making it a 38mm display.

I cannot at this time comment on durability as I have had it three days. Color is personal choice. EDIT - Watch began failing before 30 days! I thought it was me.

Functions. The Watch8 is extraordinarily bloated by location-tracking bloatware. I do not do use email, bixby, wallet, etc. from the watch, but it will not allow me to uninstall these apps. Furthermore, every app tracks your location with precision! I have no idea why outlook would need location, for example.

The Watch8 has the same processor as the Watch7. Comparing it with the Watch4, I do not see any difference in performance. I would have expected better.

The new Health features are AGE - Advanced Glycation End products. Not sure what the low - adequate - high means, and there isn't a lot of information on the web. It also does the antioxidant index - very low - low - adequate. I tried the recommendation --- eat carrots. My value did not change. Lastly, is vascular load. It is supposed to an indication of lifestyle factors affect on your health. Basically, get sleep, exercise, and good diet. Shrug.

The Watch8 is supposed to have a better battery. However, I do not see the Watch8 lasting any longer than my Watch4. I still charge the Watch8 at my noon-ish nap time, and see the Watch 8 is down to 66% at noon, and again down to 66% at night, after having been charged at noon. If I could uninstall some of the not-used apps, it may be better, and maybe not.

All in all, after seeing all the additional tracking and inability to turn it off, the questionable value of the new "features", the failure to be compatible with industry and brand standard equipment, I wish I'd gone with the Watch7.

Cons:

If you need a reliable, attractive daily case and aren't putting your phone through extreme hazard environments (like heavy construction or intense outdoor sports), this is an absolute winner. reviews.review_description:
This case looks much better in front of you than a picture can render. I have the Product Red iPhone XR and this is the red case. The color comes very close to the color of the aluminum frame and looks like part of the phone. At first glance it doesn't look like there is any case at all! The red color is a shiny, metallic red as opposed to the matte red color of the iPhone frame. It does not clash where the phone's color can be seen in the cutouts and it nicely compliments the color on the back of the phone! Contrary to what another reviewer said, this case does indeed have a lip for basic screen protection. If you lay your phone face down on a perfectly flat surface with this case on, the screen will not contact anything. That being said, it is minimal by design. If you think you may be tossing your expensive phone around in places where the screen could be impacted perhaps you would be better served with a more robust case. This case is a great value for what it is! It complements the phone's styling. It will protect your phone from scratches on the back and sides. I had an iPhone 6 Plus with no screen protector installed on the glass for four years. The only protection was the lip provided by the various cases I used. The glass never got more than the most superficial, barely visible marks in that length of time. Totally worth it to me for the arguably better user experience of the naked glass screen. Even the most pricey tempered glass screen protectors do not match the buttery smooth touchscreen experience in my opinion. My fingers do not slide the same way. Anyway, the glass on the iPhone XR is significantly tougher than previous phones and I don't anticipate a problem. I offer that information only to illustrate that, with proper care in handling, you can rock an inexpensive, minimalist case with no issues. It should be noted, as another reviewer has said, that the back of this case is NOT perfectly clear. The phone can be seen but there is a pattern or texture which is noticeable if you hold it to the light just right. Not a deal breaker at all for me. You can still showcase the beauty of your XR with this case but it could be an issue if you require a perfectly clear back. I think this pattern may have something to do with durability and I doubt it will be an issue to most users. There is a color coordinated lip to protect the camera lens and I love the custom color coordinated cutout for the flash and mic modules in the back. So many XR cases simply have a huge opening that looks like it was designed for a dual camera setup. I like the extra attention to detail. One caveat: The fit is snug. If you are like me and frequently take you case off for thorough cleaning or want to rock a different case for that day, care should be taken when removing this case. The iPhone's aluminum frame is slippery and you could launch your phone out of your hands! I bought several cases together to compare. The Ranvoo case is nearly identical to this one. That one is much easier to remove because it is ever so slightly thinner. It has the same attention to detail in the cutouts and the same pattern in the "clear" back. The tradeoff is there is virtually no raised lip to protect the screen which is why it's easier to remove. Both products are good for what they are. This Torras case is a remarkably nice product for the money. With proper care it could be the only case you need but at this price, it will be a nice option in your iPhone's wardrobe.

Snug fit with my iPhone 17 Pro so it protects my phone quite well and I’m quite happy with it. Seems to be durable as I have dropped my phone a couple of times I’m very surfaces and so far, I haven’t seen a crack anywhere. Quality seems to be solid so far but only time will tell. Feels very slick and smooth, but maybe too smooth as it has been known to slide quite easily. There is a protector for the front screen (which I did not purchase), but I decided against it as I have discovered front screens reduce the phone‘s ability to detect commands with my finger after time has progressed and dirt/detritus builds up behind the screen after a certain length of time. I was concerned at first that the edge of the case on the back where the lenses are located would raise the phone too high and not allow charging when the phone was laying down on a charge mat, but that was not the case. Although, I did discover that exact positioning is important as just laying it down doesn’t always mean the phone is charging. So, I had to make sure to watch the screen when I wanna charge to make sure the mat and the phone aren’t position to charge when needed.

All in all, this is a pretty solid product and I haven’t seen any yellowing in the plastic case as of yet, but it’s only been a couple months since I’ve been using it so maybe after a year I’ll reassess again. If there was one thing that would bug me about this case, is the raised lip of the back of the case surrounding the lenses. There was already a raised area on the phone for those lenses and this case just makes it that much more pronounced. I can only guess that the raised lip area on the back of the case is to further protect the lenses, but that also makes it harder for easy positioning for charging, and makes the phone bulkier when being placed into a pocket or bag. Still, this protects my phone and does what I want it to do so the raised area on the back is a minor issue that I can live with for now. Would I get another one? Hmmmm, maybe. Too early to tell at this point. But I won’t say no if something better comes out on the market.

reviews.review_title: Great MagSafe Hold & Premium Look without the Premium Price Tag
reviews.review_description:
Finding a solid case for an iPhone SE that actually includes strong, reliable MagSafe compatibility can be a bit of a hunt. I picked this up looking for an everyday protective cover that wouldn't break the bank, and straight out of the box, it delivered exactly what was advertised. It offers an incredible value compared to high-end name-brand cases that cost three to four times as much.

Real-World Details & Performance

The fit on the phone is absolute perfection—it snaps on snugly and feels almost like a factory-custom cover with no loose edges or awkward alignment. The translucent matte finish gives the phone a very clean, high-class aesthetic that looks much better in person than standard clear TPU cases.

Functionally, the MagSafe magnets are surprisingly strong. Magnetic chargers and accessories lock into place firmly with zero slipping. It has already survived a few accidental drops around the house without a scratch to the phone or the case itself. While I've only had it for a short time—so long-term durability over months of heavy use remains to be seen—the initial build quality feels remarkably sturdy.

Pros & Cons

Pros:

Strong MagSafe Hold: Magnets align perfectly and grip chargers securely.

Custom Fit: Wraps precisely around the phone without bulk or gaps.

Classy Aesthetic: Translucent back gives it a sleek, high-end look.

Unbeatable Value: Delivers the protection and features of expensive cases at a fraction of the cost.

Proven Drop Defense: Handled initial drops smoothly with great corner protection.

Cons:

Unproven Long-Term Wear: Too early to tell how the TPU border and translucent back will hold up against daily friction and yellowing over time.

Final Verdict

If you need a reliable, attractive daily case and aren't putting your phone through extreme hazard environments (like heavy construction or intense outdoor sports), this is an absolute winner. I would easily buy this again or pick one up for my kids' phones. Highly recommended for anyone wanting full MagSafe functionality and sleek style on a budget!

The camera protector sticks out a little further from the camera, so that makes me feel better when I drop the phone; and I definitely drop my phone! The case fits snug, no looseness. Well worth the money!

Can’t beat this case for the price. I think this is the third Supfine case I’ve purchased and each one has been great, no issues with case quality. They are thin, so not much bulk added to the phone, with good texture that is enough to hold in one hand. Easy to install/remove and magsafe works great through them all as well. I believe this is the frost on that came with a screen protector, which is an added bonus.

I’ve been really happy with this case. I wanted something that would protect my phone without adding a lot of bulk, and this has been a great balance.

The buttons are still easy to press, the cutouts line up well, and the MagSafe connection has been strong with my charger and accessories. I also like that the back is semi transparent because it lets the phone color show through while still protecting it.

I’ve dropped my phone a couple of times already with this case on, and it’s held up well so far. It still looks nice, and I haven’t noticed any yellowing.

I’d definitely recommend it if you’re looking for a simple, clean looking MagSafe case.

The magnetic connection is strong and works well with MagSafe accessories. The buttons are easy to press and the raised edges give extra protection around the screen and camera. Great everyday case for the price.

This case is very sturdy and super clear, I love that i can see the color if my phone. There is a little cut out near the bottom camera on back to make it easier to put on a wireless charger and to use other magnetic accessories. I've had this case for several months now, and it has been very protective, I'm a little clumsy and have dropped my phone a few times, and there are no scratches or cracks. There is a tiny bit of yellowing at the edges now, but I expect any clear case to yellow at least a little over time.

reviews.review_title: A good case for those who are not nit picky!
reviews.review_description:
Was going to give 3 stars for the other bad reviews and after noticing the top portion of my front case is warped a bit. However, I absolutely love this case! Aside from the warppage lol it is a very excellent material for comfort and slip resistance. The case is perfect for those who are looking for a little bit of additional protection yet don't mind not having many bells and whistles. Personally I just needed something to put my Strap onto. I use a permade strap with 3M on the back I got from here for my Fold 4. I used the same strap on my 6 and now 8. These can be purchased as a pack of 5 or 7 or so. They come in various colors also, white, green, blue, Grey, black, etc. I threw the Grey onto my case and it is all I can ask for! Still see the phones color bright as day and it does a good job at not blocking this out or being too thick. It allows for the display to be mostly open and not intervened with when typing or texting which is great. It also keeps the phone protected well and i would trust this case over many I have had in the past.

I used to just leave the front open and for most 2 part cases this is what I do. This one is slim thankfully and it does an awesome job as well at distinguishing the volume buttons from the power button as they are extruding a decent bit now and a large improvement over stock imo! Is this case perfect or the best?!

Not even close, but is it more than enough for some like me and a good fit for the 8? Yes, especially if manufactured correctly!

reviews.review_title: Unbeatable Value — Beautiful on Space Gray iPhone 14 Pro
reviews.review_description:
I purchased the B-A Purple (D-Purple) color variant for my iPhone 14 Pro, and it fits like a glove. The clear body with the lilac/purple MagSafe ring looks absolutely stunning against the Space Gray finish — it's elegant without being flashy, perfectly complementing the steel body aesthetic.

What I love:

• The clear edges and body stay true to the phone's original beauty

• The lilac MagSafe ring adds a gorgeous subtle pop of color

• Slim and lightweight — you barely notice it's on

• Includes a 9H tempered glass screen protector — great bonus at this price

• MagSafe works perfectly — snaps on chargers and accessories with confidence

On yellowing issue: Every clear case yellows eventually — I've paid premium prices for Speck and Incase clear cases that promise no yellowing, and they all yellow at the edges too. At ~$6, this case offers the same real-world performance at a fraction of the price.

FYI for iPhone 15 Pro users: Size-wise it fits the my iPhone 15 Pro, but it covers the camera control button, which is why I got it exclusively for my iPhone 14 pro ....... so keep that in mind.

Bottom line: For the price, this is exceptional. Don't overthink it. It is easy to install, gives great protection and feels durable and tactile!

title: OtterBox iPhone 8/7 & SE (3rd/2nd Gen) Commuter Series Case - Black
description: Commuter Series is the compact case that keeps your phone safe while you live life on the go. Its two tough layers come together to protect your iPhone SE (2nd Gen - 2020) & iPhone 8/7 (NOT PLUS) against drops, bumps, dust and fumbles. Slip Commuter Series into your pocket and never miss a call, tweet or text.

reviews.review_description:
I work in trades so I wanted something that would protect my phone but not make it feel like I have a scrap 2x8 in my pocket. Also being in trades it has gone through its fair share of abuse and after having this for a little over a year now the only damage I can report is some cosmetic scratches, dings, a small non important piece of plastic as well as the rubber flap that goes over the charging port ripped off (though I'm to blame on most of that...). Long story short I told myself I would get a new phone when my current iPhone 8 dies. In desperate attempts to speed that up without being too blatant (as I've now had this phone for easily 6-7 years now and I'm ready for a new one) I've thrown this thing across rooms, out of second story windows, off roofs and ladders, etc. I think you get the point... Fortunately (or unfortunately) it has protected my phone through it all.

The only things I have against it though is that the opening for the charger does give some trouble to the thicker aftermarket chargers (e.g. I have a Ryobi lightning charger that's thicker to supposedly protect it but it still charges with some "convincing"). In an attempt to handle that I ripped off that rubber flap that I mentioned before (no, that solved nothing but I felt better in the end). NOTE: It actually was starting to rip off slowly through use about 6 months in but I just expedited that process.

The other point is that after a year of use (and abuse) its texture has gone pretty smooth so the grip isn't anything to marvel at but it does its job. I somewhat handled this by cutting a bunch of grooves with a utility knife but I can understand others not wanting to follow suit.

TL;DR - Doesn't impede in screen or button usage. Great protection in a smaller and sleek design. May have some problems with charger clearance if you have really bulky aftermarket chargers.

Notes for the picture: Mostly here to show the missing rubber flap that would usually cover the charging port. There was a think plastic piece that would go right below it and create a hole that the flap would fit into but that broke off as well. Most damage is through my abuse (for example the bottom left corner) but for the most part it's still in working condition. You can also see my "custom texturing job" I did on the back lol. Does it look pretty? No. Is that my fault? Absolutely.

reviews.review_title: Great, not too bulky, yet very protective case - Just avoid Amazon shipping!!
reviews.review_description:
For the money especially, this is a great case. Unlike the defender series or others like it this doesn’t have the P.I.T.A. two-sided case that locks together and is difficult to remove. Some reviews say it’s hard to put on, they’re clearly doing it wrong as it’s VERY easy.

It’s a 2 part design, so while it comes together, it’s key to put the rubber part on the phone before snapping the hard plastic cover in place. No doubt people saying it’s a tight fit tried both at once. That’s more difficult and puts strain on the plastic.

I’m the worst about dropping my phone. ai must have dropped it (iphone 8) at least 75-100 times minimum, and I don’t even worry about breaking anything anymore. The lip of it sticks out just enough to protect the screen, and the dual layering is ultra shock absorbent. It’s also pretty thin considering the amount of protection.

I gave a 4 for durability and sturdiness as over time the outer plastic snapped on me and the inner rubber cover has a few worn areas, but at $20, replacing wasn’t particularly bothersome and it certainly lasted a good 6-9 months of hard use - better the case than my screen! Still a 5 in total as sometimes something has to break, and so perhaps it’s better being a little less sturdy.

To anyone asking, of course it fits a 7, there is no big difference in the shape of 8 and 7. Idk if the lip would protect the plus as well since the screen is bigger, but that’s an overall risk the Plus phones have.

Finally, I wish I could rate Amazon delivery separately. If you live in a city apartment building or even a house and won’t be home, they don’t bother reading delivery instructions (which always has info to access my mail room / lobby). It’s probably Amazon’s fault for having impossible schedules, but the drivers will *sometimes* try to buzz once (not always), then ignore the delivery instructions and leave the box outside if you’re not home or can’t answer. When I wondered where my replacement case was, a quick review showed some lady walking by, noticing the pile of boxes left, and took a couple small packages on top before walking quickly off, one of course was mine.

Almost more infuriatingly, customer service put it down to “delivery error” and said they’d blame the shipper.. yet Amazon is the shipper. So they blame themselves and do nothing to fix it, and outsourced customer service means people that can only answer a few basic questions before they get confused and off script. This time they promised me they were working with delivery drivers to fix the problem, yet it’s been happening for at least 2 years. If my neighbors didn’t look out for each other and bring in anything left outside, much more would have been stolen by now. And still they have my sensitive door access info, which I don’t give out lightly.. and never use it. How it’s cheaper to replace these items than just fix the problem is beyond me.

My advice, if 1-day delivery is an option, is to buy it alone so as not to make the $35 minimum and let UPS handle it, since their drivers would never leave packages out on a city street (they also take note of info like door codes, how crazy). It’s to the point where if I see Amazon shipping I dread it and have to try to stay home. At the very least a notification saying the package is outside for anyone to take would be a start.

That’s enough about Amazon shipping, just on my mind since the first order got stolen. UPS safely brought the replacement though

This is the perfect case to fit both of these needs.

It’s not obnoxiously large and overbuilt, so it goes in and out of the pocket with ease, yet, when it gets accidentally dropped, it’s generally not a problem. Unless you’re particularly unlucky and your phone drops face down on very sharp rocks, it’s probably going to be fine.

reviews.review_title: Great case, but watch your charging cable.
reviews.review_description: I see the case has undergone a slight re-design since my original one. It come with in soft inner rubber shell with an outer hard rubber shell. I guess that's to better absorb impact. The original one they were molded together. Now the inner shell appears to be removeable. That said, it seems to be well made. It's a tight fit to get the phone in. The buttons line-up where they should, so they are functional. Someone mentioned in another review that they liked the dust cover for the charging port. For me, it's a a love/hate relationship. I love the idea of keeping it closed when not charging, but since the "hinge" part of the flap has a strong reflex to close, I have to keep my phone motionless while charging or the pressure the lid has will cause the cord to pop-out just enough to stop charging without visual queue to know it happened. I actually get better results on a cheaper and thinner cord, but then it wears out the cord faster. So, for sturdiness, I give this 5 stars. But overall, due the the aforementioned charging issue, I give it 4 stars. Also, the outer case is a bit slippery, I wish it had better hand grip material, but workable if you know that.

Very comfortable hold. It is a little bit slippery at first but you get used to learning how and where to grip it right. I have dropped my phone many times with this case on and my phone is still in great condition.
Great product but it was a little difficult putting it together because I didn’t have the hand strength and I do it. No problem for my husband.
Exactly as advertised!
Good quality for a reasonable price.

reviews.review_title: Legit Military-Grade protection without the "Brick" feel!
reviews.review_description:
If you’re tired of cases that claim to be "tough" but feel like cheap plastic, or "rugged" cases that make your phone too big to fit in a pocket, the ESR Military-Grade Shockproof Case is the upgrade you’ve been looking for. I’ve tested a lot of MagSafe cases, and this one feels like it was engineered, not just manufactured.

Protection That Isn’t Just Marketing

The first thing you notice is the Air-Guard corners. They aren’t just decorative; they create a visible cushion that actually absorbs impact. I’ve already had one "heart-stop" moment where my phone slid off a high counter onto a tile floor, and it literally bounced. Not a scratch on the phone or the case. The "Military-Grade" label actually feels earned here.

The MagSafe Connection (HaloLock)

ESR’s magnets (they call it HaloLock) are notoriously strong—often stronger than the official Apple cases. 

• The "Snap": When you bring it near a charger or car mount, it grabs hold with a very secure click.

• Reliability: I use a heavy MagSafe power bank and a wallet attachment; neither budge even when I’m walking or the car hits a bump. It’s rated for 1,500g of holding force, and you can definitely feel that extra "tug." 

Design & Utility

Depending on the model you get, many of these come with the Stash Stand around the camera. This is a game-changer:

• It protects the lenses when closed.

• It’s made of a high-quality zinc alloy that doesn't feel flimsy.

• It works in both portrait (for scrolling/FaceTime) and landscape (for videos) without blocking the MagSafe ring.

The Build Quality

The back is a hard, scratch-resistant polycarbonate that stays clear much longer than cheap TPU. The sides have a nice matte grip that prevents that "slippery soap" feeling. It adds just enough "heft" to make the phone feel protected without doubling its thickness. 

Pros:

• Superior Magnets: Best-in-class MagSafe strength.

• Corner Protection: Air-Guard tech is legit for drop safety. 

• Tactile Buttons: They remain clicky and responsive, not mushy.

• Raised Edges: Significant lip around the screen and camera for "table-top" protection. 

Cons:

• Tight Fit: It’s a very snug fit, so it takes a little effort to get the phone out if you swap cases often (but that’s also why it’s so protective!).

Final Verdict: This is the "Goldilocks" of cases—it’s tougher than a standard clear case but way sleeker than a traditional bulky rugged case. If you value your phone's trade-in value and use MagSafe accessories daily, this is an absolute no-brainer. 5/5 Stars.

reviews.review_title: Great charger, but weak MagSafe magnets hold it back
reviews.review_description:
This Belkin charger is a great product overall, but it has one significant drawback that I don’t think should be overlooked.

First, the positives: my Apple Watch Ultra 3 fast charges as advertised, and so does my iPhone. The charger itself is lightweight and compact, and it comes with a 45W charging brick and a nice rubber-overmolded cable that feels high quality. From a charging and build-quality standpoint, I’m very happy with it.

Unfortunately, there’s one issue I can’t get past: the magnetic strength of the MagSafe phone mount. The magnets simply don’t feel strong enough. It doesn’t take much of a bump to knock the phone off the charger, and that’s something I think potential buyers should be aware of.

I believe the weaker magnets may actually be an intentional design decision. Because the charger itself is so lightweight, stronger magnets could cause you to lift the entire charger when trying to remove your phone. I can understand the reasoning behind that tradeoff, but I still think the magnetic hold is too weak in practice.

Belkin appears to have tried to compensate for this by adding a silicone surface to the charging area to provide additional grip against the back of the phone. Unfortunately, it doesn’t provide enough friction to make up for the weaker magnets. Personally, I would have preferred a heavier base combined with stronger magnets, even if it added some weight to the product.

If Belkin had addressed this, I genuinely think this would be a 10/10 charger. As it stands, I’d give it a 7/10. The charging performance is excellent, the included 45W power adapter and cable are nice, and the overall design is very good. The weak magnetic hold is really the only thing keeping me from loving it.

You may think this won’t bother you, but I would seriously consider it before buying. A surprisingly light bump can cause the phone to fall off the charger, and for something you may use every day for years, that matters.

If you’re comparing this with the Anker Prime, which costs roughly $30–$40 more, the additional cost may be worth considering if it provides a more secure magnetic connection. Over several years of daily use, $30–$40 isn’t much of a premium to avoid an annoyance you’ll potentially deal with every day.

reviews.review_description: Bought this for my wife to charge her watch and phone at the same time on her night stand. She loves it. Charges very well, the magnet is strong and works. I recommend getting the magsafe case. Super easy to connect your watch and phone to to get them to charge overnight. Doesn't take up a lot of space and works exactly as anticipated.

This 3 in 1 MagSafe charger is the best investment I could have made for my phone and accessories. I have an iPhone 14 pro max and I have zero issues with it charging with my MagSafe case on it. I’m not sure if the other reviewers understand that they still need to line up the magnet-it’s not just going to “catch” without taking an extra second to line it up. Once aligned, the magnet is extremely strong and my phone has never once fallen off of this charger This charger charges my phone, apple watch and airpods simultaneously and quickly. It was a little pricey however having 3 chargers in 1 that I am not constantly having to search for or replace due to broken chords is worth every penny. Do not believe the reviews that say it broke after 2 months or 2 years-this charger had only been on the market since November 2022 (2 months total) and it’s the first and only MagSafe charger apple endorses, which is why I purchased it. Well worth the money. This is an excellent charging system that is aesthetically pleasing.

When you move into the apple ecosystem, it is usually done first with an iphone, then with airpods and finally with an apple watch. When it gets to that stage you usually have two or three cables to charge all these devices, which is no longer convenient.

Before buying the product I was a little unsure, as it is an expensive product. But it was totally worth it, just for the ease of being able to charge the three products, which I mentioned above, quickly and easily, without having to be handling two and three cables (even without the need to handle multiple outlets) which greatly simplifies the cable management for those who seek visual simplicity.

The only thing not convenient is the material of the base with which the product is made, as it tends to "absorb" dust, dirt, grease etc etc in a very easy way, it is not an easy product to clean but with a little patience can be left as new. If I had to improve something it would be the above mentioned and additionally in the black version I would also try to leave the Magsafe Pads in black color, for those who have a dark palette of colors on their setup.

In my case I used the product with an Iphone 13 (normal), Airpods 3 and a watch series 8 and it charges these three devices without problems. The convenience here is that since it is a product that allows you to charge these gadgets so easily, this allows me to rarely run out of battery or forget to charge any of them.

I also like that it has a trickle charge mode for lower power devices like my watch and earbuds. Most batteries will shut off because there isn't enough of a power draw, in trickle charge mode the battery will not shut off for 3 1/2 hours.

One thing that has left me curious is that I have yet to see it either receive or draw more than 3 volts @ 20 amps since it says it is capable of 5 volts. title: NOCO GENIUS10 10A 6/12V Smart Battery Charger, Trickle Charger & Maintainer
description: The GENIUS10 is the ultimate all-in-one solution for battery charging, maintenance, and restoration, delivering 17% more power in a 115% smaller design compared to its predecessor, the G7200. Designed for 6-volt and 12-volt lead-acid (AGM, gel, flooded, and deep-cycle) and lithium-ion (LiFePO4) batteries (up to 230 amp-hours), it is compatible with a vast array of vehicles, such as cars, automobiles, motorcycles, dirt bikes, scooters, mopeds, lawn mowers, ATVs, UTVs, tractors, trucks, SUVs, RVs, campers, trailers, boats, PWCs, jet skis, snowmobiles, golf carts, classic cars, and more; including automotive brands like BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, Bentley, Maserati, Lexus, Audi, Ford, Chevrolet, Corvette, Cadillac, Prius, Toyota, Subaru, Nissan, powersport vehicles such as Harley-Davidson, Honda, Yamaha, Kawasaki, Ducati, Indian, KTM, Husqvarna, Vespa, Polaris, Seadoo, as well as lawn and garden vehicles such as John Deere, Kubota, Toro and more. Featuring an integrated thermal sensor, the GENIUS10 adjusts its charging profile based on ambient temperature, ensuring optimal performance by eliminating the risk of overcharging in hot climates and undercharging in cold ones. It's capable of charging batteries as low as 1 volt and offers a Force Mode for manually charging completely dead batteries (as low as zero volts). With precision pulse charging, the GENIUS10 restores battery health by reversing sulfation and acid stratification, improving performance and extending battery life. Its advanced monitoring system allows for safe, indefinite connection, making it perfect for long-term maintenance. The package includes a 10A charger (120-240VAC), 72-inch AC cable, 80-inch DC cable with battery clamps, and integrated eyelet terminals, mounting bracket and screws, all backed by a three-year warranty. Proudly designed in the USA, the GENIUS10 combines power, reliability, and convenience in a compact design to keep your batteries ready for whatever lies ahead.

reviews.review_title: Perfect for a second car that doesn't get driven often
reviews.review_description:
I was hesitant to buy one of these because of the reviews about fires. Don't pay attention to those reviews. This little trickle charger keeps your car battery at full and in brand new condition. I read somewhere online that if you put a brand new AGM battery in your car like I did and keep this NOCO Genius10 hooked up, the battery can theoretically last up to 10 years because the NOCO will continuously keep it charged and repaired. It seems that my battery was not the problem with my car as the starter relay on the clutch needed replacing so now my car starts again. But I put in a new AGM battery anyways and won't have to worry about replacing it for another 7-10 years as long as I keep the NOCO attached when not driving the car for long periods of time.

As for the NOCO functionality itself it has a couple buttons, one to choose what kind of battery you are using, regular 12V, AGM, or Lithium Ion. The other button I believe is for what kind of charge you want(trickle, decharge, repair) but since I have a brand new battery I simply keep it on trickle charge.

The cord length is not very long so in order for my NOCO to reach my car battery and the wall socket in my garage I used a decent gauge extension cord. The instructions say not to use an extension cord but there is no other way since my wall outlet in my garage is too far away from the car battery. I keep a smoke detector next to the NOCO and battery just to be safe. I got the NOCO on sale during Prime Day so it is definitely a good value for the money. So far so good.

reviews.review_title: Saved me from buying a new battery!
reviews.review_description:
EDIT 2/26/24: I am now the blocks "AAA". Been helping people start their cars when jump starts with cables have not worked. Definitely handy to get other people out of an otherwise expensive pinch.

I have a car battery that I purchased around 2016 (date of review 1/3/24). The car itself does not get driven much, at most 2-3 times a week no longer than 15 minutes one way.

Throughout the years I've drained it by leaving the car lights on. Its always required a jump start after that to get going again. Recently I've been an idiot and been leaving my lights on more frequently. Eventually it required me to jump start everytime I wanted to turn on the car. It was becoming a hassle and I was about to call it quits and purchase a new battery until I came across Project Farm's review on battery chargers. This was at the top of the list so I figured to give it a shot.

I was not disappointed! I charged it for 4 days straight, put it in my car, and it started right up. Not surprised considering it was just charged but the real test laid ahead. I was going to be out of town for two weeks and leave the car sitting. I came back two weeks later and the car started up, no hesitation whatsoever, as if it was a different battery!

The NOCO Genius 10 saved me about $150-200 at least in a brand new battery. On top of that, I can now use it for other batteries in the event of any similar issues. The instructions on the other hand are a bit confusing and had to rely on YouTube comments to piece it together.

For those who are confused at what to do, I did not do a 12V repair (function which this unit has) as it requires the battery to be completely charged first. All I did was charge it straight for 4 days uninterrupted.

When first put on battery to the charger it will be in standby mode. You push (or hold depending on what you need) the MODE button to select your desired option. I was charging a lead acid battery so I selected 12V. The meter at the top slowly advanceD from each of the four bars until the final bar was pulsing green which indicates its charging to full (over 80% I believe). The green charging light continued to slowly pulse even on the 4th day but I took a gamble and disconnected it from the battery. For the battery to be 100% charged, the green light should stay solid. That means my battery worked 2 weeks later after sitting and it wasn't even at 100%.

The unit can also force a charge on batteries that are extremely under voltage. Thats a separate setting that I haven't had to use yet. It can also charge AGM and Lithium but I believe the 12V repair function is only for lead acid.

Unfortunately I had to go through 3 separate orders because the first two were from Amazon Warehouse and I encountered issues with both, consecutively. I ended up getting frustrated and just purchased a brand new charger.

Pros:

Solid build quality

Excellent cable connections with weather covers

Compatible with a wide variety of batteries

Repair and Force charge batteries

Cons:

Poor instructions

Charge is slow BUT I think thats how these chargers work

TL;DR

Try this first before rushing to get a new battery it is a good investment that can save you a lot of money

reviews.review_description:
I've gone through more charging stations than I'd like to admit, and most either take up too much room or require a tangle of cables. This one keeps everything much cleaner by charging my phone, Apple Watch, and earbuds in one compact unit.

What impressed me most is how portable it is. When folded, it's small enough to slip into a backpack or carry-on, making it a great travel companion. I especially like that the charging cable retracts into the base instead of becoming another cord to wrap up before packing.

The magnetic phone charger holds my phone securely, even in StandBy mode, so I can use it as a bedside clock while it charges overnight. My watch and earbuds also charged consistently without having to fiddle with positioning them over and over.

The built-in lighting is a nice extra. I normally don't care for RGB effects, but it's easy to switch off if you prefer a darker bedroom. It's nice to have the option instead of being stuck with lights that stay on all night.

The only drawback I found is that the built-in power cable isn't very long. If your outlet is tucked behind furniture or far from your nightstand, you may need to rearrange where you place the charger. A slightly longer cable would have made it even more versatile.

Overall, this is a well-designed charging station that reduces clutter and travels well. It feels sturdy, charges reliably, and combines several useful features into one compact package. I'd recommend it to anyone looking to simplify their desk or bedside setup.

reviews.review_title: One of the Best Charging Stations I've Used
reviews.review_description:
This charging station has been fantastic.

I love that it supports my phone, AirPods, and other USB-C devices all in one place. The retractable cable keeps everything neat, and the RGB lighting can be turned off with a simple touch if you prefer a cleaner look.

The rubberized base keeps it stable, and everything feels well built. My only minor observation is that AirPods with thicker protective cases can be a tighter fit on the charging pad, but it hasn't changed how much I like the product.

Overall, it's become my primary charging station.

reviews.review_title: Great Angle Adjustment, and turns my phone into a clock
reviews.review_description:
The adjustable angle on this charging station is what really sold me. Once your phone is set on it, you can tilt it just right so the display is easy to see, and I've actually started using it as a nightstand clock. When I wake up in the middle of the night, the motion wakes the phone display and shows me the time without me having to pick it up or fumble around. That angle adjustment is mainly what I use it for, though I can also see it being handy for propping up your phone to watch something while it charges.

The flip up piece for the watch works great too. My older Apple Watch 6 fits on it fine and charges reliably every time. I've also used the front part to charge my AirPods, and that works well even with a small silicone case on them. Charging speed is right in line with other wireless chargers I've used, nothing faster or slower than expected. It folds down into a small cube that's easy to toss in a suitcase, so you have one single charger covering all your devices when you travel. Overall this is a great value since you're getting three charging stations in one, and I'm already thinking about picking up a few of these as gifts for some of the older kids later this year.

reviews.review_title: Great charging station, just a bit too scrunched
reviews.review_description: I love charging stations! The only issue I see with this one is it is very compact - like one bump could send my watch and headphones off the charger. The magnet for the phone charging part is great. The watch charger part is a little awkward because it doesn’t allot much space for your wristband/the extra space needed for where your wristband fits in the slots on your watch face. Once you’ve secured your watch properly on it, it charges just fine. I have 1st or 2nd gen Airpods so I was surprised to see it could charge them too! There is a light at the bottom of the charger - which you can turn off or turn into “nightlight” mode. There are specific colors for charging the different devices, and the manuel explains what this would look like if it is charging properly - I haven’t noticed the lights to work 100% accurately but my devices still charged especially when I had more than one device charging at a time.

reviews.review_title: Awesome charger for home and travel!
reviews.review_description:
I’m really happy with this ANTBOOK 3 in 1 wireless charging station. It’s nice to have one spot to charge my phone, Apple Watch, and anirpods instead of dealing with multiple chargers and charging bases. The built in retractable cord is one of my favorite features. It keeps my nightstand looking clean and is easy to use. My cats like to chew on cords that lay around, so I only have the cord retracted just enough so that my cats can’t chew on it and it’s still usable.

The RGB lighting is a fun touch without being over the top, and it gives my nightstand a nice modern look. I especially like that I can turn the RGB off at night when I’m sleeping if I feel it’s keeping me awake. The charging station itself feels compact and doesn’t take up much space on my nightstand. Charging has been reliable, and I haven’t had any issues keeping all three devices powered up overnight. I could really see this charger shining when it comes to traveling. One cord, one block, 3 different items it charges.

Overall, it’s a convenient, clutter free charging solution that works well and looks good. I’d definitely recommend it.

reviews.review_title: Convenient stand for cable clutter but runs hot
reviews.review_description: This charging stand is decent for cleaning up messy nightstand cables and consolidating your phone, watch, and earbuds into one compact spot. The magnetic hold is strong enough to keep the phone securely upright in portrait or landscape orientation, and the weighted base keeps it from sliding around when you grab your device. However, the unit gets noticeably hot when charging multiple devices at the same time. While it does power everything up reliably, the excess heat build up is definitely a drawback if you are concerned about long term battery health. It is a convenient organizer, but the thermal management leaves something to be desired.

reviews.reviewer_name: This birder feeder will not close properly, I’m very disappointed!
reviews.review_description: We have different iPhones in the house, from a 12 mini to a 15 Pro, and all of them snap onto the magnetic pad without issue. My wife's older Watch Series 3 also charges fine. Good to know we won't need a new station when someone upgrades.

This 3 in 1 charging station is seriously the perfect charger for travel. It folds down into a compact cube that can easily be packed or thrown into a purse. Even the type C cable folds into the back to keep from getting tangled. The light is easily turned off and on and doubles as a nice little night light. The hinges are stiff enough to hold the parts in place without falling closed. I love that it comes with the charging block. It seems like so many things these days just come with the cord but not the block. Unfortunately I couldn’t exactly get a picture of my phone charging but it does charge really fast and the magnet holds onto my phone well. Overall, I am super impressed with this little gadget. It’s so convenient and packs every charging necessity into a great compact size. I would definitely recommend it!

reviews.review_title: Very practical and convenient battery backup
reviews.review_description:
I purchased the pink 12000 mAh charger. Neat charger, I like the built in charging cables and the extra ports for the option of charging additional devices. Having the prongs for a wall outlet built in are extremely convenient. It has a little weight to it at just over 8 ounces, but it is slightly lighter than my iphone promax. It’s also just a little smaller than my phone so it is easily portable.

When I first opened the charger it was at 79% battery. I plugged it into a wall outlet using the built in, flip down charging prongs and it took about 1 hour and 20 minutes to charge from 79% to 100%. I then plugged it into my daughter‘s Amazon fire tablet to charge that. The tablet was at 1% when I started to charge and it took 2 hours and 25 minutes to get the tablet to 100%. Charging the tablet fully also did not use all of power in the charger, it had 43% battery life left. It is able to charge devices at a decent speed, not crazy fast but I would not say it charges items slowly.

I like that the display lets you know how much charge is left with just a tap of the button, as well as letting you know your percentage of battery in real time while you have it plugged in to a wall outlet.

If there is anything to add about durability or functionality later on I will add those sentiments to this review, I just have not owned the item long enough to make a good determination about those aspects.

title: NOCO GENIUS5 5A 6/12V Smart Battery Charger, Trickle Charger & Maintainer
description: The GENIUS5 is the ultimate all-in-one solution for battery charging, maintenance, and restoration, delivering 34% more power in a 65% smaller design compared to its predecessor, the G3500. Designed for 6-volt and 12-volt lead-acid (AGM, gel, flooded, and deep-cycle) and lithium-ion (LiFePO4) batteries (up to 120 amp-hours), it is compatible with a vast array of vehicles, such as cars, automobiles, motorcycles, dirt bikes, scooters, mopeds, lawn mowers, ATVs, UTVs, tractors, trucks, SUVs, RVs, campers, trailers, boats, PWCs, jet skis, snowmobiles, golf carts, classic cars, and more; including automotive brands like BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, Bentley, Maserati, Lexus, Audi, Ford, Chevrolet, Corvette, Cadillac, Prius, Toyota, Subaru, Nissan, powersport vehicles such as Harley-Davidson, Honda, Yamaha, Kawasaki, Ducati, Indian, KTM, Husqvarna, Vespa, Polaris, Seadoo, as well as lawn and garden vehicles such as John Deere, Kubota, Toro and more. Featuring an integrated thermal sensor, the GENIUS5 adjusts its charging profile based on ambient temperature, ensuring optimal performance by eliminating the risk of overcharging in hot climates and undercharging in cold ones. It's capable of charging batteries as low as 1 volt and offers a Force Mode for manually charging completely dead batteries (as low as zero volts). With precision pulse charging, the GENIUS5 restores battery health by reversing sulfation and acid stratification, improving performance and extending battery life. Its advanced monitoring system allows for safe, indefinite connection, making it perfect for long-term maintenance. The package includes a 5A charger (120-240VAC), 72-inch AC cable, 80-inch DC cable with battery clamps, and integrated eyelet terminals, mounting bracket and screws, all backed by a three-year warranty. Proudly designed in the USA, the GENIUS5 combines power, reliability, and convenience in a compact design to keep your batteries ready for whatever lies ahead.

reviews.review_title: Reliable Smart Charger That Brought a Neglected Battery Back to Life
reviews.review_description:
I purchased the NOCO GENIUS5 to maintain the batteries in vehicles that don't get driven regularly, and it has been one of those tools that quickly proves its value.

Setup was straightforward. The included connectors are easy to use, and the charger automatically detects the battery and selects the appropriate charging mode. I especially appreciate that it can be left connected for maintenance without worrying about overcharging, which gives me peace of mind when storing a vehicle for extended periods.

One of the batteries I used it on had been sitting for quite a while and was struggling to hold a charge. After connecting the GENIUS5 and allowing it to complete its charging cycle, the battery recovered enough to reliably start the vehicle again. While no charger can fix a battery that's physically damaged or completely worn out, this unit did a good job recovering a battery that I initially thought might need replacement.

The charger itself feels well-built and the display indicators are easy to understand. I also like that it supports both lead-acid and lithium batteries, making it useful for multiple vehicles and equipment around the house.

A few things prospective buyers should know:

The 5A charging rate is ideal for maintenance and general charging, but it isn't the fastest option if you're trying to charge a large, deeply discharged battery in a hurry.

The indicator lights are simple and functional, though some users may prefer a charger with a more detailed digital display showing voltage and charging status.

Overall, this is a dependable smart charger that is easy to use, versatile, and well-built. Whether you're maintaining a seasonal vehicle, motorcycle, lawn equipment, or simply want a charger that can safely stay connected long-term, the GENIUS5 is a worthwhile investment.

Helpful tip: If you're using it for battery maintenance, consider installing the included quick-connect lead permanently on the battery. It makes future charging sessions much faster and more convenient.

I bought the Genius5 after neglecting a relatively new battery in my motorcycle. Due to weather and travel, I often have long gaps between rides. Unfortunately, one of these gaps was long enough to damage the battery. I didn’t realize that batteries need a minimal charge to avoid sulfation, and mine had become severely discharged. Although my NOCO GB40 starter worked fine, the battery wasn’t holding a charge even after a day of riding. Instead of immediately replacing the battery, I decided to try saving it with the Genius5.

After charging the battery with the Genius5, I tested it with a battery analyzer, which reported it as damaged. I then ran the desulfation process, and afterward, the analyzer showed the battery was in good condition. I repeated the tests several days later to be sure, and the battery still appeared to be in good health. Now, I keep the Genius5 connected to my motorcycle whenever I’m not riding for more than a week, and I haven’t had any battery issues since. I still carry the GB40 in my panniers, just in case, but I haven’t needed to use it lately.

Some notes on the desulfation process:

The desulfation process seems to send voltage peaks, and you may hear some bubbling inside the battery. This happened to me, and from what I’ve read, it’s normal as long as there’s not too much bubbling and no vapors, heating, or swelling of the battery. The entire process takes a while, so it’s unrealistic to monitor it the whole time. However, I recommend watching it for the first 20 minutes to ensure the battery noises aren’t increasing. After that, you can leave it running while staying nearby, just in case something goes wrong. A final note on this process: because of the voltage peaks, I didn’t run it with the battery connected to the motorcycle to avoid any potential damage to the circuits. For regular maintenance charging, I do keep the battery connected.

The Genius5 is designed to work with standard batteries, gel, and even lithium ones. The one I used was a Gel Yuasa, and I’m pleased with the results. I also purchased the NOCO cables (GC002 X-Connect M6) to make it easier to connect the charger without removing the seat. The cables were a bit expensive but seem well-constructed and are quite convenient.

Final thoughts:

If you have a vehicle that sits unused for extended periods, and this happens frequently, then this charger is ideal for you. However, if you only need it once a year or less, it might be easier and cheaper to disconnect the battery from the vehicle while you’re away to prevent discharging. For my use case, the Genius5 has been worth it, and I’d definitely buy it again.

My interstate battery went completely when I went returned from a 6 week trip. Tried jump starting by using my other car but failed.

Noco is one of the few chargers that can charge a completely dead battery. Watched a project farm youtube video on car battery chargers ( see chart at 18m29s of the video) before buying. I purchased the 5A one due to time constraint ( charged 75% in 8 hours ). You can buy the 2A version or 1A version if you have all the time and just want to keep batteries fully charged. I let it charge overnight and had a fully functional battery in the morning.

This happens to me whenever I go on long trips ( 4 weeks + ). With a rechargeable jump starter, you are limited by the battery life of the starter which is only 3-4 years after which most batteries fail. The wall charger hopefully will last a long longer. Saved me a lot of time - No need to drive the car around after jump starting to get some charge into the battery. Just charge overnight and done. Love it.

Easy to use and well built. I used it to charge the AGM battery on my Ducati and it worked great. The indicator lights are clear, and the connector makes it easy to plug in whenever needed. Great for keeping the battery maintained, especially if you don’t ride every day. Overall, I’m very happy with it.

reviews.review_title: Yeah so don't mix up your fused alligator cables if you buy different models
reviews.review_description:
I bought a Genius1 and Genius5. The latter failed on first use due to my mistake mixing up the alligator clips during unboxing. I didn't look closely enough to notice that the 1 and 5 aren't just feature levels but are current ratings in Amps. The proprietary connectors are identical but the 1A unit has a 2A fuse and the 5A unit has a 10A fuse, and they're on the battery side of the connectors not the device side, so obviously the 2A fuse correctly blew when I tried using the 5A unit.

They work fine after fixing my careless mix-up, but I'd like these better if the device or fuse holder were marked with a recommended fuse rating, or the connectors couldn't mate with the wrong device, or the fuse holder were on the device side of the proprietary connector, or the unit came with spare fuses, or the fuse ratings were included in the online user guide, or the user guide were included in the box, or the safety guide were printed in a typeface legible to adult human eyes.

Anyway, keep your cables together with the devices and don't mix em up.

reviews.review_title: High quality at a reasonable cost
reviews.review_description:
This charger/tender worked well to "revive" a ~80Ah lead acid battery that sat in a low state of charge for nearly a year. After an initial 2.5 hour cycle in repair mode, followed by a higher amp charge from an older/larger charger, a noticeable improvement in battery performance was observed. A shorter repair cycle, about 30 minutes total, restored some capacity on another lead acid battery still in use. There are cheaper desulfator-only options, of questionable reliability/longevity, so the additional features offered on this model were cost-effective for my intended usage.

While I have not yet used this as a tender/maintainer for any length of time, the cabling to and from the charger are long enough to reach from one side of a car to the other. This unit did not seem to produce much heat in repair mode with ~75F ambient temp. In auto charge mode between 25% and 75%, it was warm to the touch. I'll have to try a longer charge period to see if it heats up further. UPDATE: after using repair & charge mode on a flat battery for a few hours, this unit can get fairly hot. Using this on a flat surface so air can get underneath is a good idea.

This product did not come with a manual in the box, just the warranty booklet. Tracking down a user manual on the manufacturer's site did not require much effort. The 6V and repair mode are not activated by quick presses of the single button. Pressing & holding for a few seconds activates these extra modes from standby. Some form of documentation in the box would have been more convenient than going to the website, but I digress.

I bought a used 2022 Honda Ridgeline with ~7,000 miles on it some months back. It was a "dealer demo car" and was well-maintained as a result. Now, it's got around 12,000 miles on it.

One day, I left the lights on too long with the ignition off, and had the radio playing. Stupid on my part, but my battery didn't have enough charge to deliver the amps needed to turn the engine over. I bought a Noco GB40, and it worked well - it'd start my truck when needed. Yesterday, it didn't. I guess the battery had degraded too much, so I was shopping for new batteries when the sticker shock hit me. Given the age of my truck, I thought it would be silly to replace the battery.

Someone recommended the Noco Genius5, so I gave it a shot. Amazon's same-day delivery got it to me quickly, and I basically hooked it up to the battery, plugged it in, set it to AGM mode, and let it go to work. I waited several hours for the charger light to show "solid green", indicating it was fully charged. I started up my truck; it sounded better than the day I bought it. However, on the dash, it had a note about an "emissions problem". My scan tool showed a permanent code with the Transmission Control Module and a bunch of other temporary codes. Since I didn't have any codes before, I figured I may have freaked out the electronics by charging the battery while the battery was hooked up to the truck, or maybe by touching the terminals out of sequence when removing the cables. Either way, I removed the battery from my truck, hooked up the Genius5, and set it to "repair mode".

My truck had low mileage when I bought it, at about a year old, which likely meant that it say for a while when not in use. Maybe that could have led to sulfation or stratification, which could have meant it wouldn't charge as effectively from the alternator. I also wanted to remove the battery to allow the computers to reset in the truck. If it was still throwing codes after that, I'd bring it into the dealer.

This morning, when I woke up, I noticed the Genius5 was in standby mode, meaning the repair mode had finished. I started the Genius5 back up, and set it to AGM mode again -- it took about a minute, but it said the battery was good to go with a solid green light. I Installed the battery back in my truck, fired it up, and I kid you not, it sounded better than ever -- less strained, more powerful, and all of the codes were gone. My truck had a freakout -- not due to this device, I'm sure, but likely due to me doing something stupid.

It's rare for me to review a product so quickly. This thing is amazing, has lots of neat accessories available for it, and saved me money. I'll continue using it to prolong my batteries and save me money in the long-run.

If you're on the fence, this little device is absolutely legit. 10/10 would recommend.

reviews.review_description: Picture quality is good (not great, but good enough). The zoom feature and swivel remote control works well. The camera with microphone and speaker has adequate coverage for a small to midsize conference room. Setup is not simple and requires some computer skills to get it working with Microsoft Windows 11 and Zoom teleconferencing software. However, once initial setup is done, it is easy to use. The camera only comes with a wall mount, which I had to extensively modify to make it into a stable ceiling mount, so I have optimum coverage in our conference room (which is why I rate the assembly at four instead of five stars).

Update:

Tenveo / Tongveo customer support reached out to me to tell me that the primary issue I was facing was because I had received an older version of the speakerphone. They quickly sent me a newer version and it charges with my high power delivery chargers! It also sounds better!!

I am now evaluating the 10X PTZ camera. The picture quality exceeds expectations. I am experiencing disconnect issues with it, but Adam is helping me troubleshoot and it appears that the camera is fine and the issue is cable related (the 25 foot Monoprice HDMI cable (purchased separately) is apparently too long and losing signal).

I will update this review after more testing.

I am using this system for my church. I am just a volunteer and not an AV specialist. Live, responsive, competent customer support is so rare these days and is much appreciated. Thank you, Adam!

Original review:

So far I have just used the speakerphone.

The speakerphone appears to be of reasonable quality physically, but it pales in comparison to the Anker Powerconf S500. The Anker product is made of metal and is significantly more heavy. Also, my Zoom conference call members have indicated that the microphone quality on the Anker product is significantly better.

The biggest disappointment is that Tongveo has apparently chosen to save a few pennies by not upgrading its USB-C internal components on the speakerphone - while the plug is USB-C, the internals of the speakerphone appear to be using USB-A components which do not recognize current USB-C power and data transmission protocols.

I can only charge the unit using a 5 watt or less power supply. Most of my USB-C power supplies provide more than 5 watts. In this day and age I expect USB-C to operate "plug and play". I find it frustrating that I am expected to use a low power power supply, and that my newer, better power supplies are not supported by this product.

When trying to connect the speakerphone to my laptop via my Anker USB-C to USB-C cable, the speakerphone would not connect. I finally discovered that to connect, I needed to use the provided USB-A to USB-C cable, with the USB-A end using the utilizing the provided USB-A TO USB-C Adapter on the laptop side (using this cable in the reverse direction was not supported.) Again, in this day and age I expect plug and play. The Anker product supports using the many USB-C to USB-C cables that I own.

I appreciate that I may have to trade off a little sound quality for the dollar savings provided by the Tongveo vs the Anker, but having to remember the idiosyncrasies and special cable and charger requirements associated with Tongveo product is causing me to seriously consider returning it.

Then finally, I asked AI for recommendations regarding that particular webcam and my specific laptop, once again. The final recommendation it gave me was to "install Native EMEET Software." I had read earlier that everything would be supplied automatically as soon as you plug it in, but it turns out that's not always the case. I went onto the website, and there's a place listing "downloads" where you can get the needed software for either Windows PC or Mac. So, I downloaded the Windows one ... and voila! At long last, after installing that software, the camera worked!

Apparently it's still not perfectly displaying in 4K, but no matter! The quality is is a step down from that, since my computer cannot quite support 4K. What it can display though is still a MASSIVE upgrade from what I had before! The low-light performance is excellent, and you can adjust the camera settings (contrast, saturation, etc.). I've never used an external webcam before so to me this is pretty cool. Plus, I can always use this camera on a newer laptop whenever I'm able to purchase one, and then I can have perfect 4K. But for now, attached to the laptop that I have, this camera quality is still beyond "good enough"; it's great. I'm glad I didn't give up and send this back.

reviews.review_title: RightSight feature may not work on SurfacePro with Snapdragon (ARM64) processor
reviews.review_description:
FYI: I purchased this camera after seeing someone else who presented using it. Everyone was curious what camera they were using because it was such good lighting and great video. However, I'm not sure this camera is working with full functionality on my hardware. I went through a bunch of troubleshooting, and here's the conclusion per ChatGPT... Good morning ☀️ — thank you for the detailed info. That explains everything.

You’re on:

Surface Pro 11th Edition (ARM64)

Snapdragon X (ARM) processor

That is the root cause.

________________________________________

🎯 The Real Issue

Logitech RightSight is currently not supported on Windows ARM (Snapdragon X / ARM64).

Here’s why:

RightSight depends on:

• Logitech’s middleware service

• x64 camera processing components

• AI framing pipeline extensions

On ARM Surface devices:

• Logi Tune runs under emulation

• The Logitech camera extension layer does not fully attach to the Windows Modern Camera Stack

• AI features (RightSight) fail to initialize

• Video works (because UVC driver works)

• 4K works (hardware OK)

• But AI framing = unavailable

That’s exactly your symptom set.

________________________________________

✅ Why Everything Else Works

✔ Camera app works

✔ 4K works

✔ Windows Hello works

✔ Device shows correctly

✔ No USB issue

✔ No driver corruption

Only vendor AI features fail — classic ARM compatibility limitation.

________________________________________

🚫 This Is Not Fixable Via Settings

Disabling:

• Frame Server

• Basic camera

• Studio effects

• Multiple apps setting

Will not fix it on ARM.

This is architectural, not a configuration problem.

________________________________________

🔎 Confirmation Test (Optional)

In Logi Tune:

Go to Crop.

If:

• Field of View options work (65°, 78°)

• Zoom works

• But Auto-Framing is disabled

That confirms it’s just the AI layer.

________________________________________

🧠 Why This Happens

Surface Pro 11 (Snapdragon X) uses:

• Windows on ARM

• Modern Camera Driver (MCD)

• NPU-based camera pipeline

Logitech RightSight expects:

• x64 processing environment

• Vendor extension hooks not fully exposed in ARM64 camera stack

Until Logitech releases a native ARM64 version of the RightSight service, it won’t enable.

________________________________________

📌 Current Status (Early 2026)

As of now:

• Logitech supports Intel/AMD Windows

• ARM64 support is partial

• AI features are inconsistent or unavailable

________________________________________

💡 Your Options

Option 1 — Wait for Logitech ARM-native update

This will likely come, since Snapdragon X PCs are new.

Option 2 — Use Windows Studio Effects (if available)

Surface Pro 11 has NPU-based auto framing built in.

Check:

Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Cameras → Built-in camera

If Studio Effects exists there, you can use Windows auto-framing instead.

Option 3 — Use Software Framing (Zoom / Teams)

Both now have built-in auto framing.

________________________________________

✅ Final Conclusion

Your hardware is fine.

Your configuration is fine.

Your issue is ARM platform compatibility.

reviews.review_title: The best “professional work” webcam I’ve personally used, especially for virtual backgrounds
reviews.review_description:
I bought the Logitech MX Brio after spending years using a mirrorless camera setup (Lumix GH3 + prime lens) as my desk webcam. I work remotely full-time and spend most of my day in video calls (99% in Microsoft Teams), so my priorities are a little different from the average streaming-focused review.

What I wanted was:

• excellent image quality at normal desktop distances

• reliable performance in Teams

• strong virtual background segmentation

• stable autofocus/exposure

• easy to set up

For my use case, the MX Brio has honestly been excellent.

The biggest surprise was how good the image looks in real-world meetings. Yes, my GH3 (and other mirrorless cameras) can still produce a more cinematic image in ideal conditions, but in Teams specifically (where video is heavily compressed and usually capped at 1080p), the practical gap is much smaller than people think.

As far as the camera is concerned, what matters most is consistency and signal quality, and this camera delivers both.

The MX Brio handles exposure transitions smoothly, autofocus has been reliable, and image sharpness is very good without looking overly processed. Logitech also seems to have improved color handling compared to some older Brio models that could occasionally look harsh or over-sharpened.

Where this webcam REALLY shines is virtual background and portrait segmentation.

I use a virtual background almost 100% of the time, and this camera consistently gives cleaner edge separation than several other webcams I’ve tested. Good lighting absolutely helps, but the MX Brio seems to provide a very clean image feed that works well with Teams’ background processing.

A few other things I appreciated:

• solid low-light recovery without becoming a smeary mess

• flexible field of view options

• sturdy physical build

• built-in microphone

• easy mounting and positioning

There are a couple tradeoffs worth mentioning:

• Logitech’s software ecosystem is still a little fragmented (Logi Tune, G Hub, etc.)

• if you are primarily a streamer/content creator, there may be better options depending on your workflow

• this camera, like any, benefits significantly from proper lighting and good positioning. It's worth it to invest in a couple lights and proper mounting system

But for a professional desk setup focused on video meetings, presentations, collaboration, and hybrid work, I think Logitech understood the assignment here surprisingly well.

This is the first dedicated webcam I’ve used where I no longer feel tempted to drag a mirrorless camera back onto my desk.

The camera can only go so far, but a lot of what determines the final video quality is what YOU do to create a good video streaming environment. Read: If you are in a windowless cave 50' below Earth's surface with no artificial lighting, poor video quality is on you, not the device.

reviews.review_description:
Review:

Price (3/5): At a retail price of 69.99, the price is quite high, and put this device in competition with competitors like Logitech which offer similar or better quality, different styles all for smaller price (i.e. Brio 101, Brio 200, and C920x).

Video Quality (4/5): The 1080p resolution delivers crisp and clear video, better than the average laptop camera. Although my Samsung GalaxyBook4 Pro has a signficantly better camera than this). It's fine for video conferences and online classes. If you are looking for extremely sharp and polished video recording, look elsewhere.

Audio Quality (4/5): The dual microphones are shockingy good and provide clear and natural audio. Background noise is minimal, and the quality is consistent and reliable.

Features (5/5): This is the reason to buy this camera. SO MANY FEATURES. The 4X digital zoom is great and can be accessed and changed though settings on Windows (check images attached to my review). The 95° wide-angle lens basically capures the entire room. The 360° rotation pan and tilt functionality allows you to positioning the camera exactly where you need it, and show physical documents or items during video calls without moving the whole setup. The built-in Windows Hello feature is a game-changer and the main reason I purchased this. For some devices, hello setup is easy, for others you may need enable external camera (check images attached to my review).

Design and Build: i'm not going to rate this because it's subjective. This is another reason I purchased this webcam. I love the sleek, compact and professional design. It also feels sturdy and well-constructed, and the clip-on feature is secure. It also matches my Lenovo monitor. Just keep in mind that the white is not a true white at all, it's more of a silver/grayish white.

Overall, the Lenovo HD 1080p Webcam (510 FHD) is a top-notch choice for anyone needing a decent camera from a reputable brand, with plenty of features that other brands do not offer at this price point. If you do not need these features, you would be able to get a webcam from other brands with similar quality for cheaper.
