Additionally, it does a fairly good job at removing odors , knocking out stubborn cooking smells and pet odors surprisingly well.

However, where this unit completely fails is its core effectiveness, particularly with dust removal. We have pets, and despite running this unit continuously on the highest settings, the dust removal is incredibly lackluster. reviews.review_description:
I've been looking for a new air purifier for almost a year now, doing research here and there trying to find a unit that meets all the requirments I'm looking for. I need a unit that's for a larger room, has an auto feature, has good priced replacement filters, and looks good to match my home decor. A recent 80,000 acre fire hastened my research due to the thick blanket of smoke that blanket the area (and still is) every morning. With all things considered, the Winix 5500-2 met all my requiements.

The unit arrived promptly and unpackaging was an ease. I literally had it set up ans running in about 5 minutes. The body is a hard, matte black plastic that feels sturdy and durable. The front panel is easy to remove, and secures to the unit via a clever magnetic clasp that is secure, yet simple to remove to access your prefilter for bi weekly cleaning and hepa/carbon filter replacement. There are 3 filters in total, and they fit snugly inside the filter chamber, amd ate secured in with the prefilter that snaps firmly into place.

The control panel at the top is intuituve and user friendly. The buttons are clearly marked and visual ques explain what each button does taking out any guesswork as to what they do. A stylish indicator light bar runs along the bottom of the control panel indicating the level of air cleanliness with a 3 color scheme...green for clean, orange for okay, and red for bad. You can manually run the machine on 4 fan settings, or choose auto mode and let the machine choose the settings based on the data colected from the sensor. This means hands off operation. There's a night mode that will set the fan to its lowest setting to cut down on noise, and also dim all lights on the panel. This night mode will set automatically if you have the auto mode set on the unit, a light sensor will detect (or not detect) any light in the room and go into night mode. A filter change indicator light also is on the control panel. According to what i've researched, the hepa filter should last approx 1 year. It also comes with a remote control with a battery preinstalled. I dont plan on using it, but if that's your thing, it's there.

This is the quietest air purifier I've ever owned. On level 1, it's almost undetectable, and even on level 4 turbo mode, it's no louder than a standing floor fan on high. This was a very pleasant surprise.

It cleans the air well. I'm currently using it in my 350 sq ft bedroom. I don't have the equipment to test it, but per their website I should be getting at least 4 air changes per hour which is the amount of air exchanges you need for allergies and serious air purification. I've had no smoke smell AT ALL in the bedroom when I run this with the door shut to the rest of the home and it was initially startling to walk from the bedroom into the rest of the home after the first night of using it.

This unit has more than exceeded my expecations ans meets all the things I was looking for in an air purifier. I plan on purchasing 2 more of these when money permits for my combined kitchen/dining/living room area that totals 700 sq ft. I can place these at opposite sides of the area and get more than ample coverage. I would highly reccomend this unit. For the price and the feature list, this just can't be beat. The cost is low, the replacement filters don't cost an arm and a leg, it covers a large area, and you get a lot of features.

09/28/2019

2 years later and this machine is STILL going strong. Besides the occasional vacuuming of the pre filter and the yearly filter changes, I've had this guy quietly working away in the house keeping my air clean. Can definitely say at this point that it's a durable machine!

08/20/2020

3 years later and still working! I'm only posting this update because I find myself in ANOTHER horrible fire season for California, and I'm in a zone getting insane amounts of smoke. Besides regular cleanings on the pre filter, and my yearly change out of the hepa and carbon filter, not much else to report. I really hadnt expected this thing to last this long as I run it 24/7, often on its highest setting to get maximum results. I own 2 now, I bought another one last year to get more coverage throughout the house. I would highly recommend this until to anyone.

01/03/2022

I was buying a new filter today on here and remembered that I actually had a review for this product. I've owned this air purifier for 5 years now. I just added 2 more photos (should be the last 2 in my string of pictures) just to show that I STILL own this device. 5 years of literal CONSTANT USE. I've had it set on the 3rd setting, just 1 below it's highest setting, for nearly this entire time. I have absolute confidence stating that this is a solid piece of machinery. I'm actually shocked that this guy hasn't given up on me yet! If you're worried about durability, at least in my case, yes, this is a very durable air purifier. Winix created a home run product with this one. I think that this may be my FINAL update on the product (unless of course it survives for 10 years, in which case I may throw a party for the thing!)

***I also want to add to those who say this device produces harmful amounts of ozone. That's simply not true. You can go to the California Air Resource Board, specifically to the section under California Certified Air Cleaning Devices. This will show you a list of air purifiers that have been tested by the state and produce under 0.050 ppm of ozone. This device, and all others from Winix, are on the list. That means that this device is at, or below, the levels indicated as safe. Make sure when reading reviews you guys do your own follow up research on an item. It's insane the amount of bad information that's out there! Dont take anyones word, look up what they claim!***

reviews.review_title: Super clean air purifier with unique features
reviews.review_description:
A really good air purifier with some unique features. In terms of noise, it is among the quietest at about 60 DB. Obviously there’s more noise the faster the fan spins, but in automatic mode, it senses the amount of gluten in the air and adjust the speed automatically which means most of the time it will be running at low speed unless there’s a lot of dust in the air. You can download an android or iOS app to control the fan speed and to see how much dust it is seeing in the air. You can also set it up for Alexa or Google Home to be able to control it through those devices. One need feature is being able to ask Alexa for a reading of air quality from the device. You can also enable an automatic sleep mode, which basically keeps the device on auto fan mode where it senses the amount of dust in the air during daylight, but when the device notices that the room is dark at night, it will put the fan speed to its slowest mode to ensure that there’s minimal noise during nighttime hours. Once the room is lit again and it is daylight the device will automatically switch to auto mode and if necessary, increase the fan speed to pull in more air if it detects an increased amount of dust. These are the main features of the device, but the other thing that I liked about it compared to similar models from other brands is that they say the standard filters it comes with should last 12 months where many other brands recommend changing filters after three months. This is probably because the HEPA filter that this device comes with is thicker at about 1 inch compared to what I have on other air purifiers filters that are generally 1/2 inch or less thick. I have not yet replaced my filters, but with an estimate of one year it should not be a substantial yearly cost because filter filters run around $20. And I say filters because as you can see in the images for the product, there are actually two separate filters that work together one is a white HEPA filter to filter out particles. The other one is a black carbon filter, which filter filters out smell smells. And holding both of those filters in place is a screen which is washable that is meant to capture, larger dust particles or pet hair before they hit the main filter filters. Overall, very satisfied with this device and the only thing I can’t really comment on is how long it will last as I’ve only recently started using it.

I bought this air purifier because I only have the small ones, and I noticed that they couldn’t keep up with the severity of poor air quality when we have heavy wildfire smoke in our area.

The unit itself is sleek, has easy to operate controls, and the white color matches my interior decor. The fan noise is very quiet even on High setting— it only gets loud when I use the Turbo feature.

It has a faster Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADR) compared to my other air purifiers. Within a few minutes of running it on Medium or High, it cleans the air in my apartment. The one thing I don’t like is the app— it gets laggy and sometimes unresponsive, so take note of that.

I know it sounds excessive having so many air purifiers for a one bedroom apartment, but I’m very sensitive to poor air quality and I have frequent asthma attacks if I don’t run my air purifiers.

I’m so happy with it, I bought a second WINIX 5530 of the same color so that I’ll keep that one in the living room along with the small air purifier.

I also bought replacement filters to have at hand when I need to change them out.

Powerful and works great!!!.... AND NOW I WAS ABLE TO GET IT IN WHITE!!!!, to go better with my neutral tones decor!!! Took 2 minutes to open filters stick em in, turn it on, and connect my app. Winix for the win!

Agonized and researched, and researched, and researched, before picking this purifier. I originally ordered in black, and saw the next day it hadn't shipped yet and the white one (Model 5530), was now available, so I canceled before being charged, and ordered the white one...even though there had been none purchased yet and no reviews. It had recently came on the market (at least for Amazon) and I am so glad I went with it.

It's so much nicer to look at then a big black box. BUT AGAIN.... I would have gone with the black anyhow, because of all of my research on air purifiers as far as testing and price point for the unit (as well as options/price for replacement filters.) THIS ONE CAME OUT ON TOP ALMOST EVERY TIME!!

Powerful filtration and very quiet. The turbo is a little louder, but it fades into the background, and it's nice for me to fall asleep to, honestly. I don't even notice it, especially when the TV is on. I run mine with Plasma Wave and on turbo, full time, but I use the app to set the time/schedule to go to medium overnight, after I've fallen asleep, because I like the quiet noise to fall asleep to... and then it automatically turns back on turbo at the set time for the morning. FANTASTIC!

Note: Because I'm on a budget, I already ordered a 2 pack of aftermarket filters to have on hand, but I can tell you the honeycomb carbon pelleted aftermarket ones, are filled a little too much. I'm a little concerned with what will happen regarding air flow because of this, not to mention, who knows if the carbon pellets and HEPA filter, are really of the same quality...but time will tell in the future. THE ACTUAL WINIX BRAND FILTERS THOUGH ARE WONDERFUL!!

The only difference between the 5520 and the 5530 is the 5530 is white. I love it!

Ps. For those afraid of the Plasma Wave / ion thing... You can't even tell it's on. I have asthma, and I'm extremely sensitive to those older machines that produced ions, but this one is a different kind of thing. It's double bonded or something like that, and there are ZERO EFFECTS OR ODORS from it. Do some research on the Plasma Wave technology, it's nothing like a typical ionizer, nor the purifiers of old days before we knew better, or anything of the such. Don't let anyone else fool you. ALSO, IF YOU DON'T WANT IT, THERE'S A BUTTON JUST TO LEAVE IT OFF....BUT, I SUGGEST USING IT!!! IT'S "PART" OF THE TECHNOLOGY AS TO WHY THE PURIFIER WORKS SO WELL.

Great air purifier, I highly recommend!

reviews.review_title: Fantastic Machine, Automatic, Very Quiet, Great looking
reviews.review_description:
** 3-week update **

After a few weeks a clicking noise developed in the fan when running on the sleep (lowest) speed. Looking at the fan it appears there maybe an imbalance that over the weeks developed into a motor shaft tapping. Make sure to inspect your unit for a balanced fan. I just issued a replacement on the 5500-2 so we'll see what happens.

** Original **

I spent weeks comparing units on Amazon and elsewhere. I didn't want to spent > 200 on an overbuilt fan, or be stuck buying overpriced filters. I ended up buying the Winix 5500-2 and Renpho AP002 and first impressions with the two units are that they both appear well built, quiet, and have the automatic mode I really wanted.

TL;DR;

Winix 5300-2 - Quieter w/Smarter hands off Automatic technology & Ionizer - Set and Forget!

Winix 5500-2 - Identical in Black w/Remote & washable carbon filter

Renpho AP001 - Incredible unit, Amazing filters, Low cost ownership!

Renpho AP002 - Almost identical, slightly more air volume

FILTERS

The Renpho filter has a price and feature advantage over the Winix. Both units have H13 Hepa filters, both have the honeycomb active carbon filters (for capturing VOC), and both have a washable pre-filters for catching large particles. The Renpho however has 2 bonus layers, a microbial coating on the Hepa filter, and an additional charcoal filter sitting before the carbon filter to collect larger particles. The Winix does claim the active carbon filter is washable - Renpho does not make this claim, however both appear similar so it maybe purely marketing. The Renpho filter is shorter and fatter - if you ran the numbers they both likely have similar surface area, thought the Winix is CADR rated for 360 sqr/ft while the Renpho is 330 sqr/ft. They are close.

Renpho OEM filters sell for $25 for a full replacement. Winix OEM filters sell for $50 for a full replacement. Renpo claims the filter should be changed every 6 months, Winix claims every 12. I assume this is reflected in their price strategy, however since the filters are so similar, I doubt both claims can be true - and this all depends on how dirty your air is! So cost of ownership is likely less with the Renpho.

AIR IONIZATION

The Winix comes with an Ionizer (called Plasmawave) and Renpho does NOT. The Ionizer charges any particles passing through the unit so they are heavier and will float to the ground and out of air. If you're concerned about Ozone gasses, then this is a feature you can disable and is not a feature on the Renpho.

SOUND

This is a real issue for me - I am sensitive to sound and like the home quiet at night. Deciding on a unit for my children makes this even more important, and I don't want to force them into a white machine for air filtration. In Sleep mode the Winix is significantly more quiet at (advertised) 26dB where the Renpho is at 35dB. With the Winix 10ft from the bed I can just barely hear it. The Renpho is noticable but not "loud". The Winix appears to have 5 speed modes, Sleep, Low, Med, High, and Turbo. The Renpho has just 3 modes, Low, Med, High, with Sleep mode being the Low mode with lights off. Here's the rub however - outside of Sleep mode, the Winix sounds "louder" having a higher pitched whine while the Renpho is more of a hum. If I was going to just set this on High in a corner and forget it, then Renpho is the winner. For a quiet bedroom the Winix appears the winner.

AUTOMATIC MODE

This was a huge feature for me and the Winix is a much "smarter" unit. Both units have a similar Automatic feature, sensing the air, bringing the fan speed up or down according to the readings. Both have light(s) indicating the current air quality reading. The Winix however had a light sensor that, when the unit is in Automatic mode, will place the unit in Sleep mode when the lights go out (for more than 1 min). In the morning the unit goes back into Automatic mode. This is huge if you appreciate how quiet the unit is. You can set the Winix to Automatic mode and not touch it until your next filter cleaning. If you wish to use the Sleep mode on the Renpho you will need to push the Speed button to cycle through the speed options back to Sleep - and then again in the morning cycle back to Auto. In reality you maybe better covering the lights with black tape and leaving it in Auto or just leave it in Sleep mode permanently.

REMOTE

Winix has one, Renpho not - for my needs this is a non-issue.

CHILD LOCK

Renpho has one, Winix does not - this is a great feature if young kids are around!

APPEARANCE

Personally I think the Winix looks clean, modern, and the black color blends well into a corner near furniture. The Renpho AP002 like the Renpho AP001 have their signature funky look which is fine but not as refined. It's an air purifier, so who cares, but it is also a visible piece of equipment in your home.

For us the Winix seems more appropriate for a bedroom, the Renpho for a living room. Winix higher cost of ownership justified by the features and sound levels, Renpho for lower ownership cost.

If the Renpho unit was QUIETER (ahem - hint hint Renpho) then I would just go that route - save on upfront and ownership cost.

SIMILAR MODELS

The Winix 5300-2 and Winix 5500-2 are the exact same physical unit in different colors with different filters. The 5300 is gray, the 5500 is black. Only the 5500 has a remote. The 5500 has their "advanced" AOC Washable Active Carbon filter, while the 5300 has a disposable active carbon. The 5300 Hepa filter is slightly thicker (good) and you get 4 disposable filters with each replacement. If you buy the 5500 and don't like the washable filter it comes with you can buy the 5300 replacement pack and use them instead. For $23 more we went with the Winix 5500-2 to test the AOC filter, and for the black aesthetic. Currently you can get the 5300-2 for $129 (Amazon) and when I purchased the Winix 5500-2 for $152 (now listed at $159 on Amazon).

The Renpho AP001 (often found as RP-AP001 or AP-001) and Renpho AP002 are very similar products, both using the exact same filters, having different aesthetic designs, and with the AP002 having more airflow (for supposedly the same sound levels) and covering 30 sqr/ft more space. The AP001 has a dedicated Sleep button while the AP002 Sleep mode is the first option on the Speed cycle button - more daily button work for you. Currently the AP001 sells for $99 (Renpho direct) while the AP002 for $137 (Amazon). I bought the AP002 thinking the newer model maybe more quiet than advertised. If we get another Renpho it will be the AP001 for $37 bucks less.

reviews.review_title: auto setting runs fan according to air quality
reviews.review_description:
The auto setting of this air purifier is good: it detects when the air is dirtier, indicates that with an orange or red light, and increases the fan speed accordingly. This happens when I run the filter in my kitchen and it reacts to the smoke from the stove or oven, even when it is not enough to see with your eyes. Sometimes the light changes to orange or red in the bedroom right after someone coughs or sneezes, so I think that indicates that it is probably cleaning the air of infectious particles breathed out by someone who is ill. Sometimes it indicates dirtier air and it is not obvious to me what it detected, but I trust it since it does detect things I know about like cooking smoke and sneezes. Most of the time it runs on the lowest and quietest setting (which is reasonably quiet), but runs higher when needed. It also detects the light in the room, so if it is dark at night, it runs an even quieter mode.

My sister had bought one of these air purifiers for our elderly parents in California. I don't remember whether it was smoke from wildfires or Covid that first motivated my sister to buy the air purifier, but it has been good for both of those health hazards. So when I visited them, I had seen how the auto-detection worked and when I had vacuumed out the filter for them, so I could see that cleaning and changing the filters was easy.

I first bought a unit for myself in 2023 when smoke from wildfires in Canada blew down and made the air in Chicago hazy and orangish and beaches were closed because the air quality index was over 100 and was bad enough that people were told to stay inside. Our HVAC system has 4" MERV 13 filters, but I felt that smoke was still getting in whenever we opened our doors and the HVAC filters were probably not filtering enough to completely clean the air. I also have pretty bad seasonable allergies, so this unit is good for cleaning the pollen out of the air in my house.

Just a couple months after I bought the unit for my own house, I sent another unit to my adult child in DC when the smoke from Canada blew into DC. They liked it so much that this year they bought one for their workplace office after they had to start working part-time in-the-office rather than fully remotely as they had done when they were hired during the height of the pandemic.

The unit is a bit heavy at 17 lbs. So I got tired of taking it up and down the stairs from my bedroom to the dining room or kitchen and I bought this second unit for our household. It has a different style of activated charcoal filter that has gravel-sized pieces of charcoal in a plastic cage instead of the black fiber filter that the previous units used. The new charcoal filter is supposed to last longer than the fiber filter so I think it is better. I found that generic filer replacements of the HEPA filter and the charcoal filters fit my first unit just fine. I haven't looked for replacements for the newer type of charcoal filter yet.

Results may vary depending on the actual usage environment. 12.Tested by Intertek, the test was conducted in a 1.0 m³ chamber for 120 minutes resulting a 99.9% removal rate on sulfur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, and naphthalene. Results may vary depending on the actual usage environment.

reviews.review_title: EXCELLENT for drowning out outside noise! Lasted 4 years.
reviews.review_description:
I’ll touch on the purification, but the reason I have this, and why it was suggested to me - is for a sleeping aid! That is ALL I use it for and it is EXCELLENT for such. I was miserable and tried earplugs and white noise through my speaker. My brain knew that was artificial. This thing did the trick! My savior! It has 3 speed levels. Which, I’m guessing the lowest levels is what they’re saying is more quiet than an air conditioner. Level 3 is absolutely NOT more quiet than an AC.

This isn’t about it justing be loud enough to drown out noise. I’m pretty sure it’s about FREQUENCY. Imagine the sound of an air conditioner, but a little louder and giving you a slight breeze to make your room just a SMIDGE cooler. If there are cars, birds, noisy AC condenser units outside, or people talking outside, turn this thing immediately makes them DISAPPEAR like magic. I think it’s got to do with the airwave frequencies. It brings your mental attention to your room because the purifier sound is in your room. So it keeps you in the present and kind of acts as a sensory deprivation when it comes to audio. It also makes light rain sounds disappear AND thunder!!! While not being disturbing. It’s soothing to me.

I had this thing for 4 years until the fan gave out. Using it almost every night. Level 2 will only drown out the most subtle nuances like light wind and things in the distance. Sometimes I use it if it’s a quiet night. But level 3 is what I usually use to really help me knock out. If it’s off or level 2 and I wake up to some noise outside or wind chimes, I just get up and punch the 3 and boom it’s all gone and I’m back to bed. 😴

As for purifying the air, it’s always showing a blue light to indicate clean air. But it’s still good to use because the sensor doesn’t detect EVERYthing. For me the air purification is just a bonus. I probably wait too long to change the filters but they’re easy to do! And dust doesn’t go flying everywhere when I change it. That I can see.. But remember all you gotta do is turn it back on when the filter is changed in order for it to clean that invisible dusty air back up. I assume.

Very RARELY does the light change to indicate air impurity. Maybe sometimes purple if it’s SUPER windy or there was a fire somewhere outside that you can smell. One time I was applying a diatomaceous earth powder to my room for bugs, and the light went REDD and I left it runnning for a whole day and I think it reallly helped. Probably wasn’t good at all for the machine but it kept going! I have never tried out the ion setting because the description I have read scares me. Ion wanna try it..

A few days ago, after 4 years, the fan just stopped going. And it made some noise. For the week leading up to it, sometimes the fan would slow down for 5 seconds and then go back. It sounded more like a power issue with maybe my apartment. But then when the fan stopped, I think that was my answer. Not sure how long it’s shooosed to last. I’m sure it varies. But I would say it’s worth it for 4 years.

I don’t need any pictures. What you see in the other pictures is accurate. It’s the height of the length of a coat hanger! It’s less than a coat hanger wide by a good bit, and it’s half the length of a coat hanger deep when you measure behind it. Maybe that’ll give you an idea of the size. Not bad. It’s at the foot of my bed.

Cleaning it was super simple. I’m ordering another one and it’s giving me same-day shipping. Idk. It’s cool.

reviews.review_title: A really great air purifier that has many key improvements/advantages over its competitors
reviews.review_description:
I got this air purifier for a relative that has COPD. They already had an Alen T100 that they were pleased with. But, as is common in multiple industries where a core product requires a consumable, it's often not the condition of the core product but the availability of the required consumable that dictates when a product has to be replaced. While I've been able to find enough replacement air filters for that one air purifier, when the need arose for a 2nd air purifier for a second section of the house, instead of just getting a newer Alen, I opted to start the research process all over again and, this time, the clear winner was Coway And, as well as the Alen has done over the years, it didn't take long to see how much better the Coway model was by comparison. A first major difference is in the design and aesthetics. With several color variants and another model with a more classic look, it doesn't visually stand out as much as a typical tower air purifier does. It's more stylish and "elegant". Second, there are actual very practical functional reasons for those aesthetics. Instead of blowing air on people horizontally, it blows the air straight up so that nobody feels the air blowing. It's also significantly quieter so even set on medium speed it's quieter than the Alen at low speed. That's impressive given that this model is designed to handle a space 3X as much as the Alen was. But, it's due to the design of having the air come in from the sides and then exit out the top. It just provides a much more natural method of air circulation. And, also means it can be tucked along a wall and out of the way ... with the cord blocked from view if located directly at the power outlet. Another great feature that the Coway has that I haven't seen before is that you have 4 stage filtration .... with the initial pre-screen stage being a built-in filter that can be washed ... followed by the 1st charcoal filter to catch large objects like hair .... followed by a 2nd filter that have 4 replacement options and therefore can be customized based on what types of odors or particles a person needs filtered out ... and finally the HEPA filter that catches the smallest particles that make it past the other three. Not only is this like a coin-sorter process of filtering out different things at different people ... but this is why, unlike a lot of air purifiers, the main filters can last 1 year instead of just 6 months. The built-in filter is recommended to be cleaned once a month. The charcoal filter 6 months. The "environmental/smell" filter being replaced once a year. And, the HEPA filter being able to last even longer depending on environment. Where it actually gets better at filtering over time ... but then the tradeoff is air flow reduction. That's why the official recommendation is still once a year. And, best of all, the NYT wirecutter review I'd found says Coway has made continual improvements over the years to this product, which really shows. Many manufacturer's just seem intent on constantly reinventing the wheel and it seems Coway was instead focusing on perfecting what it already had. Very pleased with the results and the good deal we'd gotten on it. While we hope the Alen continues to do well for several more years, at least it's nice knowing that we already know what to replace it with whenever it become necessary.

reviews.review_title: Quiet, Effective, and Worth Every Penny
reviews.review_description:
I’ve been very happy with this Coway Airmega air purifier. It’s surprisingly quiet, even when running throughout the day, and it has made the air in our home feel noticeably fresher and cleaner. I especially appreciate the automatic mode, which adjusts based on air quality without needing constant attention.

The design is sleek and compact, so it doesn’t take up much space, and the filter replacement process is simple. We use it in a bedroom and have noticed less dust and fewer allergy symptoms. It runs efficiently and gives peace of mind knowing it’s helping improve our indoor air quality.

Highly recommend for anyone looking for a reliable, easy-to-use air purifier. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I don't want to be one of those giddy-with-first-impressions folks in not testing a product thoroughly for months before posting a review... but this thing makes me wanna do just that. It arrived simple & understated.. and by that I mean, unpacking was easy and it did not take brute force or cleaning stray pieces of styrofoam for 30 minutes after unboxing. It slid out, I removed two pieces of protective styro caps, and unwrapped the shrink wrap. I took off the plastic wrap from the filters (which were already in place so I didn't have to read a book of instructions first to figure out where to put them). Then I simply plugged this sucker in, and it worked on auto right out of the box. It was like unboxing an Apple product -- so intuitive, so seamless, so simple. Kudos to manufacturers. And of course, as first impressions go... it looks good. So I love it even more because it's pretty.

Aesthetics aside, it is also built well... and perfectly sized. I attached photos to show that it's not too tall, nor is it too deep. It is a bit shorter than my nightstand, which is of an average height. It's a bit on the wide-side, but you can position it however you see fit. It does need about a foot on the right side to allow for proper air flow, and probably a good idea to keep the front end free & clear since the "circle" is from where it pulls in air... but I found this guy could be positioned in many places throughout my home without being an eyesore. I have it in my bedroom currently, but I plan to buy one for my family room as well, and maybe the basement also. It really does work. My bedroom is often very stuffy, especially in the winter when we have the heat temperature set to 73 degrees -- I like it warm & toasty, but my nasal passages feel otherwise. I do suffer from pollen allergies, as well as mild allergies to dust mites, grass, ragweed, mold spores, and pet dander (although I still have 2 shed-heavy fur-babies.) But my allergies are never bad enough to warrant any real attention, I just suffer through it since they're pretty mild. HOWEVER, I keep saying mild when in all reality, I didn't know the difference between no allergy and mild allergy until sleeping one night with this purifier running. Man what a difference. My nose was not all dry and cracked up feeling on the inside. It also was not runny or scratchy, which is how it often feels after running my humidifier all night (which I run to keep my nose from feeling so dry!) This machine does not mask the issue, or dampen it, or freeze/cold draft it away.... it CLEANS THE AIR. I know, I know... it's hard to imagine, but boy is it easy to feel. I slept for the last 2 nights like a newborn baby. Granted, I've only had it for 2 days but the difference from walking into my bedroom vs the other rooms of my home, cannot be ignored. My home isn't particularly old, or stuffy, or dirty, or dusty. Yes we have pets, but I am a Dyson maniac and we have a brand new HEPA HVAC filtration system; we have our ducts cleaned regularly; and, there are no smokers or other reasons for contaminated air (at least that I can find.) However, when plugging this thing in... it ran a blue and then purple light for a bit on auto, but then changed to RED (which freaked me out a bit as it sounds rather aggressive). And it ran that way for about 10 minutes. I left it to its job, and when I returned a little while later, it was back to a blue light and I could barely hear it running anymore... but the air did in fact feel lighter, crisper, and easier to breathe. It felt much like the very first time I walked onto my hotel balcony in Vancouver, Canada and took in a giant breath. It just felt... clean.

Air quality is a legitimate thing, and having poor air to breathe makes life a less tolerable for people with allergies or lung issues. Again, not something I suffer from necessarily, but I appreciate the cleaner air this provides nonetheless. So I cannot imagine how much better breathing could be for someone that does have serious allergies, asthma, or other breathing troubles. I would say this gem is a no brainer, if you do. But even if you don't, you'll still notice the difference after plugging this guy in and letting it run for about the first hour.

I do think the auto feature could become a bit of a power monger as I have never witnessed it turn off after being on auto as if to say "okay, I'm done. All clean." So I do set the timer feature when I'm not going to be upstairs and I shut it off when I'm leaving the house for awhile. Another thing to note is that there are studies about potential harmful effects to lungs when using the UV and ion cleaning features. It is recommended that you only use these settings when not in the house as breathing in UV treated air is said to be harmful as a result of O3 air, similar to breathing in air high in ozone levels. So I only set my purifier with these features when not in the room.

I can't yet speak to durability or filter tolerance, but they are priced reasonably enough that changing once or twice a year would be totally acceptable. I will update if I find that longevity or level of purifying impact worsens, or if cleaning/upkeep isn't as great with this machine moving forward, but for now... I am a Coway air purifier believer.

** UPDATE - after 7 months of constant use, I will say that my initial reactions were still pretty accurate in that this purifier does do what it claims to do. I notice that it is reactive to smells, smoke and other air-purity issues when they are occurring, even when I am simply cooking sausage or something extra smokey or fragrant in the kitchen -- while I have this unit upstairs in my bedroom, which is a considerable distance from the kitchen (bedroom in front of the house on 2nd floor, kitchen in the back of the house on the 1st floor.) So I know that it indeed works because I can hear it begin to run rapidly when I accidentally burn something or even when making bacon or something that has a smell or odor. I also know that it is filtering dust and pet hair, because both of my Coway purifiers (I have one upstairs and the tower unit downstairs) needed HEPA filter replacements at 6 months. The manufacturers suggestion is 6 months for the carbon odor filter, and 1 year for the thick, HEPA filter.. but my HEPA filter was so dirty at 6 months that the "change filter" light came on for the tower unit, so I figured I would change this 1512HH unit at the same time, and it definitely needed it. The filters were both clogged with so much dirt, dust and pet hair.. I couldn't believe this stuff was floating around my house for it to grab. In fact, even strands of my hair were in the filter! And my hair is pretty long, well below shoulder-length. I figure it must have sucked it in from the floor. Pretty cool purifier... I still give it 5 stars and 2 thumbs up after 7 months of use.

reviews.review_title: A little pricey, but performance is worth it
reviews.review_description:
I’ve had this air purifier for a little over a month now and have really liked it. It seems to do a really good job at cleaning the air in the large room I have it placed in. It’s about 20 feet away from our kitchen and will almost instantly switch into turbo mode when we start cooking. You can also see the display numbers go up which is neat to see it doing its job!

It is also light enough where you can move it from room to room if there’s a reason. It’s placed in a pretty large open concept, Family room/Kitchen combo. The prefilter seems to be a pretty neat idea as it catches all the bigger dust particles and dog hair. I vacuum this off about once a week.

reviews.review_title: Amazingly quiet and scrubs the air clean.
reviews.review_description:
I am very happy with this air purifier. Since I keep it in my bedroom, quiet oparation is a must. It didn't disappoint in this regard. It is so quiet I sometimes have to check to see if is on. Other purifiers are quiet when you first get them. But they almost always have a cheaper sleeve bearing fan motor that inevitably begins to rattle an buzz after you have had it for a while. Also, it really cleans up the room air compared to my last air filter. I hardly ever have to dust anymore. It has a lot of extra features, modes and displays. I just set the fan to speed 1 and let it run 24/7.

reviews.review_title: Astoundingly effective, whisper quiet, highly recommend.
reviews.review_description:
I bought a $90 tower purifier which took a long time to clear the air and which was noisier than a jet engine. I lived with it, but when the Canadian wildfire smoke descended upon us in NYC, I loaned it to my downstairs neighbor, who had elderly and special needs family members, and I ordered this as a replacement.

It's more than double the cost of the other unit, but based on the reviews from the New York Times and other review sites, the quality and performance are well worth the investment. So I splurged and got this unit.

While I was waiting for it to arrive, the air pollution got really bad and I had been coughing, eyes were watering and I was forced to wear an N-95 mask at home just to breathe.

When the purifier finally arrived, I turned it on and the sensor light went red to indicate the high level of contamination in the air. I opened the doors of every room of my apartment to let it go to work and after a few minutes at full power, the light turned from red to purple, and about 5 minutes later, it went blue. I took my mask off and the air was pure and fresh. It is an absolute superhero at cleaning a large volume of air very quickly. I was thoroughly impressed.

The sensor is very sensitive and will turn purple if you are just cooking something that releases strong scents into the air (sauteeing onions and peppers, etc.) and it goes red if you're burning anything.

Another upside is that my kitchen smoke detector has stopped going off if I'm grilling something, because the purifier keeps the air quality under control.

At the highest setting, it's about as loud as my old purifier at the middle setting, which is to be expected, as you would only set it that high to quickly clear out a room or if there's smoke from cooking, etc.

But the massive volume of clean air it blows out in exchange for that short term annoyance is staggering.

However, at the 2nd highest setting it is barely detectable, producing a pleasant, white noise background sound that you quickly tune out. It makes falling asleep very easy, and if you have the air conditioner on you can't hear the purifier at all.

At it's lowest setting, it blows out a nice stream of air but is utterly and completely silent. You couldn't even hear it at night time in a small, quiet room with the door shut. Amazing.

They say you never regret buying the best. They know what they're talking about. This is worth every penny and then some. 5 stars, all day.

reviews.review_title: Ok, Let's Clear The Air For A Moment.........
reviews.review_description:
.........This Coway Air Purifier is outstanding, and I am not sure why it gets any bad reviews at all, unless someone just receives a bad unit from the factory (it happens, folks). Also, we have not had any of the bad "odors" that some people have complained about, either with the Coway air purifier itself, or with the replacement filters. However, the black colored model does look a lot like a large subwoofer, if that bothers anyone....lol. I did a LOT of research for an air purifier to replace the Bissell "My Air" air purifier that we had in our master bedroom, and this Coway air purifier kept coming up as a top pick everywhere. The Bissell "My Air" works well, but it's just too small to keep the air in our large master bedroom suite constantly clean, especially with our ever-shedding German Shepherd puppy always being in the bedroom with us at night.

This Coway air purifier came well packed. It was double-boxed, and reinforced with cardboard packing material inside, and shrink-wrapped (no damage to the boxes or Coway unit at all). This Coway air purifier is very easy to setup. All that needs to be done is to open the front panel and unwrap the plastic around the charcoal and HEPA filters. Then replace the front cover, plug the unit in, and turn it on. Just don't forget to unwrap the filters before turning the unit on.

This Coway air purifier is fairly quiet on the first 2 fan speed settings, but it gets pretty loud on the 3rd setting. However, the fan moves a LOT of air on the 3rd setting. The Auto and Eco modes are nice features, and they both seem to work well. We just keep the Coway air purifier in Auto, with the ionizer turned off, all of the time, as the ozone produced by the ionizer irritates my throat while sleeping with the unit on all night.

I actually tested the dust sensor function in auto mode by shaking a dust rag in front of the Coway air purifier, and the fan speed ramped up from setting 1 to 3 for about 5 minutes, until the air was clean again, and then it went back to the 1st fan speed setting automatically. The dust sensor sensitivity is also adjustable by pressing the fan speed and ionizer buttons simultaneously for 2 seconds. Then use the fan speed button to adjust the 3 sensitivity levels (the unit is set to the middle "standard" setting at the factory). We have not had to change the dust sensor sensitivity level, as it seems to work well on the standard setting. Also, it is recommended that the dust sensor be cleaned with a cotton swab every 2 months. It is located behind the little door on the upper right of the unit.

The large, bright power LED also indicates the dust particles ptesent in the room. Blue is clean air, purple is semi-dirty air, and red is really bad air quality. If the bright LED bothers anyone at night it can be turned off by holding down the ionizer button for 3 seconds.

The 1,4, and 8 hour timer is a handy feature, if needed, but we never use it. We just run this Coway air purifier in Auto mode all of the time, and it works like a charm. It uses very little power (around 36 watts on high with the ionizer off), so I don't feel any need to constantly turn the unit on and off. The charcoal and HEPA filter indicator lights come on individually when it is time to change the appropriate filter, and the lights are reset by holding down the filter button for 3 seconds. The filter change timer can also be factory reset by holding down the filter change reset button for 2 seconds when neither of the filter change indicator lights are on (if the filters are changed early).

The manufacturer recommends cleaning the washable mesh pre-filter every 2 weeks, changing the charcoal filter every 6 months, and changing the HEPA filter once a year. The charcoal and HEPA filters are NOT washable, and must be replaced. Only the mesh pre-filter is washable and reusable. I would take these filter cleaning/changing intervals with a grain of salt, and mileage may very, depending on the air quality in the individual home. I have seen many 3rd party companies that make the filters for this Coway air purifier. Most of them are much cheaper than the OEM Coway filters, and they have good reviews. However, we have only used the OEM Coway filters so far, and while being kinda over-priced, they work very well. Oh, and as previously mentioned, don't forget to clean the dust sensor every 2 months or sooner, as well. The rest of this Coway air purifier can be wiped down and vacuumed out as part of regular maintenance.

Overall, this Coway brand is an excellent air purifier, and I highly recommend it, especially for anyone with allergies, asthma or pets in the house. It also filters cooking odors very well. Just keep in mind that this Coway air purifier is fairly large, so it needs plenty of room to function properly. Also, the shiny piano black model does attract finger prints like a magnet, if that bothers anyone. Oh, yeah, and as I previously mentioned, the black model looks a lot like like a large subwoofer. It is a unique design for an air purifier, to say the least. However, those minor "issues" should not detract anyone from purchasing this great Coway air purifier. Pick one up today!

reviews.review_title: Compact, Smart, and Perfect for a Bedside Table
reviews.review_description:
This compact air purifier has been an absolute lifesaver for my bedroom allergy flares. It is small enough to sit comfortably on a nightstand or in a tight corner, yet it keeps the air feeling noticeably crisp and clean all day long. Setting up the companion app over WiFi was painless, and it gives you a clear look at your actual indoor air quality in real time. The absolute best feature is the auto mode, which lets the built-in sensors monitor the room and kick up the fan speed automatically whenever it detects pet dander or dust floating around. 

When it comes to noise, it is practically silent on the lower night settings, meaning you can easily sleep right next to it without any annoying humming or clicking. While the marketing text claims it can handle up to a thousand square feet, it truly shines as a dedicated unit for a standard bedroom, office, or nursery where it can cycle the air constantly. The fabric pre-filter on the outside also does a fantastic job of catching heavy pet hair before it even reaches the main filter, making maintenance a breeze.

reviews.review_title: Senses and removes odors, unlike the 211i model.
reviews.review_description: I bought the model 211i first as we have a fairly large house and we were disappointed. I have had terrible allergies this spring so purchased the larger, well recommended unit and it basically did nothing to help. The blue light was always on indicating clean air but it did nothing to get rid of pollen and odors. It was basically a fan that moved air so we returned it. This unit (which is the SP1i model) functions much better to remove smells and VOC's. Our combined family room are roughly 700sq feet and we keep in the family room. It senses food cooking odors from about 25 feet away and helps remove them. I think this has a much more sensitive detector sensor and better filter; we are keeping it.

reviews.review_title: A must during wildfire smoke or cooking smoke or if you have pets & dust allergies
reviews.review_description: I bought this because of its great reviews online by Consumer Reports as well as others on youtube who have tried this product. This has an exceptionally high rating that I bought 2 for my family as well. It was very useful for us during the wildfire smoke. Also useful when someone outside our window or a passerby is smoking cigarettes. Also useful when cooking & the trapped air is wafting all over in the living room, bedroom & kitchen. Since it is very lightweight, you can easily carry it to the bedroom or near the kitchen area or living room to suck out all the bad smelling air or toxic air. Highly recommended. And because it has an app, you can check the smoke level in your phone. The filtration & filter replacement lasts a long time. Easy to replace filter, value for your money. Odor removal is quick after just a few minutes of it being on. Also perfect for those who have pets & dust allergies. Provides immediate relief when smoke if trapped inside your apartment or house or small area room. A must have in every part of the house.

reviews.review_title: Quiet, Effective, and Smart Enough to Just Let It Run
reviews.review_description:
I picked this up mainly for pet dander and general dust in my bedroom, and it's made a noticeable difference. Within the first day or two, I could tell the air felt cleaner, and the auto mode does a good job of ramping up when it detects something and quieting down when the air's already clean, so I'm not manually adjusting settings all the time.

The HEPASilent technology lives up to its name. Even on higher fan speeds, it's nowhere near as loud as other purifiers I've owned, and on the lower settings it's practically silent, which makes it easy to leave running overnight without it being disruptive.

WiFi connectivity works well through the app, letting me check air quality readings and adjust settings remotely, which is a nice bonus if I want to kick it up a notch before getting home. Setup was straightforward and it paired with my WiFi with no real hiccups.

Given the square footage rating, it feels appropriately sized for a bedroom or smaller room rather than something to rely on for whole-home coverage, and that tracks with how it's marketed. I keep it in my bedroom specifically and it handles that space with room to spare.

My few hesitations keeping this at four stars: the filter replacement cost adds up over time, and the app occasionally lags or takes a moment to sync current air quality data. Neither is a dealbreaker, but worth knowing going in. Overall, a quiet, capable purifier that's earned its spot in my bedroom.

reviews.review_title: Clean air indoors when fires rage outdoors
reviews.review_description: Although it's a smallish unit, it held up to the recommendation I received. Our location has been in the middle of 18 mountain and grassland fires for the last month. As of 16 August 2026, the AQI fluctuated for the last month between "Unhealthy for sensitive groups" and "Very unhealthy." My asthmatic wife couldn't go outdoors for at least two weeks. This unit purified the air in our living room, and we put it in the bedroom at night for better sleep. This product was recommended by my niece, who lives in the Rocky Mountains, which also experienced several mountain fires.

This is my second Blueair purifier. After owning a larger unit and seeing for myself how dirty the filter gets, I completely trust in the efficiency and reliability of Blueair products. We recently went through exposure of intense smoke that caused red flag days. We were very comfortable with the quality of air in the house thanks to Blueair. This unit shows you, by easily seen colors, your current air quality. And at night time, you can turn the light off so as not to disturb sleep. This unit also connect to a phone with Bluetooth.

The perfect air purifier for your bedrooms. I love that everything is controllable from your phone. You can customize all kinds of settings . It’s not loud or distracting. It looks modern so it fits in with any decor. You can set it to turn off and on when you want it to. The filter life is very long and best of all it detects when there are pollutants in the air.

reviews.review_title: Air feels good and clean no real issues with it.
reviews.review_description: It's really nice to have, bigger than I expected, but that's even better. It works nicely, and I enjoy having a way to see the air quality on my phone. I used to always get a runny nose due to dust in my room whenever I cleaned, but this has helped me not get as many runny noses anymore. I can see very little, if any, dust in the air (like when you see it in the sunlight). I tested it by blowing out a match in front of it to see if it really detects stuff; it went to max fan speed, which makes me believe this is working. Speaking of fan speed, it's really cool and nice to feel; I honestly replaced my AC with this most of the time. The main reason I would not give it 5 stars would be the lights. I hate sleeping with any type of lights, and whenever I change it using the buttons, it sometimes leaves a light on even in night mode, which in turn I would need to fix by going on the app, which allows me to turn it off. Other than that, the air feels very fresh, and I can hardly smell anything; it feels clean and nice in the room I use it in. It does need to be connected to an outlet instead of battery, which makes it hard to put it in the middle of the area without a cable being in a way, but for it's price, i would say it's really good, the filters aren't too expensive and I would only need to replace them once every 6 months based on how much im using it.

reviews.review_description: Great so far. Very easy to use and very effective for a moderately sized row house. Within 15 minutes on the highest setting I could feel the difference in the air quality. I put it in different rooms daily. It's light enough to carry from room to room. I keep it on a low setting at night. It's quiet and a powerhouse. I'm really happy with my purchase.

I only just got this yesterday and used it last night for the first time but I feel compelled to write a quick review already. This thing is a game. changer. Ever since moving to Texas, I suffer from terrible seasonal allergies. I never have in my life until now (turns out I'm allergic to a handful of trees that are native around here. Fun.) Some years are worse than others but this year is baaad. For the past few weeks my mornings have had me waking up congested and unable to breathe, blowing wads of snot out of my nose (sorry!), and with a itchy/scratchy sore throat. First thing I do is take an allergy pill and wait in misery until it finally seems to kick in around mid morning. (I've had a terrible time finding meds that work too. It just sucks.) I don't know why I never thought to get an air purifier. I guess when I thought of air purifiers I'd always think of the fancy Dyson ones that cost hundreds of dollars. I mean, puh-lease. Not happening. Then I found this little guy. Had great reviews, was the perfect little size for our master bedroom (216sqft), and reasonably priced with reasonably priced replacement filters. In a plee of desperation I talked my husband into us trying it. It got in yesterday (quicker than expected, yay!). I immediately unboxed it upon getting home from work and plugged it in. It says you only need to run it for about 15-20 minutes on high to cycle the room but I set that little baby on high with a two hour timer and let it run. When it was time for bed, I set the 6 hour timer on sleep mode. The sleep mode is great. It's a lot more quiet than I expected. I still expected to be able to hear a little white noise from it (which doesn't bother me at all) but unless I lift my head off the pillow and really listen, I can only just baaarely hear it. And I have it on my side of the bed about 3 feet away. Our home air system is louder than it on sleep mode. If you enjoy white noise, you could probably just run it on low and be fine. It has a button to turn off the indicator lights at night too so you don't have bright lights keeping you awake if that's a problem for you. Anyway, I woke up this morning with NO allergy symptoms. None. No congestion, absolutely clear nasal passages, and NO sore throat at all! I'm blown away. I'll try to come back and revise this review if my opinion changes but after the first night and the relief I was FINALLY able to feel from my allergies this morning I absolutely rate this thing 5 stars. Worth every penny!

This small, quiet and efficient air purifier is ideal for our needs. It fits neatly into any room, is unobtrusive, and is simple to operate and maintain. The build quality and overall aesthetics is top notch. The cost of replacement filters is reasonable and can be done in less than a minute... about every six to eight months. We noticed that the unit quickly removed any smoke and cooking odors from the area while running. Highly recommend!

Bought one for my mom and one for my sister in law. Good thing I bought it for my sister in law because a couple months later the devastating wildfire in the Palisades of Los Angeles happened. So the entire LA county was full of smoke. Hopefully it helped but I'm not entirely sure how well it cleans the air because the amount of air that gets pushed out the top is not as forceful as my own air filters at home. My decades old Hunter air purifier has a ton more air flow it's almost like a high power fan. But I think it is able to move so much air because it doesn't have a pre-filter like all the new air purifiers use. It just uses replaceable HEPA filters and I know it works because I see all the dust it catches in the filter before I have to replace it.

As for the Levoit it has a pre-filter which catches most of the dust and dirt but you never know how much actually gets through to the actual HEPA filter.

I recommend the Levoit for smaller bedrooms, it's too small to do anything in a large room. At least it's fairly quiet on the lowest and middle setting.

reviews.review_title: Pet Odor and old house odor, bye bye!
reviews.review_description:
Edit to original review: it’s been several months at this point and I have two in our small farmhouse. They work amazing, best purchase we’ve made.

So far: it’s perfect, surpassed all expectations, ALL.

Backstory: we’re living in a house from the late 1800s, that has been dormant for about ten years until we moved in a couple years ago. We have five pets, four cats which are strictly indoor and use an automatic litter box (Popur S7 which does great for the smell, it can only do so much though) and one fat, lazy, stinky pitbull. The house is musky, it’s old, it had way too much mold in the detached basement when we moved in. And the pets? They stink bad too, this is coming from someone who is very particular about the house smelling good. The litter box is horrible, the dog is gross, the house is old.

I went searching for an air purifier, I’ve been wanting the SHARK never change, but couldn’t break down and buy it for $300. Didn’t try it out, can’t say if it’s good or not.

While I was looking at reviews, I found the shark had only 5,000 reviews on Amazon, and it was at 4.3 stars. Okay, that’s not too bad. But this Levoit one had over 100,000 reviews and 4.8 stars. That’s nuts in comparison. I done a lot of looking on Reddit and found that the shark wasn’t even mentioned in the majority of good quality reviews, so I disregarded it.

This specific one happened to be in budget and also has amazing reviews.

We received it last night and set it up this morning, yep this morning, in our cat’s litter box room which is also unfortunately our closet. That room is the worst room of the house in my opinion. It’s been running for about 6 hours and I already notice a huge impact. It’s easier to breath, the air doesn’t feel so heavy, and the litter box is nonexistent, even right after they use it. Hubby sprayed cologne on himself and not 20 seconds later I walked in and it was gone, already sucked away. I put a box fan on it to help circulation and have it on 3.

I’m buying another. Maybe two more. If I remember I’ll come back and review again when it gets a little later in the month. We’re leaving for vacation next Monday, so I’m curious how it will hold up against the cats stagnant litter box, which usually stinks pretty bad when we get home after a week.

TLDR; Amazing for pet odor, amazing for muskiness. Perfect and worth every penny.

We have 2 in our house and looking to purchase a 3rd. Love these things! Ours run all the time and after a couple of years are still going strong! I've recommended them to quite a few people. I can't attest to any personal allergy relief since my immediate family doesn't really suffer from much (maybe due to the purifiers) but I do feel a peace of mind having them in our home, especially with pets! Does a great job to trap dust and debris. I am always very surprised to find how much these things pick up when I check/change the filter. I also appreciate the white noise that it gives off. We do run ours on the 3 setting most days and it provides a nice background noise, which is a personal preference for my family. There are 2 other lower settings which are much much quieter. The purifier is easy to use and easy to maintain (filters can be a pricey). I will actually clean the filter a few times before purchasing new and have found that works great for us and saves an extra buck. We have two white ones and find that they look nice and blend in well with the rooms they are placed in. One of the purifiers is in a space between the living room and kitchen area (most traffic and use) and the other is near our home office and entry. I feel that they do a good job for the space size. Would definitely recommend!

Impressive. It is whisper quiet, and extremely effective. I’ve been sick all week from the wildfire smoke in the Denver area. I happened to be talking to a friend on the phone when I received my LEVOIT air purifier. I set it up while we chatted and within half an hour I could tell that the air quality had improved. I was breathing easier and my friend said she could hear it in my voice - it wasn’t as rough and nasally. It says it is for a room up to 222 square feet, but it is portable (under 10 lbs), about the size of a wastebasket, it plugs in to a regular outlet, and I can physically only be in one room at a time. But it was very cost-effective, under $100, so I may go ahead and get another one for the kitchen next week. (I am a senior on a fixed income, but this is a necessity if I want to be able to breathe in my own house when the air quality outside is so bad.)

reviews.review_title: Levoit Air Purifier Home Allergies, Asthma
reviews.review_description:
I love the Levoit Air Purifier! It is very quiet all of the time, but if you use the night time sleep mode, you can just barely hear it at all. The fan has three speeds as well as the sleep mode. You can set the sleep mode for up to 8 hours, the best I remember. I do use sleep mode but not with the timer. You can turn off the display panel and I do that at night because I prefer a totally dark room. I run it all day on low and so far, a week out from getting it and setting it up, there are no signs of anything that needs to be cleaned from the outside as I've seen in other reviews. I don't have any pets, just nasty carpet. I call it nasty, because all carpet is nasty to me. I dislike carpet so much! I don't have a choice, though. I think the filter is supposed to last around six months, so we shall see. I bought a replacement filter when I bought the purifier and several filters for the humidifier, as well. It looks like I may have to change the Humidifier filter once a week as a week out, it is starting to turn brownish-yellow around the top of it. I don't smoke and do try to keep an extremely clean place, so not sure what the discoloration is. I'm the only one who has ever lived here. I use distilled water but also bought the demineralization kit and extra filters for the humidifier in case I run out of distilled water and have to use tap water. I clean the humidifier every day. It's not hard to do once you do it. I love the modern look and it is built very well. It's really not hard to use at all. I believe it is super effective combined with my also Levoit Humidifier. I have them on opposite sides of my small bedroom as I couldn't put my humidifier under the smoke alarm. My skin feels much softer and cleaner using the both of them. I could instantly tell a difference in how well I could breathe using the them. As before purchasing them, I couldn't breathe out of my nose at all. The humidity is brutal here. I have been able to get the humidity down to 58, which is something the local meteorologist said couldn't happen in these heatwave temperatures! Ha! I only use GENUINE LEVOIT filters and they're a bit more costly, but I prefer to use the real deal and have less problems/headaches. It can be a bit catchy to find them on Amazon and the generic ones keep popping up; however, I went straight to the Levoit store to get the genuine ones. Blessed to be able to somewhat better control my Asthma and all-season Allergies with the help of these two awesome products! Thank you, Amazon and Levoit! Sorry for combining reviews but I need to do a copy and paste for the humidifier as it will save me time doing it this way.

reviews.review_title: Fingers crossed this helps my allergic dog!
reviews.review_description:
I got this air purifier for my bedroom. My dog has a very severe dust mite allergy. He was literally disintegrating. His hair was falling out and his dandruff was like a blizzard. He had full body yeast and it smelled like a dirty gym sock on steroids.

Despite having no carpet, rugs and bedding that are washed weekly, and dust mite covers on both of our beds, he was still miserable. He is so allergic that out of desperation I'm trying everything I possibly can to minimize his exposure while his immunotherapy does its job.

The vet said that short of having hospital level air purification I would never get rid of all the dust mites, but I can limit his exposure with air purifiers, so we are giving it a try. There's no way I can accurately gauge how much this air purifier is reducing the dust mites, but it has to be better than it was before I got it.

My dog gets 3 medicated baths a week and is about to start immunotherapy, so I can't really credit any progress to the air purifier alone, but there is no doubt it will help reduce the total number of dust mites he is exposed to.

I also got a larger air purifier for my living room/kitchen. I live in a camper currently as I recently moved and am building a home. Since we live in cramped quarters with less ventilation than a sticks and bricks home, the dust mites and other allergens are far more concentrated.

I've noticed since having these two purifiers running that our home smells fresher and cleaner, any smells do not linger. I've tried my hardest to deep clean any dust collected around the house in all the little nooks and crannies that you can't see and hopefully the purifiers will help keep that to a minimum. For some reason even in the dead of winter we seem to have a lot of dust. Again, probably because the space is so small. It seems the smaller the space, the bigger the mess! Thankfully it doesn't take as long to clean a smaller space.

I'm not sure if I'll ever really know how effective these are, but I can say I've noticed a big difference since I got them in the quality of the air. We have wood heat so there's not a furnace constantly blowing air around. They provide air flow in what used to be pretty stagnant areas in the winter when the a/c isn't running.

The stinky sock yeasty dog smell has been reduced quite a bit, and any other lingering smells like cooking or flatulence from my gassy teenager don't tend to hang around as long lol. So they have been a win-win! They seem to work very well.

I don't use the timer features because I let them both run 24/7, but it's nice to have that as an option if it's ever needed. I really appreciate the small footprint of this purifier because there's not much room in a camper. I have it on my bedside table. You can see in the picture about how big it is next to my 40oz swig.

Even on high it's very quiet, but I'm one of those "can't sleep without a fan" people so I enjoy the sound lol. Between this and the fan at the foot of my bed pushing air towards it, our air in the bedroom ought to be squeaky clean!

5.0 out of 5 stars Compact, Efficient, and Quiet – A Game-Changer for Allergy Sufferers

I’ve been using the Levoit Core 300 Air Purifier for about two months now in my 200 sq. ft. bedroom, and it’s exceeded my expectations in every way. As someone who deals with seasonal allergies and pet dander from my cat, I was looking for an affordable, reliable solution to improve indoor air quality without breaking the bank or taking up too much space. After researching options, I settled on this model, and I’m thrilled with the results.

The setup was incredibly straightforward – just unbox, remove the plastic from the filter, plug it in, and you’re good to go. The design is sleek and modern, with a cylindrical shape that fits neatly on a nightstand or floor corner without dominating the room. At around 8.7 inches in diameter and 14.2 inches tall, it’s compact enough for apartments or offices, yet powerful for its size.

Key features include a 3-stage filtration system: a pre-filter for larger particles like dust and hair, a True HEPA filter that captures 99.97% of airborne particles as small as 0.3 microns (think pollen, mold spores, and fine dust), and an activated carbon filter to tackle odors, smoke, and VOCs. It has three fan speeds plus a sleep mode that dims the lights and runs ultra-quietly at just 24dB – quieter than a whisper, making it perfect for nighttime use. There’s also a timer (2/4/6/8 hours) and a display lock to prevent accidental changes.

In terms of performance, this little unit punches above its weight. It refreshes the air in a 219 sq. ft. room up to 5 times per hour on high speed, according to the specs. I tested it during a smoky day from nearby wildfires, and within an hour, the air felt noticeably fresher – no lingering smells or stuffiness. My allergy symptoms have reduced significantly; I wake up with clearer sinuses and less sneezing. It’s also energy-efficient, using only about 45W at max, which keeps my electricity bill in check.

Pros:

• Affordable and great value: At under $100, it outperforms many pricier models in small to medium rooms. 3

• Quiet operation: Sleep mode is a lifesaver for light sleepers. 1

• Effective filtration: Handles pet dander, dust, and odors exceptionally well. 2

• Easy maintenance: Filter replacement is simple, and indicators remind you when it’s time (every 6-8 months).

Cons:

• No built-in air quality sensor or auto mode – you have to manually adjust speeds (though the upgraded Core 300S adds smart features if you need them). 5

• On the highest speed, it can get a bit noisy (around 50dB), but it’s still tolerable for short bursts. 3

• Best for rooms under 300 sq. ft.; for larger spaces, you’d need multiple units or a bigger model.

Overall, the Levoit Core 300 is a fantastic entry-level air purifier that’s reliable, user-friendly, and effective for everyday use. If you’re dealing with allergies, pets, or just want cleaner air in a small space, I highly recommend it. It’s ETL, CARB, and Energy Star certified, so you know it’s safe and efficient. Worth every penny!

title: Instant Pot Duo 6 Qt 7-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, Stainless Steel
description: The Instant Pot Duo: the original all-in-one cooker that made fast, versatile cooking a household staple.

reviews.review_description: I was slow to warm up to this appliance in my kitchen. I bought it to quickly cook a corned beef for St Patrick’s day. When it arrived I promptly threw away my old rusty but well used rice cooker (how many appliances can I really fit in my cupboard anyway?). It did a wonderful job, but honestly having never used a pressure cooker before I felt like I was programming a sensitive bomb that may go off in my kitchen at any moment! Every little beep or noise was frightening! I almost peed my pants when I released the pressure valve and loud hot greasy steam erupted from its behind angrily! That was not a fun clean up job! So after St patties was over it sat for months till I eventually pulled it out again to try making rice (yeah no I can’t seem to cook it on the stove). The rice cooked great in about the same time it took my old rice cooker. I now love my pot because of what happened last week. We got home late and I grudgingly wandered into the kitchen late one night wondering what I was going to make for dinner. I found a small jar of Thai peanut sauce and a freezer burned chunk of raw chicken way in the back of my freezer. I tossed both in and set it for 12 minutes. I didn’t expect it to actually work, but what came out was a pot full of juicy Thai peanut chicken I tossed over rice! So Yummy and quick and easy! I’m excited to see what else will work well now!

I’m very happy with my Instant Pot! It’s easy to use, cooks food quickly, and makes meal preparation so much more convenient. I love that it has multiple cooking functions in one appliance, which saves both time and space in the kitchen. It’s also easy to clean. Great quality and definitely worth the purchase. Highly recommend!

Over the years, I have purchased hundreds of items from Amazon, and for the most part, got what I expected. I never reviewed any of them. But from the moment I received my Instant Pot, I felt that I had purchased something that not only exceeded my expectations, but will make my life easier (and more delicious)!

I am a holistic nutritionist and a follower of a lower carb/paleo/primal lifestyle (and yes, it is not only a food regimen, but a lifestyle). Many of the meals I prepare require advance planning and preparation, and I am OK with that, realizing that it is an investment in my family's health and wellbeing. I was looking for something that would support my food choices and perhaps make it a little less time-consuming. I have used a crockpot extensively over the past years and while I appreciate the ease of use and the ability to put a meal on the table soon after I got home in the evening, there is that "everything tastes the same" factor I was running into with my family.

So I began thinking about ways to cook my meals faster and realized that a pressure cooker may be the answer. But, I am scared of pressure cookers. Even though my head tells me that people have been using them for many years with no problems, my heart said there was a strong chance I could blow up the entire kitchen, myself included. I had no idea there were electric, programmable pressure cookers out there that would virtually eliminate that worry until I began researching them, first on Amazon, and then on other websites. I eventually purchased the Instant Pot over the others because of the stainless steel insert (no aluminum), the size of the pot (I wanted a larger capacity), and the ease of use.
