reviews.review_title: A perfect addition to my kitchen
reviews.review_description:
While visiting my sister, I used her set of Cuisinart knifes. She place the time of purchase somewhere between 5 and 7 years, and they were wonderful. Easy to handle, not to heavy, and a great variety of knives for cutting different types of foods. The steak knives are the best I have ever used, the Santoku (the blade is wide in height and snub nosed) cut a left over roast into very, very thin slices for hot roast beef sandwiches.

In early July, I purchased the Classic Forged Triple Riveted set of 15 knives and the block, because the set held most of the knives I was looking for and they fit right into my kitchen décor. And, my struggle of 59 years in my kitchen, trying to cut vegetables, fruits, meats and breads and struggling with knives has come to an end. It is such a mental and physical relieve to start a meal knowing that cutting "whatever" will no longer be a struggle. My new knives are the best I have ever purchased and I have purchased a lot of knives. Wish I had know a long time ago about Cuisinart knives, didn't know that they made anything but electric appliances for the kitchen.

A little bit of a down side, be prepared for a larger than normal knife holding block, and it is heavy, but again the length of the knives make it necessary and are worth the block size and weight.

Would I recommend them to my best friend.....in a heart beat! But...would I purchase this set again, no, but I would purchase the solid metal handle set, as the paring knife handle has cracked from the rivet to the edge of the handle. I care for my knives, I hand wash and dry them and put them away, I am concerned that if one handle cracks after a month and a half of use, how long before another on cracks.

Overall, I would have given this set of knives a 5 star except for the cracked handle.

As with most quality kitchen knives, proper care is important. Hand washing and drying the blades promptly will help preserve both the edge and the appearance over time. Even stainless high-carbon steel benefits from avoiding prolonged moisture exposure and should not be left soaking or placed in the dishwasher.

One aspect worth mentioning is that exceptionally sharp knives require some extra attention, particularly for users who are accustomed to less aggressive factory edges. Overall, this is a versatile knife set that covers the majority of common kitchen tasks while offering an attractive presentation and comfortable ergonomics. reviews.review_title: Gorgeous knife set for the home chef, all the knives you'll need to start out as a professional chef
reviews.review_description:
I absolutely love Hoshanho knives and cutting boards, all are top-quality professional grade IMO as a home chef. They aren't always cheap, but the price is less than what you would pay for some name brand professional knives, and I would put these up against most of them in terms of looks and quality.

There are three knives in this set, an 8-inch traditional chef knife, a 7-inch Santoku and a 3-3/4-inch paring knife. This should handle 90% of a chef's needs. All three are part of their Egret line of knives. The Egret line is made from a matte finished blade, with a shiny stripe above the edge, which makes for a very nice contrasting look. Each has an octagonal olive wood handle with a piece of black G10 material near the bolster. My first impression of these is that they are gorgeous, specially with the contrast of the matte and shiny finish of the blade and the light and dark contrast on the handle. They are all extremely sharp out of the box and should stay that way with proper care and maintenance. Speaking of the box, they come well packaged in a nice presentation box, with each knife covered in clear plastic and having safety covers over the tips and tails of the blades (tip only on the paring knife).

The weight of the 8-inch chef's knife is towards the tip of the knife, about a 1/4-inch in front of the bolster. The 7-inch Santoku's balance point is right at the bolster and the 3-3/4-inch paring knife's balance point is about a half inch behind the bolster. IMO, all the balance points are where they should be for each style of knife. Cutting and chopping is fast and efficient. The Santoku knife has dimples on the bottom part of the blade that allows food to easily slide off the knife as you are cutting. All have flat tops for easy gripping of the blade if you like to cut that way.

The handle has a 1-inch length of G10 plastic at the front and the remaining olive wood handle is attached to the blade without any pins. The transition from the wood to the G10 material is smooth; I can't feel the transition on the paring knife, although I could feel it on the larger knives, it is only a slight bump and does not affect functionality. The light-colored olive wood has nice graining, and the three handles have similar color and grain patterns, making them look cohesive. The handle diameter is smaller on the paring knife and larger on the chef and Santoku, each fits my hand well and I always feel in control, even with wet hands.

This is a knife set that you would proudly use during food prep and look professional while using it. Every Hoshanho knife I have is super sharp and retains its sharpness with minimal maintenance, this one is no exception. I swipe the blade about 5 times per side on a smooth leather strop before each use and again before I put it away, and the blade stays very sharp. I've had other Hoshanho knives for over a year now and they have stayed sharp with an occasional honing and use of a strop; I've yet to sharpen them with a stone. Make sure to wash with mild soap and water after use and wipe dry with a towel for long life. I also use a small amount of mineral oil on the handles to keep the wood grain vibrant. If you take care of these, I can easily see them lasting years.

reviews.review_title: Japanese style knives factory produced in China. Fair knives, pricey, some concerns with durability
reviews.review_description:
I saw these and jumped at the opportunity to get a set of genuine, high quality Japanese knives. The ad states "Professional Japanese knife set." This led me to believe these were made in Japan with their well known quality standards and craftsmanship. The more I looked at them and researched things, the more I realized these are a set of mass produced knives made in China.

These are "designed in Japan" but "made in China." So that prompted me to examine these a little more closely about the rest of the claims. I found that companies can get around the country of origin thing by stating that these were designed in one country but then mass produce them in another country.

The seller claims these knives have 9 layers of steel. It is difficult to determine by looking at them, but apparently these do have a hard steel core and 4 layers of steel bonded on each side according to online research. The center core holds the edge, which is ground at a 12 degree angle. Most of my hunting and kitchen knives are ground at a 20-25 degree angle, making these extremely sharp in comparison, but also possibly prone to chipping the hard steel. The bands of texture on the sides of the blades are actually laser or acid etched, and it is difficult to determine if these are just cosmetic or are the actual delineations of the steel layers.

I do feel a bit deceived, in that these are not produced in Japan but are mass produced at a factory in China. I don't know how they'll hold up over time. My chief concerns are possible brittleness since they claim a very high 62 HRC hardness, and how deep the tangs may be positioned in the wooden handles for strength. Wood handles can split or work loose. These will need to be used more gently in some cases and not hit against bone or used with a great deal of force. As for the cost, these appear to be highly priced at $179.99 for a set of three factory made knives from China. These are probably worth substantially less, with better knives available at that price.

reviews.review_title: Sharp, Complete Set, and Looks Great on the Counter
reviews.review_description:
I bought this Cuisinart 15-piece knife set because I wanted one complete set instead of having random knives from different brands taking over the kitchen drawer.

The stainless steel design looks clean and modern, and the wooden block keeps everything organized and easy to reach. I also like that the set includes the sharpening steel and kitchen shears, so it covers more than just the basic knives.

The knives feel balanced in the hand and came sharp enough for everyday prep like slicing vegetables, cutting meat, and handling general kitchen work. I definitely recommend using the sharpening steel regularly because even good knives need a little maintenance.

The biggest improvement for me is organization. Now I actually know where the knife I need is instead of opening a drawer that looks like a culinary junkyard. 😂

Overall, a very complete, attractive, and practical knife set for everyday cooking.

**it has been 3 wonderful years with these knives and they're still as sharp as the day they arrived! I have had no need to have them sharpened, and honestly, I still have no complaints. They. Are. AMAZING.

I can't say enough good things about these knives.

I recently moved into a new house and of course needed to upgrade some items. First on my list was a good knife set since I'm a avid cooker. Despite some bad reviews, I went ahead and ordered these.

First things first; they are SHARP. I can only cut with one hand and these bad boys slice through tomatoes like nobody's business. One handed cutters dream!!

Second, they are GORGEOUS. I am beyond proud of displaying them.

Third, they have a wonderful balance to them.

They are durable, there is nothing flimsy about them!! I have had several knife sets, but these are my absolute favourite!!

Some people were complaining about them rusting, and fair, that COULD happen. But if treated right, they wont do that.

My number one rule is these do NOT go in the dishwasher. In certain circumstances, they don't even see soap.

They are washed immediately after use, thoroughly dried, and returned to the block. Should spots appear, I use stainless steel cleaner.

They are still as beautiful as the day I took them out of the box.

They also have required no sharpening since I got them.

If stored and taken care of PROPERLY, these knives will never need replaced.

They are every bit what I had hoped for and worth every penny spent.

I highly recommend them to anyone who asks and even to those who don't!!!

If you want knives you don't care about or you'll throw in the dishwasher, these are not for you.

Take care of your knives, love them, respect them, and they will deliver excellent performance time and time again.

Except for a few minimal scratches, the product arrived in good condition. The knives are all sharp and sturdy as well.

reviews.review_title: Excellent All‑Steel Knives That Perform Better Than Expected!!
reviews.review_description:
I’ve owned several Cuisinart knives over the years, and this all–stainless steel set is definitely one of their winners. Each knife is forged from a single piece of steel, giving them a sleek, modern look and a sturdy feel.

I’ll admit when I first saw the stainless steel handles, I assumed they would be slippery, especially when chopping veggies. Luckily, that wasn’t the case at all. They’re surprisingly comfortable, well‑balanced, and offer a secure grip even during longer prep sessions.

The standout for me is the 7” Santoku knife (C77SS-7SAN-25K). It’s a Japanese style incredibly sharp, solidly built, and the longer blade length gives you great control. If you’re used to a 5" Santoku, it may feel a bit heavier and may take a little bit of getting used to, but once you do, it’s hard to go back. Like the rest of the knives in the set, this one arrives razor‑sharp and stays that way as long as you care for it properly.

My next best favorite is the western style Chef's knife (C77SS-CF-25K) which is what most folks like including the chefs as it allows to cut a wide variety of vegetables and fruits. It has a curved edge("belly") with a pointed tip.

My Third favorite cutting knife is the Slicing Knife (C77SS-SL-25K) which is specifically useful for slicing large cuts of either cooked meat or fish. It has a long, narrow blade with a pointed tip. I found this to be useful for cutting larger fruits like Watermelon, Melons or gourds etc. as the longer blade allows you to cut/slice them their vertical length.

To keep these knives in top shape, here are a few care tips I personally follow:

Use the right cutting surface: Stick to wood or plastic cutting boards. Harder surfaces like glass, stone, or metal will dull the blade quickly.

Hand‑wash only: Clean with warm, soapy water and dry immediately with a soft cloth. Make sure the knife is completely dry before storing it.

Avoid scraping with the sharp edge: If you need to move chopped ingredients, flip the knife over and use the back of the blade or a scraper.

Store properly: Always use the included sheath. Storing knives loose in a drawer can damage the edge and create a safety hazard.

If you follow these simple steps, these knives will stay sharp and serve you well for a long time. Overall, this is a great quality set that delivers excellent value and performance. Highly recommend!

These knives work well for my needs. I am not a great cook so I mostly use them for slicing veggies or bread etc. My only complaint is that when I keep them under the cabinets it is hard to pull some of the knives out due to the angle of the wood block. I did not have this issue with my last knife set. They feel nice in your hand with a good weight to them. So far they wash well and look great!

reviews.review_title: Solid Knife Set For The Price
reviews.review_description: I have had these knives since 2018. They came with a decent edge but that was promptly ruined by some careless roommates. That said, once I was able to out a decent edge back on them, these knives have served me very well for years. With a quick hone every few uses, these knives have maintained a pretty impressive edge for a cheap set. They no longer are dishwasher safe as they have started to get small rust spots if run through the dishwasher. However, seeing as they've made it 7 years already, I'm happy to hand wash them.
Excellent Product my old set wire after decades. I decided to upgrade. These are sturdy, well balanced love the built in sharpener. Takes up very little space as compared to my old set decades ago.

title: Martha Stewart Knife Block Set 16-Piece - Lockton High Carbon Stainless Steel Forged Full Tang Chef Knives, Acacia Wood Block, Triple Riveted Handles, Linen White & Gold
description: The Martha Stewart Lockton 16-Piece Knife Block Set delivers professional-grade cutlery with the polished aesthetic you'd expect from Martha Stewart's kitchen line. Every blade is forged from high carbon stainless steel and built with full-tang construction, giving you the balance, control, and edge retention that serious home cooks demand. Triple-riveted ABS handles provide a secure ergonomic grip that holds up through years of daily use. The smooth-grained acacia wood block keeps your knives safely off the drawer and beautifully organized on the countertop. reviews.review_description: I’m really impressed with this knife set for the price! The knives are sharp, work really well for everyday cooking, and the block itself is so aesthetically pleasing sitting on my counter. It has a much more expensive look without the expensive price tag. Definitely a great option if you want a nice-looking knife set that gets the job done without spending a ton.

reviews.review_title: Bought for looks, surprisingly very pleased with quality and performance!
reviews.review_description: For the price these are really quality! I am super happy with them! Nice weight and feels great in your hand. All of them are very sharp and cut extremely well! Beautiful Ivory and gold color. They look very classy sitting on the counter. I've had them three months now and they are holding up well. I am hand washing mine as I want the gold to stay fresh looking for years to come. But they are nicely made with a quality finish, and I do believe they would hold up fine in the dishwasher. The blade thickness for the price is quite impressive. In all honesty, I bought this set for the way it looked. My kitchen is very gold heavy on decor. I own much more expensive knives, the workhorses you hide away in the drawers because they aren't aesthetically pleasing, but these are performing way above my expectations and feel as if they will have some real durability for some time to come. reviews.review_title: Beautiful knife set that looks even better in person!
reviews.review_description: I absolutely love this knife set! The ivory handles with the gold accents are so elegant and give my kitchen a high-end look. The acacia wood block is also beautiful and feels sturdy. It fits perfectly on my countertop without taking up too much space.

I’ve had the set for a little over a week now, they are on the lighter side but as someone with a lot of hand pain I actually appreciate that. They come VERY sharp, like passed the tomato test with flying colors. The scissors are good but could be a tad sharper but that’s just preference. Overall very good value for the price

reviews.review_title: I received a damaged, recirculated returned item :(
reviews.review_description:
I must’ve received the same set that’s been returned over and over again. Rather than continuing to recirculate a clearly defective return, why not send out a new, quality item?

I purchased the green set, and as several other reviewers have mentioned, the color is not really Sage green—it’s much closer to avocado, although not quite that bright. More importantly, the oxidation and chipping on the gold metallic parts are very noticeable and simply shouldn’t be present on an item being sold as “new.”

At a discounted price, this might be a reasonable thrift-store purchase. The actual steel quality seemed decent for a Chinese-made set, although the handles felt somewhat plasticky. That said, these obviously aren’t top-of-the-line pieces, so I wasn’t expecting premium construction.

Ultimately, my main issue isn’t necessarily with the Martha Stewart brand itself, but with this particular vendor.

reviews.review_title: Looks nice but steak knives are bendable and flimsy.
reviews.review_description: I watched this item for a year before buying and was so disappointed when it arrived. Knives are very sharp but flimsy. Just not the quality I was expecting at all. These knives looked good in the picture and the blades appear to be sharp. Otherwise, I was surprised at the poor quality of the knife handles as well as the wooden block they sit in. The bottom of the white handles on a couple of the knives looks as if they were patterened after crumpled paper. They are cracked, and the wooden block is discolored in some places as if it was put together with different shades of stain.
Best set a knives we’ve bought…all our guests think we payed way more than we really did. Durable and sharp . Get set.

reviews.review_title: Lovely knife set, works very well.
reviews.review_description: Beautiful set, looks great on my kitchen. Very careful they are very sharp. Comfortable grip and very stur, really recommend it. The only thing I dislike is that the knife storage doesn’t fit tight on the hole, but not a big deal for me. We use it every day and gets compliments from my family. Very sturdy knives.

So I have had this set since November 2020 - 3 FULL YEARS - and it still looks and performs like the day I first got them!! They are beautiful, sharp, feel good in the hand/nice weight and handle, and are easy to use. JUST TAKE CARE OF THEM AND HAND WASH THESE KNIVES!! Of course, if you put them in the dishwasher, water will collect in the handles and rust may develop if the blades don't dry completely. I think that was one of the "Don'ts" that was mentioned in the description by the manufacturer. Mine are still perfect!! And I do have my favorite - the Santoku Knife!! ❤️
Beautiful set..but they will rust so just dry them throughly

reviews.review_title: Catch them on sale for $20 and it's a fair deal.
reviews.review_description: I've had these for almost 3 years now. They're "decent" if you catch them on sale at $20. ONLY if you have the talent and means to resharpen them occasionally. They are fairly sharp when new but lose the edge quickly. "Razor" sharp? NO WAY! The cheap steel has a limit on how sharp they can be sharpened, and they don't hold the edge very long, before needing resharpened. The scissors are pretty cheap. The handles are hollow, so they have to be dried almost vertically, or you'll get water dripping when you put them in the block. A couple handles have dents, possibly from dishes being set on them in the sink? I have only recently started trying them in the dishwasher, so far, no issues. They're holding up ok, with no sign of rust or spotting. I gave my daughter my much old, much larger set of "decent" Farberwear knives when I ordered these. Wish I'd waited til they arrived, she would've gotten this new set. The block is solid and heavy.

We love this set.

Very as sharp. Great buy.
Son una joya en tu cosina este set !! Los amo

Save your money and sanity, buy something else. I needed a new set of knives for a small kitchen and chose these for the reasonable price. Don’t waste your money. They hold water in the handle, rust at any sign of liquid on the blade, not at all comfortable to hold in your hand (the handle/tang is literally UNcomfortable at times), the brand name is stamped very cheaply into the knife block so it even looks cheap/bad on your counter. These knives were marginally sharp to begin with, but have dulled significantly over the last three months. How in the world this knife that got 4.3 stars is completely beyond me, one star for this is generous.

For the price, it’s not a bad deal, but there are a couple of things worth mentioning. The blade seems to lose its sharpness pretty quickly compared to other knives I’ve used. It worked great at first, but after a relatively short period of regular use, I noticed it wasn’t cutting as smoothly anymore.

The other issue is rust. I put it in the dishwasher a few times, and it started showing signs of rust much sooner than I expected. If you buy this, I’d definitely recommend hand washing and drying it right away to help prevent that.

That said, considering the cost, I still think it’s a decent value. It gets the job done and is reasonably priced, but don’t expect premium durability or long-lasting edge retention. Overall, good for the money, just be prepared for a little extra maintenance.

title: Cuisinart C77CR-10P 10pc Stainless Steel ColorCore™ Color Rivet Set with Blade Guards
description: This classic 10-piece cutlery set features premium knives with high-quality stainless steel blades for a wide variety of cutting tasks. Backed by a lifetime warranty, each knife is specially designed with an ergonomic handle for comfortable control to ensure chef-caliber performance.

reviews.review_description: Love this set! They are sharp! They store easy and I love that they are color coated so I’m not digging in my knife drawer for the knife I need. Dishwasher safe and stores safely.

First and foremost, the quality of these knives is outstanding. The stainless steel blades are exceptionally sharp right out of the box, providing precise and effortless cutting. Whether I'm chopping vegetables, slicing meat, or dicing fruits, these knives handle each task with ease and accuracy. The sharpness of the blades has remained consistent even after multiple uses, which speaks to the durability and quality of the steel.

The ColorCore™ color rivets are not only visually appealing but also practical. Each knife has a different color rivet, making it easy to quickly identify the knife I need. This feature adds a touch of fun and style to the kitchen while also improving efficiency during meal prep. The rivets are securely fastened, and the knives feel well-balanced and comfortable in hand.

The included blade guards are a fantastic addition. They provide extra protection for the blades, ensuring they stay sharp and undamaged when stored in drawers or knife blocks. The guards fit snugly and are easy to put on and take off, adding an extra layer of safety when handling the knives.

Another standout feature is the ergonomic design of the handles. The handles are comfortable to hold, with a good grip that reduces hand fatigue during extended use. The weight and balance of the knives are just right, making them easy to maneuver and control.

The 10-piece set includes a variety of knives that cover all essential kitchen tasks, from a chef's knife to a paring knife. Each knife is thoughtfully designed for its specific purpose, making this set versatile and comprehensive. The included scissors are a useful bonus, adding to the overall value of the set.

In summary, the Cuisinart C77CR-10P 10pc Stainless Steel ColorCore™ Color Rivet Set with Blade Guards is an excellent knife set that combines quality, style, and practicality. The sharp stainless steel blades, colorful rivets, and included blade guards make this set a standout choice for any kitchen. I highly recommend this knife set to anyone looking for a reliable and stylish upgrade to their culinary tools. It has exceeded my expectations and has become an essential part of my kitchen routine.

These knives are terrific. Reasonable price. They are very strong and very very sharp. So glad they each have a protective sheath. These are made differently than the last set I had, and with this Stainless Steel ColorCore, I feel certain that the color will not peel off these. I highly recommend these.

reviews.review_title: High quality steel. Holds an edge.
reviews.review_description:
Meet cleavers are not just for cutting meat. I have had this knif for around a year. This is the best knife I have ever used for cutting ALL my food, not just meat. All the reviews that wrote that they can't get a sharp edge on it, don't know how to sharpen a knife! This is one of the easiest knives I've ever sharpened. The steel is not to hard where it becomes brittle. It's also not to soft where it won't hold an edge. The hardness is just the correct balance. It holds an edge better than my $150 great brand camping knife. Once the food is cut on my chopping block, I can easily scrap up the food onto the side of the knife, having the blade go under the side of my hand and pushing it onto the knife then picking up the food and putting it into a bowl, frying pan ect., just the way the chefs do in Chinese restaurants. It is much more efficient that way. That is what makes this a much better option for cutting ALL my food, rather than using a regular chefs knife. I know. I used to be a chef in a five star restaurant in CT. This knife is just as good as the expensive $140 knives that were bought from a restayrant supply company for the restaurant I worked at . So, buy it. You won't be disappointed with it!!!

Pros:

1. Built-in Sharpener: The standout feature is the NeverDull built-in sharpener, which is incredibly convenient. A quick sharpening stroke every few uses keeps the knives in prime condition without needing additional tools.

2. German Stainless Steel: The quality of the German stainless steel is immediately noticeable. The knives are sturdy, corrosion-resistant, and retain their sharpness impressively well.

3. Variety and Versatility: The 15-piece set includes all essential knives, from chef’s and paring knives to steak knives, making it versatile enough for nearly any kitchen task.

4. Ergonomics and Comfort: Each knife feels balanced and comfortable to hold, with ergonomically designed handles that reduce hand strain, especially when preparing large meals.

Cons:

1. Block Size: The block is substantial, which is great for stability, but it can take up a bit of counter space. Smaller kitchens may find this a challenge.

2. Price Point: While the quality justifies the price, this set is on the premium side. Budget-conscious buyers might find it a significant investment.

Overall Impression:

The Ninja K52015 Foodi NeverDull 15-Piece Premium Knife System is a reliable and stylish choice for both casual cooks and culinary enthusiasts. The self-sharpening feature alone makes it worth considering, as it simplifies maintenance and keeps the knives performing like new. For anyone looking for a quality, all-in-one knife set that blends function with aesthetics, this is a top-tier choice.

Who It’s For

If you’re a beginner who wants a real DSLR experience without feeling overwhelmed — this is your camera. It’s also a great backup for experienced shooters who want something reliable, portable, and affordable.

⸻

Final Verdict

The Canon EOS Rebel T7 is proof that entry-level doesn’t mean low quality. It’s a fantastic intro into the world of serious photography, and once you start using it, you’ll wonder why you waited. Sharp photos, simple learning curve, and real Canon reliability.

reviews.review_title: Great Entry-Level DSLR with Solid Image Quality
reviews.review_description:
Great Entry-Level DSLR with Solid Image Quality

I purchased the Canon EOS Rebel T7 as my first DSLR, and it’s been a great experience so far. This camera is perfect for beginners who want to learn photography without getting overwhelmed by too many features.

Pros:

• Image Quality: The 24.1MP sensor delivers crisp and vibrant photos, especially in good lighting. I’ve taken some fantastic landscape and portrait shots.

• User-Friendly: The interface is intuitive, and the built-in guide mode helps explain settings and functions. Great for those new to DSLR photography.

• Wi-Fi and NFC: Easy to transfer photos to your phone or tablet using Canon’s app. A big plus for quick sharing on social media.

• Battery Life: It lasts a full day of shooting if you’re not constantly using Live View or flash.

Cons:

• No 4K Video: It records 1080p, which is okay, but if you’re looking to shoot high-quality video, this might be a limitation.

• No Touchscreen or Articulating LCD: The screen is fixed and not touch-sensitive, which can make navigating menus slower compared to more modern cameras.

• Autofocus in Live View: Slower and less reliable, especially when shooting video or using the screen instead of the viewfinder.

Bottom Line:

If you’re just starting out and want a reliable DSLR without breaking the bank, the Canon T7 is a solid choice. It’s not packed with advanced features, but it gets the job done and does it well. Ideal for hobbyists, students, or anyone learning the ropes of manual photography.

Read more

The Canon EOS Rebel T7 is an excellent entry-level DSLR camera that offers great value, especially with the included EF 18-55mm and EF 75-300mm lenses. Whether you’re a beginner learning the basics of photography or someone looking for an affordable camera with solid image quality, this kit delivers.

Pros:

✅ Image Quality – The 24.1 MP APS-C sensor captures sharp and vibrant images with great detail, even in low-light situations.

✅ Dual Lens Kit – The 18-55mm lens is great for everyday shots, while the 75-300mm lens offers solid zoom capabilities for wildlife, sports, and portrait photography.

✅ Built-in Wi-Fi & NFC – Easily transfer images to your phone or tablet for quick sharing.

✅ Simple to Use – The camera is beginner-friendly, with automatic shooting modes and an easy-to-navigate menu.

✅ Full HD 1080p Video – Decent video recording quality for casual videographers.

Cons:

❌ No 4K Video – Video recording is limited to 1080p, which may not be ideal for serious videographers.

❌ Fixed LCD Screen – The display does not tilt or swivel, making it less versatile for vlogging or tricky angles.

❌ No Image Stabilization in the Lenses – Handheld shots, especially at higher zooms, may require a tripod for steady images.

❌ Slower Autofocus – Compared to higher-end DSLRs or mirrorless cameras, the autofocus speed is moderate, especially in live view mode.

Who Should Buy This?

✔️ Beginners & Hobbyists – If you’re just starting with DSLR photography, this kit is an excellent choice with everything you need to learn.

✔️ Casual Photographers – Great for family, travel, and portrait photography.

✔️ Budget-Conscious Buyers – You get a lot of value with two lenses included.

Final Verdict:

For the price, the Canon EOS Rebel T7 offers solid performance, good image quality, and an easy-to-use interface. While it lacks some advanced features found in more expensive cameras, it remains one of the best budget DSLR kits on the market. If you’re looking for an affordable way to step into DSLR photography, this kit is a great choice!

If I could give this 0 stars, I absolutely would.

I purchased this camera listed as new, not refurbished. When it arrived, I was initially very pleased. I’ve used Canon cameras most of my adult life, and this one seemed no different—great picture quality, easy to use, and the included accessories made it feel like a solid value.

However, that positive impression didn’t last.

After just three uses, the camera completely failed on the fourth shoot. I took one picture and the camera stopped functioning entirely. At first, I assumed it was a dead battery. After recharging, I tried again—nothing worked. The flash would fire, but the menu wouldn’t even come up. At that point, it was clear this was not user error—it was a defective unit.

Then things became even more concerning.

When I attempted to register the camera with Canon, the system indicated that the camera and one of the lenses had already been registered. That should never happen with a product sold as “new.” It strongly suggests this item may have been previously used or resold. About a week later, when we tried again, that warning mysteriously disappeared—which only adds to the suspicion.

At this point, we contacted Amazon, since we were still within the return window. I simply wanted a replacement or refund for a clearly defective product. Because we no longer had the original packaging, we were told we had to deal directly with the third-party seller, Beach Camera.

This is where the experience completely broke down.

Despite receiving a defective camera that failed almost immediately, Beach Camera:

Refused a straightforward exchange or refund

Opened a vague “investigation” instead of resolving the issue

Attempted to offer only $88 compensation for an $800+ broken camera

Required me to pay return shipping

Charged a 20% restocking fee—even though the product was defective

Charging a restocking fee on a defective item is unacceptable. Passing the cost of their failure onto the customer is worse.

Thankfully, Amazon ultimately stepped in to make things right, although I now have to cover costs upfront and wait for reimbursement. Without that support, this would have been a complete loss.

Bottom line: Most vendors—and Amazon—stand behind what they sell. Beach Camera does not. They failed at every stage: selling a questionable “new” product, refusing to take responsibility for a defect, and attempting to penalize the customer for their own failure.

I strongly recommend avoiding this vendor.

Read more

title: Canon EOS R100 Mirrorless Camera RF-S18-45mm F4.5-6.3 is STM Lens Kit, 24.1 Megapixel CMOS (APS-C) Sensor, 4K Video, Wi-Fi & Bluetooth, Beginner Photographers and Creators, Digital Camera, Black
description: Experience the fun of RF mount content creation with the smallest and lightest EOS R series camera, the Canon EOS R100 4K camera for video recording. Excellent still-image capabilities start with its 24.1 Megapixel APS-C size CMOS Image sensor and DIGIC 8 processor, along with Dual Pixel CMOS AF with the ability to detect human faces and focus on their eyes. The EOS R100 camera can record Full HD video at up to 60 frames per second, and detailed, high-res 4K from the central area of the sensor at 24 frames per second. The Canon EOS R100 4K digital camera features continuous capture of up to 6.5 shots per second when set to One-Shot AF. Built for excellent mobility, EOS R100 video camera is a great starting point for users looking for mirrorless cameras with interchangeable lenses. The versatility and small size of the RF-S18-45mm F4.5-6.3 IS STM lens gives you the flexibility you desire without taking up your whole camera bag.

reviews.review_title: Amazing quality and perfect for beginners!
reviews.review_description:
I bought the Canon EOS R100 mirrorless camera after reading online that it's one of the best budget-friendly options to get started with photography, and it absolutely lives up to the hype! Its suitability for beginners is fantastic, and the overall ease of use makes learning a breeze.

The image quality is honestly amazing right out of the box—the attached photos (including the close-ups of nature and my dog) are some of the first ones I took! The autofocus is quick and accurate, and the speed of the camera is great for capturing moments on the fly. It comes with all the basic accessories you need to get going; I just popped in my 128 GB memory card and was ready to shoot. Highly recommend!

reviews.review_title: Easy to use starter mirrorless camera. Canon quality.
reviews.review_description: Great starter mirrorless camera. Excellent picture quality you would expect from canon. I use mine for astrophotography. Very easy to use. Wifi works great.

reviews.review_title: Beginner-Friendly and Addicting Camera to get into Photography
reviews.review_description:
TL;DR: If you're looking into photography as a hobbyist/beginner this is an amazingly compact powerhouse. It doesn't break the bank AND allows you to save your money for lenses.

This camera is addicting.

It's my gateway to beginner photography and I want to take pictures of everything. I took it to my local Renaissance Faire, take daily pictures of my sister's cats, candid photos of my friends and family, flowers and shops during my wife and I's daily walks, etc.

It's so light and compact that the thought of getting larger and longer lenses on this would make it look really silly. Its Continuous shooting mode is fast enough to capture some horse back riding during the Ren Faire and I captured my wife's arrow mid-flight (although blurry) at 1/4000 when we participated in archery.

The GUI is so beginner friendly and explains what each mode does (Manual/Aperture Priority/etc.). It actually helped me understand what each is used for so my wife took plenty of pictures with the right settings quickly. If you dig deeper into the menus there's more granular options like Manual Focusing, Viewfinder/Display brightness, Display options, etc. There's a ton and it's a hassle to navigate through them all... Until you find out you can create your own custom quick access menus. These quickly allows me to navigate to my favorite menu options that I frequently tinker with without moving through all of the other options one by one.

The body is so small that I was afraid it would easily slip out of my hands. That was not the case as the grips on the right-hand side is grippy enough that it feels like it you can hold it with a light squeeze while adjusting focus with your left hand on the lens. This kit also provides a strap that allows the camera to be hung around your body for quick access.

The performance on the batteries lasts for at least a day with heavy usage so I recommend another battery just in case. Unfortunately, it does not come with a charger and the manual's "Charging the Battery" section talks about charging the battery with a charger. So buy a charger that's compatible with LP-E17 batteries.

The autofocus' performance is so impressive that it's enticing my wife to get one for herself.

Disclaimer: These photos are taken with the Canon RF50mm F1.8 STM Lens, Fixed Focal Length Prime Lens and NOT the lens included with this kit (Canon RF-S18-45mm F4.5-6.3 IS STM Lens).

Read more
Takes amazing pictures

I love this camera. Bought it for my boyfriend for Christmas and I am always stealing it from him to use it and go take photos of whatever I want. Yes it doesn't have its own zoom, however I love that fact that you can't take the photo (even of something further away) and crop it and it's still crystal clear. Unlike my samsung ultra camera it starts getting all pixelated... this camera is great for on the go, it's not small but it's not super big. It fits in a small bag or even in regular sized backpack without adding too much weight. The price wasn't too bad either all things considered. Also, not to mention one of my favorite part; Uploading photos directly to your phone from the camera itself using Wifi!! That feature comes in clutch 100%.
i’d say good quality for a beginner camera , has good quality, charges well, comes with kit lens , you might need to add other lens for like portrait or for zoom a 55-210 mm lens but still nice one

I got this camera to take with me on a trip to Italy. I wanted to play with it before I went, and I have been very happy with the quality of pictures. Very easy to use and as a beginner I just played with the different settings. I would highly recommend this camera to anyone, and I have been so happy with this camera. Well worth the money!

I love it. So easy to connect and upload pics wirelessly to your phone. Beautiful pictures. Simple to use, especially for beginners. It’ll do everything for you. But it does have so much more to offer for those who know what they’re doing too. Amazing camera, small, light weight, easy to handle and carry around.

title: KODAK PIXPRO AZ528 16MP Digital Camera, 52x Optical Zoom, Wi-Fi, Black
description:
The Kodak PIXPRO AZ528 represents the pinnacle of the Astro Zoom collection, combining fifty two times optical zoom with six frames per second burst shooting for photographers who demand both extraordinary reach and decisive speed. A sixteen megapixel BSI CMOS sensor paired with optical image stabilization delivers sharp, detailed images even at extreme telephoto distances, while burst mode ensures you capture the decisive frame when subjects move unpredictably or fast.

Built-in Wi-Fi connects to your smartphone via the free app for wireless photo transfer, remote live-view control, and immediate social sharing straight from the field. Full one thousand eighty p HD video records wildlife sequences, travel adventures, and event coverage in smooth, clear detail. A rechargeable lithium-ion battery powers extended sessions, and the camera accepts Class ten SD, SDHC, or SDXC memory cards up to five hundred twelve GB. Whether photographing birds in flight, athletes in competition, or landscapes across a canyon, the AZ528 gives you the reach and speed to capture what others simply miss.

reviews.review_title: It does not come with a SIM
reviews.review_description: Great camera and super beginner friendly. The zoom on it is phenomenal and I love how easily it connects to Wi-Fi and transfers photos to my phone easily. It doesn't come with an SD card though, so you're only able to take three pictures when first bought if you don't have one.

I didn’t expect to love this camera as much as I do, but it’s honestly been such a good investment for me. The picture quality is amazing—everything comes out so clear and vibrant, even when the lighting isn’t perfect. I’ve taken some of my favorite photos with it already, and it just makes everything look so much better without me having to try too hard.

What I really like is how easy it is to use. I’m not super technical, but I was able to figure it out quickly and actually enjoy the process. The autofocus is super fast, so I don’t miss moments, which is really important to me.

It also feels really nice in my hands—like it’s sturdy and made to last. I’ve been using it a lot and the battery holds up well, so I’m not constantly stressing about it dying on me.

Overall, I genuinely love this camera. It’s made taking pictures way more fun for me, and I find myself reaching for it all the time now. Definitely one of those purchases I don’t regret at all.

I like this camera a lot. I bought it for optical zoom, and I'm very pleased with the shots I'm able to get, which is mostly wildlife and waterfowl. I take all of these types of shots using the SCN>Pet Mode. I learned that little trick many years ago on a Panasonic camera I had. So for my uses, this is a pretty good camera, particularly for the reasonable price. Pay attention to instructions to achieve focus by first pushing the button down halfway. You'll hear a tone and see a green bordered rectangle when the camera feels it has focus. It doesn't always, but you'll get the hang of it to achieve a pretty decent level of what you expect.

I used to have an old Easyshare years ago, and operationally, the PixPro is very similar, though far superior. So this was an easy camera to learn for me. Once you've familiarized yourself with its operation, I think most people will find it fairly simple to use. It is also comfortable in your hand. With the kind of shots I'm taking, I'm usually using a tripod. Keep that in mind.

I've included 4 photos, which you probably won't be able to see that well, but all were taken on near max zoom except the deer, which I was very close to.

The encasement of the camera is a little strange and super easy to mar or scuff. When I tried to clean it with a cloth, I then had scuffs and lint. I found the best thing to clean the encasement with is the red antibacterial Wet Ones wipes.

I would not say the battery life is long. But the batteries are cheap. And I bought two of them in a package deal with a double charger. It connects by USB C to my OnePlus car charger, so I'm getting supervooc charging. Very fast! No need to charge slow by connecting to the micro USB! Easy battery in and out of the camera. I rotate 5 batteries including the one that came with the camera.

I have no complaints about the regular photos I've taken of landscapes, sunsets, people, etc., but I usually use my phone for things like that.

Also, it's super easy connecting my devices, both tablet and phone, to the camera's WiFi. Additionally, the PixPro app works extremely well with both devices, which are OnePlus, but I haven't updated that app on either device. I'm a little afraid it won't work right if I do. If there's ever a need, I'll update it 😉

Read more

This is an amazing camera. In a world of technical terms, it does take some time to learn how to use it. Things to do (or) know. This camera does use an (LB-060) reactangular shaped (lithium rechargable battery) which is included but I recommend buying a second battery. It does not come with a memory card. You will need to purchase a minimum of (32gb) memory card. Do yourself a favor, download the user's manual .pdf file from the internet. Just type in the full name of the camera followed by "users manual" and you will have what you need to set up your camera correctly. It has a lot of features that work great, probably more than you need if you are not a professional. After having to purchase multiple cameras, this one is by far the best value for the price. It does take some patients and tweeking but when you are done I found this camera much better than my GoPro 12, in my opinion. Although I wouldn't classify it as an action camera, it does take great stills as well as videos. This is a great value all in one camera! 1080p is so close to 4k it's very hard to tell the difference. That's what this camera is a 1080p but the small difference is worth avoiding all of the 4k headaches.

I was looking for a camera that wasn't necessarily state of the art and expensive, but still had some potential to get pictures of the Milky Way on a vacation. This served that purpose. Easy to understand and work. Lightweight. I'm no experienced photographer, but I'd say this would probably be a great entry level camera to use if you wanted to get into it.

We wanted a camera with a long optical zoom that was affordable, and this one is. It's been fun trying to learn to use it and we've gotten some great shots of wildlife--mostly ducks and birds. It's relatively easy to use for a "beginner," and has some nice features--like charging the battery without removing it from the camera.

However, I'm not impressed either with panoramic shots or the color. In fact, we are quite disappointed with colors that seem muted. I know we can brighten shots with a phot editor, but it would be nice to get that true color from the camera itself. I know the reviews aren't great for this product so we were warned. I'm not really sorry I bought the camera, just a little disappointed in the color quality. But if you mostly want it for the zoom capability, this is definitely a choice in the lower budget range.

This is a beautiful camera! So far it has worked for what I wanted it to. I like taking pictures of the birds at the birdfeeders. It’s very easy to use. When you have it zoomed in, you have to have steady hands or it is very blurry. It got a great photograph of this Carolina chickadee.

Ordered this for my wife to take pictures of birds in our yard using a lens hood and UV filter (both must be purchased separately). It has not been used indoors. The major problem with this camera is the lack of a viewfinder. Pictures must be set up using the small LCD screen on the back of the camera. Unfortunately, when you use the camera outside, the screen shows your own reflection looking back at you and you can't see what you are aiming at. I contacted Kodak customer service to see if anything could be done about this: perhaps a non-reflective coating that could be applied to the screen. This was their reply: "...when hit with sunlight the screen will look black and the only thing you can do is hover your hand over the top of the camera to keep the sun from hitting the LCD screen before pressing the shutter button." Unless you have 3 hands or are using a tripod this is an unworkable solution. The shutter and zoom controls are on the right side of the camera so you hold the camera on the right. You need to steady the camera with your left hand when the zoom is extended because the camera becomes front heavy. Using this camera is like standing in a crowd and holding your cell phone over your head to try to take a picture of something you can't really see. Sometimes you get a good picture, most times you don't. It's not point and shoot - it's guess and hope.

title: KODAK PIXPRO AZ405 20MP Digital Camera, 40x Optical Zoom, AA, OIS, Black
description:
Forty times optical zoom in a compact, travel-ready body—that is the promise the Kodak PIXPRO AZ405 delivers to photographers who refuse to miss a distant shot. Whether photographing wildlife from a nature trail, capturing performers on stage, or pulling tight close-ups of sports action from the stands, the AZ405 delivers true optical clarity that digital zoom cannot replicate.

The twenty megapixel CMOS sensor captures high-resolution images with rich detail, while optical image stabilization keeps every frame sharp at any zoom level. Multiple automatic shooting modes and scene detection make the AZ405 approachable for beginners while offering enough creative control for enthusiasts who want to grow. Powered by standard AA batteries available anywhere worldwide, this bridge camera is always ready without proprietary chargers. Pair with Class ten SD, SDHC, or SDXC memory cards up to five hundred twelve GB and transfer photos via USB to your computer for easy sharing and printing.

reviews.review_title: Great point and shoot high zoom (40X) camera and video camera
reviews.review_description:
I am very happy with this straightforward point and shoot that you can select aperture or shutter priority and just let it do whatever. In the setting you even have a night shot setting. I took this to Africa, see on picture from then. I have found that sometimes you are unable to get close, so I always look for a high optical zoom. Digital zoom causes you to lose pixels for zoom although once past 40x this camera does do digital zoom. It has some memory inside but you expand it significantly by inserting an SD card. It runs with 1.2V rechargeable batteries but I use 1.5V Lithium rechargeable AA batteries.

I have used it for both pictures and videos. I have no complaints. My old camera display delaminated from the electronic backplate. This probably happened to the heat. This is a great camera and you can download a much more detailed user manual than the one that came with the camera. I highly recommend this camera.

reviews.review_title: No Frills outstanding camera with 40x optical zoom that is easy to operate
reviews.review_description: Great photos from long range at a bargain price. Ot does not stream or connect to wifi, but I have other cameras that do that, but I never use those functions. Easily transfers photos and video to your computer via SD card or cable. Very easy to use the it takes great zoom shots for the money.. Love it!

reviews.review_title: Stunning, feature packed digital camera, in a light, relatively small package
reviews.review_description: This camera is a Kodak, so I already had some pre-conceived ideas about what it should be able to do. It not only does everything I wanted it to do, but it does lots more. It is easy enough to use that an absolute beginner can use it right out of the box (almost - you need an SD card), but it is also complex enough to satisfy the needs of a seasoned pro photographer. The zoom is an incredible 40X, and is almost too much - at the max zoom, it is like holding a telescope in your hands and trying to keep it still enough to see - it is truly amazing and fun to play with. The image quality is right up there with much more expensive units. I would give this little camera more stars if I could. All these quality features at this price point? It's a no-brainer - if you need a camera, get this one! You won't be sorry.

While this camera is not of the same quality as my old Nikon, it will do in a pinch. It was inexpensive for one, lightweight, has a good grip to hold, quick response and quieter than the Nikon. It's a good camera if you're just knocking around hiking like I am when I use it. It is not professional quality IMHO. I used to work for Kodak a long time ago and know what professional work should look like. Anyway, this camera is a kind of pinch-hitter for me while I'm on a budget. It will do, but meanwhile I'm saving up for a new Nikon...

This camera is terrible in every aspect and design, to get the SD card out you have to open the battery compartment, which when doing so you loose all the settings as in date and time on the camera and you have to completely reset everything. If you use the cord to download the pictures to your computer instead of taking out the card it drains the batteries very quickly. Even when not using the cord to download, the batteries drain very quickly, it's such an issue that it's one of the trouble shooting things that they have listed with this camera. There solution is to shut off any apps or things on the camera you're not using, tells you to turn down the brightness of the screen. Really your solution to this problem is to disable features that are on this camera, what's the point of having those features if when using them they drain the batteries very quickly. Let me explain what I use this camera for, to take pictures of items I sell on line. I put in a new set of energizer batteries, tested them with my ohm/volt tester, they tested 1.58 volts. I took 17 pictures downloaded them by using the cord and then I took 10 more pictures and the camera shut off and right before it did it said batteries expired. So I took the batteries out and tested them and they tested 1.28 volts, which will make most things still run, like my game cameras. There's definitely an issue with these cameras and the power they use and how fast they drain batteries. I've also have had it lock up and stop working several times and it wouldn't shut off or do anything, had to open up the battery compartment which takes all the power from the camera so it will reset and then close it and then turn it back on. I had a Sony Cyber shot which they don't make anymore, for over 10 years and I took literally thousands of pictures with it and it cost half as much and the pictures were clearer and of higher quality than what this camera is capable of taking. I would still be using the Sony, but some how it developed a gray spot that was showing up in all of my pictures and it was causing potential buyers to ask what that spot was on the item. So I had to stop using it and bought this camera thinking it would work great for what I was doing and also work great for taking pictures of nature and wildlife. I wish I would have sent it back right away, but I figured I would give it a chance to get better, because they said it would if I did the update. Well it's only gotten worse with time instead of better.

Read more

I use my camera for work and find it very easy to transfer photos to my computer. In the past, transferring images from my phone to the computer took a long time and cluttered my photo roll with pictures I didn’t want to keep. This camera takes great pictures and is very user-friendly. I also appreciate the option to use AA batteries since I never have to worry about keeping them charged.

Absolutely LOVE this camera! The zoom is phenomenal and it's easy to use. I did make the mistake of using my old digital camera cord to try and upload photos which did not work, but customer service was very responsive and helped me figure out what I was doing wrong (I forgot exactly why the old cord didn't support the camera). Would definitely recommend.

I used this product for photographing a model in amble light situations. I am not a professional but even after doing some research and studying this camera for use, I could not find a pleasant photo to show for it. I tried each camera setting, adjusted each of these setting, and even fixed the lighting in each of my photo areas. Still, my photos would come out blurry, noisy, Or underexposed. I tried to give this camera the benefit of the doubt and see if the video setting was any better than the photo. I admit this camera has decent quality, video recording but, after trying to view that same video on a computer(Lenovo- chrome book) I was unable to see the file or video. Which again became a big disappointment. Although I read the reviews before purchasing this camera I still had to give it a try for myself! After trying this camera out I would not primarily recommend this camera to any friends! I can say that you get what you paid for. This is a nice cheap camera which has potential if you’re invested in learning how to use it or invested in purchasing camera accessories to make your photos pop. 2/5 Stars.

title: Sony Alpha a7 III Mirrorless Camera with 28-70mm Lens Black
description: Advanced 24.2MP Full-frame Image Sensor w/ 1.8X readout speed Advanced 24.2MP Back-Illuminated 35mm Full-frame Image Sensor. Improved AF and tracking plus up to 10fps continuous shooting capture decisive moments. Reliable operability ensures confident shooting. A light, compact body enhances mobility. 4K HDR3 4 movie recording capability.

reviews.review_title: Pro level at an accessible price
reviews.review_description:
Compared to the 2 Canon DSLRs I have owned in the past, it blows them out of the water in terms of auto focus speed and accuracy. For low light, I've never seen anything like it in the consumer market, not counting the A7s ii which I haven't tried yet. The version that I bought came with the kit lens and it's performance is fine. It's not the best to use for the ultimate low light capabilities, but it's reliable enough. Interestingly enough, the kit lens even has firmware that you can update. I have successfully used my Canon glass with it using a Simga MC-11 adapter. The Canon 17-40mm f4L and Canon 70-200 f2.8L focused quickly. My Sigma 8-16mm lens focused well, though it's meant for APS-C sensors. Oddly enough my Canon 50mm 1.4 paired with the A7iii and Sigma MC-11 takes about a minute or two before the aperature control is functional but once it kicks in, this combo turns night into day. I also use a 35mm 1.8 OSS Sony lens that I used with my a5100 and even though it puts it into APS-C mode which sacrifices quality, it's still good enough.

I can even use my Canon 580ex ii successfully with this (manual mode/no HSS) with a Fomex flash trigger.

The reason I bought this however was for video. 4k is stunning, though I have to say, plan for paying a but extra for a UHS-II card to get it to work. The S&Q setting is nice for switching over to slow-mo very quickly.

The menu system is a bit much but at least it includes a lot of features that are missing with Canon. Battery performance is quite incredible.

Overall, I can't see why this camera wouldn't satisfy most pros unless they work in a harsh environment in which case, the weather sealing probably won't be enough. The compact size of it though is nice when you don't want to draw attention.

Read more

This camera has changed the GAME! I am so incredibly impressed with this quality of the photos it takes. Even with the kit lens, I’m so impressed! I had bought a brand new Canon Rebel T7 and put a 50 mm & 85 mm lens on it and this camera with the KIT LENS blows that camera and prime lenses out of the water! I love this camera so much. It’s the best purchase I’ve ever made! The touch focusing feature is awesome. The auto ISO is incredible. The shutter sound sounds so boujee (LOL) when I snap a picture with this camera, I just feel like a professional! I’m trying to start a photography business and practicing with this camera has made such a difference! If you were wanting to get in Photography - spend the money. It is well worth it.

Update: I had my 2nd shoot with the camera yesterday. I am completely blown away by the difference in the photos that this camera takes versus the DSLR Canon camera that I had. I shot these with a 35 mm prime lens and just WOW! I am still new at this but I am so thankful I made the purchase. If you are starting Photography, whether it’s a hobby or you want to go pro, this camera is the way to go! I am a Sony gal for life now!
Very nice camera

Was on a Canon RP camera before deciding to upgrade. Was nervous at first because of the fear of the item coming in broken. When I tell you, that I am beyond impressed with this Camera. From how well it functions, to the picture quality is superb, the image stabilization is top tier. The size is amazing too fitting perfectly on my hand. And above all else, how easy it is to handle. The battery life is also another plus, being able to shoot at least around 710 pictures in one charge. Definitely recommend!

Truly a steal. I’ve been skeptical in the past buying used equipment, but this easily saved me hundreds with no decrease in product quality. It came essentially brand new and has been able to produce stunning photos out of nothing. I took it outside and quickly discovered two little hairs on the sensor, which I’m led to believe is why the original seller let it go. No issue to me, a $20 cleaning kit got rid of it. The photos it did appear in don’t at all feel ruined as I’ll just edit them out. Definitely my favorite purchase I’ve made, and I’d recommend it to anyone looking to make an equipment jump without spending an arm and leg. The colors are just great. Love it.
Excellent camera with amazing image quality. Autofocus is fast, low-light performance is great, and it’s perfect for photography. Very happy with this purchase.

I've had this camera for about 10 months now and it is probably the worst photographic decision I have ever made. I only wish I could have returned it while I had the chance.

Let me start of by saying I've been a professional photographer for 15 years and mostly photograph models in a studio setting or outdoors. I use natural light and also strobes. I started with Nikon, went to a Canon 5dmkii, have had other canons and also 3 fuji x series cameras

Firstly, what kind of company ships a $2000 camera without a battery charger? I get it, it can plug into your computer to charge or car adapter via USB-C. But that means more wear and tear on the USB port which will eventually be loose and then have issues. When I get home I prefer to take my battery out and put it on the charger which will tell me when its charged.

Second. I read all the reviews who talked about the poor color science and then all the videos who said all the things you had to do to fix it. I never realized how bad it actually is. When I would view my photos from my canon in camera raw or capture one I was only one click away from getting an accurate representation of what I had originally seen. Sony has its own version of Capture One (I also use the pro version) and the images look like garbage from the moment they appear on the screen. they even look worse then what you get in Lightroom.

The next issue is the awful menus. Do I need to be the next person to complain about the menus? ISO is on page 9 of the menu. White Balance on page 12. Sure, you can set a custom quick menu, but I would have expected updates to make it better.

Another thing I was kind of surprised about were the files sizes. I guess I kind of thought they would be like my Canon where a 24 megapixel image had a raw file of 24 megabytes. I did not expect the raw files to be double that. a typical raw file on the Sony is about 48 megabytes, and the matching jpeg is 12 MB.

I just can't stand shooting with this camera and the struggle of working on the images. Luckily I'm not too heavily invested in the Sony ecosystem so I can change back to Canon or even Fuji

reviews.review_title: A Smooth Transition from Fujifilm X-T3
reviews.review_description:
The Sony A7III with the 28-70mm f/3.5-5.6 kit lens has been a great transition for me from the Fujifilm X-T3. The first thing I noticed was how much simpler and more intuitive the menus and button layout are—getting used to it was effortless. While I do miss the X-T3’s 10-bit video capabilities, the full-frame experience is on another level in terms of depth and low-light performance.

One of the most surprising aspects has been the battery life—it’s incredibly good. I initially thought about getting a spare battery, but for someone like me who isn’t doing heavy professional work, it doesn’t feel essential.

The kit lens is decent for a beginner setup, offering good sharpness and versatility, but I can already tell it will be my first upgrade. I find myself needing a lens with a wider aperture for better low-light performance. So, the A7III feels like a solid upgrade.

title: Nikon D5100 16.2MP Digital SLR Camera & 18-55mm VR Lens
description: Let your creativity get better with the Nikon D5100 DSLR Kit that comes with a DX lens. The High Dynamic Range of this camera with lens lets you shoot extreme contrasts with stunning clarity by combining two exposures to give you a wider dynamic range. With a three-inch 921,000-dot Vari-angle LCD, you can capture shots from any angle and even view playback in rich detail on the Nikon D5100 DSLR Kit. This Digital SLR features an Effects mode that gives you a variety of special effects like Night Vision, High/Low Key, Miniature Effect, and Color Sketch for shooting your very own full HD D-Movie. Exceptional sound-recording and auto-focus flaunted by the Nikon D5100 DSLR Kit only make your movie better. The built-in DX-format CMOS sensor (with a wide ISO range) and EXPEED 2 engine let you use this camera with lens to capture moving objects with utmost clarity and minimal noise even in low-light conditions.

reviews.review_description: Great camera, bought used but when it arrived it looked brand new.

I absolutely love this camera! The picture quality is amazing, the colors look beautiful, and it’s very easy to use. It’s lightweight, compact, and perfect for taking high-quality photos and videos. I actually love this camera. Its appearance is nice and compact, it's strap that it comes with held up so far. Its auto focus is actually pretty good for the price this camera goes for! The settings are pretty simple and straightforward. It's definitely a budget option for someone starting out like me but actually nice. The battery life is LONG, I've only had to charge it like two or three times since I got it. I think I have taken it on a few trips by now.

Now I admit a lot of photos I had taken the first few times after I got it, were pretty blurry but after figuring out how to do the auto focus (half press the shutter button, fully pressing down after the green outlined rectangle appears), photos were not blurry.

The durability of the camera seems pretty good in all honesty.

Overall, I heavily recommend this for any beginner photographers out there like me who can't just throw out a bunch of money on a digital camera. I wouldn't say this camera is good for a while, like to use for professional photos but it's a start for sure!

Really great digi for cheap! I was initially a little skeptical about buying since I wanted the photos to be high-quality and still have that nostalgic feel to them, but this camera does it all! It's simple to change the temperature settings and easy to understand for someone who never uses cameras except for the one on my phone. Videos are also fairly good quality; the camera is extremely shaky, though, so make sure you're either okay with that or you get a hand-held stabilizer.

I bought it for a concert, and it fulfilled my every wish! Just be warned, the item DOES NOT come with an SD card; you'll have to buy it separately, but I got a 64gb one that fits a TON of photos on here. reviews.review_title: Kodak FZ-55 PixPro Camera - Black version
reviews.review_description:

This one only charges the battery internally, unless you buy an external charger, which I would highly recommend one always have an external charger for extra/spare batteries for your camera! Also didn't like you only access the manual by reading or downloading on-line. What is wrong with manufacturers today? They SHOULD supply manuals with their products, no matter what it is. Not have the end user go hunting for it, and many times when I went seeking a manual for a product I bought, if the manufacturer may have discontinued the item, they tend to remove the manual, and now it's no longer available to access, even though you may have bought the item new, no manual with it is just dumb and lazy on their part. If I am printing it on paper, then they sure didn't save any trees, and maybe I had to print it several times before I got the fomatting right to put it in a notebook or folder for future reference, wasting paper and more trees. Manufactures take notice, you ARE NOT doing the trees or the end user any favor by EXCLUDING manuals from your products!

LIKES:

Easy to use, but then I have been accustomed to digital cameras for a very long time, so I can navigate around them very easily, and I found this one very easy to navigateonce I checked out all the buttons and what they did. Has a nice LCD screen for viewing your photo's after taking the shots, one thing I don't quite understand is the "slideshow", you get 3 options to pick from #1, #2 or #3, #1 just shows the basic snapshot and really does nothing. #2 will do some type of effect, as does #3, but to me, they make no rhyme or reason for even being there at all.

They don't copy to your computer when transferring the photo's to your computer, you'd have to use another program, like some kind of video editor to create a slide show with similar or like effects. And the issue is, it's NOT a slide show of the photo's in the camera or on the SD Card, it only affects the ONE PHOTO you're viewing, so it's not a slideshow by any means. When I selected it to see what it did, it just affected the one photo I was viewing, I had expected to see a slideshow of ALL the photo's I had taken or be allowed to select a specific number to create a slideshow that could be saved as a video exported file from the camera, but none of that is possible. The photos are good, and I have attached a few here to show the cameras' capability in low light conditions, the two photo's of the same kitten (Cordellia-001/-002) are indoors in low light, the older cat (Apollo), taken outside is nearing sunset. Even with the Dislikes and the few faults it has, I can recommend the camera, it seems to take nice photographs, I haven't tried videos as yet, I have some projects in mind for that for YouTube later on. reviews.review_title: A fantastic way to get into Full Frame without breaking the bank!
reviews.review_description:
Finally, after waiting almost 20 years to jump into Full Frame, I elected to pull the trigger on the Canon RP. I've been shooting with various Micro 4/3, Fujifilm, and Canon EOS gear - love them all. But as I mentioned, I was always intrigued by Full Frame, but due top the high costs and size involved with that system, I deferred. After seeing the great deal for the RP and the 24-105 kit lens, I knew that this was the time.

OK - right off the bat, the RP is a wonderful camera - well-built, yet very light and smallish. It's a delight to hold in the hand, and you have a variety of options. Now keep in mind, my style of photography involves scenic, architectural, portraits, and landscapes - all of which this RP handles quite well. If you're a fast moving sports enthusiast, or a birds-in-flight aficionado, then forget about this camera.

I ordered mine with the RF 24-105 kit lens (not the L version) as part of a package deal and considering the cost vs performance ratio, this is a superb package price for the kit.

The kit lens is fairly good, but like most kit lenses (but not all), the edges are a bit soft and fuzzy. You can get around some of that by setting the camera to an aperture of 8 and above. The center areas are quite sharp. The 24-105 MM range is superb and should endear itself to most photographers.

I'd like to start saving for the F4L version of this lens to provide greater clarity across the frame - but in the meantime, this kit lens is really ideal.

So overall, considering the price of this kid, the fact that it's full frame, includes a nice kit lens that would cost $400 separately, you can't go wrong here.

reviews.review_title: The perfect balance of beautiful video and beautiful photos
reviews.review_description:
I previously had a Canon T3i and I absolutely loved that thing. It was amazing the results that camera could do for its time and I will always think it's one of the best budget cameras ever made. However, I've recently gotten more into video and that is one thing the T3i wasn't meeting my needs for. It was missing so many features like autofocus and modern video resolutions and frame rates.

Therefore, my search for a new camera began. I seriously debated nearly every camera in this price range from every manufacturer. Sony, Fujifilm, Panasonic, you name it. However, it seemed like they all had one fatal flaw to them. Sony with their weird coloring, Fujifilm with the overheating issues, Panasonic with the awful autofocus. Some were better at photos, some were better at video. However, I needed something that would do great with both, as I wanted this to be something I could shoot professional portraits with but also shoot vlogs. At the end of the day, all signs pointed to this camera, and I'm so glad this is the one I chose.

I'm not a super-advanced user, however, I do think I've moved past the beginner stage of photography and videography. I think this camera really fits me perfectly as I'm not incredibly overwhelmed with options and features that I don't know how to use, but it still has a ton of capability that allows me to learn more about photography and videography. I've also just been using the 24-105 kit lens that comes with this bundle on Amazon.

The video on this is amazing. HUGE step up from the T3i. The face detecting autofocus works great and nearly all of my shots are perfectly in focus unless it's super dark which it has a little more of a struggle with but obviously any camera would. I was a little hesitant about the fairly disabled 4k capability with this camera due (disabled dual pixel AF, crop factor, 30 min time limit, 24 fps max) especially since other cameras in the price range have a more robust 4k capability. However, I've found that 1080p meets my needs just fine and looks absolutely gorgeous. It's also much more friendly on the file size and processing in video editing.

The photo capability has shocked me even more than the video. I knew this would obviously be a great camera for photos, but I didn't realize what a step up from my T3i it would be. I honestly thought my T3i photos would look just about as good as this camera since the T3i does admittedly take amazing photos. However, this blows it out of the water. The autofocus on this is SO much better. With the T3i, fast moving subjects were nearly impossible to get in focus. This does so much better. The full-frame sensor on this camera makes a huge difference too. The low light performance is so much better and the size of these photos is insane. You can zoom in to the photos so much and it's still amazingly clear.

As for the body of the camera itself, it feels incredibly well made. Grabbing my T3i now feels like a cheap plastic toy compared to this thing. It feels very solid and durable. The grip on the camera is incredibly easy and comfortable to hold.

The only negative thing I've encountered so far is the kit lens that comes with this bundle doesn't have a physical switch between autofocus and manual focus. You have to go into the camera settings to switch between them. I don't find myself doing this very often as the autofocus is amazing but when I do need manual focus it's a little bit of an inconvenience.

Overall, it's an amazing camera and I'm very happy that I went with this one.

Great lower end camera, my only beef so far is the poor packaging. The box is almost all air, and there are no packing peanuts or anything to cushion this thing or protect it from the ups drivers. Camera came wrapped in a foil that most companies wrap a 10 dollar remote control or phone charger in, not a 1000 dollar camera.
