I started a photography business and I've been using my Canon Rebel T1i for the past year. It's been a great camera and I love it, but now that I'm starting to do more weddings, I needed a more semi-professional camera to keep up with the pace and strain of your average wedding. I had been looking to get the 50D for some time and after I was paid for a wedding and the 60D was announced (looks like Canon is making the XXD line more consumer oriented), I knew it was time to get the 50D.

Having come from using the T1i, the first thing I had to get used to was all the buttons. Seriously, there are more buttons on the 50D because parameters like meter, white balance, etc. have their own button rather than having to go through menus like on the T1i. But this makes adjustments much faster, since there are less menus to dig into. And the adjustment wheel on the back of the camera is awesome, again because it makes adjustments quick. I no longer have to press a button to adjust exposure compensation, I can just use the wheel on the back.

The camera is also quieter than the T1i. Shutter and mirror noise from the 50D are noticeably quieter than the T1i. This will help greatly with the weddings I'll be shooting and with more photojournalistic shoots.

Everything else about the camera is a step up from the T1i. Just a few things I really like are the faster burst rate (6 fps sounds like a machine gun) and having all the focus points be cross type, which aids greatly in low light focusing (espcially with a fast prime, like my 85mm f/1.8). All this will help me capture weddings much better.

The only drawback is that the 50D with a grip (I bought an Opteka) is quite big and heavy. The T1i with a battery grip felt pretty hefty, but the 50D with a grip feels like I'm carrying around a brick. I'm sure over time I'll get used to the weight, but for now I usually think twice about carrying the 50D around. It does help a lot to get a padded shoulder strap (I found one by Targus that was only $10).

As I continue to grow my photography business, I have confidence now tackling more jobs with the 50D compared to just having the T1i. I look forward to really putting the camera through its paces.

There are already a lot of detailed reviews about the 50D. With that in mind I'll keep this brief. My background: I'm an amature with a lot of SLR experience. I started taking photography classes in high school...back when there were only film SLRs!. Photojournalism was also my major for one year in college. And since it's been an on and off hobby of mine. I have a Canon SD 700 IS but this 50D was my first DSLR.

Maybe it's because I work long hours and I'm not outside during the day, but most of my 50D photos so far have been in the late afternoon or evenings, or indoors. As such I've used ISO 1600 quite a bit. The images to my eye look fantastic! Within the menu system there are High ISO Noise Reduction and Long Exposure Noise Reduection options that can be turned on/off as needed.

If one is to compare image quality of the 50D to the 40D, I think it's interesting to remember the 50D takes larger, higher resolution images. In other words, the 50D images start out with more detail. And from the research I did it appears the 50D's images can be sharpened and still have more detail than the 40D. There are good explanations of this on the web. Amazon censored out the article links I included but if you contact me I'd be happy to provide them.

Anyway, suffices to say I'm very happy with my 50D's IQ so far. I also like it's super fast and accurate focusing! I haven't used Live View very much but that feature has had its useful moments. The LCD screen is gorgeous! And the controls and menus are easy to navigate. To be honest, they were a bit overwhelming the first couple days but then quickly became second nature. I also bought Jeff Revell's Canon 50D: From Snapshots to Great Shots. It's a "beginner" type book IMO, but still a good intro to this camera and a primer of DSLR basics if you're transitioning from film to digital like I was.

I bought the 50D body only from Amazon and got the Canon EF 50mm f1.4 USM Standard & Medium Telephoto Lens for Canon SLR Cameras from Adorama; they matched the price and they've been very easy to work with. OK that's enough from me! If you happen to have any questions let me know, I'll try to answer best I can. Cheers!

reviews.review_title: Better Than I Thought It would Be
reviews.review_description:
This is my first Canon SLR in a very long while, and was unsure of the move from Nikon, but decided to check it out. Overall this is a nice camera. Noise level is indeed more than Nikon, my old D90 did some beautiful shots at high ISO where the 50D strugles. I would not go any higher than ISO 800 or so with this camera. Thing is I never do, so this is fine for me, but might be a problem for some.

The button layout I would say could use some work. Nikon I would give a major advantage here as all there buttons are easy to get to and navigate, where the Canon I have to look and fumble around to find even the basic stuff. I admit allot of this has to do with me needing to needing to know the camera better and will improve over time, but the D90 I picked up in like 20 min of using. Don't get me wrong, I don't think Canon's is bad, but could use some more work is all.

The camera is fast and starts up almost before I know I want to turn it on. (almost)Though I do feel Canon do need to add more AF points the nine it has seems to do the job well, even when following moving objects it keeps right up with it without a hint of wanting to slow down. Just make sure your memory card can keep up with this camera when your shutter is on auto fire. Like some reviews have stated, I have noticed the tracking does tend to want to go to brighter areas in the frame. This has not been a big issue with me, but is something you might want to watch for.

Another thing I really like is the solid build. It feels like a tank and knowing that metal and weather seal will keep this running long after I should of stopped shooting and had put it away. Nothing on this camera feels weak.

I was worried about soft images, though it is not a problem for this camera. Yes, if your using lower price glass you may see some softness, but this is not the camera doing it. With the 28-135 lens I got some pretty sharp shots with it and think its a good basic Lens, Yes my Primes (I like my primes) do better, but did enjoy using the lens on this camera for simple walks when I only wanted one lens with me and nothing else. Also I have noticed that this camera has no image overlay or multiple exposure settings. These are common on Nikon cameras, even there cheaper models, and I find it upsetting that there not on this camera. Yes you can do these in photoshop, having CS4 this is not a problem, but I prefer to do things in camera and only use PS for minor tweaks and adjustments. Canon really needs to add these.

At the price right now I would have to say this camera is a steal and a better deal over the 7D which really does not add much. I might take a stronger look after a price drop or two but right now this is a much better deal and I think anyone looking for a good buy on a SLR built as strong and performs as fast and accurate would be happy with buying the 50D.

The nespresso capsule portafilter works well with original capsules only. The easily interchangeable K-cup single cup coffee and several cup filter coffee side works great. reviews.review_title: Poor Nespresso pod adapter and press. Everything else seems good.
reviews.review_description:
This was basically the only option for nespresso, keurig, ground coffee, and frothing in one footprint. It does some things well and other things...probably unacceptable.

First the good: there are 3 temperature levels for "coffee" pours (keurig and ground), and the highest level is considerably hotter than anything my old keurig cafe+ or instat dual pod makers could produce. It takes about 30 seconds longer to first pour from the instant machine, but that instant machine was lightning quick. It's about on par with the keurig to first pour. If you are frothing milk with your drink (cappuccino or latte), it's actually much quicker to first pour than the keurig cafe+ was. The Chefman froths the milk quicker and warmer.

I had to return my first device. It arrived with a loose water sensor, and the cap of it went flying out of the box when I pulled the water reservoir out of the box. I couldn't find the clear plastic cap, and the device would not work without it in place. So there may be quality control issues there.

The frother is considerably noisier than either the keurig or the standalone frothers that I have used (both are electric). Otherwise, the machine is reasonably quiet.

I haven't tested the ground coffee or ground espresso, but I have run plenty of keurig and nespresso pods through it. The keurig pours work well. reasonably fast and very hot (if you set it to be hot). It will pour up to 12oz on the coffee/keurig side and (supposedly) 8oz on the espresso side.

Now for the bad and the reason for the 3 stars: the nespresso adapter and press is borderline unusable. First of all, you have to manually press the nespresso pod into the adapter, then twist on the top (the top is supposed to the pressing down for you). Even after doing that, the device does not push enough water through the pod and out of the adapter. If you setup a 2oz pour, you might get 1.5oz. Basically, I have to make everything a "double" to get enough drinkable product, and there's always a bit of a mess with excess water at the top of the adapter when I remove it. There is also a drainage system built into the device, so nothing spills on the counter, but I also have to clean that excess water out of the drain tray. This cannot be working as intended.

The first quirk is that it will always overheat if you use the steamer first, so you need to run a single shot somehow. All in all, so far, I like this machine a lot. It's functional and pretty. I've been using a high end single group brewer and am enjoying the simplicity of a super auto. reviews.review_title: Honest review and it’s very disappointing to write.
reviews.review_description:
I’ll start by saying that I am a coffee addict. I have entirely to many appliances and manual devises for making coffee and espresso drinks.

This machine was appealing due to variety and price point. There are far more negatives than positives in this review. I used for more than a week before leaving this review.

Cons:

- This machines self cleans and it does it constantly. If you’re wanting to make more than a couple beverages before filling the small water reservoir then look elsewhere. It cleans itself when it starts up, while it’s sitting idle, and when it goes to sleep. I have made all the cleaning intervals as long as possible and it still cleans over and over.

- The water reservoir is 3 times smaller than it should be for the level of self cleaning.

- I went through 5-7 espresso pours to see if the quality would increase as the manual says. I changed the grind setting during and after and the espresso is still very weak. The pucks are not pucks when discharged, they are just balls of grind goo. It doesn’t press hard enough.

- The milk system requires you to have a cup and a clean cup of water nearby at all times. It constantly runs a clean cycle on the milk so you can’t just leave it out for a few hours between cups on a weekend morning.

- The touchscreen isn’t very responsive. Hit it 4-5 times and it might stop or go backward in options.

- The settings are all in ML so have a conversion chart handy for our US cup measurements.

- The waste water reservoir needs to emptied multiple times a day just like the water needs filled multiple times a day.

- If you enter a descale phase while making an espresso separately to add to a latte, it will just start to descale and ruin your drink. You then have to go through the whole descale process before you get your next drink. This is very unfortunate when you’re in a morning rush to get to work.

Pros:

The drinks are hot.

I was super excited for this machine and the reviews, while limited on Amazon were pretty good. I was left very disappointed and returning the unit because it doesn’t function properly as it should and the quality of drinks is very low compared to others I have and use frequently.

Read more

To start out, I was exited to receive it. Item was packaged well.

It was easy to unpack and a few steps was to setup the machine.

This coffee machine is absolutely unique, there isn't anything else out there. I did my research.

When you turn it on, put water in, it does a self cleaning. Then you have the selections for many different type of coffees. Latte, cappuccino, regular, espresso, and on. You can have different users and have different types of coffee on each user. Each coffee is adjustable in the setting, such as temperature of the water, milk, how much coffee do you want in volume, how strong you want to coffee to be and so on. It's fantastic.

It grinds up the coffee beans, sucks up the milk from a cup you place next to it to make the latte, it steams the coffee. It makes the layers like the real cappuccino as it shows in the pictures.

Fully automated. It will tell you when you have to empty the ground coffee trash bin.

When you turn it off, it does an automatic cleaning. You'll put some clean water in a cup for the milk straw, which it will be sucked up and cleaned inside out. You won't ever have to clean the inside. It does it automatically.

Not to mention, this machine looks high tech, elegant and it will definitely bring the attention to your guests and everyone in the house.

This coffee maker is smart and had a lot of attention to every detail put in.

I hardly ever leave a review, but this, I highly recommend this product even it is high priced.

reviews.review_title: Very easy to use, small water tank, multiple issues - 2 month update
reviews.review_description:
Zulay Magia Super Automatic Coffee Espresso Machine

**Update 9/20/2023** I've been using the machine now for about 2 months and wanted to provide an update. First, you can edit your custom drink after you set it, so I wanted to correct that. The constant auto cleaning is still annoying. There is a lot of coffee waste. In 2 months, I was able to fill up a standard size ziplock of unused coffee grinds. This is caused by several reason.

1. Coffee grinds get in and all over the brewing unit inside. Guessing when it's grinding, there isn't a good seal between grinder and brewing unit. So make sure you pull it out about once a week to shake it out.

2. There is a small tray below brewing unit that catches grounds from some part of the process. This doesn't do a good job at catching the grounds as it builds up behind the tray.

3. The unit will randomly stop making coffee right after it grinds the beans and presses the coffee. No errors, no reason, you hear it go through it's process of pressing the coffee, then it just stops and dumps the grounds in to the coffee ground box. This has happened several times in the last two months.

**Original review**

It works great and is simple to use. The espresso taste just as good when I manually make it on a standard espresso machine. It's menu has multiple coffee types which are all one press and it's all handled for you. From grinding the beans, pressing the coffee, and adding the milk/foam all in one unit. There is also another menu to make more premium drinks like White Chocolate mocha. It will list the ingredients you need and the amounts and after you add the extra ingredients it will start making the drink.

There are multiple profiles you can choose to setup up different custom coffee setups per user. You can't rename the profiles, they are just user1, user2, etc... You also can't customize a coffee type more than once. So if you wanted to created different sizes of a drink, you have to use different user profiles. You also cannot edit your custom drink after you set it. You have to delete and recreate it.

Cleaning the machine is pretty simple and straight forward. It does an automatic flush of the funnel and frother unit on startup and shutdown. However, I feel that's too much and just waste the limited water in your bin. I get running the cleaning on shutdown, but I don't see the need for it to also run on startup. While there is a cleaning setting, there is no setting that lets you turn off automatic cleaning. It also alerts you when to clean the internal components, like empty the coffee grind bin. Everything about the unit is easy to clean and maintain.

The water tank is placed on the back of the unit. This will cause problems for those with counters that are not deep. The unit itself already will take up most of the counter depth because its so big. So you may have to keep pulling your unit out just to get the water tank off and out to fill up. This will be frequent unless you only drink the 2oz /4oz espresso drinks only. But even then, with all the cleaning it does, you'll still find yourself filling the tank frequently. Personally, I think they should have just made it wider than deeper. A side water tank would have held more volume and would have been more convenient to refill.

The quality of the build of the machine is nothing to be excited about. It's made of all plastic and kind of makes it look cheap. Internal components are mostly plastic as well. However, it's all pretty sturdy.

For roughly $800 out the door, it's just lacking. It's like they've done just enough but didn't polish it out. I would peg this more in the $500 line just due to its automation as I'm sure there is complexity there. But outside of that, it's disappointing for having paid this much.

Read more

My only gripe is the amount if wasted coffee when grinding beans. I pull enough ground coffee out of the machine when cleaning to fill a sandwich bag. I thought I was doing something wrong but people seem to always have this issue. It also needs descaled pretty often. Besides that I love it!

UPDATES

Had to update and drop a star since I just remembered I had a review out there. Here are my additional gripes:

The cake pan is always filled with liquid and it’s impossible for me to get it to the point where it isn’t. I followed all troubleshooting steps and it still gets filled.

The milk frother was hit or miss on working well and just recently stopped working all together.

It was a nice two year run but I don’t feel that I got my moneys worth.

Since I struggled with individual customization for a while (till I figured it out) - I thought I should do a step by step on how to customize coffee for each user in the family. You can follow it through with pictures added to review.

1) On the main screen - touch the "User" icon on the top left (Picture 1)

2) You will see a 10 user screen (BTW - You can edit names of each user by selecting that user and touching the name "user1" on the top center) - Here you touch "+" sign at the bottom left to pick the coffee style you want to customize for this user (Picture 2)

3) Select the coffee you want to customize - using "Latte" as an example here (Picture 3)

4) On return - you will see "Latte" added to "user1" (Picture 4)

5) Now is when it gets strange - when you touch "Latte" icon - it will start making "Latte" with default recipe (have a cup under drip ready before touching "Latte" icon!!)

6) WHILE it is brewing Latte for you - it will display the "Brewing" screen - bottom left of that screen you see three bars (Picture 5) - touch on it and the customization screen pops up (Picture 6)

7) Adjust your recipe to what you desire and touch "return". Now your recipe is stored in your user profile for FUTURE brews when brewed from your user profile.

The strange/weird thing is that it starts brewing coffee before you can customize - so you are technically customizing FUTURE brews...

Now some pros/cons:

Pros:

1) The machine looks beautiful

2) A large number of recipes

3) Automatic functionality is super impressive

4) Customization ability is amazing - one can adjust coffee, temperature, time (assume that translates to volume) of hot milk, time for foam, and liquid volume for coffee.

5) User profile storing is even more impressive for a machine in this price-range (it was frustrating while I was trying to figure it out though!)

6) Quality of coffee produced is excellent (See picture 7) - foam quality is good, temperature is good (and can be adjusted).

7) Support is VERY responsive to email contact. Couple of my questions were answered in matter of hours.

(Edit: sorry - pictures seem to be in some random order on posting)

Cons:

1) Screen stays on as long as machine is plugged into the wall (it does go into a "screensaver" display) - no switch to turn it off. I worry about screen burn-in and also light pollution at night. Power usage is less than 10 watts while machine is off but screen is on. (I put it on a smart plug and I turn it off after making coffee via Alexa/Google).

2) Water container is in the back and needs to be lifted "up" - which means this unit can NOT be under a cabinet. You would need approximately the height of the machine clear above it to take out and refill container.

3) The dispensed coffee puck container is on the side - so again - you need to keep the right side of the machine clear. Only drip tray can be removed from the front. My DeLonghi machine prior to this had everything removable from the front.

4) Everything is through the screen - that could end up being a single point of failure - not quite like mostly mechanical coffee maker I had before.

5) In my case - dispensed pucks are non-existent (it looks like a slushy liquid) - See picture 8 - I am going to reach out to them to find out if this is something that will be fixed over time or if I need to change some settings (will update review when resolved).

Taking 1 point away for above items.

For now - I am happy with it (24 hours so far). Only unknown is how robust it is and how long it would last. I will come back and update review periodically.

Warranty is for 1 year - I am thinking I will get extended warranty from Asurion on Amazon (can buy it within 30 days after purchase).

reviews.review_title: Looks Great, Works Great, Tastes Great
reviews.review_description:
I got this coffee maker a little over 2 years ago, mainly because of its aesthetics, specifically the design and layout were visually pleasing to me compared to other coffee makers. Also all my appliances are black and stainless.

On the two cup setting, it takes about 6 minutes to brew. When it's done the coffee is really hot, and I have to wait about 5 minutes before drinking it, or drop in an ice cube and I can start drinking in about 30 seconds to a minute.

I found a combination of things with this coffee maker that turns a good cup of coffee into a great one. The ninja branded measuring spoon that comes with it is more important than you might think. They've literally hit the nail on the head regarding the exact amount of coffee grounds that should be used. It's very simple, one flat scoop for every standard size cup of coffee you want, and remember the word flat. Also there's markers on the water tank so scoops and water match up.

I personally found if I use a flat scoop of coffee grounds, not letting the coffee grounds be higher than that, it tastes perfect every time for me. So I would say that's a huge key to a great cup of coffee on this device.

Next up, paper filters improved the taste significantly! The goldish mesh metal filter that comes in the box does not filter out all the coffee grounds. I even tried other brands of metal filters to see if they improved that, but it didn't. You will likely have some coffee grounds in the bottom of your coffee cup if you stick with the included metal reusable filter.

At first I didn't think it was very many coffee grounds, but then one day I immediately poured the coffee into a glass after brewing it. Then I held the glass above my head and shined a flashlight at the bottom, and there were a lot more grounds that I saw that way, than when I was getting close to finishing a cup of coffee. Meaning, I was likely swallowing a lot of grounds and would have never known that.

So I stopped using the Ninja metal filter and started buying and trying #4 cone paper filters and that did 4 things. 1. No more coffee grounds in my coffee cup. 2. No more upset stomach after drinking coffee. 3. The oily stuff that kind of floated to the top of the coffee was gone. 4. The taste of the coffee significantly improved.

I would strongly suggest trying a box of paper filters to see if it improves the taste for you.

Do not attempt to use a paper filter and the mesh filter at the same time. I tried that once and it significantly reduces the flow of the coffee out of the filter area. This causes the water to build up in that filter area and overflow from there on to your countertop.

In closing, this is a good coffee maker, but if you use flat scoops, a good brand of paper filters, and purified water, I think those might be the keys to turning a good cup of coffee into a great one.

Other reviews were mildly critical of the "sneak a cup" functionality, but I've found it on par with that of my last two coffee makers (Krups and Cuisinart). Yes, a couple of drops of coffee will still splash on the hot plate while you pull the carafe out, but I've never used or seen a pot yet that didn't do that, and the spring mechanism on this carafe is at least as robust as any I've seen on other coffee makers.

Where this pot really shines is in the clear, detachable water reservoir. That obviously offers you the (completely?) unique option of detaching the tank to fill it over the sink before brewing, which I've done a few times and anticipated doing regularly. Frankly, however, I find it unnecessary because the reservoir itself provides an unusually large opening/target for pouring directly from my filtered water pitcher.

But there are other benefits to the reservoir design, including the fact that it allows you to easily monitor the conditions inside . . . i.e., when the moist environment inevitably leads to mildew, you will know it (and, because the reservoir is transparent to any ambient sunlight, mold/mildew should theoretically take longer to manifest in many kitchens.) More importantly, you'll be able to easily clean the reservoir in a sink of hot soapy water (with a little bleach) without repeated electric cleaning and rinse cycles for the whole brewer, followed by awkward attempts to wipe the nooks and crannies of the integral, typically black reservoir with a white paper towel to see if any undesirable residues remain.

But perhaps the greatest advantage of this design is in what it will save you if you should *ahem* forget to put your carafe in place before you hit "brew." I've only done this twice in my life but, ironically, both times occurred within the last six weeks: once with my last Krups pot and once with this new Ninja. (Put aside for the moment what such forgetfulness might be saying about me.:-) At the very least, I gained valuable, first-hand experience in how the Ninja's design saved my a$$ while the typical integral design on the Krups resulted in a ruined coffee maker, which prompted my purchase of the Ninja in the first place.)

When you fail to put the carafe under the filter spout on a coffee maker that offers the increasingly ubiquitous "sneak a cup" feature, the spring mechanism on the filter holder is never engaged and the water that's dripping down over your grinds to make coffee is never given proper egress below. So your mistake may go unnoticed for quite some time since you won't hear the kind of gushing and sizzling sound that an older model without the sneak a cup feature would produce when dripping coffee is merrily dispensing and burning on the naked hotplate below. Instead, the water stays in the filter holder, eventually having nowhere to go but over the sides, which, on the vast majority of drip coffee makers, means that the brewed coffee--complete with floating grinds--will spill over and back into the reservoir itself. That is exactly what happened to my Krups, and, despite hours of repeated cleaning cycles and an aborted effort to dismantle the innards, I realized the pot was shot (no pun intended) and would never process water properly through its (clogged) pump pathway again.

Enter the Ninja. After making delicious coffee for a week or so, I, once again, got distracted by something (probably my Yorkie yapping to get out for a morning pee) and neglected to actually seat the carafe on the coffee maker before hitting brew. When I got back in, I noticed the problem just before the brewing coffee was about to overflow the filter holder. The difference was, even had I been a bit later, I would have only had to deal with a messy countertop and not a ruined $80+ coffee maker. In other words, if the Ninja coffee filter overflows, the brewed coffee will NOT go back into the reservoir because the latter is physically higher and isolated from the former in a way that would not permit that. So, should you repeat my negligence, you will hear coffee suddenly dripping on your hotplate and counter top, but you won't have to buy a new coffee maker.

The only "negative" to the pot is that the carafe lid does not flip up via the common thumb depression above the handle. You have to slide/turn it to remove, which is more easily done with two hands. But this is a very, very minor ding in my view and not worth deducting a star for an otherwise very well-designed, highly practical, and elegant-looking appliance.

reviews.review_title: Great coffee maker with all the features I need
reviews.review_description:
I've been using this coffee maker every day for over a month, and I have zero complaints. The coffee comes out consistently great, and since I usually brew 4 cups, the Small Batch setting has been perfect.

I use disposable paper filters instead of the included reusable one because it's more convenient for me to just throw them away after brewing. Cleanup is quick and easy.

I've also tested the Keep Warm and Delay Brew features, and both work exactly as expected. The coffee stays at a good temperature without tasting burnt, and the scheduled brewing has been reliable every time.

Overall, it's been a fantastic coffee maker with no issues, and I'd definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a dependable machine that consistently makes great-tasting coffee.

reviews.review_title: Actually does improve the flavor of coffee compared to others. Capable, but not super well designed
reviews.review_description:
UPDATE: For our second brew, I ran it on "Classic" instead of "Rich". I really was a significantly superior brew. It tasted good with the old machine, but really fine with this one. Now after over a week of use- it's a consistent result every day, and a cup of coffee is, indeed, superior with this machine and all else being equal.

I found another issue, though. There's a gap between the back of the carafe lid and the handle. Steam escapes there, and it gets very hot. I have fairly large hands and I tend to put my thumb there. I have gotten burned a couple of times. It's painful but not long lasting. It's not the steam alone, but the fact that the little bit of steam heats the material for the entire brew time plus serving time. Cleaning is getting burdensome. The carafe needs a re-design.

I got this to replace (?) a very basic Mr. Coffee that is about 5 years old, that is one of my favorite examples of design. It's as simple as can be: an on/off switch and a carafe that is capacious and very easy and fast to clean. It has very few right angle areas that would make it hard to clean. (They have changed the design since we bought it, and not for the better.) It still works.

This Ninja is nice, and the filter basket will barely sit on the scale while I weigh the grounds into it, but it's going to tip over, and often. Once the coffee is made, you can't pour all of it from the carafe, because the plastic rim extends around the edge and into the lip, and it has a square edge. The lid of the carafe, has a strange pipe that extends to near the bottom of the pot. Why? You'd have to use a round brush to clean it well. I've made one pot of coffee so far. I used the rich setting. My wife liked it, but I thought it was much more bitter than yesterday's coffee. It was visibly darker (remember, I weigh the grounds, so that's constant). I found the liquid measure to be the same as the coffee make we've been using. Tomorrow I will try the "classic" setting. I don't really need another clock to set, or a timer, or really any of the features this sports beyond "on/off".

I will also mention that the reservoir works well. But it's clear plastic. So with our regular water, it will get mineral spots (and it's virtually impossible to clean with all the strange grooves and right angles). So we have to use distilled water. I like a spotless kitchen. (The reservoir in the old one doesn't need hand cleaning because it's mostly black plastic with a frosted window to gauge water level. It much much easier to see the water level with this Ninja, though.)

I've had the 12 cup model for about 1.5 years now and have been happy with it.

It brews good coffee, is easy to use and easy to clean. My only complaints are the buttons are somewhat "stiff" to press compared to my old Cuisinart and the printing is rather small for older eyes but not an issue on a daily basis. I broke the carafe about a year ago and it was pricey to replace but at least it was available.

My favorite feature is the removable reservoir which makes it simple to keep clean. I like to get it ready to brew the night before and my old Cuisinart would get microbial gunk growing in the reservoir which was extremely difficult clean out and probably not healthy. No such issue with the Ninja. I just leave the lid off the reservoir after brewing and it drys out very quickly. Plus it is easy to clean out if needed.

I LOVE the Ninja drip coffee maker!

1. The coffee tastes fresh.

2. The heat plate keeps the coffee in the pot hot.

3. The pot design does not spill or drip when you pour the coffee into the cup.

4. The maker doesn't steam while brewing. I can keep it pushed under my cabinet without worrying about it ruining the bottom of my cabinets.

5. The removable water reservoir means I dont have to store the maker by my sink.

6. It's easy to clean.

I really like this coffee maker. The only thing missing is the programmable feature, but I don't really mind. I can still set everything up and press the button when I arise in the morning. I love the side reservoir, which I didn't think I would like at all, but it's awesome and takes up practically no extra space. It's easy to clean and use, and the best part is that the coffee tastes great. I love the Bold and Small Batch options, too. Also love the cone filter. Unlike some coffee makers I tried, the basket seats securely and doesn't overflow. Overall, a great coffee maker.

reviews.review_title: “Beautiful color, easy setup, and great coffee!” ☕💚
reviews.review_description:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Love the color and how easy it is to use!

I just received my new Keurig, and I’m really happy with it so far! The dark green color is absolutely beautiful and looks even better in person. It fits perfectly on my coffee station without taking up too much space.

Setup was quick and easy right out of the box. Within a few minutes, I had it ready to brew my first cup. I like that it has multiple cup-size options, and it fits my travel mug without any issues.

The coffee brews quickly, is nice and hot, and the machine is much quieter than I expected. Overall, it feels well-made and is perfect for anyone who wants a simple, reliable coffee maker without a lot of extra buttons.

If you’re looking for a compact Keurig that looks great and makes a good cup of coffee, I would definitely recommend this one!

I absolutely love my new Keurig K-Express! From the moment I took it out of the box, it was incredibly easy to set up and start using. Within just a few minutes, I was enjoying my first cup of coffee.

What impressed me most is how quickly it brews. Mornings are busy, and having a fresh, hot cup of coffee ready in about a minute is a game changer. The Strong Brew button is one of my favorite features because it gives my coffee a richer, bolder flavor without any extra effort.

The compact design fits perfectly on my countertop without taking up a lot of space, and the removable water reservoir makes refilling simple. It has been reliable, easy to clean, and consistently brews a great cup every single time.

If you're looking for an affordable, dependable single-serve coffee maker that delivers great-tasting coffee and is simple to use, I highly recommend the Keurig K-Express. It has exceeded my expectations, and I couldn't be happier with my purchase!

First, an introduction, this will take some going through, bear with me. First, I had refused for years to get a Keurig, as I did not feel the quality and richness of a good strong cup of coffee was possible. But I finally got tired of trying other methods of brewing, from using a regular single cup espresso maker, moka pot, pour over, French press... I finally opted for the ease of a Keurig mini-plus. Coffee was ...eh... I switched coffee brands, to what I feel has to be the best commercial brand. And the coffee was EXcellenT! About a year later, despite regular cleaning cycles, the thing just stopped working. I tried to take it apart, watched some youtube videos which just solidified the fact that the company made these non-serviceable. P.O.'d at this obvious tactic to sell more, I waited a few weeks, but went and got another one. Same deal a year later. Another one. This last one gave me signs before ending it's own life. I would have to run several cycles where nothing would come out... till finally something... drip... by drip... several hours later, the thing would start running again, only to stop again the next day or two. Finally, it just died.

So I REFUSED to get another. These things are ridiculous, right? So I got a new French press. Coffee is great!! But... omg... what a pain cleaning that thing every.... single... time... I mean, really, it's no big deal. But, it CAn be. So I saw this thing on sale, I thought, well, it's HAlf the price of the other ones... and I def want something different this time. Cut to now....

This thing has SEVERAL issues that I don't like. First of all, it is a thinner cheaper plastic, and has a cheap looking shine to it. Ok, I'm over it. The plastic... I mean, can't they make these things with glass reservoirs.... the plastic reservoir has screws on the inside of it. I don't care if they say it is food safe... Plastic is also considered food safe... but that doesn't mean it is.. those are just bureaucratic rhetoric lies. But I digress,...So this coffee maker has an adjustment for high altitude... is THAT what ruined my previous Keurigs? High altitude? Hmmm. Ok, so maybe that's a plus. It also has different sizes that you can choose -8,10, & 12 oz. With the mini-plus, you choose the size by the amount of water you pour in. That means that this one measures what it sucks in. Hmmm. The mini-plus had the controls on the top. Easy peasy. This one has the controls on the side. It also doesn't have rubber feet on the bottom. So when you try to push the buttons, the thing slides away from you. Impossible to push any buttons with one hand, you have to use two. Even with rubber feet, you have to use two hands. I'm not a paraplegic, but it's rather stupid to have to hold the thing to press a button or two, or three. Which is what you have to do. It's just really awkward because you really have to hold it in the back to keep it from moving when you press the button in front. And you have to do that without touching the reservoir, which will pop out if you tried that.

But let's get to the coffee. So with the mini-plus, the first liquid out of the machine, was dark coffee. As it was finishing, the coffee would be a little more clear, but not pure water. With this machine, for the first few seconds, it is spewing out crystal clear WATER. I don't even know how that is possible. But this, it does. It also claims to be faster than the mini-cup. I hestitate to say "brews faster", because it doesn't brew, Keurigs simply spew water into and through the k-cup, it's a pressurized system, not a true brewing system. And it definitely IS faster. And that's a problem, as evidenced by the watery coffee that it spews out. Sure enough, the "coffee" tastes like water. This is the 8 oz brew, mind you, with the machine set to "strong". I first tried the 12oz, and ended up pouring it down the sink. The 8 oz wasn't much better. My next step is to switch out cups while it's pouring out the water at the beginning of the cycle and see if I can get a stronger "brew".

All in all, it's convenient enough. But it will sit on my counter, mostly unused, for when I have those really lazy, sleepy, or sick days, when all I want to do is pop in a capsule, and deal with the rest of it... Very disappointed. Perhaps if you live in a low altitude area, the mini-plus would work for you. I really do recommend that one above this.

reviews.review_title: short lifespan, bottom-of-the-line features, and -extremely- prone to spilling while brewing
reviews.review_description:
I used this machine daily for 17 months. Then, quite suddenly, it died: it wouldn't pump water or heat coffee. 17 months is a very short lifespan for a coffee machine. (Another of my Hamilton Beach machines also lasted a little less than 18 months. Perhaps the entire brand suffers from durability issues.)

This machine's coffee is as good as the coffee I've had from $50 Hamilton Beach machines. But I regret buying this machine, and indeed, I am never going to buy another Hamilton Beach product. In so many ways, this machine's features are limited or poorly implemented:

1) Extremely prone to spilling coffee all over your countertop. This is not a problem with the carafe; instead, it's a problem with the spring-loaded nozzle that transmits coffee from the machine to the carafe. About once every three months, this Hamilton Beach machine (and others that I've had) floods my countertop. Many other reviewers have detailed this problem: see "Hamilton Beach strikes out again" (which has the best detail), "flow cutoff sucks, leaks", "Coffee Goes All Over the Counter", and more. See also the picture at the bottom of this review.

A recommended solution is to use a little less ground coffee than you normally would, and then to use the machine's "bold" setting. But this hasn't stopped my machine from flooding on occasion.

This alone is a fatal or near-fatal flaw. But there is more...

2) Water reservoir: not removable (and thus difficult to wash). Also, the water gauge, which lets you see how much water is in the reservoir, appears on only one side of the reservoir -- rather than both sides, as with many other machines. Depending on how you position this machine on your countertop, you may need to bend at an odd angle to see the gauge.

3) Carafe: before making coffee, you push it into the machine so that it sits atop the holder, just as with most other coffee machines. But if you push it in as far as it can go, you have gone too far; the carafe won't be well positioned, and your coffee will spill outside the carafe. (But the carafe itself is better than the carafes from Hamilton Beach machines of a few years ago, because it's less likely to spill when pouring.)

4) LED indicator lights: they're white, which makes it a little more difficult to see whether they're on during the daytime. Any other color would have been better.

5) Power cord: not retractable, as it is on other low-cost coffee machines. As a result, the power cord will spill out over your countertop at least a little.

6) Buttons: they are very shallow and stiff; they require too much force to press. Again, it's not a huge problem. But to press the power button or any other button when the carafe is less than half-full, you need to firmly hold the machine itself with one hand, while pressing the button with a finger of your other hand. If you just attempt to press a button without holding the machine in place or otherwise anchoring it, you'll simply tip the machine over onto its side.

7) Battery backup: there is none. If you lose power for a second, or unplug your machine just for a moment, you will need to reset the current time, the time at which you want coffee-making to start (if you use that feature), and any special settings that you have. This isn't easy, as Hamilton Beach doesn't make it simple for you to set the time or, especially, the time at which you want coffee-making to start. The lack of a backup battery for these features seems like great cheapness on the part of Hamilton Beach, given that ordinary consumers can buy 3V lithium batteries for less than $1.

8) Coffee-filter holder: it has no handle, and to use it, you must slide it into the machine just so. All of this makes it a little difficult to manipulate.

9) As mentioned at the top of this review, the machine died in less than 18 months.

This machine is worse than you would hope, even given the low price. And the flooding problem, while it happens to me only once every three months or so, is terrible when it does happen. Avoid Hamilton Beach.

reviews.review_description: I love this flexibility for occasional guests who stay the weekend. 4-6 People and 5 drink coffee and dinner parties. I've had it just over a month. I was surprised it didnt come with the filter piece and took it from the previous. Im keeping expectations on that it won't last forever. Great if one drinks decaf or my daughter who loves only iced coffee. Since I don't use it every day may be my perfect alternative solution! So far so good!

reviews.review_title: AMAZING PRODUCT & CUSTOMER SERVICE TEAM! (What more could you ask for?)
reviews.review_description:
Let me tell you about how AMAZING not only their products are but, also how AMAZING they are as a company! I bought my duo March 28, 2025. This past Saturday we woke up to our coffee pot no longer working && giving us an error code. My spouse && I done all sorts of trouble shooting for HOURS working on this coffee maker. I finally gave up! I was shocked because I had owned Keurig before && they ALWAYS held up. I caved && called customer service. They was SHOCKED to hear that this coffee pot was only a few months old! They tried to help me troubleshoot it as well. Just a few steps && they couldn’t get it either. The customer service guy sent me a link to send my proof of purchase && I had to wait for them to look it all over. Within 24 hours I was approved for my warranty && of course the next day was Sunday. It’s now TUESDAY && my coffee pot is here! I’ve never seen a name brand company ship a product so fast! THANK YOU KEURIG && THANK YOUR CUSTOMER SERVICE TEAM! I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THEIR PRODUCTS! They stand behind them 100%! I got this coffee pot when my k-cup coffee maker I had bought a year ago went out. (That’s a different story.) I got this specific maker because my spouse loves a pot every morning before before he goes to work && I like to use the single side occasionally for my drinks! I have SPOILED him with this Keurig && I absolutely BABY this coffee pot! He tells me all the time every cup is just as good as the very first. (If you keep it very clean && well maintained yours will do the same!) When this went out you would have thought he lost his best friend! Needless to say he was ecstatic when I told him the new coffee pot come in today! I will always buy Keurig from here on out! You couldn’t ask for a better product. (My was obviously a flunk. That happens occasionally with ANY product.) You also couldn’t ask for a better customer service!

reviews.review_title: MORE AND MORE, Continuous issues, only 30 days old, DO NOT BUY THIS MACHINE!!
reviews.review_description:
I bought this on Jan 2 and have been using it for only 24 days. Today I continued to get a "add water" message (with a full tank) and "error 8" message followed by "dry". I cleaned the tank and re-filled several times and unplugged the machine to re-set it as online has indicated. I was finally able to get the machine to brew. Mind you this is a brand new machine and after 24 days has issues. I use filtered water so this should not be an issue. I have notified Keurig to see if there are solutions to fix these issues. I will keep this rating updated, but use caution when purchasing this machine.

EDIT: So I have been able to get the coffee machine to work once again. After getting errors, I unplugged the machine for a period of time, flushed out the water tank, and plugged it back in with fresh water. I was able to get it to function normally for the past several days. I use the timer and it have brewed coffee without issue for a few days. The single use side is functioning normally. Don't know if unplugging it reset whatever chip is inside but it works for now. If it continues to function normally over the next few months I will change my star rating. For now, I am skeptical of long term use.

02/08/25 UPDATE: DO NOT BUY THIS MACHINE!!!!!!!! I experienced same issues as listed about. Tried to repeat the "fix" three times without success. Contacted Keurig, but I am not optimistic I will receive a full refund. Amazon also closed my ability for a return on 02/01/2025, so I now can ONLY DEAL WITH KEURIG. If I could give zero stars I would.

02/28/25 ANOTHER UPDATE: Was able to finally get Keurig to send me another machine on 02/16/25. On 02/28/25, I received the new machine. Unpacked and carefully followed the directions to the "T". Plugged in the machine as directed and it failed to turn on. Tried a different outlet, nothing. Tried another machine and it powered up without issues. Not an outlet problem. It was clearly a machine problem walked around the house trying the machine on various outlets, nothing. Called Keurig and they ran through troubleshooting, nothing. Machine DEAD ON ARRIVAL. They tried to tell me since this was a warranty replacement machine, it no longer was subject to warranty. EVEN THOUGH THIS MACHINE WAS DEAD ON ARRIVAL. I was able maintain my composure and convince Keurig to send me another machine, which will be here in 7-14 days. Stay tuned folks! BTW way, my first machine still has the above issues and continues to periodically stop working, then work, then not work... I would love to have my money back, but Keuring rather spend more money on shipping and returns than refund my purchase price. Come on Keurig, you can do better.

EDIT: 04/20/25, ANOTHER UPDATE. Since my last update on 02/28/25, I received a third replacement machine from Keurig to replace the dead one. Got #3 all set up on 03/03/25 and ready to go and it worked until 03/28/25, exactly 25 days, then I got the dreaded "add water" and "error 8" message. Called Keuring and asked for a refund, but they still refuse since I bought it from Amazon. Asked to get another comparable machine, which they didn't have in stock (UGH). Ordered #4 replacement. On April 3, 2025, #4 replacement machine arrived. Got #4 all set up and on 04/20/25, it stopped working like the others. This one only lasted 17 days.

EDIT: Keurig has started ignoring my calls. I was referred to a "specialist" who told me I needed to send my #4 machine in first BEFORE I could get sent a replacement. As I did not want to send them my machine without a replacement first, they started ignoring my emails and are now refusing to correspond with me at all. #4 machine continues to brew 2 cups then shut off reporting it is dry when there is a full water tank. I will never purchase another Keurig product and you should seriously consider doing the same. Four unusable machines in 8 months is ridiculous!

reviews.review_title: Keurig has changed the game again!
reviews.review_description:
The Keurig K-Duo Single Serve & Carafe Coffee Maker is an absolute game-changer for households that want both quick morning speed and full-pot brewing capability. By seamlessly combining single-serve K-Cup convenience with a classic 12-cup glass carafe, it replaces two separate appliances with one sleek, space-saving countertop setup.

Brew speeds are impressive on both ends. Single-serve pods deliver a rich, flavorful cup in under a minute, while a full 12-cup pot brews in just a few minutes without over-extraction or bitterness. The control panel is intuitive, with clearly labeled buttons for cup size and carafe settings. Maintenance is equally straightforward, featuring accessible filter baskets and clear fill indicators.

The Keurig K-Duo hits the sweet spot between weeknight simplicity and weekend batch brewing. For anyone seeking speed, versatility, and dependability without cluttering their kitchen counters, this coffee maker is an exceptional choice.

reviews.review_title: Nearly Eight Years of Service—Good Enough to Buy Again
reviews.review_description:
I originally purchased the Cuisinart DCC-3200 PerfectTemp 14-Cup Programmable Coffeemaker on October 31, 2018, for $75.92. Nearly eight years later, it still makes excellent, hot coffee. It recently began making a slight squeaking noise during the brewing cycle, so I decided to play it safe and purchase the same model again on August 2, 2026.

That should say plenty about how much I like this coffee maker. It is dependable, easy to operate, makes a full 14-cup pot, and has served me well for almost eight years. I would not have bought the exact same model again if the first one had not performed so well.

My only complaint is the price increase. The original cost $75.92, while the replacement cost $107.43 before tax—an increase of $31.51, or about 41%. Even with the higher price, its performance and longevity made it worth buying again. Five stars.

reviews.review_title: Love it for a consistently good and easy cup of coffee
reviews.review_description: Love love love it for a consistently good cup of coffee and so easy! This is our second one of this exact same coffee pot, the previous one lasted about 7 years until it got a crack somewhere and started leaking so the value for the money is definitely there. We debated getting something different this time around but I couldn’t stray from something that we already knew worked great and we never had any issues with. Consistently brews a great flavor and temperature cup of coffee, easy to clean and set up. Would definitely recommend, and the fact that you can set it up the night before and program it to brew is a great feature!

One of the best and cheapest, good looking coffee makers out there. I have one at home and one at the office for years and it works everyday. The coffee is hot, it keeps it fairly hot not burned, easy to fill, easy to add coffee. I have bought many coffee makers and some are much much more expensive. But just for a good consistent pot of coffee once you get the correct measurements of coffee and water I think there is none better. It came with the gold filter which is good since I never use paper, it has a few brew temp and carafe temps and you can set the timer to brew automatically. It does not take up much space is fairly easy to keep clean. The water tank though does take a bit of work to get clean and keep clean though. Over time it gets pretty rank and I cleaned mine by spraying soap and Clorox in it and using a dishrag to clean it out. I then rinsed it out in the sink all the time being upside down so as this would not enter the brew track. Once cleaned and rinsed then filled with water and ran a couple of pots of water through it and its as good as new. Now unless your a professional, I don't recommend doing this LOL but it never stopped working and never stopped brewing a good cup of coffee. Looks and works as good as the day it was purchased. I did buy another one and had a funeral for the old one after many years. It still worked, so it was hard to part with but the wife said we had to get a new one. Sheesh, Why? O well you know how that goes.

I ordered this coffee maker after researching it as thoroughly as possible. Much to my disappointment, the initial batches of coffee tasted like plastic. I ran carafes of filtered water through the device several times, but the taste of plastic persisted. Then I used ChatGPT to see what information was available and sure enough, this is a common problem. It would have been nice if Cuisinart had addressed this issue in the manual. This is why I am giving a 3 star rating.

My next step was to use coffee cleaner, followed by 2 more carafes of filtered water. I could still smell the plastic in the filter basket, so I washed it with a strong mixture of Dawn detergent. Then I ran another carafe of water through it. That finally seems to have gotten rid of the plastic taste in brewed coffee. The entire process probably used several gallons of filtered water and took several days to complete.

Otherwise, this coffee maker is well designed and of good quality. The plastic components are thick, unlike the current Moccamaster plastic parts which are thin and flimsy by comparison. (The Moccamaster also has a tube attached to the carafe lid that’s unnecessary, cumbersome and hard to wash. Their old models have a separate tube which isn’t used for the same reason.)

I desperately needed a replacement coffee maker and I’m glad I persisted in my efforts to get rid of the plastic taste instead of returning it. This makes good coffee as other reviews have stated. Just be prepared to get rid of the plastic taste.

UPDATE

As of February 7th, I need to revise my rating to 4 stars. Except for the problem with the plastic taste I explained above, this is a high-quality product that makes good coffee. I love the 1 - 4 cup feature which is what I use to make 24 ounces of coffee. If you drink coffee black and enjoy the flavor of good coffee, you will love this feature. This makes the best coffee I've ever tasted. That said, the initial plastic taste with no mention of it in the manual is a major problem that has to be overcome.

UPDATE AFTER USING FOR 6 WEEKS:

I've been using this new Cuisinart almost every day for 6 weeks, and have NEVER had any issues

with the carafe leaking/spilling OR the condensation on the maker lid leaking water onto my

countertop when I open it up to add coffee grounds and pour water into the reservoir.

Not even once. The only thing I can think of to explain SOME of those carafe complaints

is that they are trying to pour from the carafe TOO fast. I must admit 10 years ago when I FIRST got

my old Cuisinart2800, I tried pouring from the carafe and poured too fast and spilled. But just a slight

slow down fixed it and no issues since. But other than that pour speed issue, I have no idea what those

reviewers were doing to cause the maker or the carafe to leak water as they described.

Everything else I wrote in my initial review still stands too!

=============================================================

I read thru a LOT of reviews on this Cuisinart DCC3200NAS (this is the SS and Black).

I JUST set it up on my countertop last night and ran a pot of plain hot water thru it as suggested.

This morning I made my first pot of coffee in it!! 9 cups. Very tasty coffee!

BUT this review is NOT about how good the coffee is. Nearly all the reviews have established that its great.

This review addresses a few of the most common complaints about this coffee maker.

FYI: This new 3200 replaced a refurbed Cuisinart DCC2800WFR I had for 10 years that recently started leaking water.

The MOST common complaint is the carafe. I am honestly NOT sure why. The new carafe seems IDENTICAL

(except black plastic vs white) to the carafe that was on my 2800 that I used for 10 years with no issues.

Spout dripping: The easiest way to MAKE the spout drip is pouring too fast. Just slow your pour down a TICH.

I put water for 9 cups in my carafe and poured it into my water reservoir in about 10 seconds without spilling a

drop. It works exactly the same way AND as well as my 2800 carafe did for 10 years. No spills. No issues.

HELPFUL HINT: Make SURE the 3200 lid is FULLY opened (past 90 degrees) before you try to fill the reservoir.

Then just rest the carafe spout on the SIDE of the reservoir with the water level indicator. Pour. Done.

Carafe Lid not hinged and/or too tough to take off and/or put back on properly:

Not hinged is true! But why is that bad? I don't know. It snaps off and on easily for me. Has for 10 years.

And I don't even bother taking the lid off to fill the carafe with water. Just fill it thru the spout hole!

The new carafe lid DOES require a SLIGHTLY firmer push to pop it off and back on than my old carafe, but I'm

guessing in 12 months this one will pop off and on a little easier than it does now too.

HELPFUL HINT: Pop the carafe lid off by LIFTING the tab that your thumb sits on when holding the carafe.

Pop it back on in reverse: Insert spout side first, then pop the thumb side down. Done. Easy peasy.

The 3200 control panel is significantly different from my old 2800. I read a couple reviews that suggested

the 3200 control panel was difficult to understand and use properly!?! I found the exact opposite to be true.

Once you know exactly what option each button controls (button labels seem clear & obvious to me), setting the

options properly is completely simple. As you press each button, it cycles thru the available settings for that option.

Stop pressing that button when that option is set to your liking. If you miss it, cycle around again. Done.

The basket the filter sits in DOES need to be PUSHED fully back down such that it "pops" down into the maker after

being removed (in my 2800, it just dropped in loosely). BUT that is obvious to the careful user since it requires that

same "pop" to remove that basket in the first place. If that basket is NOT popped down into place, the carafe lid

won't reach (much less push up on) the spring loaded valve on the underside of that basket, so that valve would stay

closed, and as your maker dumps more water into your filter, coffee grounds will overflow your filter and go

everywhere including the bottom of the water reservoir. PS: Same thing happens if you put a LIDLESS carafe

in the coffee maker! Lid isn't there to push up on the valve, so the valve stays closed.

I found the 5 "Coffee is Done" beeps and the 2 "Heating Pad Off" beeps to be the right volume for my house.

Not loud, BUT loud enough that on a normal (ie: semi-quiet) morning, I can hear it from the next room easy.

AND it is super fast and easy to turn the beeping off and back on with the "Tone" option button if you need to.

Bottom Line for me:

I am boggled by all the carafe and reservoir filling issues so many reviewers have! I have NO dripping issues or

lid issues with my carafe, NO reservoir filling issues, and NO setup or control panel issues. All 5 stars.

Now lets just see if it stands the test of time like my 2800 did!

I love this coffee maker. We had this model for at least 5 years. Still worked perfectly but I decided I'd like to buy a new one. I was pleasantly surprised that Cuisinart still makes this coffee maker, the same as previously had, but slightly different buttons etc a bit sleeker, but same functions. It is worth the money. I'd like to buy another one just to have it in the future, as often often times, you cannot always get the same coffee maker in the future.

I highly recommend this wonderful coffee maker by Cuisinart.

This has been a great coffee maker. Its large capacity is great for when you have company it fits in a small footprint and it keeps the coffee hot! The programming is easy to use and it brews fairly quickly. I am very pleased with it.

This BKSP1 (black stainless appearance) 14-cup coffeemaker replaced a 12+ year old Cuisinart 12-cup unit we used until it finally quit working. Great coffeemaker and it produced great coffee. My research to replace the old unit settled on the BKSP1 model and Amazon delivered straight-a-way.

I got it all cleansed out, programmed and set up for begin brewing at 4:45 the next morning. It brewed a great pot of coffee and all worked wonderfully ... EXCEPT that the clock on the BKSP1 was running FAST. It had "gained" almost an hour since I had set it up the day before. Thus the coffee was actually brewed at ~3:45AM.

I reset the clock and kept watching it as I would walk by the coffeemaker and noted that it was gaining time or running FAST. I went through this for several days and finally sent a message to Amazon C.S. and they immediately replaced with another BKSP1 and I returned the original unit.

I went through the setup process with the #2 BKSP1 and was hopeful that the clock would keep proper time ... however it did not. The clock on the #2 BKSP1 also ran FAST. The coffeemaker worked just fine in all regards ... save for the clock running FAST.

So, I reached out to Cuisinart/Conair C.S. with this "fast clock" issue and they replaced the #2 BKSP1 with the #3 BKSP1. I did all the setup with #3 and lo & behold ... the clock on the #3 BKSP1 also runs FAST. All other elements work just fine, brews great coffee, but the clock just has a mind of it's own.

So (you can guess what is next), I reached out to Cuisinart/Conair C.S. (again) with the fast clock issue noted in graf above. A ticket was established and I was shipped a #4 BKSP1 to replace the #3 unit.

Can you see where this is going? The #4 BKSP1 unit was set up and put into service and the clock on #4 also runs FAST.

So ... it appears that there is something common going on with the BKSP1 model units.

This time I called Cuisinart/Conair C.S. (I had been establishing all other tickets via the inter-web and e-mail). The lady with C.S. was simply excellent and she noted my BKSP1 ticket history and said she would have another unit shipped out straight-a-way. She asked if I still wanted the same BKSP1 model or would I want to get the SP1 model (SP1 is the brushed stainless appearance). I figured what the heck ... I would get the SP1 this time.

In a couple days I received the #5 SP1, got it all set up and ready to brew coffee the next morning at 4:45. I would glance at the clock on the #5 SP1 as I walked by the unit and the clock was ACCURATE. I was again hopeful that the clock would hold and keep proper time.

At 4:45AM the brew cycle started and it actually was at 4:45AM. The clock held it's accuracy for one day at that point.

It has now been 3-days and the clock on the #5 SP1 is "spot on".

So (there is the 'so' word again) I noted on the boxes the coffeemakers were shipped in had the countries of manufacture stamped on them. The BKSP1 units were all manufactured in China. The SP1 unit was manufactured in Indonesia. AHA - I said. There is a manufacturing plant issue going on.

I did an extensive observation letter to Cuisinart/Conair about my situation and thoughts of what is going on.

BTW - In addition the BKSP1 units all dripped extensive moisture droplets down the back side of the unit when the top lid was opened to removed the coffee grounds. This had me wondering if there was a leak as there was water all over the counter under the BKSP1 units.

Turns out the drip lip on the upper back of the BKSP1 appears to be 'flat' without adequate slope to have the water droplets flow back into the reservoir. Also the drip lip is not as deep as what I noticed on the SP1 units.

I also observed (on both the BKSP1 and SP1 models) that there is a lot of moisture condensation that collects on the upper front panel where the control buttons are located. To me this could affect the electronics that I'm guessing is located near or behind this panel.

Ergo couple items of note for Cuisinart/Conair:

1) Production molds for the BKSP1 and SP1 are NOT the same between the China and Indonesia manufacturing plants. Thus the drip lip issue noted above.

2) The chips/electronics being used in the China plant for the BKSP1 are defective and can't keep proper time.

All-in-all ... The Cuisinart 14-cup coffeemaker is an excellent product and works very well and produces great coffee. Save for the units (in my case) that are manufactured in China where the chips/electronics they are using just don't work. Adding to that the manufacturing mold difference that slightly changes the size of the drip lip on the upper back.

I would suggest getting the the SP1 model and keep your fingers crossed that it is also manufactured in Indonesia as opposed to China. At least until such time as changes are made in the manufacturing facility in China to correct the noted issues.

Cheers,

Nolan K.
