reviews.review_title: “Beautiful color, easy setup, and great coffee!” ☕💚
reviews.review_description:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Love the color and how easy it is to use!

I just received my new Keurig, and I’m really happy with it so far! The dark green color is absolutely beautiful and looks even better in person. It fits perfectly on my coffee station without taking up too much space.

Setup was quick and easy right out of the box. Within a few minutes, I had it ready to brew my first cup. I like that it has multiple cup-size options, and it fits my travel mug without any issues.

The coffee brews quickly, is nice and hot, and the machine is much quieter than I expected. Overall, it feels well-made and is perfect for anyone who wants a simple, reliable coffee maker without a lot of extra buttons.

If you’re looking for a compact Keurig that looks great and makes a good cup of coffee, I would definitely recommend this one!

I absolutely love my new Keurig K-Express! From the moment I took it out of the box, it was incredibly easy to set up and start using. Within just a few minutes, I was enjoying my first cup of coffee.

What impressed me most is how quickly it brews. Mornings are busy, and having a fresh, hot cup of coffee ready in about a minute is a game changer. The Strong Brew button is one of my favorite features because it gives my coffee a richer, bolder flavor without any extra effort.

The compact design fits perfectly on my countertop without taking up a lot of space, and the removable water reservoir makes refilling simple. It has been reliable, easy to clean, and consistently brews a great cup every single time.

If you're looking for an affordable, dependable single-serve coffee maker that delivers great-tasting coffee and is simple to use, I highly recommend the Keurig K-Express. It has exceeded my expectations, and I couldn't be happier with my purchase!

First, an introduction, this will take some going through, bear with me. First, I had refused for years to get a Keurig, as I did not feel the quality and richness of a good strong cup of coffee was possible. But I finally got tired of trying other methods of brewing, from using a regular single cup espresso maker, moka pot, pour over, French press... I finally opted for the ease of a Keurig mini-plus. Coffee was ...eh... I switched coffee brands, to what I feel has to be the best commercial brand. And the coffee was EXcellenT! About a year later, despite regular cleaning cycles, the thing just stopped working. I tried to take it apart, watched some youtube videos which just solidified the fact that the company made these non-serviceable. P.O.'d at this obvious tactic to sell more, I waited a few weeks, but went and got another one. Same deal a year later. Another one. This last one gave me signs before ending it's own life. I would have to run several cycles where nothing would come out... till finally something... drip... by drip... several hours later, the thing would start running again, only to stop again the next day or two. Finally, it just died.

So I REFUSED to get another. These things are ridiculous, right? So I got a new French press. Coffee is great!! But... omg... what a pain cleaning that thing every.... single... time... I mean, really, it's no big deal. But, it CAn be. So I saw this thing on sale, I thought, well, it's HAlf the price of the other ones... and I def want something different this time. Cut to now....

This thing has SEVERAL issues that I don't like. First of all, it is a thinner cheaper plastic, and has a cheap looking shine to it. Ok, I'm over it. The plastic... I mean, can't they make these things with glass reservoirs.... the plastic reservoir has screws on the inside of it. I don't care if they say it is food safe... Plastic is also considered food safe... but that doesn't mean it is.. those are just bureaucratic rhetoric lies. But I digress,...So this coffee maker has an adjustment for high altitude... is THAT what ruined my previous Keurigs? High altitude? Hmmm. Ok, so maybe that's a plus. It also has different sizes that you can choose -8,10, & 12 oz. With the mini-plus, you choose the size by the amount of water you pour in. That means that this one measures what it sucks in. Hmmm. The mini-plus had the controls on the top. Easy peasy. This one has the controls on the side. It also doesn't have rubber feet on the bottom. So when you try to push the buttons, the thing slides away from you. Impossible to push any buttons with one hand, you have to use two. Even with rubber feet, you have to use two hands. I'm not a paraplegic, but it's rather stupid to have to hold the thing to press a button or two, or three. Which is what you have to do. It's just really awkward because you really have to hold it in the back to keep it from moving when you press the button in front. And you have to do that without touching the reservoir, which will pop out if you tried that.

But let's get to the coffee. So with the mini-plus, the first liquid out of the machine, was dark coffee. As it was finishing, the coffee would be a little more clear, but not pure water. With this machine, for the first few seconds, it is spewing out crystal clear WATER. I don't even know how that is possible. But this, it does. It also claims to be faster than the mini-cup. I hestitate to say "brews faster", because it doesn't brew, Keurigs simply spew water into and through the k-cup, it's a pressurized system, not a true brewing system. And it definitely IS faster. And that's a problem, as evidenced by the watery coffee that it spews out. Sure enough, the "coffee" tastes like water. This is the 8 oz brew, mind you, with the machine set to "strong". I first tried the 12oz, and ended up pouring it down the sink. The 8 oz wasn't much better. My next step is to switch out cups while it's pouring out the water at the beginning of the cycle and see if I can get a stronger "brew".

All in all, it's convenient enough. But it will sit on my counter, mostly unused, for when I have those really lazy, sleepy, or sick days, when all I want to do is pop in a capsule, and deal with the rest of it... Very disappointed. Perhaps if you live in a low altitude area, the mini-plus would work for you. I really do recommend that one above this.

reviews.review_title: Mine did not last a year.
reviews.review_description: I loved this keurig for my family. It was perfect for my dsuggter, who had just started drinking mainly decaf coffee. Bought in Oct 2025, and it just stopped working after I cleaned it with descaling solution in June 2026. I had previously cleaned it earlier in the year without any issues. Not sure what went wrong. Not sure if I will buy another one. It was a good thing while it lasted.

reviews.review_title: Excellent Coffee Maker – Fast, Easy, and Great-Tasting Coffee
reviews.review_description:
I’ve been using the Keurig K-Express for a while now, and I’m very happy with it. It’s compact, stylish, and fits perfectly on my kitchen counter. The Warm Stone color looks modern and elegant.

The coffee brews quickly, and I love the Strong Brew option because it gives my coffee a richer, bolder flavor. The 42 oz water reservoir is convenient since I can make several cups before needing to refill it. It’s incredibly easy to use and clean, making it perfect for busy mornings. If you’re looking for a reliable single-serve coffee maker that delivers great coffee every time, this is an excellent choice. I would definitely recommend it!

I got this to replace my original Keurig. The old k50 or whatever it was. This thing takes up less space, looks more sleek, and works better than the original. It's faster, the coffee tastes better, it has the strong button. Also, I keep my coffee maker in my bedroom, and with the old one if you wanted it to be ready to make a quick cup of coffee it had to be turned on which meant that it had lights illuminated. I had to cover them with tape. This new one can go from being turned off to making a quick cup of coffee immediately. And after 5 minutes it automatically turns any illumination off. That means it doesn't make light in my bedroom at night. It's just a way way better version. It's quieter. I love it I'm so glad I got it. I will say that I got this brand new, and it was a really good deal, and I can see why because the manual includes an offer for discounted coffee that expired over two years ago. I'm guessing Keurig punched out a few too many of these models and they've been sitting in a warehouse for too many years. My advice is buy it now before it goes out of stock. It is an excellent coffee maker.

title: Keurig K-Elite Single Serve K-Cup Pod Coffee Maker, with Strength and Temperature Control, Iced Coffee Capability, 8 to 12oz Brew Size, Programmable, Brushed Slate
description: The Keurig K-Elite® single serve coffee maker blends premium finish and programmable features together to deliver both modern design and the ultimate in beverage customization. With a striking brushed finish and metal details, it’s a stylish addition to any kitchen. The Keurig K-Elite® coffee maker features a Strong Brew setting when you want to brew a bolder cup of coffee, and an Iced setting to brew hot over ice for a refreshing, full-flavored iced coffee. It features five brew sizes, so you can brew 4, 6, 8, 10, or 12oz of your favorite coffee, tea, hot cocoa, or iced beverage in minutes at the touch of a button. Choose from hundreds of delicious varieties of K-Cup® pods, or brew your own ground coffee using the Universal My K-Cup® Reusable Coffee Filter (sold separately). In addition to a host of programmable features like temperature control, the Keurig K-Elite® coffee maker provides hot water on demand for instant soups and oatmeal, and the large 75oz removable water filter let you brew multiple cups between refills.*Cup not included*

reviews.review_description:
I’ve been really happy with the Keurig K-Elite. It’s one of those appliances that does exactly what I need it to do without making my morning more complicated.

It heats up quickly, is easy to use, and I really like having several cup-size options depending on how much coffee I want. The Strong Brew setting is probably my favorite feature because I prefer a bolder cup, and it actually makes a noticeable difference. The large water reservoir is another big plus since I’m not constantly having to refill it.

I also appreciate that it gives you more control than a basic single-serve machine while still keeping everything convenient. The controls are straightforward, cleanup is easy, and it consistently makes a good cup of coffee.

If you like the convenience of K-Cups but want a machine with a few more useful features than the basic models, the K-Elite is a solid choice. I use mine regularly and would definitely buy it again.

I’ve always gotten keurig products from Costco, but I needed a new one because the other one I had for like 4 years broke down on me. The product never fails me and it’s seriously my go to product. The reservoir has enough water to do two rounds of coffee and it’s easy to use. Can’t go wrong with it

reviews.review_title: Great Keurig with two features I would miss now
reviews.review_description:
I purchased this Keurig K-Elite for my daughter, but I have been using it too, so I’ve had a chance to try the main features myself. We purchased it recently, and it has already been a great buy. I have used Keurig machines for years, and this one has a couple of features that really make it stand out.

What I like:

• The iced coffee feature works really well

• It makes better iced coffee than just brewing a regular K-cup over ice

• The iced setting seems to get the strength and ratio right so it does not taste watered down

• Works with regular K-cups for iced coffee

• Hot water on demand is very useful

• Great for tea, oatmeal, hot cocoa mixes, and other hot drinks

• Easy to set up

• Directions were easy to understand

• Brews regular K-cups nicely too

• I like the variety of cup sizes

• The water reservoir size is convenient without making the machine too bulky

• Feels quieter than other Keurigs I have used

• Fits nicely on the countertop

Things to be aware of:

• It is quieter than some other Keurigs, but it is not completely silent

• It still makes some normal brewing and heating sounds

• If placing it under cabinets, remember the handle needs extra clearance when opened

• I do recommend keeping up with descaling because I think it helps with both taste and machine longevity

• We use our Keurigs heavily, and while none have lasted forever for us, we keep coming back to the brand

Overall:

This is a great Keurig, and the iced coffee and hot water features are what make it feel special. It is easy to use, brews well, and has features I would really miss now.

I love the K-Elite Keurig coffee I would say this is my third one after many years. They seem to last me about three years. This one is identical to the previous ones that I’ve owned, however there’s one function that I do not like. The power button will not stay on. I have read that this is a new function of the Keurig machines to save energy. It turns off after a short time of brewing, your 1st cup of coffee. When I go back for my 2nd cup, I have to restart the machine and wait for the water to heat. Otherwise, I love the Machine and have actually used the iced coffee which I never used on my previous machine.

Keurig is always a good machine. I bought this K-Elite model to replace my old classic model with 48 ounce reservoir mainly because of the larger 75 ounce reservoir so I wouldn’t need to refill as often. However, I’m having to refill just as much as often as because when the water level decreases to near half way it’ll stop and say Add Water. At least on the old one it wouldn’t do that until it was nearly empty. It brews to 4 different sizes but the coffee is watered down too much if you select the larger sizes; so it defeats the purpose. I could have replaced the old with the same model and done just as well. The brewing is very good, fast, and great tasting coffee using the 6 and 8 oz sizes.

Love this and still working strong!! It has been great! Lots of coffee made in this house 🤗 Brew size selections are a good fit. The temp control and stronger options are great for two different coffee lovers! Brews quickly, easy to clean!! Should last a good while!!

reviews.review_title: Nice Coffee Maker as Expected from Keurig
reviews.review_description: I received my Keurig K-Elite Single Serve K-Cup Pod Coffee Maker yesterday so I don't have a lot of use to review it by but I will say that having had several Keurig coffee makers in the past I like the look, feel and utility of this model. I read several reviews prior to purchase that claimed the temperature of the brew was not as hot as was set in the machine. I experienced the same and wanted to understand it better. I have my machine set at 190 for the temperature. I used a calibrated Thermapen ONE Thermometer, the one chefs use and rely on, and the temp of the coffee in my cup right after brewing completed was 158. Then I measured the brew as it exits the machine but before it got into my cup and it was 187. Turns out my ceramic cup was at room temperature and some of the heat from the brew was used up to heat my cup, which lowered the resultant temp of the coffee in my cup. Bottom line: my machine is very close to the temp I set for the brew. If I preheat my cup the coffee in my cup will be very close to what I have my machine set to. So I am happy and my coffee maker is performing as specified.

First let me tell you I drink at least 8 cups of coffee a day and this Kuerig meets the demands. Brew time is faster if it’s been working for awhile like two cups. This makes strong coffee and regular flavor. Husband likes strong. It is not portable and the kcups can be from any where. It is a good size and really takes up very little space on my counter.

I maintain mine based on manufacturer opinion. I love it that much I don’t want to be without it.

title: Ninja Luxe Café Premier 3-in-1 Espresso Machine, Drip Coffee, & Cold Brew
description: The Ninja Luxe Café Premier 3-in-1 Espresso Machine, Drip Coffee, and Rapid Cold Brew Maker is the ultimate guided coffee and espresso experience, no guesswork required. Perfect for beginner espresso lovers and anyone looking for café quality without the work. This intelligent machine features Barista Assist Technology that guides you through every step of the espresso and coffee making experience, from grinding the beans to frothing the milk. Comes with a 70 oz removable water reservoir for easy refills, an assisted tamper for the perfect puck, a built-in conical burr grinder with 25 settings, weight-based automatic dosing, a self-cleaning steam wand that automatically purges after every shot, and a dual froth system that combines a magnetic whisk with the automated steamer. Complete your home cafe by pairing with the Ninja Luxe Café Knock Box and Ninja Luxe Café 28 oz Shareable Pitcher. Ideal for everyone from DIY coffee enthusiasts to busy professionals. Expertly craft summertime iced lattes and cozy winter peppermint mochas with confidence and ease.

reviews.review_description:
My wife had always wanted an espresso machine without spending a fortune. The night she ordered this one, she could barely sleep. When it finally arrived, her excitement was through the roof.

We've been using it regularly since it was delivered on May 29, and it has exceeded our expectations.

The reality is that this is an excellent product at a reasonable price. There isn't a single part that feels cheap or flimsy. The machine feels sturdy, well-built, and refined, and it looks great sitting on our coffee bar.

I think the stainless-steel finish is a great neutral color that fits into almost any kitchen. If you're looking for something a little different, Ninja offers other color options on their website. You can certainly spend more on a higher-end model, but for our family, this machine has everything we need.

If you're looking for Starbucks-level speed every morning, it's capable of delivering that. However, I'd encourage you to slow down and enjoy the process. There's something incredibly satisfying about crafting your own coffee and producing a drink that feels café quality from the comfort of your home.

The instructions and videos are so well done that they leave you feeling confident from day one. After a little practice, you'll feel like you could walk into a coffee shop and tell the barista, "Thanks, but I'll make my own coffee today."

To wrap up this admittedly long review—because Ninja deserves it—they absolutely knocked it out of the park. Between the build quality, ease of use, and quality of the drinks it produces, this machine has earned a permanent place in our kitchen.

As an Air Force veteran, I appreciate products that do what they promise, and this one delivers. I'm extremely happy with this purchase and would recommend it without hesitation.

Read more

I love this machine! I was expecting to be disappointed as things are not always what they are hyped up to be but it is great. It is easy to use, makes great coffee, espresso and frothed milk as well as easy to clean. Also saving me a small fortune as I no longer go to the fancy coffee place because I now make my own. It fits on my counter and under my cabinets perfect. I will note that mounting the handle can be pretty tight at first but it does loosen with use. The grinder is a great addition and am very happy it is truly an all-in-one machine. I have had mine for two months without any issues.

This Espresso Maker is so beautifully designed! Our daughter-in-law was a barista for a couple of years and she raves about the quality of the coffee. It looks a little intimidating at first, but the videos and instructions are excellent and within no time it will be second nature to you. The machine is able to sense a lot of what needs to be done and guide you through the process. The only "wish" I would have is that during the cleaning process, you need to vacuum out the burr grinder which is a bit of a hassle. But for this level of quality coffee, it is worth it!

reviews.review_title: Fantastic for casual use. Not for hot rods.
reviews.review_description:
I’ve owned this machine for about 8 months and I am comparing this to my Breville Barista. It’s a great device, if you’re getting it for the right reason.

I have this one in my office at work and it’s a fantastic machine. Fast, easy to use, minimal clean-up, no fuss. It does the thing. Easy to follow steps leading to fast and delicious beverages. If you are looking for something fool-proof with a variety of drink options this is absolutely for you. An average achieving 4th grader can set up and run this machine. You will not go back and you will save sooo much money in the long run getting yourself un-addicted to $7 lattes.

If you are looking to tinker, tune, hot-rod or slap on a bunch of aftermarket parts, this isn’t the device for you. Go for a more traditional machine. This machine works best when you run it as is and let it do its thing. It doesn’t even have enough clearance for most puck screens, and I think it throws off its calibration. The wastewater tray is also pretty small. I empty it much more than I do on my Breville. You can make a variety of drinks in this and many are great (cold press works well) but some are more gimmicky. Regular brew coffee doesn’t taste great. Also it’s harder to use this as a dedicated on demand hot water source for tea and such. It doesn’t have a dedicated spigot for hot water. Lastly the water frothing feature is awesome, but for some reason the steam wand (which has restrictive movement and you must use the stock pitcher) the wand always dribbles on me when I’m cleaning it. I think it’s a personal problem.

Read more

Do you want a good cup of coffee? This is the machine. First time buying one of these machines. I was a little nervous at first. I bought the stainless steel Ninja Espresso machine. I’ve been using it for two weeks. I absolutely love it. The machine I used before used K cups and and that was getting old fast. With fresh coffee beans the coffee is delicious. The machine fits perfectly on my rolling cart. It takes maybe five minutes from start to finish for my caramel macchiato in the morning. And the temperature is perfect. The thing that I love the most about this machine is it comes with a video on how to help you to use it for the first time. It’s very simple to use. Of course I’m still getting used to it, but it works beautiful so far. It’s a well-made machine. If you’re looking for a good espresso machine for the first time, I recommend Ninja.

reviews.review_title: I’m in love with this coffee machine
reviews.review_description:
Worth every penny!! This is by far the best machine you can get for your money. If you are not a professional in making coffee and you get your daily fix at starbucks, do yourself a favor and invest in this instead. So easy to use and the results are amazing. I recreate Starbucks drinks on the daily and the only investment you make is the initial Ninja luxe, syrups and good coffee. If you break down your numbers you will see it makes so much more sense. I promise you, you will get a pro in no time.

Cleaning is easy too, just a few parts to take care of. You get a booklet that explains step by step all the set up and has awesome recipes too.

I have not used the frother in my video since I ran out of milk, but it makes cold foam, thick froth and like a latte froth and you have the option to choose if you are using dairy or plant based milk. Froth turns out amazing every single time.

Cold brew option is pretty good, not original cold brew good but for recreation of iced coffee drinks it tastes great and you wouldn’t be able to taste the difference.

If you are new to brewing your own espresso, the Ninja takes out all the guesswork and weighting and pressure and temping etc out of the equation. It automatically adjust the grind suggestion based in the coffee you choose, beans, weights the amount of grinded beans and pulls an excellent shot every time. I thought I had good coffee before but tasting it now proved me wrong. Use coffee from a local roaster or make sure the beans are not older than 3m for the perfect result. I use the Lavazza crema and have been getting good results but prefer beans from local roaster since they are the freshest.

Don’t doubt it and get yourself a Ninja Luxe you won’t regret it!

Read more

reviews.review_title: Best coffee maker I’ve ever bought
reviews.review_description: It’s definitely the most expensive coffee maker I ever paid for, but it is well worth it. The coffee taste so much better being fresh ground just before you you brew it. There’s nothing better than warm frost creamer to go in your coffee taste like roasted marshmallows.

This machine does a lot, and somehow doesn’t feel overwhelming. The ability to make espresso, drip coffee, and cold brew all in one setup is a huge win, especially if you don’t want three different machines taking over your counter.

The built-in grinder and guided settings make it really easy to get a good cup without having to mess with a bunch of complicated adjustments. Espresso comes out rich and consistent, and the drip coffee is well-balanced. The rapid cold brew is a nice bonus and actually tastes smooth, not watered down.

The milk frother works well and is pretty much hands-off, which is great if you’re not trying to play barista at 6am. Cleanup is also easier than expected for a machine with this many features.

It’s not perfect, there’s a bit of a learning curve at first, and it takes up some space, but once you get used to it, it’s a solid all-in-one system.

Overall, great option if you want café-style drinks at home without overcomplicating your mornings.

title: Mr. Coffee® 5-Cup Mini Brew Switch Coffee Maker, Black
description: Enjoy great coffee simply made with the Mr. Coffee 5-Cup Coffee Maker. It makes up to 25 oz. of coffee, just right for two 12-oz. cups, and the compact design fits nicely into small spaces. The updated, ergonomic carafe design with ounce markings takes the guesswork out of measuring. Just set it up, turn it on, and brew. Grab-a-Cup Auto Pause allows you to stop the brewing cycle to pour a cup, then continue brewing until complete. The easy-to-use ON/OFF switch indicates when the coffee maker is on, and reminds you to shut it off. All you need to do is sit back, sip, and enjoy!Care & Maintenance: Make sure your coffeemaker is unplugged and has cooled completely before cleaning. Remove the brew basket, filter carafe, carafe lid, and wash them in a solution of hot water and mild liquid soap, and dry thoroughly.

reviews.review_description:
Arrived so quickly. It arrived 2-3 hours after i ordered it which was great because my current coffee maker suddenly quit working that same morning. It was a Mr. Coffee 12-cup that lasted for 13 years so I figured that i got my money's worth. So I thought I would go with Mr. Coffee brand again.

Anyway, this time I decided to try the 5-cup because I no longer need a 12-cup as I now live alone. I've only had it for 3 days but so far I love it. It works great. I don't like warm coffee and this little coffee makes makes hot coffee, but not too hot to burn you. It stays hot until you turn it off. It is not programmable but that is not a feature that I'm crazy about anyway. The handle on the carafe isn't too small, just the right size. The carafe has a wide opening which makes it easy to clean and the glass carafe is just the same glass as a 12-cup, only smaller. The basket uses the 7" filters which I was already using in my old unit so I didn't have to buy new ones. I don't like the cone filters and I'm glad this one doesn't require them. I especially like that it doesn't take up as much counter space because I have a small kitchen and don't have much counter space to spare.

It doesn't brew as fast as a large coffee maker but that is no problem for me. I turn it on when I get up, then go get dressed. By the time i get back to the kitchen, it is finished. It does have the pause feature if you are in a hurry. So far, I'm very pleased with this little coffee maker and don't share any of the negative reviews. I did run plain water through the unit before making my first pot of coffee to clean it through and through. There was no bad plastic smell, no smell of any kind, and no bad taste of any kind from my first brew of coffee as others have mentioned. I don't grind my own coffee beans but I use Folgers pre-ground coffee, so i don't know anything about grinding your own beans and how this would be any different. i know some people are really picky about that kind of stuff, but I am not. I am more concerned about convenience. If you like stronger coffee, just add more grounds or less water, or both as there is no adjustment on this unit to make the coffee stronger or weaker.

As I have only had it for 3 days, I don't know anything about the lifespan of this unit, but so far, I am very pleased and loving the little coffee maker. I will update the review if it doesn't last long.

It is perfect for small kitchens, dorm rooms, etc., and is very light wright. It looks just like a 12-cup coffee maker, only smaller, without lots of bells and whistles- just a basic coffee maker. ( I've had 2 Keurigs in the past and neither one lasted more than a year- too expensive to keep replacing every year. I won't buy anymore of those) This little unit is perfect for me. Glad I found it and hope it last a long time.

reviews.review_title: convenient sized coffee maker for one person
reviews.review_description: Bought a 5 cup mini brew coffee maker to use for travel a few years ago. I remember it produced a pretty good tasting coffee. I broke the carafe and wasn’t sure whether to replace it or not but I’m glad I did. Again this one works pretty well even though there’s no bells and whistles for this coffee maker. Makes as good a cup of coffee as my more expensive coffee maker.

reviews.review_title: So glad I hit the buy button!
reviews.review_description:
For a long time I've searched for Mr. Coffee's 4 cup coffee maker but all I've found here and on eBay is one that's not used. That one is at a ridiculous price when you add in a highway-robbery price for delivery. What would show up in my searches on Amazon was this 5 cup version. I had resisted buying it for about a year, but finally ordered it a few nights ago -- then promptly cancelled the order because some reviews made me think I wouldn't like it. Fast-forward to last night shortly before midnight. I decided to give this maker a chance to prove it was worth buying, so I hit the buy button. It was here, waiting for me when I woke up today.

I love it. The design differences between this model and the 4 cup one were things I thought I would hate, but I don't. Really, I have only one quibble. The filters don't fit nicely in the filter holder, but that doesn't affect how they perform. Over time I may be disappointed if the pot's lid gets coffee stains on it. Cleaning this 5 cup model is easier than the 4 cup one is. That's because my hand fits more easily in the pot for drying it, thanks to the bigger size. I also like the finish on this model. It's mostly a matte white which will go with the matte white toaster oven I'll be receiving tomorrow.

I also like the on/off switch that is on both models. I use an Echo smart plug that I can turn on via my voice as soon as I wake up: "Alexa, turn on coffee." The switch is always in the on position but the plug is off until I tell Alexa to turn on the coffee. When the maker is on, I appreciate the fact there is not automatic shut off after a certain length of time, like there is with other coffee makers. When having two mugs of coffee, I often don't get around to drinking the second mug till an hour or more later. I want it to be hot when I'm ready for it. Reheating coffee in the microwave is not the same as having the pot on the heat. There's a scientific reason for this.

Now about the coffee: it tastes great with both models. I think it takes the 5 cup model longer to make the coffee but it's really not an issue. I will never brew 5 cups. Most often, I will use the 2-cup setting with 3 scoops of coffee. I like it strong. Someone needs to let Mr. Coffee know they are lousy at measuring cup sizes. My mug (which looks bigger in the photo than it actually is) holds 11 ounces. The 2 cup setting delivers a little less than 11 ounces. I think Mr. Coffee uses the usual cup size other coffee makers do: just 6 ounces per cup (not the expected 8 ounces for those of us who use a regular measuring cup for our cooking needs). But the 2 cup setting gives me less than 12 ounces. It's closer to 10.5 ounces. I doubt I'll ever use more than the 4 cup setting which will give me two mugs of coffee.

The pot is easier to pour from versus the 4 cup version. Getting the last little bit out of the 4 cup version is difficult, but super easy with the 5 cup version.

It's obvious I love this 5 cup model. I hope Mr. Coffee won't stop making it in the future like they did with the 4 cup version. When I need a new coffee maker, I want this model to be here, ready and waiting for me to hit the buy button again.

UPDATE: After using the coffee maker for a while I noticed the lid on the pot has a faint stain that I can't wash off. I expect it to get worse over time so I ordered the black version so I could use the black pot in my white coffee maker (see photo). I know it'll get stained too, but I won't be able to see it. Totally worth it. I'm adding two photos to show how it looks if you want to avoid the coffee stains. You can just use the black pot or you can adapt the white pot to accomplish the same thing. Just remove the just the white lid and snap the black lid into the white pot. Photos show what I mean, I hope. This white pot/black lid is what I'm happiest with.

My mother loves the wide mouth cup. Much easier for her to clean thoroughly, the way she likes. It brews coffee quickly and she loves it.

reviews.review_title: Great for someone living alone that just wants a small pot of coffee! Works great!
reviews.review_description: I bought this for my elderly aunt who’s 87 and still lives alone. She doesn’t like newer technology with too many settings and options. She just wanted a simple small coffee pot that would make body for her each day and this one works great and is very affordable. The only thing is it uses the smaller coffee filters so you’ll need to get some of those. However if you have regular ones they’ll fit you just have to kinda smash them in or cut them. Amazon sells a big pack of the smaller filters for like $3 or less so it’s worth it if you just need a small simple coffee pot

reviews.review_title: 5 stars but a disaster-rethinking buying another
reviews.review_description: I've been a Mr. Coffee user for 40 years. I love the 4 cup makers. This is the second time since Feb. 2025 that the coffee maker has stopped working. The first time 7 months into using it, it was replaced. So what to do this time. I am 10 months into using the replacement item. It makes great coffee and makes sense for a one-person user that's why I gave it 5 stars. BUT, it is a disaster in terms of longevity. What has happened to the quality of the product. QUALITY of things has gone down with the coffee maker.

Sitting here with my fresh brewed coffee from my new Mr. Coffee maker. Since I'm the only one in the family that likes coffee, this mini brewer is great for two cups. It's a simple machine that does not have all the frills like a 12 cup maker i.e. no timer, smaller carafe, small size, no automatic off heating plate. BUT for two quick cups of good brewed coffee, it's perfect.

reviews.review_title: Went with the OG that I grew up with in my mom's home.
reviews.review_description:
Finally, after FOUR unsuccessful attempts, I found something decent.

For the last three months, I have ordered THREE 5-cup coffee makers for my small apt that did not work out.

- The first I had to cancel b/c it was never shipped after 2 weeks.

- Next one, the timer did not work!

- Another one, the plug would not dislodge from the back of the unit's plastic housing - I tried pliers, etc but the damn thing was stuck INSIDE the small compartment and at risk of being completely ripped off if I kept trying.

- And then the final one - the glass carafe was as THIN as a light bulb that it broke when trying to gently wash it!

This Mr Coffee model is probably not the best for consumers expecting "luxury" quality for such a low price, but it brews, pours, and stays hot with no issue. AND the glass carafe is MUCH thicker and less "delicate" when handling it. The only star left off is that you need to be more careful of how you position the paper filter and the overhead spout that shoots water into it - If done the wrong way, the paper filter may fold at one side, thus leaving grinds on the bottom.

STILL at this price, and for my needs, go with the old goat of MR COFFEE - just like mom used.

title: Elite Gourmet EHC4128 Automatic 4-Cup Drip Coffee Maker, Black
description: Start your day off with the Elite Gourmet 4-Cup Automatic Coffeemaker. It’s compact and has a sleek design that takes up minimal counter space & stores easily when not in use. It’s perfect for small spaces such as office kitchens, dorm rooms or recreational vehicles. Quickly and effortlessly brew your favorite coffee to jump start your day or for an extra cup anytime. No need to stop at a local coffee house to buy a cup of joe just to make it through the day. Enjoy your favorite ground coffee without paper filters by using the included reusable filter. Simply add desired amount of fresh water for each brew. Cleanup is a cinch; all removable parts and accessories are top-shelf dishwasher safe. Enjoy a fresh, hot & delicious cup of joe on the go with the Elite Gourmet 4-Cup Automatic Coffeemaker.

reviews.review_description:
I knew this was tiny when I ordered it. I am not a fan of pods. I have done French press for single-serve. But I wanted a drip maker I could use a paper filter with (this takes #2 cone filters...or the included "permanent" filter, which is not the same as a paper filter, but I digress). But this is perfect for me ... their "four cups" makes just slightly more than a mug of coffee. See the photo. And that's not a huge mug. If you like drip coffee, but don't want to brew enough for the Waffle House, this is for you. Good value.

UPDATE: Now that I've had this awhile, not taking away any stars, but there are a couple things to note. As some other reviewer(s) have mentioned, you can't use the power switch without holding the unit down with your other hand. It requires too much pressure, and the unit is too light. The decanter is miniature in every way, including the pouring lip. So if you think you have to pour slowly from your full-size decanter that doesn't have a wide lip, you really have to slow down with this. When will product designers learn? EVERYONE likes a wide lip on the decanter, not just servers. NOBODY likes the little narrow ones. We're pouring into mugs, not espresso cups. And finally, the "sneak a cup" feature on this doesn't really work ... it continues to drip. I think maybe the spring is too weak, but it also could be the gasket isn't pliable/wide enough. But if you can't wait for this tiny little batch to brew, you are really jonesing. Anyway, still five stars, because, look at the price.

Best single serve ice coffee maker ever!! I’ve been using it for almost a month now, everyday (because now I’m addicted!), with no issues. Coffee comes out perfect & I love the cup that came with it, perfect for on the go! I’d give it 10 stars. Worth the price. Cute looking in the kitchen, small and fits anywhere. Quiet machine. Tells you how much water can be in the machine at once, if you overflow the water capacity it will spill out everywhere - but that was my fault on how I figured that out lol - I’d buy again and again!

reviews.review_title: Perfect Coffee Maker for Everyday Use
reviews.review_description:
I really like this coffee maker. I've been using it every day for about three months, and it has worked perfectly without any issues.

One of my favorite features is the reusable filter. It helps reduce waste, and I like not having to buy or throw away paper filters. The size is also perfect for one or two people. It makes just the right amount of coffee for my morning routine, and I can easily take some with me to work.

This is a simple coffee maker, but that's exactly what I was looking for. I enjoy starting my day with a hot cup of coffee, and bringing coffee from home has helped me save a lot of money by not buying coffee every day. Personally, I like to drink my coffee black, so I'd rather spend my money on high-quality coffee beans than on expensive coffee drinks.

Overall, I highly recommend this coffee maker. It's affordable, reliable, easy to use, and perfect for anyone who wants a simple machine that makes great coffee every day.

My upper cabinets are low and I don't have much counter space, so I was excited to find this coffee maker that is so compact. With the lid up, the height is only 17", so I don't even have to pull the machine forward to prep my coffee.

The machine heats the water just the right amount so the coffee comes out hot and flavorful, not burnt or oily. The plate keeps the brew at a good temp.

The only flaws is that the light gray warming plate has no sealant on it, so drips stain it.

However, this machine is still a great buy due to the low price point, efficient footprint, and awesome coffee.

reviews.review_title: At first, it was great. Then it wasn’t.
reviews.review_description: I’m being gracious with giving this coffee maker 3 stars. It makes good coffee, & at first, I was really happy w/ it, but about 45 days in, it began overflowing while brewing, sluggish & slow, & all around a mess. I do not recommend.

I only drink one cup of coffee daily. I love Starbucks Instant coffee, but I missed the smell and taste of a Drip. This is the Perfect solution. Great Price...Treat yourself. It has a wire basket but I get some cone shaped filters for a 2 cup and it's great. Enjoy! You Will Not be disappointed. Fast and Easy to. Use.

reviews.review_description: Love this coffee maker. The price was great and so easy to use. Easy to clean and coffee taste great. Replaced a former maker of the same model. Brew time great.

It works and does exactly what I need it to do. Brew Coffee. What a concept. And you don't need a Training Class on how to use it and how many buttons to push and program it. I like my Coffee Strong and Hot, so I use enough coffee and a little less water. And you turn it ON or OFF. Amazing!!! It's almost like it was designed to do that or something. Good Job Mr. Coffee.
Easy to use. Doesn't have a bunch of gadgets you have to figure out. Just a regular coffee maker. I'm happy with my purchase. No k cups, no descaling, just makes coffee the old fashion way.

reviews.review_title: These work great but don't last long!
reviews.review_description: For the past ten years I have been using this 12-cup Mr Coffee model. I never turn it off... use it 24/7. They last from six months to just over a year. I have bought about ten, five through Amazon. It used to be the switch would fail (even though never turned it off), but I replaced switches and would generally get well over a year from them. Then, two of the machines (over the years) developed internal leaks, and I could not find the leaks from the bottom, but they were leaking. Two or three of the machines had heating coil failures. The price has continued to increase over the years, so I bought a 12-cup Black and Decker this time. I have owned it two days and I like it fine. The carafes are interchangeable with the Mr Coffee ones (I have a lot of those), so that's nice. I already ordered my second Black and Decker, because the price is great and I hate being without my daily coffee (hot tea actually). I throw two larger tea bags where the coffee filter and grounds go and make tea most of the time. For the second pitcher I throw one more tea bag on top and so, get two pitchers from three tea bags... the tea bags cost $3.25 for 24 bags, so I get 16 12-cup pitchers of nice strong tea for $3.25.

So in my humble opinion, coffee pots shouldn't be as expensive as some of them are. Pour water over the coffee grounds and into a pot with a heating element under it. With that being said I have seen some coffee pots run in the Easley over $100 range. Now okay I understand if you want to have a clock involved so it can start your coffee for you, that's fine and I'm sure that'll cost a couple extra dollars, and if you want something really nice and prestigious looking because you care what your guests think about what you've spent on random items then yeah drop a hundred bucks on a nice one maybe it's stainless steel or something and has a good company logo on the front of it.

Personally, I'm not that difficult. I get up in the morning I push the button on this thing and by the time I get out of the shower I've got a nice hot pot of coffee waiting for me and life is good. The only thing I wish this had and this is only because my previous pot did have this option is that if you don't turn this off it'll just stay on all day and you really don't want to cook that empty pot all day. There is a light on the button so if you're leaving the house and the light is still on yeah you might want to shut this off. And honestly after a couple weeks I got into the habit of making sure I shut it off as I picked up the pot to pour my coffee so it hasn't really been an issue, it was only a problem for a week or two because like I said my previous pot automatically shut off so I got lazy and just let it do its thing. So anyway, if you're just looking for something to make your coffee, and you don't really want to spend $50 or $100, I've had this for quite a while now and it works great. I do have well water which has a lot of extra minerals and crap in it so I do find myself doing a 50% vinegar solution which you pretty much need to do with any coffee pot from time to time but in my case a little more often... And other than that, I expect this thing's going to last me a few more years.

reviews.review_description: So simple to use. I didn't want a programmable coffeemaker (don't need bells and whistles). Just a simple on/off switch. The coffeemaker is lightweight (don't need it to be heavy), and easy to move around the countertop. Pull away from the wall when making coffee, put back against the wall when done. *** updated 1/16/2021***

It’s been a few weeks. I tried one more time but the flavor is still there. Maybe it’ll go away but I had also purchased a pitcher that boils watet for tea and it’s great with a. French press we had that I forgot to use. This product I declare as junk for me and regret the purchase thus rating it a one star. I no longer have incentive to try again so it’s unlikely I’ll come back for another updated review.

********

I’m going to start this review off by talking about filters. There are cone filters and then there are flimsy filters. Until I went back to these flimsy filters, I never fully appreciated the cone filters and this will impact future machine purchases for me.

Cone filters pack flat meaning storage is less invasive. The hood their shape and are less likely to spill and the won’t collapse when transferring to compost or garbage. It’s a little thing but I appreciate it.

So, the point of all this, is that mr coffee uses the flimsy filters. Surprisingly there are a lot of machines that don’t use the cones, which is disappointing.

First impressions:

The plastic look and felt cheap. I saw reviews that commented about the cheapness of this machine and shrugged it off. Other machines are made of plastic after all. This plastic looks and feels somehow cheaper. I instantly had a negative association to it.

The side windows which advertised visibility from both points was a selling point for me. What was failed to be mentioned is that you can’t read the clear numbers when contrasted against a black background or steam. I wrote the marks in with permanent marker to be able to see when filling.

One feature I did like is that the spout moves out of the way and the lid snaps it back into place. Simple and elegant engineering. I would never clean these grounds out when hot though. Recipe for spilt grounds and burns.

The prep

It requires a washing and a single run to remove the plastic flavor, per instructions. I ran 4 times after I washed and before the first use. The plastic smell seemed gone.

The usage

The first cup seemed fine. Additional uses the plastic taste and smell crept in strongly. I ran a cleanse through it four more times and it’s still there rendering expensive coffee undrinkable.

My wife felt like the first coffee had a weird flavor, so maybe I didn’t notice the first time? The fact we have flushed this so many times and the flavor persists is deeply concerning to me. I’ve owned a few coffee machines and never had this issue persist for so long. I’m going to keep trying and if something changes, I’ll update. I’d like this to be a good machine for me, but it’s not.

The water heats quickly! This is a lot faster than my older coffee makers!

The lighted switch is more subtle than I’d like. It’s a dot vs the entire switch, but in the end my wife and I turn it off after the last cup and it’s not an issue as we both stay at home now. There is no auto shut off.

The drip stop works okay. A few drips will come out if you pull early, but it does stop while you pour a cup. A critical feature for my wife.

The carafe pours well at an okay speed without dripping down the side. Some will leak if overly full and you have to pour slooooowly to avoid spillage. This seems better designed.

This steams a lot and should not be under a cabinet when running. It WILL damage the cabinets. It’s easy to pull out and push back in.

The summary:

Would I purchase again? No. Even if the flavor fixes itself, I have concerns about the cheapness of this machine and the plastic used and the health impact. I couldn’t find anywhere that discussed if it was bpa free. I hadn’t been concerned because sunbeam owns me coffee, but after seeing and feeling the cheapness of the plastic, and with the plastic taste still present, I’m concerned.

It is cheap, the functionality seems good for just a weeks ownership, but the lack of drinkable coffee is an issue. Even if that’s resolved, there’s concern in the back of my mind about the long term health impact of this machine.

Hopefully this is helpful. I’d recommend spending more money as I feel I wasted $28 and will be purchasing a new coffee maker, again.

description: With a programmable timer that lets you set your brew up to 24 hours in advance, you can wake up to fresh coffee every morning. reviews.review_description: We're simple people when it comes to coffee. We drink a lot. Love the 12 cup size. reviews.review_title: Beautiful sleak design, but the thing stopped working after only a few weeks.

reviews.review_title: Love it and worth the cost!!!

This is the 2nd Bella product I've bought. I also have the narrow 2 slice toaster in the same color. The coffee maker is programmable, compact and brews quickly. Bella makes some of the most attractive appliances out there. If you want quality and want to spice up your kitchen, check out the beautiful offerings brom Bella. Very happy with my purchases.

Bella is the love of my life. She is so pretty and smells incredible. She makes my coffee every morning. I am always happy to see her. I take care of my Bella by emptying the grounds and leaving the top open so it can dry out. It stays clean and I can brew up to 12 cups. reviews.review_title: Excellent Coffee Maker - the BEST actually...
reviews.review_description:
We've owned several Keurig coffee makers over the years, and we're big fans of single cup brews.

Unfortunately, we've also had every single Keurig machine break down on us...which has become very frustrating, AND expensive.

Combine that with the fact that our favorite K-cups have gone WAY up in price, it just wasn't sustainable any longer to continue with Keurig.

After looking around at alternatives, I found this Ninja coffee maker and I thought the option to brew a full carafe or single cups of coffee to be exactly what I was looking for.

For those that use the feature, there is also an automatic brew option, so you can set it before bed, and wake up to a carafe or cup of coffee in the morning without the wait if you should so choose.

I can't really speak about the issues I've read on here regarding leaking carafes, etc. because we really only brew one cup at a time.

For this purpose, this coffee machine works perfectly.

It does take a little longer to brew a single cup than a Keurig, but the coffee and options you have are so much better than a Keurig.

Because you can fill your filter basket however you like, you can make your coffee as strong or as weak as you like because you're no longer limited to a pre-measured K-cup.

So, the coffee tastes far superior to K-cups, AND overall, it's MUCH cheaper to buy coffee.

Also, your coffee options are no longer limited to brands that produce K-cups. You can buy ANY coffee.

I know, some people will say you can buy K-cup pods and fill them with your favorite coffee...but I've done that plenty of times, and they ALWAYS taste weak to me.

Fast forward to today, we've had this machine for over a year now and thankfully we've had zero problems with it at all (unlike our previous 5 Keurig machines).

Personally, based on our experience with this Ninja, I would definitely recommend this coffee maker to anyone who loves coffee, and I would absolutely purchase it again - with zero hesitation.

It also is a stunning-looking machine that would look amazing on any countertop.

Definitely the best coffee maker I have ever owned.

reviews.review_title: 2nd Ninja Coffee Machine and it just gets better!
reviews.review_description:
Imagine spending $400 on a drip coffee maker and throwing it out in less than a year. Yeap, replaced a Moccamaster with a Ninja Specialty and I could not be happier. Love coffee, mostly drink 4-6 cups of freshly ground coffee a day. I had an older basic Ninja for several years before giving it to my son and wife, thinking it was a win win, so that when I visited I could enjoy a great cup of coffee, while at home I thought I would upgrade to a superior coffee machine (Moccamaster recommended by Wirecutter). The Moccamaster was a rip off. Could not fathom spending that kind of money, just to throw it away. Right? Tolerated it for less than a year then couldn't stand it anymore. In the garbage it went. Lesson learned.

Ninja Specialty surpasses my expectation. First it makes excellent coffee. Can choose classic or bold, cup, mug, half or full pot, and the machine adjusts accordingly. The ease of use now is great, don't have to pull the machine out from under the cabinet anymore since the filter holder pulls out the front area. The water reservoir can also be removed from the side and be filled or washed. Has its own scoop that shows how much coffee is recommended depending on the brew cycle. Have not tried the frother yet. Another improvement is that if you want to grab a cup before the brew finishes you just move a lever to the left, which pauses the brew, this is important because all the machines I ever had, when you pull the carafe out, some coffee drops still drip on the hot plate which fizzles and stains the base. What a great great well thought out and tested machine. Highly recommend!

Ninja appears to build products that are built around what their customers want while others appear to build products based on profitability and greed, using their brand well initially as a trap then turning their goods into garbage and charging excessively for inferior products. Again, lesson learned.

reviews.review_title: For under $200, this is a great machine!
reviews.review_description:
I never write reviews, but if you’re like me, you’re going to research new coffee machines like it’s your second job… hah. So here I am, about a month into owning the 10 cup model with an honest review. I LOVE IT. Between me and my husband, we use it 2-3x a day and have nothing but praise for it. We are not coffee snobs by any means, but we wanted to get away from kcups/nespresso pods (due to the waste) and after using a Keurig for many years, decided to make the switch to this very popular machine. I didn’t have too many requirements other than something programmable and the ability to brew different amounts.

I’ll start with the things I love about it:

1. Easy setup + use. After everything was washed and I ran a clean cycle, the machine was ready for use. To brew coffee, you select the size then choose if you want “classic” or “rich”. Once you select, it starts blinking and then will begin to brew shortly after. Brew times are fairly quick, no complaints there. A full carafe (on the classic setting) brews in roughly 8 minutes. The delay brew option is easy to use as well. I usually set up the machine at night for my husband so he has coffee waiting for him at 5:30a when he gets up for work. The machine brews in a few minutes and is fairly quiet — it does beep several times once done, but does not disturb me or our young toddler. I don’t find it loud or disruptive.

2. Features. Honestly, this machine is well equipped for under $200. Several options for brew sizes, the classic vs rich, option to brew a specialty 4oz cup (not espresso since it doesn’t get hot enough, but I’m not picky and it works for a quick at home option), brew over ice, and of course the built in frother. It would be nice if the frother warmed the milk too, but I just pop it into the microwave to heat prior to frothing. Froths nicely! I also really love the included measuring scoop. It attaches to the machine for convenience. I follow the guides for number of scoops and use it every time I need to measure the grounds.

3. The aesthetic look of the machine and feel of quality. It looks nice on my kitchen counter and doesn’t take up a lot of room. Plus it’s nice the frother folds in to make it even more compact. The included glass carafe feels good and doesn’t feel cheap or too thin. Overall I feel the quality of the machine is nice for the price.

I read a lot of the complaints, which I’ve had zero issues with. There is no plastic taste/smell anywhere on the machine. I did thoroughly wash each piece and ran a clean cycle prior to use, but I didn’t even notice a smell when I unpacked the machine. Coffee is plenty hot and there is even a “stay warm” feature you can choose after brewing your coffee (it does automatically come on after brewing a half/full carafe), but sometimes I will use the multi serve option and brew it into the included carafe then turn on the stay warm feature if it’s going to take me more than a bit to drink the 2 cups I usually get from it. I have never once had any grounds in my coffee after brewing. You can use the included filter or brew using #4 cone filters.

I really love this machine and do not miss my Keurig at all. Of course time will tell if it stands up to daily use, but as of now I’m thrilled with this purchase and hope to have it for several years. Hope this review helps someone! Enjoy ☕️

reviews.review_description: Buy this!! I love waking up to the smell of coffee, and this machine does it right everytime. So, like you all ,I've been a coffeeholic for many years. Like you ,I've struggled to have a decent maker in my kitchen. I recently finished up with my Cuisinart mod#CHW-12. Had it for 5yrs. It got to point of no longer producing a well tasting cup. We did the Vinigar cleaning etc. So, i spent MANY hours searching online for a decent Maker. Problem was the abundance of poor reviews encompassing many manufacturers! It's now 2018 and we have trouble creating a Kit Coffee Brewer thats decent! I did a switch and desired a maker that will produce a single cup as wife n i both have coffee at different times and mostly need the one 16oz cup. In searching for the 12cup Carafe / or single cup Maker ,my choices became limited. Read the reviews and pulled the trigger on this. It's only been 1wk now but i can honestly state that it is the BEST maker I've ever used! I ran a full 12cup Carafe first off, thn dumped. Then did same for the single cup side. ( full 14oz). Then ran 12cups clean water through for both. Then did the Coffee that I'll drink. No issues. Had to play round wth the exact amount of grounds for the single side so to get the outcome i desired. Has clock, easy to pre prog., and, the single side will turn off when done. The Carafe side will stay on (hot plate) for 2hrs after brewing complete. You can simply press On/Off button to turn off anytime. For those who have an over-spilling issue with the grounds within the gold filter basket?, you are using TOO MANY grounds! The single side comes with a gold reusable filter which also encompasses two - Level markers. One is min and the other is Max. If you fill above the Max level, WELL, overflow of grounds will prob. occur. On the Amazon site you'll see the Reusable filter for the Carafe side in " frequently ordered with". I also ordered that as i don't like paper filters. It performs well. Water level for Carafe is helpful. It's towards the right rear, on the side. It's accurate. Brew time for 12 cups was good. I've learned to warm up my Mug when using single side as it is not as hot as Carafe as no hot plate for the Mug. I use single side to run water for tea as well. What would make this model perfect? If it sounded out a tone when brewing is complete. It also has No charcoal filter as with my Cuisinart. No biggie as i always have used filtered water to begin with. Coffee is better when there's no Chlorine in the H2O! Filling either the Carafe or single side is easy and Max level markers are visible enough to get it right. Carafe pours very well and i like that the Carafe lid stays attached as u simply press thumb to open but it's not required to pour. Single side grounds chamber pulls out easily. reviews.review_title: Very happy with this coffee maker!
reviews.review_description:
Delighted with this coffee maker! It arrived on time and in good condition. I had a very expensive coffee maker that quit working and thought I would save some money and try this Hamilton Beach version. SO glad I did!

The set up was easy and that first morning I was very happy with my hot delicious, coffee!

The single serve option is important to me and it works perfectly. I LOVE having a single cup of coffee without using a k-cup!

Highly recommend this machine!

It's about what you'd expect for a mid-range Hamilton Beach coffee maker. Normal price of $80 feels a bit steep, but I think it's worth what I paid for it on prime day. It does what it says on the box/product listing and it works better than the dollar store coffeemakers you'd find in an economy hotel room. Looks to be of quality from afar, is somewhat cheap and plastic feeling when you actually use it. Just sturdy enough that I'm not concerned that I'll break it. Single serve and full carafe functions do not share a water tank, and you fill the single serve reservoir with exactly as much water as you want to brew into coffee. Pretty intuitive and I guess pretty standard for this type of coffeemaker. But if you are used to filling the tank once a week and brewing a set 6oz or 8oz this is not that. "Brew Options" button toggles between bold and regular brew strength.... And that's it. There's no way to set brew temperature, but the default temperature is fine. It brews a single serve in about 3 minutes or so. Faster than a drip coffeemaker of yesteryear but if you're expecting it to be as fast as a pod system you're looking in the wrong place. The thing that matters most though is how the coffee comes out, and I have to say it's worth the extra hassle of using loose ground coffee and filters as it's much better than pod-brewed coffee. The slower brew speed results in a better coffee. Much more cost effective than pods too. The reusable single serve filter is surprisingly easy to rinse out. For $50 it's not bad. I would not pay $80 for this. At a price point of $80 I expect to at least be able to choose a brew temperature, even if there are a few pre-sets instead of by-degree. If you can get this for under $60 and you are specifically looking for a coffeemaker that doesn't use pods, then I can recommend it. Otherwise at full price, I don't think it offers enough to differentiate it from other $60 coffeemakers to justify the extra $20. It does have a clock in it and the ability to set a time to automatically start brewing at a set time, which is a feature I really don't use, but for some maybe this will make the $80 asking price worth it as I am not sure if this feature is commonly available in cheaper options.

reviews.review_title: Great coffee maker- single cup or full pot
reviews.review_description:
This the best coffee pot I've ever owned, seriously. I appreciate good coffee and regularly buy beans from a local roastery. I am not a barista nor do I claim to be a coffee expert. I enjoy good coffee and a drip coffee maker is good enough for my daily habit.

This maker can be used to brew single cups on one side or a full pot on the other side. Typically, I am the only coffee drinker in my house. Sometimes we have guests. This coffee maker allows me to serve both situations easily.

To use the single serve side, I fill the cup that I'm planning to use with the correct amount of tap water and add it to the single serve side of the maker. This is accessed from the top under a small lid that flips up. This side is designed to only hold enough water for a single serve amount of water. I don't use manufactured pods as I prefer fresh grounds but this maker apparently can handle pods too. I grind my beans or use pre-ground coffee and add that to the slide out tray on the single serve side just above the cup location. There is a metallic mesh screen that holds the grounds on the single serve side and I find that I waste less coffee than when I try to make only 1 or 2 cups in a large pot. The single serve side has a nested set of plastic circles that sits under a tall mug when not needed. These little circular risers can be un-nested and stacked to allow a shorter cup to be closer to the dripping coffee (see photos). This allows the maker to accommodate a variety of sizes of cups. The single serve side takes about 2 minutes to brew. I think the coffee tastes great and I can control the strength of the brew based upon how many grounds I add.

The full carafe side is much like any basic drip-coffee maker. There’s a small reservoir that holds enough water to brew a full pot of coffee. There’s a flip lid and a basket for coffee grounds. You can use paper filters or buy a separate metallic, re-usable mesh filter that fits inside this basket. I like these baskets as it’s less wasteful than using paper filters daily and I don’t have to remember to constantly purchase filters. I’ve used the same mesh filter for over 7 years now. It doesn’t filter as finely as paper filters do and the last sip of coffee contains a small amount of grit / sediment but this seems normal to me now. If someone doesn’t like this idea than I would warn them not to drink the last sip. It’s pretty easy to avoid.

The coffee maker has a very obvious and easy to use manual switch that selects whether you are brewing a full pot or a single serve. Only one side can be used at a time. You simply move the switch to the left or right as the illustrations show to select which side you wish to utilize.

I frequently use the timer feature. Prior to work I have one 16 oz metal travel mug filled, warm and waiting for me when I wake up in the morning.

The display is bright when you touch a button and dims to normal again after about 30 seconds so it doesn’t light up the kitchen at night like a beacon. There is a single bright green LED light that indicates that the timer is set and ready to go. Personally, I like this feature as it is an obvious acknowledgment that the timer is ready to go at the time that I programmed in. Some might find this too bright but it’s hard to imagine it being a nuisance to most people.

Other reviewers have indicated the their carafe broke instantly upon the first use. I’ve used my carafe several times without issues. I also noticed that a new pot is around $10 so if it does break down the road, I can probably replace it easily. Some said that it tastes like plastic, I haven’t experienced this. Some said that it leaks after 3 months – I’ll try to update this review later but so far so good – no leaks. Others say it takes too long to brew. I think it takes about as long to make coffee as every other coffeepot that I have owned and if you set it up the night before, you won’t have to wait for it. It can be ready for you whenever you tell it to be ready. I even read that some people were annoyed that they had to slide the coffee pot out from under a counter in order to add water to the top of the coffee maker. I once added felt pads to the bottom of a coffee maker to make this process easier. Without a dedicated water line and a commercial coffee apparatus, I’m not sure how the manufacturer would avoid this overly burdensome task. You have to add water somehow; that’s how coffee works.

I have not had any negative issues at all with this coffee maker and I’ve been using it daily for over 1 month. It’s easy to use, it’s easy to program and I like that I can make a full pot or single cup depending on my needs. I definitely recommend this unit.

reviews.review_title: Exactly the coffee maker that I was looking for!
reviews.review_description:
I bought this coffee maker after my previous one finally broke. I was specifically looking for a few key features which this coffee maker had. I wanted a coffee maker that had a mechanical On/Off switch, and I wanted a coffee maker that did NOT automatically shut off after a period of time. The reason I wanted these features is because I am slowly but surely turning my home into a “smart home” and I have been wanting to automate as many things as I can. Surprisingly at the time I was looking at this coffee maker I don’t believe there was a coffee maker with native Apple HomeKit compatibility. To my knowledge as of October, 2023 there still isn’t. That wasn’t a big deal, because I have a smart outlet that I plugged the coffee maker into. Now I can have the coffee maker turn on and start brewing coffee at whatever time I set up the automation for, so that when I finally get out of bed the coffee is already brewing. Yes, I could have done that with an automatic coffee maker that has a built-in timer, but this is great because I can program the outlet to turn on/off at various times or set up stipulations that someone has to be home in order for it work (preventing the coffee maker from doing its thing when we are away from home and forgot to turn off the auto feature on other coffee pots that we have had.)

I also really appreciate the fact that it doesn’t auto shutoff after 2 or 4 hours. I know that is meant to be a safety feature, but with my smart home it is an unnecessary feature. I have an automation set up that when the last person leaves home it shuts the outlet off. Normally I don’t assume that the automation will work, but in case I forget it will take care of it for me.

Another feature, and I am not sure if this was a deliberate feature or not, but I have noticed that when it is brewing, occasionally it will pause brewing for a short time (maybe 30-45 seconds??) and that is good, because it allows me to pick up the coffee pot when it is still brewing and pour myself a cup if I am too impatient to wait for it to finish. It DOES have “pause and pour” meaning that there is a check valve that shuts off the flow to the carafe so that the coffee doesn’t just continue to keep pouring out on to the burner, but with this pause there is typically ZERO drips. May sound like a little thing (and truthfully it is), but that little drip gets on to the burner and the water quickly evaporates leaving coffee residue which I would have to clean up later. If I wait until the brewing temporarily pauses on its own then I prevent even a single drip. Like I said it is a small thing, but it is just one more small little thing that makes me really like this coffee pot even more.

It is so ironic in a day and age when things are getting more technical and more sophisticated that I would willingly choose a coffee pot that is as simple as it can possibly get. I have had coffee makers that were far more sophisticated, but in the end I want to be able to control the coffee maker via my smart home and not have the coffee maker control itself.

Lastly, I wanted to mention that the coffee pot is very reasonably priced at just under $30. The fact that I got a good quality coffee maker that is exactly what I was looking for and it also was among the lowest price that Amazon had to offer is a win-win for me! I have zero regrets buying this coffee maker. Actually, that’s not true — I wish I would have bought it sooner! If you’re on the fence, go ahead and get it — it’s a beautifully simple coffee pot which is exactly what I was looking for!

My last coffee maker was the keurig duo. After 3 years it started making noises and brewing the wrong cup suzes. I searched every coffee maker for a replacement and found this ninja. I loved everything about it especially the ground coffee basket. It has an attached frother on one side and slide in basket on the other side which holds the ground coffee basket. The ground coffee scoop attaches to the side. It was packed in the ninja box in another. Everything was wrapped separately. It took a lot more time unpacking it than it did to set it up. It brewed the coffee which was surprisingly too hot to take more than a tiny sip. I really liked this machine and it came in moss green. I left for an hour. I have been loving this coffee maker! I have had a favorite coffee maker for years, and it suddenly died. I agonized over a replacement, because I liked that one so much and used it several times a day. It is still made, but the reviews reflected that it is not made for durability like it was when I bought it. I absolutely love this Ninja! I generally use coffee pods, so this is right up my alley. It is so quiet! It will make a variety of sizes for ups, mugs, travel mugs, and iced coffee. One of the features I look for is the ability to brew a strong cup from a pod. The “rich” function on this machine, does the trick! It doesn’t just run water straight through the pod, so that the flavor is lacking. It puts water through the pod in increments to get as much flavor as possible. I used the “over ice” function for the first time yesterday, and it also works slowly enough to pull as much flavor as it can. It was delicious! The brew time is really short, and yet the coffee tastes wonderful, and the temperature is perfectly hot. The machine and it’s components are very easy to clean. It takes up more space from front to back, but has very slim lines and looks good on the counter. The water tank is easy to remove, clean, and fill. I know a couple of people have mentioned having an issue with “exploding pods.” I had this happen ONE time, but I immediately realized why. When you put the pod in the machine, if you just pull the lid down, it may not fully puncture the bottom of the pod appropriately. This causes the hot water to overfill the pod, and it bursts from the pressure. There is a super simple fix!! All you have to do is place the pod in the machine, and press it down, so you feel it puncture the bottom of the pod. THEN close the lid to puncture the top! That’s it! Nothing difficult or time consuming. Just press the pod down before you close the lid. Problem solved! I haven’t had any issues since! 😊 I really am enjoying the ease of use and versatility of this machine. I think it is well made, and will be used for a long time. It is sturdy, without being bulky or heavy. The materials are sleek and easy to clean. I looked at dozens of coffee makers, and read SO many reviews before I made this purchase. The comments about the potential “exploding pods” had me a little concerned, but as I said, that won’t ever be a problem for me after realizing what can cause the issue. I’m an extremely picky person when it comes to my beloved coffee maker, and this Ninja has won me over!

reviews.review_title: Excellent Coffee Maker for Strong Coffee
reviews.review_description:
When my name brand (not K) coffee maker went to the big coffee bean in the sky, I decided that $200 was a bit pricy for something that lasted only 4 years. For the most part, I grind beans and use the filter. We don't drink a lot of coffee and I like being able to customize each cup. So I went on a search for the ideal single serve coffee brewer. After trying 2 other brewers, each with problems, I decided to give Ninja the old college try. Boy, am I glad I did.

My husband for the most part, drinks a regular cup of coffee with cream and sugar. I make a hot latte every day. I have a really good moka pot, but I wanted a machine capable of making a really strong cup of coffee, which doesn't seem to exist in the majority of name brands. I gave up on the big K a long time ago.

I don't use the frother. Maybe one day I will. What caught my immediate attention is the large (and I mean LARGE) filter coffee holder. It holds at least 1/2 cup of coffee! It's ginormous. I use 3 scoops to 12oz water, set on "rich" for my latte, mixed with 8oz hot milk. At first I thought I did something wrong, or that it was defective. A little water came out, and it stopped. On try #3, I decided to let it sit. Sure enough, after a minute or so, it continued. (Perhaps I should have looked at the instructions first?). Lol. What it was doing was allowing the water to soak into the grounds, to extract the coffee.

This is the first time in our almost 40 years of marriage, that my husband said his coffee was too strong (and he lived in Germany for 20 years).

The maker automatically detects whether you have inserted the filter or kcup. The display is intuitive and easy to program. It remembers your last setting. The brewer is Ninja quality. I've owned several Ninja appliances over the years, all still going strong.

If you want a regular cup of coffee, Ninja will provide. If you want a truly strong cup of coffee, Ninja will give it to you. If anyone thinks it doesn't brew a strong cup, they're either not using enough coffee, they're using the wrong blend, or they haven't tried using the filter. Also, all accessories are stored onboard. There's a nifty drawer on the right side that stores the filter or kcup holder, while your using the other. It's a very well thought out machine. The price is very reasonable.
