reviews.review_title: This Keurig is My Favorite Kitchen Appliance and It's Well-Worth the Money We Spent!
reviews.review_description:
***Updates are located at the bottom of this review.***

***Original Review***

Up until recently, I had never been much of a coffee drinker except for the occasional seasonal flavored latte drinks but I was having trouble keeping up with my very active twin toddlers. We already had a standard coffee maker but I didn't want to brew a whole pot of coffee at once and single-serve coffee makers seem to be very popular so I figured it couldn't hurt to give it a try. I had seen several different Keurigs from the basic ones to very fancy ones but wanted to purchase one that both fulfilled my needs to brew a single cup of coffee and wasn't too expensive so I opted to buy the Keurig K55 Coffee Maker in black.

When the Keurig arrived, I eagerly opened up the box to get it set up and start using it! I found it fairly simple to set up since there is a Use and Care Guide included and it's easy to follow the step-by-step instructions. I'd say the setup only takes a few minutes and then you are ready to brew your first cup of coffee. There are lights on the brewer that illuminate and walk you through the brewing process but once you are used to it, it becomes second nature and now, I don't even have to think about it, which is good in the early morning when I'm not thinking straight and need my coffee!

Brewing: To brew a cup of coffee is very simple. You'll need to turn on the brewer by pushing the power button. The power button and heating lights will illuminate and the Keurig will make some noises while it heats up. When the three cup sizes illuminate in blue, you know it's time to brew your coffee. Set your coffee mug on top of the drip tray and lift the handle for the K-cup pod holder. Place a K-cup pod in the holder and lower the handle completely until the three cup sizes are blinking. The three sizes are: small cup (5.25 ounces), small mug (7.25 ounces) and large mug (9.25 ounces). Select your size and the coffee will be ready in about a minute. If the water reservoir is low on water, the "add water" light will illuminate and the process won't continue until you've filled the reservoir. Once it's stopped dripping, you may remove your mug and enjoy your coffee! If someone else wants to brew a cup of coffee right after yours is done, all they have to do is remove your K-cup pod since they are single-use pods, add theirs and repeat the process.

Water Reservoir: The reservoir holds 48 ounces of water so you don't have to fill it up every time you want to brew a new cup of coffee, which is one of the reasons I selected this model. I make about two cups of coffee every day so I end up refilling the reservoir every few days. There are filters to use with the water but I purchase bottled water so I haven't used the filters at this point. When the reservoir needs to be filled, I remove the reservoir, take off the lid, fill it up with water, place the reservoir back in the Keurig and replace the top.

Cleaning: I feel this Keurig is fairly simple to clean. The drip tray is removable and I usually wipe it down with a damp paper towel a couple times a week and wash it in water, soapy water occasionally. I also like to wipe down the exterior since the front part of the Keurig gets splatters of coffee on it. You can also clean the pod holder, funnel, needles and water reservoir and lid. Be careful as the two needles used to puncture holes in the K-cup pods are very sharp.

Coffee Pods (the best part!): The Keurig K55 Coffee Maker uses the K-cup pods, which you can purchase nearly everywhere and there are many brands and flavors to choose from. You don't need to buy any specific brand with this coffee maker. As long as they are K-cups, they should work and I haven't come across any pods that don't work. I've been having a lot of fun purchasing different flavors and brands since I have several friends and family members who also have Keurigs so it's a lot of fun to swap coffees! I prefer flavored coffees and there are so many out there to try but my favorites are the Green Mountain flavors in Caramel Vanilla Creme and Wild Mountain Blueberry. There are K-cup pods in different price ranges and it's nice to have that option since everyone has a different budget. The nice thing with this brewer is that the flavors don't tend to blend from one cup to the next. For instance, my mom and I have brewed cups of coffee one right after the other (different flavors) and neither of us have noticed the other flavor in our respective cups. I've only brewed one cup of apple cider with this and haven't noticed the previous coffee flavor in the apple cider or the apple cider in my next cup of coffee. In this brewer, you can use all kinds of coffee flavors from flavored to medium and dark roasts to hot chocolate to apple cider. I typically choose the small mug (7.25 ounces) setting since I like the flavor. It isn't too strong or too watered-down for me but others may prefer other settings.

Programmable Auto Off Timer: You can set the brewer to turn off two hours after the last cup of coffee has brewed (included in the instructions). I just turn the Keurig on and off as I need it but it's nice to have that option.

Noise: Some people have stated that this brewer is noisy. I've found it's the noisiest when it's taking water from the reservoir and it sounds like a loud hum. It's not too loud when it's brewing the cup of coffee. I occasionally get up earlier than my husband and kids and brew a cup of coffee and no one has woken up (I'd say there is about 30 feet between the kitchen and bedrooms with the doors closed). When we have guests and they brew coffee before I wake up, I can't hear it at all.

This Keurig is made in China and mine had a packaging date of August 2016, a month before I purchased it. I've been using it for two months and haven't had any problems with it at all. It measures about 12 inches deep (from front to back), nine inches wide (side to side) and 13 1/2 inches tall. I've had several family members use it and my parents and in-laws have found it fairly simple to use after I show them how to brew the coffee since we all have different models. Ever since I started drinking coffee, I've had better success with staying more alert and awake to take care of my twins and buying this Keurig has been well-worth every penny we spent on it! I have no regrets buying it and have been having a lot of fun finding different flavors to try. As with all of my reviews and especially any appliances and electronics reviews, I will periodically update this review, add in any new information I discover and adjust my thoughts and star rating, if needed. If you, or someone you know, is interested in a Keurig, I highly recommend this one. It's a great model that is nice on your wallet and will brew a great cup of coffee as often as you'd like!

***Update 04/25/2017 - I've had this Keurig now for almost eight months and it's still working great for us! I typically brew four cups of coffee a day now to keep up with my kids and I've had no trouble with using this Keurig. When we have guests and are switching pods a lot, I never notice a strange taste at all (since we all like different flavors). reviews.review_title: One Week With My Keurig K55. I Love It!
reviews.review_description:
There are numerous detailed reviews of the Keurig K55 and other models on Amazon and I see no reason to repeat or refute other reviewers' opinions, so I'll limit my review to my impressions based on one week's use and experimentation with various coffees and other beverages that my wife and I have tried and enjoyed.

I don't consider myself to be a "coffee snob" but I drink a lot of coffee and insist on a good. fresh cup of coffee, properly brewed to my personal taste. For more than 20 years, I've used Saeco super automatic espresso/coffee machines such as this one:https://smile.amazon.com/Saeco-Philips-Intelia-Espresso-Machine/dp/B019771XIE/ref=sr_1_1?s=kitchen&ie=UTF8&qid=1481465394&sr=1-1&keywords=saeco+super+automatic+espresso+machine&refinements=p_89%3ASaeco ranging in cost from about $600 to $2,500 depending on the model. These super automatic machines allow you to load whole bean coffee of your choice into a hopper and at the push of a button, it grinds the beans, loads them into the brew unit, dispenses the coffee, then dumps the used grounds and is ready to brew another cup at the touch of a button. They are completely adjustable so you can brew your coffee as strong as you like, from espresso to fairly weak American-style coffee. They also have a steamer which allows you to make cappuccino and other coffee beverages. I love these machines and they make great coffee, but they have disadvantages. First, because you have to load the whole beans in the hopper, it isn't easy to change to a different coffee if other family members drink decaf, for example, or prefer lighter or darker roasts. Also, they only brew coffees, no other beverages. Lastly, they are complicated and require quite a bit of maintenance.

Enter the Keurig K55, which is their least expensive basic model but does everything I expect. I purchased it for my wife who likes to drink my lighter coffee as well as various teas, hot chocolate, cider, etc. My thought was to let her use the Keurig and to continue making my coffee in my Saeco but I've found that the Keurig makes very good coffee and suspect that my Saeco will be retired because the Keurig is so much more convenient to use and maintain and I'm completely satisfied with the coffee I'm brewing in it, perhaps not quite as "great" as that I make in my Saeco more than satisfactory, and far superior to the coffee I buy in restaurants, donut shops and convenience stores.

I won't recommend particular k-cup coffee brands because there are so many of them and everyone has different preferences. One of the main advantages to the Keurig is that there are so many choices available, with three brew strength/ water level settings, as well as a great variety of other hot beverages such as black and herbal teas, hot chocolates, ciders, and more.

You can also buy reusable k-cup holders and any ground coffee you like. This may save a little money and also allows you to choose your favorite coffee even if it isn't available in K-cups. I ordered a set of these reusable k-cups and have tried them with several ground coffees, comparing them to the prefilled k-cup versions of the same coffees. The k-cup ones are as good or better than the ones I've loaded myself using the reusable k-cups and are SO MUCH easier and more convenient to use. They're a little more expensive but still reasonably priced, particularly if you buy them in bulk from Amazon, Sam's Club, etc., or find them on sale at your local supermarket. On average, I'm paying less around 40 cents a pod for mine. Other k-cup beverages such as teas and hot chocolate tend to be less expensive than the premium coffees I buy.

The real advantages to the Keurig are convenience, ease of use and the variety of coffees and beverages you can make with it, including iced teas and other iced beverages. My wife and I can share a single machine and make our own preferred beverages quickly and easily. After she makes a flavored beverage, I simply run a shot of hot water through the machine to remove any off-taste before brewing my coffee.

Although I won't recommend specific brands due to personal tastes, I will mention that I prefer well-balanced, slightly acidic medium to medium dark roasts. I don't like breakfast blends or other light roasts, nor do I like really dark roasts such as those typical of some coffee shops such as Starbucks, although I have tried some of the dark roasts from Starbucks k-cups and others and they are fine, just not to my taste. I usually use the medium water level (7.25 oz) setting. Depending on the coffee I'm using, this usually gives me a rich, well-balanced, fairly strong cup of coffee. For some lighter roast coffees I prefer the low (5.25 oz) setting. My wife doesn't like strong coffee and usually uses the high (7.25 oz) setting. Teas, ciders and hot chocolate usually taste better with the high water level setting.

If you are considering giving the Keurig a try, I recommend that you consider buying one of the many sampler k-cup packs available on Amazon. Some are coffee only and others include assorted flavored coffee, cappuccino, tea, hot chocolate, cider, etc. The one I bought is this one: https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00KSIE39I/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o07_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 . It was a good choice and my wife and I quickly discovered our favorites. We've also bought a few others to try (on sale) at my local supermarket. All were good, even though some weren't to my personal taste. Once you decide on your favorites and the brew strength you prefer, you're all set to make good, fresh coffee and other k-cup beverages easily and conveniently.

I mentioned at the beginning of my review that I'm not a "coffee snob" but I do insist on good fresh coffee, brewed to my personal taste. The Keurig accomplishes this. I realize that many people ARE purists (coffee snobs, in my parlance). If so, you probably won't like the Keurig but for 95% of all coffee drinkers, the Keurig is great. I'm more than willing to give up my "perfect" cup for one that's almost as good and so much easier and more convenient to brew, not to mention all of the other beverages it will make.

I can see why the Keurig has become so popular. It fully deserves the five star rating I've given it. I highly recommend it to most coffee drinkers. I'm less convinced that it's the best solution to brew tea. It's okay but I still think it's worth the effort to brew tea by steeping it (using the Keurig to dispense hot water for brewing it if you wish). However, K-cup hot tea and iced teas aren't bad and are certainly quick and easy.

reviews.review_title: Well-Designed with Superior Performance -The Very Best Coffee Maker That We Have Owned In 40 Years
reviews.review_description:
In the forty years of our marriage, we have owned several well-known brands of coffee makers. However, we feel that the Keurig K55 coffee maker has proved superior to any of our previous coffee brewers.

Last year I invested in our first Keurig coffee maker, and I chose the K15 for individual servings. This worked out so well that a few months later, I bought another for my office and I loved my second Keurig as much as I loved the first one. Then last winter I decided to purchase another Keurig, only a different model that would accommodate several servings.

I bought the K55 model because it has various featured options. This includes offering the choice for different hot beverages without the extra step to refill the tank each time with water, and this is due to the larger 48 oz. water reservoir. In addition, this enables us to make a variety of hot beverages in rapid succession, within a few seconds instead of waiting for all the water to reheat. Furthermore, the Keurig K55 offers a personal ‘custom tailored’ brew by letting us determine the strength of our coffee, and we have a choice of three. The smallest amount for a 6 oz. provides the strongest brew and the other two servings are an 8 and 10 oz.

I like strong coffee, or sometimes I like to have flavored coffee, and my sister-in-law likes the same coffee that I do. My husband prefers a milder brew, and he never drinks flavored coffee. My son drinks tea, and likes to try different varieties and my grandson loves sampling different selections of hot chocolate.

The Keurig K55 has a fast set-up, with easy to follow and systematic directions from the manual. It offers us a variety ways to make coffee, tea or just to heat water and all without any major modifications, because it just goes from one task to another.

Below are some of the general features, and all are well designed and ‘user friendly’.

CONTROL PANEL:

All the controls are on the top right of the coffee maker and I like the flat slope surface that slightly slants down toward my eye level, and therefore, I don’t need to step on my tiptoes to read the buttons.

On the panel, there are 5 press buttons and each one has an LED light to reduce ‘user error’.

Power: Green LED

Auto Off: Green LED - (this is the automatic timer and when activated will automatically power off after 2 hours).

3 Brew Size Servings – corresponding size to the serving size and each with a Blue LED

a. Cup Size - yields 6 oz. – which will provide the strongest brew

b. Small Mug - produces 8 oz.

c. Large Mug – dispenses 10 oz.

Aside from the 5 press buttons to regulate the Keurig coffee maker, there are 3 other LED light indicators.

1. Add Water – a Blue LED will light up

If there is not enough water, the coffee maker will not work, therefore I consider this indicator as a safety feature, as well as a resolution to a possible ‘user error’.

2. Descale – will light up with a Red LED light

This is another handy feature, to indicate necessary cleaning maintenance.

3. Heating – while the water is heating, a red LED powers on, and then powers off when the water is hot and ready for a brew.

WATER RESERVOIR:

Included with the Keurig K55 is a Charcoal Water filter Cartridge Kit with 2 charcoal filters. This will eliminate the unwanted chemical taste that is in some water systems, and good tasting water is essential for a delicious cup of coffee. The recommended life span for each charcoal filter is approximately 2 months or 60 ‘full-tank’ refills. There are several selections for Replacement Charcoal Filter-Pods available on Amazon.com.

The water reservoir attached to the left side is easy to remove with a slight lift up and outward motion. It fits inside a base and the tank is easy to remove and replace without any struggle. Alternatively, remove the reservoir tank cover, and pour water in from a bottle or a container.

DRIP TRAY:

This is much more than ‘just a drip tray’, under the cover is a 1” deep receptacle that will accommodate 8 oz. of a liquid spillover. Therefore, if the user makes an error and pushes the wrong brew amount for a smaller cup, this will save the kitchen counters and the floor from a major flood.

In addition, this coffee maker will accommodate my 7 ¼” coffee thermos by sliding the drip tray out from bottom base, and I can have my thermos filled when placed on the bottom flat tray base.

THE KEURIG K55 ACCOMMODATES REUSABLE COFFEE FILTERS:

My favorite coffee is from fresh beans that I grind myself, and therefore it’s important to me that a coffee maker will accommodate a reusable filter. The K-Cup pod holder on the K55 is very easy to remove and it literally takes less than 10 seconds. Just tap the bottom of the pod holder with a finger and the K-Cup holder slides out with ease. The reusable K-cup filter then slides in place within the groove, and works with perfection for a delicious cup of fresh ground beans, or any ground coffee.

The reusable coffer pod filter that I use is the Keurig My K-Cup Reusable Coffee Filter (Single) – and this is compatible with the Keurig K55 model.

I purchased this from Amazon last spring, and in addition, I use this same filter with my Keurig K15.

https://www.amazon.com/Keurig-5048-Reusable-Coffee-Filter/dp/B000DLB2FI/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1486296530&sr=8-1&keywords=Keurig+My+K-Cup+Reusable+Coffee+Filter+%28Single%29

In conclusion, the Keurig K55 is a well thought-out designed coffee maker, with user-friendly features. This machine comes with a ‘Charcoal Water Filter Cartridge Kit and 2 charcoal pod filters, which guarantees excellent coffee, even though we have ‘hard water’ (which tastes awful) in our water system. In addition, I love that Keurig does NOT use a breakable glass carafe, which was the thing that broke most often with our previous coffee makers.

reviews.review_title: Easy to use and small space
reviews.review_description:
I’ve been using the Keurig K-Mini Mate for about three months now, and it has quickly become one of the most practical additions to my morning routine. Living in a condo with limited counter space, I was hesitant to buy a bulky coffee maker. The K-Mini Mate solved that problem instantly. It is remarkably compact—less than five inches wide—meaning it slips effortlessly into tight corners without cluttering the kitchen.

Despite its small footprint, the machine delivers exactly what you need from an everyday single-serve brewer. The operation - EASY TO USE. You pour water into the rear reservoir, drop in your favorite K-Cup pod or one of those reusable pods - place your mug on the drip tray, and press the brew button. Within a couple of minutes, you have a fresh, piping hot cup of coffee ready to go. If you remove the drip tray at the bottom, it fits a full 7-inch travel mug with ease.

In terms of performance, the temperature of the coffee is consistently hot, and the flavor extraction is great for a pod system. It brews relatively quietly compared to older Keurig models I have used in the past, which is a huge plus if you are waking up earlier than the rest of the household. I also appreciate the automatic off feature, which shuts the machine down 90 seconds after your last brew. It is a subtle touch, but it gives me peace of mind knowing I will not accidentally leave it running all day.

Cleaning and maintenance are as straightforward as it gets. The removable drip tray catches any accidental overflow or drips and washes easily in the sink. Because you pour fresh water in for every single cup rather than keeping a large standing water tank, the water always tastes fresh, and there is less worry about stagnant water sitting in the reservoir overnight.

reviews.review_title: Super easy to use-- perfect for travel!
reviews.review_description: I bought this after our old single serve Keurig broke after many years. I love the convenience of the size and how easy it is to use. The old one had a little learning curve to it but this one is user friendly. We use it when we travel since I drink tea or decaff coffee and my husband drinks caffeinated coffee. We bring our own K-cups so we can both have what we prefer, and it doesn't take up much room in the baggage.

We bought this to replace our dinosaur Keurig. We had the OG silver, bulky, heavy Keurig. It lasted us a lifetime then died a sudden death. We actually mourned! We have a camper now so I bought this new mini to be a space saver. I like it. I don’t love it yet but I like it. It’s small, lightweight and does the job. It splatters quite a bit, so we drape a lightweight kitchen rag over it while it brews. I’ve also noticed it doesn’t push out all the water every brew. After each brew we immediately remove the pod and toss it. Then randomly I open it later and find the pod area filled with water. Where does this water come from?? Tapping the brew button forces that water to be purged but I have to know why it’s there! It never seems like our cup of coffee is lacking a couple tablespoons so I just don’t know. Maybe a small bit is held back each brew until it creates enough to send it to the pod area. I’m perplexed. Also, if I brew plain water for tea after we have brewed coffee, I have to flush it out with 2 cycles of water or my tea is yucky, ashtray smelling tea. It really clings to that coffee smell!! That being said, love the size and weight, it brews really hot, pretty darn fast and the color is cute. So, 4 stars.

I absolutely love this Keurig K-Mini coffee maker. I never thought I'd resort to such a small coffee maker but I am so happy I did. It is so compact and makes the coffee so quickly. reviews.review_title: Excellent Coffee Maker - the BEST actually...
reviews.review_description:
We've owned several Keurig coffee makers over the years, and we're big fans of single cup brews.

Unfortunately, we've also had every single Keurig machine break down on us...which has become very frustrating, AND expensive.

Combine that with the fact that our favorite K-cups have gone WAY up in price, it just wasn't sustainable any longer to continue with Keurig.

After looking around at alternatives, I found this Ninja coffee maker and I thought the option to brew a full carafe or single cups of coffee to be exactly what I was looking for.

For those that use the feature, there is also an automatic brew option, so you can set it before bed, and wake up to a carafe or cup of coffee in the morning without the wait if you should so choose.

I can't really speak about the issues I've read on here regarding leaking carafes, etc. because we really only brew one cup at a time.

For this purpose, this coffee machine works perfectly.

It does take a little longer to brew a single cup than a Keurig, but the coffee and options you have are so much better than a Keurig.

Because you can fill your filter basket however you like, you can make your coffee as strong or as weak as you like because you're no longer limited to a pre-measured K-cup.

So, the coffee tastes far superior to K-cups, AND overall, it's MUCH cheaper to buy coffee.

Also, your coffee options are no longer limited to brands that produce K-cups. You can buy ANY coffee.

I know, some people will say you can buy K-cup pods and fill them with your favorite coffee...but I've done that plenty of times, and they ALWAYS taste weak to me.

Fast forward to today, we've had this machine for over a year now and thankfully we've had zero problems with it at all (unlike our previous 5 Keurig machines).

Personally, based on our experience with this Ninja, I would definitely recommend this coffee maker to anyone who loves coffee, and I would absolutely purchase it again - with zero hesitation.

It also is a stunning-looking machine that would look amazing on any countertop.

Definitely the best coffee maker I have ever owned.

What a great great well thought out and tested machine. Highly recommend!

Ninja appears to build products that are built around what their customers want while others appear to build products based on profitability and greed, using their brand well initially as a trap then turning their goods into garbage and charging excessively for inferior products. reviews.review_title: 🔄Updated Review — Now 8 Months of Daily Use (see full update below)
reviews.review_description:
🔄 Updated Review — Now 8 Months of Daily Use (see full update below)

⭐️Original Review:

My husband and I are huge coffee lovers and have tried many types of brewers over the years. This Ninja was purchased in early August, and I intentionally waited until October to write my initial review so I could give a thorough, real-use perspective.

My husband loves experimenting with flavors, foam, and different styles, and he is thrilled with how much versatility this one machine offers.

This coffee maker is used at least 4–5 times every single day (no judgment 😅), and every time we use it, we’re able to make something different — hot coffee, iced coffee, lattes, cappuccinos, and more.

☕ What You Get:

Coffee maker unit

Smart scoop (labeled per serving size)

Frother wand attachment

Tempered glass carafe with smart funnel

Permanent filter + filter basket

Flip-top water reservoir

De-clogger tool

Instruction manual

Usage & Features:

Cup Size Options:

Cup

XL Cup

Travel Tumbler

Multi-Serve Tumbler

Half Carafe

Full Carafe

You can switch between sizes easily with a simple knob turn.

Drip Stop Feature:

Acts like a quick pause, allowing you to pour a cup mid-brew without making a mess — super useful when brewing larger amounts.

Even when making a small cup, it still tastes like a full, properly brewed pot — not watered down like some machines. It takes a few minutes to fully extract flavor, which makes a noticeable difference.

☕ Brew Styles:

Classic

Rich

Over Ice

For iced coffee, I fill a cup with ice, add fresh coffee grounds to the filter, and brew using the “Over Ice” setting — it comes out perfectly balanced and not diluted.

Frother Wand:

One of my favorite features.

Add milk or creamer to a cup, place it under the wand, and run it for about 30 seconds — it creates a smooth foam that takes drinks to another level.

Cleaning & Storage:

Cleaning is simple and low maintenance:

Filters remove easily for rinsing

All removable parts are dishwasher safe

Grounds are easy to discard and clean out

When the descale light comes on, running a vinegar + water cycle through the reservoir gets everything back to normal quickly.

The adjustable platform is also great — it flips up to fit larger tumblers or the full carafe.

⚠️ Things to Know:

This machine does not use pods or K-cups

It is designed for ground coffee only

Personally, I actually prefer this — it’s much easier to clean a filter than deal with small reusable pods.

⭐️ Original Conclusion:

This quickly became my favorite appliance in the house, and I recommend it to anyone looking for a reliable, versatile coffee maker.

🔄 8-MONTH UPDATE (HEAVY DAILY USE — 4–5x A DAY)

I originally reviewed this after about 2 months of use. I’ve now been using it for closer to 8 months, and it’s still used heavily every single day — plus regular large iced coffee batches.

I wanted to come back and share a true long-term update for anyone wondering if it holds up.

☕ Real-Life Performance After 8 Months:

•No wear or damage

•No cracks or weak points

•No rust anywhere

•No slowing down or performance issues

•Still brews consistently hot coffee every time

•It honestly performs the same as it did when it was brand new.

Cleaning & Maintenance (Still Easy):

Regular hand washing

Occasional dishwasher use

reviews.review_title: For under $200, this is a great machine!
reviews.review_description:
I never write reviews, but if you’re like me, you’re going to research new coffee machines like it’s your second job… hah. So here I am, about a month into owning the 10 cup model with an honest review. I LOVE IT. Between me and my husband, we use it 2-3x a day and have nothing but praise for it. We are not coffee snobs by any means, but we wanted to get away from kcups/nespresso pods (due to the waste) and after using a Keurig for many years, decided to make the switch to this very popular machine. I didn’t have too many requirements other than something programmable and the ability to brew different amounts.

I’ll start with the things I love about it:

1. Easy setup + use. After everything was washed and I ran a clean cycle, the machine was ready for use. To brew coffee, you select the size then choose if you want “classic” or “rich”. Once you select, it starts blinking and then will begin to brew shortly after. Brew times are fairly quick, no complaints there. A full carafe (on the classic setting) brews in roughly 8 minutes. The delay brew option is easy to use as well. I usually set up the machine at night for my husband so he has coffee waiting for him at 5:30a when he gets up for work. The machine brews in a few minutes and is fairly quiet — it does beep several times once done, but does not disturb me or our young toddler. I don’t find it loud or disruptive.

2. Features. Honestly, this machine is well equipped for under $200. Several options for brew sizes, the classic vs rich, option to brew a specialty 4oz cup (not espresso since it doesn’t get hot enough, but I’m not picky and it works for a quick at home option), brew over ice, and of course the built in frother. It would be nice if the frother warmed the milk too, but I just pop it into the microwave to heat prior to frothing. Froths nicely! I also really love the included measuring scoop. It attaches to the machine for convenience. I follow the guides for number of scoops and use it every time I need to measure the grounds.

3. The aesthetic look of the machine and feel of quality. It looks nice on my kitchen counter and doesn’t take up a lot of room. Plus it’s nice the frother folds in to make it even more compact. The included glass carafe feels good and doesn’t feel cheap or too thin. Overall I feel the quality of the machine is nice for the price.

I read a lot of the complaints, which I’ve had zero issues with. There is no plastic taste/smell anywhere on the machine. I did thoroughly wash each piece and ran a clean cycle prior to use, but I didn’t even notice a smell when I unpacked the machine. Coffee is plenty hot and there is even a “stay warm” feature you can choose after brewing your coffee (it does automatically come on after brewing a half/full carafe), but sometimes I will use the multi serve option and brew it into the included carafe then turn on the stay warm feature if it’s going to take me more than a bit to drink the 2 cups I usually get from it. I have never once had any grounds in my coffee after brewing. You can use the included filter or brew using #4 cone filters.

I really love this machine and do not miss my Keurig at all. Of course time will tell if it stands up to daily use, but as of now I’m thrilled with this purchase and hope to have it for several years. Hope this review helps someone! Enjoy ☕️

reviews.review_title: Nearly Eight Years of Service—Good Enough to Buy Again
reviews.review_description:
I originally purchased the Cuisinart DCC-3200 PerfectTemp 14-Cup Programmable Coffeemaker on October 31, 2018, for $75.92. Nearly eight years later, it still makes excellent, hot coffee. It recently began making a slight squeaking noise during the brewing cycle, so I decided to play it safe and purchase the same model again on August 2, 2026.

That should say plenty about how much I like this coffee maker. It is dependable, easy to operate, makes a full 14-cup pot, and has served me well for almost eight years. I would not have bought the exact same model again if the first one had not performed so well.

My only complaint is the price increase. The original cost $75.92, while the replacement cost $107.43 before tax—an increase of $31.51, or about 41%. Even with the higher price, its performance and longevity made it worth buying again. Five stars.

reviews.review_title: Love it for a consistently good and easy cup of coffee
reviews.review_description: Love love love it for a consistently good cup of coffee and so easy! This is our second one of this exact same coffee pot, the previous one lasted about 7 years until it got a crack somewhere and started leaking so the value for the money is definitely there. We debated getting something different this time around but I couldn’t stray from something that we already knew worked great and we never had any issues with. Consistently brews a great flavor and temperature cup of coffee, easy to clean and set up. Would definitely recommend, and the fact that you can set it up the night before and program it to brew is a great feature!

One of the best and cheapest, good looking coffee makers out there. I have one at home and one at the office for years and it works everyday. The coffee is hot, it keeps it fairly hot not burned, easy to fill, easy to add coffee. I have bought many coffee makers and some are much much more expensive. But just for a good consistent pot of coffee once you get the correct measurements of coffee and water I think there is none better. It came with the gold filter which is good since I never use paper, it has a few brew temp and carafe temps and you can set the timer to brew automatically. It does not take up much space is fairly easy to keep clean. The water tank though does take a bit of work to get clean and keep clean though. Over time it gets pretty rank and I cleaned mine by spraying soap and Clorox in it and using a dishrag to clean it out. I then rinsed it out in the sink all the time being upside down so as this would not enter the brew track. Once cleaned and rinsed then filled with water and ran a couple of pots of water through it and its as good as new. Now unless your a professional, I don't recommend doing this LOL but it never stopped working and never stopped brewing a good cup of coffee. Looks and works as good as the day it was purchased. I did buy another one and had a funeral for the old one after many years. It still worked, so it was hard to part with but the wife said we had to get a new one. Sheesh, Why? O well you know how that goes.

I ordered this coffee maker after researching it as thoroughly as possible. Much to my disappointment, the initial batches of coffee tasted like plastic. I ran carafes of filtered water through the device several times, but the taste of plastic persisted. Then I used ChatGPT to see what information was available and sure enough, this is a common problem. It would have been nice if Cuisinart had addressed this issue in the manual. This is why I am giving a 3 star rating.

My next step was to use coffee cleaner, followed by 2 more carafes of filtered water. I could still smell the plastic in the filter basket, so I washed it with a strong mixture of Dawn detergent. Then I ran another carafe of water through it. That finally seems to have gotten rid of the plastic taste in brewed coffee. The entire process probably used several gallons of filtered water and took several days to complete.

Otherwise, this coffee maker is well designed and of good quality. The plastic components are thick, unlike the current Moccamaster plastic parts which are thin and flimsy by comparison. (The Moccamaster also has a tube attached to the carafe lid that’s unnecessary, cumbersome and hard to wash. Their old models have a separate tube which isn’t used for the same reason.)

I desperately needed a replacement coffee maker and I’m glad I persisted in my efforts to get rid of the plastic taste instead of returning it. This makes good coffee as other reviews have stated. Just be prepared to get rid of the plastic taste.

UPDATE

As of February 7th, I need to revise my rating to 4 stars. Except for the problem with the plastic taste I explained above, this is a high-quality product that makes good coffee. I love the 1 - 4 cup feature which is what I use to make 24 ounces of coffee. If you drink coffee black and enjoy the flavor of good coffee, you will love this feature. This makes the best coffee I've ever tasted. That said, the initial plastic taste with no mention of it in the manual is a major problem that has to be overcome.

UPDATE AFTER USING FOR 6 WEEKS:

I've been using this new Cuisinart almost every day for 6 weeks, and have NEVER had any issues

with the carafe leaking/spilling OR the condensation on the maker lid leaking water onto my

countertop when I open it up to add coffee grounds and pour water into the reservoir.

Not even once. The only thing I can think of to explain SOME of those carafe complaints

is that they are trying to pour from the carafe TOO fast. I must admit 10 years ago when I FIRST got

my old Cuisinart2800, I tried pouring from the carafe and poured too fast and spilled. But just a slight

slow down fixed it and no issues since. But other than that pour speed issue, I have no idea what those

reviewers were doing to cause the maker or the carafe to leak water as they described.

Everything else I wrote in my initial review still stands too!

=============================================================

I read thru a LOT of reviews on this Cuisinart DCC3200NAS (this is the SS and Black).

I JUST set it up on my countertop last night and ran a pot of plain hot water thru it as suggested.

This morning I made my first pot of coffee in it!! 9 cups. Very tasty coffee!

BUT this review is NOT about how good the coffee is. Nearly all the reviews have established that its great.

This review addresses a few of the most common complaints about this coffee maker.

FYI: This new 3200 replaced a refurbed Cuisinart DCC2800WFR I had for 10 years that recently started leaking water.

The MOST common complaint is the carafe. I am honestly NOT sure why. The new carafe seems IDENTICAL

(except black plastic vs white) to the carafe that was on my 2800 that I used for 10 years with no issues.

Spout dripping: The easiest way to MAKE the spout drip is pouring too fast. Just slow your pour down a TICH.

I put water for 9 cups in my carafe and poured it into my water reservoir in about 10 seconds without spilling a

drop. It works exactly the same way AND as well as my 2800 carafe did for 10 years. No spills. No issues.

HELPFUL HINT: Make SURE the 3200 lid is FULLY opened (past 90 degrees) before you try to fill the reservoir.

Then just rest the carafe spout on the SIDE of the reservoir with the water level indicator. Pour. Done.

Carafe Lid not hinged and/or too tough to take off and/or put back on properly:

Not hinged is true! But why is that bad? I don't know. It snaps off and on easily for me. Has for 10 years.

And I don't even bother taking the lid off to fill the carafe with water. Just fill it thru the spout hole!

The new carafe lid DOES require a SLIGHTLY firmer push to pop it off and back on than my old carafe, but I'm

guessing in 12 months this one will pop off and on a little easier than it does now too.

HELPFUL HINT: Pop the carafe lid off by LIFTING the tab that your thumb sits on when holding the carafe.

Pop it back on in reverse: Insert spout side first, then pop the thumb side down. Done. Easy peasy.

The 3200 control panel is significantly different from my old 2800. I read a couple reviews that suggested

the 3200 control panel was difficult to understand and use properly!?! I found the exact opposite to be true.

Once you know exactly what option each button controls (button labels seem clear & obvious to me), setting the

options properly is completely simple. As you press each button, it cycles thru the available settings for that option.

Stop pressing that button when that option is set to your liking. If you miss it, cycle around again. Done.

The basket the filter sits in DOES need to be PUSHED fully back down such that it "pops" down into the maker after

being removed (in my 2800, it just dropped in loosely). BUT that is obvious to the careful user since it requires that

same "pop" to remove that basket in the first place. If that basket is NOT popped down into place, the carafe lid

won't reach (much less push up on) the spring loaded valve on the underside of that basket, so that valve would stay

closed, and as your maker dumps more water into your filter, coffee grounds will overflow your filter and go

everywhere including the bottom of the water reservoir. PS: Same thing happens if you put a LIDLESS carafe

in the coffee maker! Lid isn't there to push up on the valve, so the valve stays closed.

I found the 5 "Coffee is Done" beeps and the 2 "Heating Pad Off" beeps to be the right volume for my house.

Not loud, BUT loud enough that on a normal (ie: semi-quiet) morning, I can hear it from the next room easy.

AND it is super fast and easy to turn the beeping off and back on with the "Tone" option button if you need to.

Bottom Line for me:

I am boggled by all the carafe and reservoir filling issues so many reviewers have! I have NO dripping issues or

lid issues with my carafe, NO reservoir filling issues, and NO setup or control panel issues. All 5 stars.

Now lets just see if it stands the test of time like my 2800 did!

This has been a great coffee maker. Its large capacity is great for when you have company it fits in a small footprint and it keeps the coffee hot! The programming is easy to use and it brews fairly quickly. I am very pleased with it.

This BKSP1 (black stainless appearance) 14-cup coffeemaker replaced a 12+ year old Cuisinart 12-cup unit we used until it finally quit working. Great coffeemaker and it produced great coffee. My research to replace the old unit settled on the BKSP1 model and Amazon delivered straight-a-way.

I got it all cleansed out, programmed and set up for begin brewing at 4:45 the next morning. It brewed a great pot of coffee and all worked wonderfully ... EXCEPT that the clock on the BKSP1 was running FAST. It had "gained" almost an hour since I had set it up the day before. Thus the coffee was actually brewed at ~3:45AM.

I reset the clock and kept watching it as I would walk by the coffeemaker and noted that it was gaining time or running FAST. I went through this for several days and finally sent a message to Amazon C.S. and they immediately replaced with another BKSP1 and I returned the original unit.

I went through the setup process with the #2 BKSP1 and was hopeful that the clock would keep proper time ... however it did not. The clock on the #2 BKSP1 also ran FAST. The coffeemaker worked just fine in all regards ... save for the clock running FAST.

So, I reached out to Cuisinart/Conair C.S. with this "fast clock" issue and they replaced the #2 BKSP1 with the #3 BKSP1. I did all the setup with #3 and lo & behold ... the clock on the #3 BKSP1 also runs FAST. All other elements work just fine, brews great coffee, but the clock just has a mind of it's own.

So (you can guess what is next), I reached out to Cuisinart/Conair C.S. (again) with the fast clock issue noted in graf above. A ticket was established and I was shipped a #4 BKSP1 to replace the #3 unit.

Can you see where this is going? The #4 BKSP1 unit was set up and put into service and the clock on #4 also runs FAST.

So ... it appears that there is something common going on with the BKSP1 model units.

This time I called Cuisinart/Conair C.S. (I had been establishing all other tickets via the inter-web and e-mail). The lady with C.S. was simply excellent and she noted my BKSP1 ticket history and said she would have another unit shipped out straight-a-way. She asked if I still wanted the same BKSP1 model or would I want to get the SP1 model (SP1 is the brushed stainless appearance). I figured what the heck ... I would get the SP1 this time.

In a couple days I received the #5 SP1, got it all set up and ready to brew coffee the next morning at 4:45. I would glance at the clock on the #5 SP1 as I walked by the unit and the clock was ACCURATE. I was again hopeful that the clock would hold and keep proper time.

At 4:45AM the brew cycle started and it actually was at 4:45AM. The clock held it's accuracy for one day at that point.

It has now been 3-days and the clock on the #5 SP1 is "spot on".

So (there is the 'so' word again) I noted on the boxes the coffeemakers were shipped in had the countries of manufacture stamped on them. The BKSP1 units were all manufactured in China. The SP1 unit was manufactured in Indonesia. AHA - I said. There is a manufacturing plant issue going on.

I did an extensive observation letter to Cuisinart/Conair about my situation and thoughts of what is going on.

BTW - In addition the BKSP1 units all dripped extensive moisture droplets down the back side of the unit when the top lid was opened to removed the coffee grounds. This had me wondering if there was a leak as there was water all over the counter under the BKSP1 units.

Turns out the drip lip on the upper back of the BKSP1 appears to be 'flat' without adequate slope to have the water droplets flow back into the reservoir. Also the drip lip is not as deep as what I noticed on the SP1 units.

I also observed (on both the BKSP1 and SP1 models) that there is a lot of moisture condensation that collects on the upper front panel where the control buttons are located. To me this could affect the electronics that I'm guessing is located near or behind this panel.

Ergo couple items of note for Cuisinart/Conair:

1) Production molds for the BKSP1 and SP1 are NOT the same between the China and Indonesia manufacturing plants. Thus the drip lip issue noted above.

2) The chips/electronics being used in the China plant for the BKSP1 are defective and can't keep proper time.

All-in-all ... The Cuisinart 14-cup coffeemaker is an excellent product and works very well and produces great coffee. Save for the units (in my case) that are manufactured in China where the chips/electronics they are using just don't work. Adding to that the manufacturing mold difference that slightly changes the size of the drip lip on the upper back.

I would suggest getting the the SP1 model and keep your fingers crossed that it is also manufactured in Indonesia as opposed to China. At least until such time as changes are made in the manufacturing facility in China to correct the noted issues.

Cheers,

Nolan K.

reviews.review_title: Best coffee machine I’ve ever owned (and I’ve had a few!)
reviews.review_description: I researched extensively before buying this espresso machine. I came across a number of reports of defective machines but decided to take a chance based on Ninja’s reputation. I’m so glad I did! The machine is extremely solid and well built. It can make everything from regular coffee to espresso to iced coffees. This is a very sophisticated machine and reading the manual is essential for a good result. The coffee produced smells and tastes amazing. The milk frother works better than any frother I’ve had before. The bean hopper holds a large amount of coffee beans which I appreciate. I find the speed of the machine to be good and comparable to other espresso machines I’ve had. I’ve seen reports of the coffee produced being too hot or too cold but mine has been perfect for me for each type of drink. Given the many different types of coffee beverages this machine makes with ease, I highly recommend it. In fact, I went to stay with relatives for a month over the holidays and I took the machine with me!

I'm very happy with this machine and its ability to make different types of coffee. I don't intend to use it for drip at all, but I've been using it for espresso-type drinks with excellent results. The fact that it makes brewing easy, while still keeping you mostly in control, mostly means you're learning about WHY something is working or isn't working. This machine helps you tweak temperature, strength, and extraction separately. You get guidance, but it's up to you if you listen to it based on what you're trying to extract. Is it perfect? No. It's not meant to be, though. It's meant to be convenient for a beginner. That said, it's expensive, but you do get good functionality for that price.

I wanted something that wouldn't take away my ability to tweak, in case I got more into espresso, but if I decided not to I could still get good coffee. This delivers.

Well thought out design that makes great espressos, classic coffee, and even cold brew tastes great. The Pro version is worth the extra. We have a secondary grinder for another set of beans but still use the machine’s tamper and the rest still works.

I bought this beautiful machine in December of 24 as a Christmas for myself from my husband and I actually had surgery on Tuesday and that may seem irrelevant but stay with me. On Tuesday of this week 07/14/26 is when my baby decided to start smelling like something was burning and would not turn on. I was devastated 💔. reviews.review_title: Great product but it stopped working after 8 months. The warrantee was honored.
reviews.review_description:
I've used Keurig coffee makers for many years. I really like the K-Supreme. It's compact, brews a cup of coffee quickly, has a strong brew option and I like having the serving size options (4, 8, 10 and 12oz). The problem I had is it stopped working after 8 months - it would not power on. Granted I used the coffee maker a lot - 5 to 6 cups a day - but it should last longer than 8 months. My guess, and it's just a guess, is the thermal fuse went - there was a slight "burnt electronics" smell when it stopped working. Keurig did honor the 1 year warrantee and shipped me a brand new replacement unit at no cost and I did not have to return the defective unit. A word of warning, I had to prove the unit was purchased on Amazon and shipped directly by Amazon. Apparently, Keurig may not honor the warrantee if the unit was purchased from a third party seller. The warrantee claim process was challenging at best. The call center is most likely overseas. Information like your email address is repeated back to you in a Alpha Charlie Bravo manner. Even with that, the Agent got it wrong and I waited about a week for an email to start the claims process. A call back confirmand they had my email address wrong. I submitted the required proof of purchased information and my claim was denied. Another call resolved that when I pointed out the receipt showed I purchased the item on Amazon and I told the Agent I had additional proof the unit was shipped directly by Amazon. My claim was then approved and I received a brand new replacement with all accessories in about one week.

reviews.review_title: Great coffee maker so far upgrade over previous generations
reviews.review_description:
OK so this review is an overall review of not just the product but Amazon as well. I have had this machine around 3 months now.

The machine itself is amazing. The ease of use from the previous generation one is night and day.

Things i like:

The handle on the water reservoir.. finally.. LoL. The reservoir plastic is also thicker and more durable. My previous model reservoir was thinner plastic and cracked and it was also curved. This machine's water container is rectangular so more solid. That in itself makes this machine worth it.

This machine makes hotter coffee and the over ice feature is nice.

I love the grey color.

What i dont like:

Lid will not close all the way with reusable K-cups. Will not close even with the Keurig branded ones. This is only cosmetic it seems though. Functionality seems unchanged.

When i use this coffee maker the LED lights in the kitchen will flicker. The previous model did NOT do this and had similar wattage rating and a grounded plug. The wattage is listed on this newer machine is 1520W. the only other thing on the same circuit is the LED lights.

This coffee maker does NOT have a grounded plug. Maybe this is why the lights flicker?

I got a great price on this for Black Friday time. The first one i got was DoA and would not turn on. It had very obviously been repackaged and retaped. Getting an Amazon chat associate is not as easy as it should be. The AI questions absolutely suck! I was able to finally get a rep on chat and they did make it right. Had UPS come and pick it up at my home which saved me a trip to the UPS store that has lines out the door. The new machine I received is working great so far!

Read more

I upgraded my previous Keurig coffee maker that I bought in 2013. It was worth the upgrade.

I like how easy this machine is to use.

Easy setup: Right out of the box there was little that needed to be done. Just remove factory tape, plug it in and run a single water only cycle and good to go.

Taste: I use a quality coffee. I played with the "strong" button and that was one of the best cups of coffee I've had.

Speed: Hot water on demand. This machine heats the water right before it hits the pod. There is no internal reservoir the water is first pumped into to heat first. This means the speed of use is much faster. My previous unit had this and it took a bit longer to get that first cup. Because there is no internal reservoir there is less places for scaling to take place. Using filtered water also reduces this buildup.

Extraction: This unit is cooler than some other units and extracts at 192 with a final cup temp of about 165. This is less than coffee enthusiasts recommend. I taste no difference as my coffee still had a rich and bold flavor. For someone who enjoys coffee without all the fine tuning this works great.

Ascetically pleasing: I love how small this unit is and how it looks on the counter. It doesn't have a LCD readout with the time or a way to auto set for an automatic cup. The hot water on demand eliminates this need. Just turn it on and you have a cup in maybe a minute. Also, without an LCD display, less to break.

Clean up: The area that the pod is inserted in is not concave as my previous unit was. It can be easily wiped clean. My previous unit could get a buildup of crud around the pod area. That can't happen with this unit.

Descaling setting: While I've not used it yet, I like that it has a descaling setting when I do clean out my machine. My previous didn't have this and it took longer to run cycles.

Cons: Factory taste!! My first two cups of coffee tasted like crap. I assumed this was because it was still getting the factory taste out of the unit. On the 3rd attempt I used the "strong" button and wow I tasted a difference. I'm also using zero water for my coffee.

Overall if you want a "no thrills" machine that makes coffee fast and very well then I recommend this product.

Read more

Perfect for individuals or couples who don't drink enough coffee to make a full pot and waste the rest. My wife and I typically only drink about 3 cups each morning. We used to brew coffee by the pot, but even limiting the brew to four cups, we still ended up wasting a cup.

Our previous Keurig K-Supreme stopped working, so we tried another brand that offered both K-Cup and coffee pot capabilities. We were expecting company for Christmas, and this seemed to be a good idea at the time.

The Keurig K-Supreme provides a much more robust flavor and gives a comparable amount of coffee in about half the time of the other brand. We purchased the other brand about a month before Christmas, so we could try to adapt to it. After a week, I ordered the K-Supreme and stored it until after the company left at the end of the holidays.

The K-Supreme is easy to use, fits on the coffee station counter, and under the cabinet with no problem.

If there is any fault with the K-Supreme, it is the tendency to fail after several de-scaling periods. I think the solution would be to de-scale the unit more regularly and not wait until the warning light goes off. It may be the mineral content of our water, but we do use and replace the water filter in the tank regularly. I have seen cleaning tablets offered on Amazon. I plan on giving those a try.

The only other nit to pick, and it is probably the result of using fine-ground coffee in the mesh pod that comes with the brewer. We had purchased ground coffee for use in the brewer from the other company. It works just fine and does not pass the fine grounds through the mesh, but the grounds get so tightly packed during brewing that it is difficult to clear the grounds from the mesh cup. After the ground coffee is gone, we will switch to medium grind.

reviews.review_title: Filter traps air bubbles & machine needs to be burped occasionally.
reviews.review_description:

reviews.review_title: Steaming hot cu of coffee and beautiful coffeemaker
reviews.review_description: I’m Swedish and a coffee aficionado, so I am hard to please. This coffee maker is superior and outshines much more expensive coffeemakers. It is sleek and good looking on the counter, simple to use and makes a fantastic cup of coffee—hot and delicious! You can’t go wrong with this fine product.

This coffee pot has been my favorite so far, I don’t drink but a cup a day, therefore the size is more than enough for me. It’s perfect size to sit on my counter and not take up to much room. reviews.review_title: A simple yet efficient Coffee pot.
reviews.review_description:
I loved this coffee pot as soon as I unboxed it. It was simple, yet elegant. I had always wanted to use the programmable features of being able to set up a time of when my coffee could be brewed in the morning without me, but I always got frustrated over all the buttons needed to press in order to set a simple time. I would get discouraged and instead of messing with it, I would just decide to turn my pot on as soon as I woke up. When I purchased this one I looked for 5 simple things.

1. Was the coffee hot enough when it was brewed.

2. When poured, did the coffee spill all over the place

3. Did it have a clock and did have a programmable feature

4. Was it reliable and sturdy

5. Was the price right

After reading almost 90% of the comments, I decided to take a chance on this one. I will tell you, the coffee in my WHITE (I'm not sure about the black) coffee pot comes out extremely hot and I love my coffee to the point of burning. I add a significant amount of creamer and if my coffee is warm, my creamer will make it luke warm and by then, I no longer want to drink it. I have ABSOLUTELY no issues with the temperature of the brewed coffee. Second, The carafe in this coffee pot pours water and coffee efficiently. Every other coffee pot I've owned, water would pour everywhere whenever I filled the water basin up in order to start a pot, but this one is fantastic. I haven't spilled any coffee or water while using this coffee pot. I read multiple comments about this issue and I'm not sure why they would have this problem unless they were in a rush and trying to pour all of the coffee out of the pot at once. Three, The clock and programmable function on this coffee pot are wonderful! Fast, Easy, and reliable. You push a button to program the time and push the hour and minute buttons to finish it. The programmable function, where you can set your coffee pot up the night before and it will start to brew at a specific time in the morning WITHOUT you needing to touch it, is just the BEST feature ever! Its so easy to program, so easy to set up, and it has yet to fail me. I set my coffee pot for 4 am and by 4:20 I'm walking into my kitchen, making my coffee to go and out my door by 4:30. Easy and efficient. Four, reliable and sturdy. As I stated above this coffee pot is VERY reliable, I've had it a little over 2 months and it's never once not functioned as promised. It's never overflowed, I've never had coffee grounds in my coffee, I've never had the stop and pour function release ANY coffee when I've had the coffee stopped mid pour, and my coffee has always been hot. The sturdy part is where I'm just a little disappointed. When my pot first came in the ONLY part I felt could've been improved, was the cheap feel of the carafe. The design is great, as I stated before. The water never drips for me, but the handle seemed weak and the glass was thin. I planned on ordering a second carafe, in the future just in case the handle broke off from my current one, but unfortunately I didn't even get a full three months before it broke. And the way it broke was not how I thought it would. This cold Sunday morning I was pouring myself a cup of newly brewed coffee and I put the carafe against my cold ceramic coffee mug. I usually pour my coffee into a metal travel mug and therefore I never touch the metal to the glass, but this morning was different and I am battling the flu and didn't have much energy to hold the carafe over my cup so I poured it with it against the mug and immediately I heard a crack. At first I thought it was my mug, but upon further inspection I noticed a crack along the lip of my coffee carafe. I was shocked to say the least and of course disappointed. I can't think of any other reason other than temperature change being the culprit. I wasn't pushing up against my mug, I wasn't forcing the lip into the cup, I wasn't forcibly leaning the pot against the rim of the cup, I was simply not holding the carafe away from my mug. I let it touch the cold cup and this I believe may be the reason it cracked. I have put in a request for a replacement carafe and I'm hoping they will be able to help me. My coffee pot is white and it's particularly hard to find white coffee pots, so I hope they have a white replacement part. When I hear back from them I will surely update my review. As for the right price, I couldn't have asked for a better price for a functional coffee pot. All other coffee pots are $40 and beyond and have so many features that most don't use. I am a simple person with simple needs. This pot gave me everything I needed without an outrageous price tag.

Even though my carafe cracked, I would still recommend this coffee pot, that's how reliable and efficient it truly is. I will make sure in the future to watch out for temperature changes when it comes to the glass of my carafe. If I wash it and it's cold, I would make sure to warm the glass up with warm water before placing it in the pot to receive hot coffee. If your mornings are cold, pour the coffee over your cup and don't make contact with cold ceramic. I also have granite counter tops, so I would recommend putting a pot holder on your counter before placing your carafe down onto it if you don't plan on putting it back into the pot. Just a few suggestions that I myself will be doing for now on. I hope I helped anyone looking for some info and like I said, I will update you on my interactions regarding my replacement part.

**I contacted this seller regarding my replacement and it was such a wonderful transaction that I HAD to make sure to update you. I have now had my NEW carafe for about 3 months after the first one cracked and to be honest, it's Wonderful! The first carafe I got felt weak and I was concerned it would give out and indeed it did. I called the manufacturer searching for a replacement carafe (one I would purchase myself) and they were fabulous. They informed me that there is no replacement carafe for this particular machine, so they would be replacing the WHOLE coffee pot for FREE. I was taken aback by this response and had to double check to make sure I heard correctly. Indeed I did, all I had to do was cut the plug off the old coffee pot and take a picture of the wire and plug. I had to make sure the numbers on the plug were visible in the picture. I double checked the photo and then sent the evidence. I didn't have to deal with shipping costs or long waits or any hassle. It was fast, efficient and absolutely stress free! The best part, I PAID FOR NOTHING! I received a brand new replacement for my cracked and broken carafe. This company was kind, respectful, and on the ball. I hope you try them out, I'm truly impressed and I recommend this coffee pot to anyone!

reviews.review_title: I Thought Buying a Cheaper Returned Model Would Work, but Got Ripped Off
reviews.review_description: I bought a "returned" model, assuming it would be functional and cosmetically ok. But it had a 1" X 1" gauge broken off the plastic. Fortunately in the back, not the front. I was disappointed because the sales into never said it was defective or even refurbished. Just returned, which means like new. Anyhow I put tape over the gap so insects can't get it. A couple months later, the spring broke on the "swipe a cup" feature so I lost the feature. Black & Decker has always outlasted other brands so I was very surprised but maybe I'm using more grounds lately and weighed it down. The last straw was when the maker quit working altogether less than a year in. The on button stays on, can't turn it off, and nothing happens. It doesn't brew at all. Very disappointed. I think this "return" was probably damaged before I bought it. It must have been dropped, since the plastic casing broke off. I won't buy returned items anymore.

I have owned 3 B+D Coffee Makers over the last dozen years and they were as good as and as durable as any others out there. But this one was a complete waste of money. I primarily use one hand to remove and replace the carafe from the coffee maker. But with this one, it is a two handed proposition, because of a change in design, they have raised the rim of the heating element, which necessitates holding the maker with one hand, while trying to extract the carafe from the maker and not dragging it across the counter top. This is a truly bad design change and a very regrettable purchase. Truly the disadvantage of not being able to see one on the shelf and instead of relying on previous purchases. Too much trouble to repackage and return, but then, I shouldn't have to.

reviews.review_title: Really nice quality for a fair price!
reviews.review_description:
After one year of daily use, the BLACK+DECKER CM1160W-1 has proven to be a reliable and well-built coffeemaker. The build quality is excellent for its price range: the materials still feel sturdy, the white and stainless-steel finish looks good, and the carafe remains strong, easy to handle, and completely leak-free.

It brews quickly and quietly, which makes it perfect for everyday mornings. The size is compact, so it doesn’t take up much counter space, and the coffee always tastes clean with no plastic smell or strange aftertaste.

I don’t really use the programmable features—most of the time, I simply brew my coffee and then unplug the machine once I’m done. Even with this simple routine, the machine has held up perfectly with no issues.

Overall, after a full year of consistent use, I can say this is a dependable, efficient coffeemaker with excellent value for the money. Definitely a purchase worth recommending.

reviews.review_title: Buyer beware - don't make the mistake of buying this product
reviews.review_description:
I wanted to love this coffee maker so much, I really did. It's definitely a fun design and looks great, and it worked like a charm for a couple of months, but then I started having the same issue that so many others started having when their pot wasn't very old. It started steaming up a storm (literally making the machine soaking wet with steam sweat as it tried to brew) and brewing very, very little coffee... and having a burnt taste to what actually did end up in the pot. On top of that, the carafe is incredibly thin and fragile. My first one cracked by the handle within weeks, and after some teeth pulling I managed to get a replacement from the company... but then, a little over a month later, the brewer itself stopped working.

I know I've read about a 1-year warranty, but I honestly don't even think it's worth the hassle trying to get a replacement for a crappy coffee brewer that's just going to crap out on me again after a few months.

For example, when I tried to get a replacement carafe...

I first contacted Amazon and was told I had to go directly to Nostalgia, so I did. I emailed them first, but after many days did not hear back. I then found a phone number and called. After a looooooong hold time I finally spoke to someone and she was very nice and said she was sending me a new pot (despite their website saying they were out of stock). A day after I spoke to this lady on the phone someone else replied to my email and said they couldn't send me a new carafe. I told her that I spoke to someone who said they would send me a new carafe to which this person basically replied, "so she did." It sounded like the person on the email didn't want to send me a replacement at all despite them actually having them in stock. I'm glad I got someone on the phone, because they did come through... but that's still a bit shady - hence why I don't even feel like dealing with trying to replace the whole crappy unit now that it's crapped out on me.

I'm sadly tossing this in the trash and putting money towards a top rated and top notch coffee brewer.

No fun nostalgia in my kitchen, design wise, but I'd rather have functionality any day of the week.

title: Cuisinart 12-Cup Coffee Maker, Programmable PerfecTemp Thermal Carafe Coffee Machine with 1-4 Cup Setting, Brew Strength Control and Brew Pause, Stainless Steel, DCC-3400NAS, Silver
description: The Cuisinart® 12-Cup* Coffee Maker is a fully programmable coffee machine featuring a decorative stainless steel insert on the handle for easy pouring. *Cup equals approx. 5 oz. (varies by brewing technique). This PerfecTemp® coffee maker delivers hotter coffee with expert coffeemaking technology to ensure hotter coffee temperature without sacrificing flavor or quality. The water window ensures accurate filling, while the 60-second reset recalls your settings and brewing progress in case of a power loss, so you always have your coffee just the way you like it. This Cuisinart® coffee maker has a gold-tone coffee filter and charcoal water filter that deliver the highest quality brew, and you can adjust the strength for a fully customizable coffee experience. In a rush? The Brew Pause™ feature lets you enjoy a cup of coffee before the brewing cycle finishes. With 24-hour programmability, a self-cleaning setting, a 1-4 cup setting, and an optional ready alert tone, this Cuisinart coffee machine ensures your coffee will be ready right on time, every time.

reviews.review_description:
I bought this coffeemaker because I was looking for a insulated carafe with a cone filter. I decided on this because it is compact for its 12-cup capacity and the price point is very reasonable. A bonus is that it has a changeable charcoal filter so I can use regular tap water rather than filtered water. The coffee stays hot for about 3 hours. It has all the features I was looking for and after using it for several mornings I was quite happy with it.

HOWEVER, days later I noticed that the bottom of the carafe was hot beyond touch (about 200 degrees) right after brewing but cooled down over time. I called Cuisinart who insisted there is no hot plate on the thermal coffeemakers and that they would get back to me in a few days. So I simply returned the unit to Amazon. I loved the function of this coffeemaker so much that I bought the newer model of this unit from a department store for $20 more. The carafe plate on it also heats up during brewing as well! So I'm assuming the plate heats up only during brewing so coffee won't be brewing into a cold thermal carafe. All I know is I'm keeping it. It brews excellent coffee. Just be aware that you want to allow the carafe bottom several minutes to cool down before you set it on something that heat could ruin.

reviews.review_title: Almost great but a major flaw
reviews.review_description:
I ordered this coffee maker from Amazon because it met three criteria: A thermal carafe, automatic brewing and availability. I needed to replace a different Cuisinart I got about seven fears ago. This has updated electronic features and a larger capacity. It brews coffee and holds the heat the way I like it.

But it has a major flaw. The carafe’s pour spout is defective. To prevent it from spewing coffee next to the target cup, the spout literally need to rest on the rim of the cup. I don’t know if this is a design flaw for a one-off, but it’s annoying as hell. I don’t have the energy for the hassle of returning it.

Two other things: First, I don’t know why manufacturers in this small appliance space stick with dark plastics. It make thing harder to see, especially for the vision impaired. Second, don’t look for Cuisinart to be helpful.

Update: 9/30/25 - Give Cuisinart credit. They sent me a replacement lid. But the probem is the carafe design itself. It is impssible to pour without coffee draining off the spout, down the outside of the carafe and onto the table or whatever.

Update 1/28/2026 - Cuisanart has won me back. My DCC-3400NAS' carafe leaked when pouring. You first replaced the lid, but that didn't work. Last week, you replaced the whole carafe with a spare lid at no cost. Thank you.
