reviews.review_title: Those legs are ANNOYING to assemble, but otherwise decent chair
reviews.review_description:
The hardest part about putting this thing together is the legs. It says "slap on floor" or something to get the screw holes to line up. THEY WON'T! What you really need to do is get it as close as possible to lining up, then put the bolt in at an angle but DO NOT SCREW IT IN! Put the tool into the bolt and then use the two to press inwards and kinda pry back the leg piece until the bolt stands upright like it should. THEN screw it in! A screwdriver won't work because it tends to slide right back out if you aren't holding it in place when you start to screw in the bolt. So when you remove the screwdriver to put the bolt in, you'll lose the alignment anyway. And you need the tool (included with it) in the bolt to be able to apply enough pressure while at an angle to "catch" the screw hole before pulling it into line.

HEAD. ACHE.

Aside from that, here's my assessment of the chair's use compared to about 4 or 5 others that I've used in my lifetime:

The assembly is easy and straightforward after you get those leg screw holes lined up. The arms seem to be shorter in length and height than some other chairs I've had. But that's a good thing for me because when the seat is at the correct height, the arms of other chairs were rubbing against the underside of my *GLASS* top desk. Occasionally that little bit of give in the chair when I get up or descent when I sit down would snap the arms against the glass of my desk, and it always sounded like I would break it. Thankfully, I didn't.

Also, I love the fabric covering! I ordered this specifically for that one reason. The one I'm about to throw out now has the typical vinyl covering and as it aged, it cracked, especially on the arm rests, and my arms were getting torn up by it! While this cloth will also wear over time (especially being microfiber), it shouldn't create sharp vinyl pieces to scratch up my arms, so that's a plus!

The back of the chair has a really thick dense foam that isn't quite conforming to my spine just yet. It's going to take some wearing in to really feel comfy. My worry is that once it breaks down enough to wear in, the foam may deteriorate very quickly afterwards. That's something to watch for in the future though. The arms may have a lighter foam, or maybe the foam just conforms better to sharper points, like elbows. But they seem to have more give to them, for which ever reason. The back also doesn't lean back as far as some gaming chairs I have had. That could be bad for me as I sometimes get *very random* vertigo and need to lie flat for a few minutes until it goes away. With this chair, I'll probably have to stumble to a couch or bed to lie down if it happens.

The seat itself is not too long or short either. I've had some that were short enough I felt like I would fall off the front of the chair. And others that were so long that when I saw back, my knees were ON the seat of the chair. This one is, thankfully, right in between. The foot rest isn't anything special nor bad, but it "attaches" in the slides with a bolt on the back of one side. That will make it easy to remove when it's time to buy another chair. With the exception of the gas lift, most of this will be easy to take apart to fit inside of a large trash collection container when it's time for that. (Yes, I've gone through enough chairs for that to be a concern now!)

I never use the lumbar supports, so I can't give any information on that.

reviews.review_title: A Good Chair, but a Few Defects Make Me Worried
reviews.review_description:
The delivery was very fast — it arrived way earlier than I expected.

The box was in great shape, and the inside looked fine as well.

Assembly should have been really simple, and the instructions didn’t look complicated. But it seems there were a few issues from the factory, which made the process much harder than it needed to be. I was able to put it together, but some of the problems I ran into made me worry a bit about the chair’s durability.

I’ll upload photos, but here are the main issues I found:

• One of the holes on the base wasn’t drilled properly.

It wasn’t drilled all the way through, so I couldn’t get the screw in. Since it’s one of the four holes that support the backrest, it’s pretty concerning.

• The armrest didn’t align correctly.

The left side went on easily, but the right side was an issue — the backrest-side hole wasn’t at a right angle and was bent inward. Because of that, I couldn’t fit the armrest properly and had to screw it in while it was slightly lifted. I’m worried this might cause problems later.

• Both backrest zippers were broken.

Not a huge deal, but both zippers arrived broken. I saw other reviews mentioning the same thing, so I guess this happens pretty often.

Because of these issues, I’m giving it 3 out of 5 stars.

Aside from the assembly problems, the chair itself is really comfortable, and I don’t feel any discomfort sitting in it. I got it on sale too, so the price was great.

If it weren’t for the issues above, I probably would’ve given it 5 stars.

It's extremely versatile and very comfortable even for all day gaming. The lumbar pillow is the perfect firmness. The seat width is such a breath of fresh air. I can change how I'm sitting regularly and comfortably with plenty of room. All of its movement is smooth, i.e hinges, support column, wheels. My favourite feature so far is locking the recline in the exact angle I want with a quick push of a lever. It was easy to put together (though it took a bit of hand strength for some spots, like the last screws on the sides, so it may not be very easy for anyone with dexterity concerns.)

It's almost completely noise-free and what noises it does make are quiet. The fabric is holding up well so far (2 months at the time of review). As a seamstress, I had concerns since the faux suede types usually aren't, but it's doing well. And the temperature regulates great. No overheating or sweating. The only thing struggling occasionally are the zippers on the neck and lumbar pillows. Sometimes they slip open since the fabric is so tight over the inserts, but they can be closed again and the zippers aren't technically broken yet. The footrest is a nice addition but doesn't extend far enough out to fully stretch my legs out. An extender that collapses into the main bars for the footrest would be needed since the bars are exactly the depth of the seat when put away. It they were longer they would stick out the back underneath the seat.

All-in-all, a fantastic purchase that my weary body is appreciating when I'm at my computer. I'll try to remember to update this on the durability in a few months!

reviews.review_title: Bad, bad, and also not good.
reviews.review_description:
This chair looks great. I bought it because it had pocket spring construction and the seat wasn't your typical "chunk of foam on a piece of plywood"...and it was red. I hate it. It creaks and wobbles every time you move in it. It took me a solid hour to get one of the arm rest bolts threaded, then the next day, the arm fell off. It's back on, but I have no faith that it will not say goodbye again. The fabric is so slippery that after you sit in it for 15 or 20 minutes, you start to slide forward, out of the chair. Microfiber. Yuck. Warning: Do *not* try to lean back when the chair is in the upright position or you'll end up sitting on the floor (after the seat scrapes your back on the way down.) The headrest is in the right position and is quite comfortable. The lumbar cushion is uncomfortable and, if you do give it a try, it helps in pushing you out of the chair. Sitting on it doesn't help. If you decide to recline, make sure you have a friend there to take a video...so you can post it in the 'funny videos' area of YouTube. It reclines, but the spring isn't adjustable and has so little tension on it that you may end up somewhere you don't want to be. (e.g., the floor)

I don't know who this chair was made for but it certainly wasn't me. Maybe it was you. I'm not a gamer. I just wanted a decent (and fairly comfortable) chair for my desk. Maybe if I was a 16 year old gamer I'd be ecstatic. But I'm not. While I'm at it, how does that tubby guy in the picture get his hugeness on that seat and cross his legs? I'm probably half his size and fairly flexible and I can't do that. I tried. Didn't work. I can easily get one leg up on the foot rest though - two if you cross them.

Finally, on top of all of this, the pneumatic cylinder seems to lose air on a random basis.

As much as I thought I would like this chair I do not. In fact, as much as I hate to say it, this is probably one of the worst chairs that has ever been introduced to my rear end...and back...and arms. I have been in old, wooden office chairs devoid of all padding and/or adjustment that were more comfortable.

Even though it says "FREE RETURNS", I would return this chair in a heartbeat - except that I'd have to disassemble it and get it back in the box in a satisfactory manner. You should buy this chair, but only if you want a nice-looking, fabric covered chair that you will never enjoy sitting in. For me, it's just money wasted.

reviews.review_title: Chair is for little people, but it’s still nice
reviews.review_description:
I guess I misread the size this chair is intended for (description says 54”-62” - but I saw it as 5 foot 4 to 6 foot 2 because of the 300 lbs weight limit) - I mean, I guess that’s really my fault.. but seriously, WHO IS 300lbs and 4 foot 6? So needless to say the lumbar support is in the totally wrong place for me being 6 ft - but I’m sure it’s well placed if you’re a petite person for which it was intended.

Anyway, I’m keeping it because it works for my daughter that is 5’ 6” (she says it’s “super comfy”) and the chair design looks really sharp and modern (we got the Gray on White frame).

The reason I’m not giving it 5 stars is because there’s no way the seat cushion can handle 300lbs, I’m only 210 and my butt fell asleep after 2 hours of sitting in it.. also, the arms flex so much using them to get up out of the seat I’m afraid they will snap under my weight (again, I’m not even close to the 300lb weight limit it’s intended for).

While the lumbar adjustment goes in and out towards or away from your back, it’s good to note that it does NOT adjust up or down.

Props to the mfr for keeping the parts to a minimal and reusing the same screw sizes for most of the build, that was helpful so I didn’t have to worry if I was using the correct screw lengths or washers.. they also include a really nice T Allen wrench instead of the standard L style (which is a super nice touch) - so all this kept the assembly simple and I was done in less than 20 minutes.

Putting my misunderstanding to the side, the reason this gets dinged a star is due to the seat having weak arms, thinner than expected seat padding, and the inability to adjust the lumbar support up/down.. other than that it’s actually a good solid and stylish chair for somebody in the 4 1/2 to 5 1/2 foot, sub 200lb demographic.

reviews.review_title: Decent chair but not for us taller people
reviews.review_description:
I really wanted to like this chair but, while there are things I do like about it, there are too many things I find fault with.

For context, I am 73 years old, am 6’3” and weigh in around 265lbs. My last chair was designed for big and tall people and it fit me to a tee. I worked from home for two years during the apocalypse and that chair was super comfortable and I could spend over 8 hours a day in it with no problems. Unfortunately the faux leather wore off so I needed a replacement. I retired a couple of years ago and now only spend a few hours a week in front of the computer so I really don’t need anything too fancy or expensive.

After researching a bunch of chairs, I settled on the Tralt Mesh Back Ergonomic Computer / Gamer Chair. I’ve never had a mesh chair before so I expected it to feel a lot different from my old all faux leather chair and it does feel a lot different but it’s what I expected.

The good:

1. Price. For $130.00, I think this is a pretty good deal.

2. Assembly. Fairly quick. It took me about 30 minutes to unbox and assemble but I took my time so you could probably do it in 15-20 minutes easy. All parts lined up correctly and all bolts screwed in without any problems.

3. Weight. This chair is at least 50% lighter than my old chair so carrying it fully assembled upstairs was easy for me.

4. Appearance. Very nice.

5. Adjustments. Raising and lowering the chair is smooth and easy. Control lever and hydraulic piston work well. Tilting mechanism is also smooth and easy.

The not so good.

1. IMO, this chair is NOT for anyone over 6’ if you are going to spend any time in it. The Amazon description says this will fit people who are 5’2” - 6’4”. Nope. The measurements shown in the description PHOTOS says 5’3” - 6’2”. Also nope. The front of the seat cushion hits my legs about half way up the thigh. It should hit closer to the knees. This makes me feel like I’m sitting on the edge of the chair. If the seat cushion was 24” in depth instead of 19-1/2” this would solve that problem. Also, if the lumbar support was positioned correctly, it might fit and feel better as well.

2. Lumbar support. As other reviewers have stated, the lumbar is too low and hits your tailbone, not the lumbar area of your back. This setup might be acceptable for someone shorter but for anyone 6’ or taller this is a problem. The lumbar is adjustable but it’s kind of a moot point in my case.

3. Arm rests. They are adjustable and slide forward but for taller people, even if fully adjusted forward, the arm rests still sit too far back and are not comfortable.

4. Stability. When I sit in the chair it doesn’t feel super solid. I don’t know how to explain it but I feel like I am going to tilt off to the side. It’s just a weird feeling. The chair doesn’t actually tip side to side but it’s just this odd feeling I get when I sit and even when rolling forward.

5. Weight capacity. The description says the chair has a weight capacity of 330lbs. This is probably true but, after using the chair for a while, I wonder about the longevity of the chair for someone heavier like me.

Look, as I said earlier, for the price this is a good deal. I only use the chair once or twice a week so decided to keep it as returning it was more of a problem than I wanted to deal with. If the seat cushion was 3-4” longer, it would fit my legs much better and I would be a lot happier.

Compared to other chairs I’ve owned—like my previous Secretlab, which was much heavier and more substantial—this one feels lighter and a bit less sturdy. That said, the material is soft to the touch. reviews.review_title: Good chair, comfortable for work day use, a little creaky.
reviews.review_description:
I've had the chair for 7 months, and it is a good pick overall with no buyer's remorse. I am 6'2 and 180lbs and sit in the chair for ~7 hours a day. The support is okay, as they are just adjustable lumbar/neck pillows and nothing rigid. I have a 30" waist, and I would say a 34" or 36" is around the max to fit within the seat bolster. The arms do not adjust out, only up and down, which is not an issue for me. If you are larger, that is something to consider. The recline feature works hilariously well as you can recline nearly flat and not fall over.

The leather is still in great shape with hardly any creasing and no damage or wear to the material. It's comfortable to sit in for the whole day. The chair was very simple to assemble in ~5 minutes and comes together like every standard office chair with 4 bolts for the base, and 6 for each arm.

This chair has started to creak which can't be helped. I would give it a 3.5-4 rating due to this alone. The creak comes from the pressed steel pin the chair tilts on at the top of the post, so it can't be tightened or adjusted in any way. It is a little obnoxious, but my only real issue with the chair.

To compare, I have a $1,500 Humanscale Freedom Task Chair with Headrest at home, and I feel no real difference in the chair's comfort or overall quality. The Humanscale does have better built-in ergonomic adjustments like the arms, seat pan depth, and lumbar position versus the Corsair, which only includes a couple pillows for lumbar and neck support. The Humanscale is really underwhelming for the price, very loud with the smallest movements, and not that comfortable. Do not feel compelled to spend more expecting better quality.

Overall, I would probably purchase the Corsair TC500 Luxe for a little more next time for more adjustability, and the built in lumbar system.

reviews.review_title: Looks good in pictures and description. Return before 30 day window ends.
reviews.review_description: Looks good in pictures but shows it flaws quickly. I love the Corsair brand and took a chance on this chair because it looks great. Some issues I found include: lumbar cushion is too large and impractical/uncomfortable; unusable. Head cushion is fine, but taller people will have to slouch for it to fit your neck and cause lower back pain; remove it and there is no neck support at all. back cushion material is very thin and will quickly give way to the lumbar frame, which is not comfortable at all. The entire chair mechanism and controls are cheap quality. Even in the locked position the chair still rocks back and forth to a small degree. You are constantly flexing your muscles just to stay in one because of the sway. The bolt holes are flimsy and even when tightened beyond capacity, the entire chair still rocks and flexes. No stability at all. Arm rests are completely fixed in place and can only go up and down. Arm rest surface is hard and uncomfortable. Arm rests stay in place when leaning back causing your arms to completely come off the arm rest or having to stretch both arms just to stay on the armrest, another huge inconvenience and ergonomic issue. Seat cushion is just thin as the back support. Thin cheap poly stuffing across metal frames. Get ready for serious lower back issues. Unless you are a small child, this chair is not for you. Now I know why they only give you 30 days to return the item. The chair shows its issues after that window closes.

reviews.review_title: Glad I bought it…Well not for long
reviews.review_description:
I was hesitant to buy this chair. Every review I read was an emotional rollercoaster. One minute it’s great, one minute it’s trash, I wasn’t sure what to believe. I decided to just commit to it and order since I’ve always wanted this chair, and it matches my Corsair peripherals. I ordered it Monday, it came Wednesday, which is pretty awesome. Everything was well packaged. Branded bags, a lot of protection surrounding the products, I was impressed. It does NOT come with physical instructions, but you can just find them online. Super straight forward install which took me a solid half an hour at most. Now, the final verdict. First sit down and I was really impressed. The bottom cushion is honestly nice, and the two back pillows work well and fit my body like a glove. I’ve already used this for a consecutive couple of hours and I’m happier than I was in my other chair. I was rocking a Respawn 110 Pro, which is very large and plush but is very cheap feeling in comparison. For those looking to get this chair, every single one of the complaints I’ve seen did NOT fit my experience. Whether it be the parts, the bolts, the cushion, whatever. But I do understand where some of these may come from. Let me advise that this chair is absolutely perfect for me. Im 5’11 and 145 so I’m not your average bodybuilder. It still has some room but just be mindful of that since it does seem like it’s meant for the “smaller” peeps. Besides that, everything feels great and is premium. It left me surprised, and I will continue to not trust reviews and just get the dang thing myself. Glad I made the decision.

EDIT:

LMAO I sold it less than a year later because it started hurting to sit for long periods of time. The chair formed to my seating position but it never felt soft/comfortable enough. Sadly my 5 star didn’t last that long. Recently got a GT Player suede chair for half the price and it’s 10 times better. It’s ight you live and you learn. Just get an ergonomic chair if you want comfort

reviews.review_title: An amazing chair at a reasonable price.

To start with, the chair is made out of a breathable material and provides back support that can be adjusted for more or less firmness. reviews.review_title: High-End Quality Without the High-End Price Tag
reviews.review_description:
This is an impressively high-quality chair at a very competitive price point. While there are a few minor details that could be improved, the overall craftsmanship and thoughtful design make it a standout choice for a home office. One of the most impressive aspects was the packaging. The box was meticulously taped on all sides, preventing any dust or particles from entering; a level of care I wish was standard for all furniture companies. Inside, rather than using messy styrofoam that breaks apart and litters the floor, the company used neat bubble-style wraps for each part. This attention to detail ensured that even though the chair is heavy, every piece arrived clean and in perfect condition.

The build quality is excellent, starting with the solid metal base that gives the chair a reassuring heaviness and stability. Assembly was relatively straightforward for someone used to DIY projects, though a second person might be helpful if you aren't familiar with fixing things. The headrest is particularly noteworthy; unlike more expensive chairs I’ve owned where the headrest constantly slips, this one is very sturdy. The lumbar support is also highly effective, allowing you to adjust both the height and the support strength. The 3D armrests are another highlight, moving back and forth, twisting, and flipping up 90 degrees so you can either use them for support or move them out of the way to push the chair fully under the desk. The seat cushion is equally impressive, with 3.14-inch thick foam that feels deep and resilient, giving me confidence that it won't flatten out or lose its shape with regular use.

There are a few areas where the product could be refined. The armrests are made from a PU-padded material, which I find to be a negative as it is prone to friction damage over time; I would have preferred a simple high-quality plastic or a full mesh/cloth finish. Additionally, the assembly gloves included were far too small for an average adult. I also have a suggestion for the company regarding the extra hardware provided: since these chairs often come with spare screws or tools, it would be a fantastic and unique innovation to build a small, dedicated compartment into the frame of the chair to store these extra materials. I haven't seen this feature on other chairs, but it would be a very pragmatic way to ensure the spare parts aren't lost over the years. Despite these small points, this remains a five-star quality chair in my opinion.

reviews.review_title: A review after a year of owning this chair
reviews.review_description:
It’s been over a year since I bought this and have decided to write my review. My experience with this chair during this time- since I bought it and up till now is overall good experience. It’s not the greatest chair out there available on the market, but especially for the price and usability, I would say it was worth it.

A few Pros worth mentioning:

• adjustability

• comfortable cushion

• lightweight and easy to move around

A few cons worth mentioning:

• No reclining- just a “rocking back and fourth” which you have to twist below the seat to adjust the sensitivity- which I find very tedious, tiring, and long.

• Headrest is honestly not the best and kind of protrudes your head forward a bit- although adjustable, still not as comfortable as I would like.

• Cushion will eventually wear out- BUT not too much and still lowkey comfortable, but I started to felt the need to change my sitting position more overtime.

As stated before the chair is decent- especially for the price. For me personally, I love that the seat encourages you to sit up straight and nicely, but naturally, it does get “tiring” after a bit of time. Even then, not sitting the way it intended to- is ironically the most comfortable way to sit on it. The seat does not get too hot which is also nice. If the chair had actual reclining, this chair would be perfect. Also, the chair has some decent height adjustability aswell. The building process was easy and didn’t take that long to do. Overall, if you needed something that was comfortable enough, cheap, and reclining is not a need, I would recommend this chair.

reviews.review_title: 45 minutes assembly -- piece of cake. Nice chair.

Before I finally landed on this chair I read about a million articles with buying advice for ergonomic desk chairs, looked for second hand expensive chairs, read so many Amazon reviews. Obviously you can spend a whole lot of money on an ergonomic desk chair (even used ones), but I really didn't want to.

I just bought this today, so the jury is out on long term wear, ,but I can say that the components feel solid, assembly was easy, it is *very* comfortable so far, and -- even more to the point -- VERY adjustable in so many different ways that physical therapists etc recommended in the articles I read. I am 5 foot 5; in order to put the chair at the right ergonomic height for my particular desk and keyboard, I need a footrest so my feet aren't dangling. But that would be the case with any chair in my setup. The headrest is great, the arms are soft and comfortable, the back support piece is perfect, and everything can be adjusted as you sit in it. Rollers are quiet and stable on laminate floor.

The box was a good size and heavy enough (~32 lbs) to be awkward for an unfit middle aged lady to wrangle down apartment steps; however, the Amazon driver brought it straight to my door. The chair was carefully packed. Whoever wrote the assembly instructions (which are in English and Spanish) for this chair is some kind of technical writing genius -- I have never seen clearer or more easy-to-follow instructions. From slicing open the tape on the box to finished chair was 45 minutes for me. All you need for assembly is included -- also fabric gloves (for protecting your manicure? I guess?) and extra bolts and washers.

Super buy. If I'd known I could get such an affordable and massive upgrade from my previous garbage chair I would have done it long ago. Great value for the money. I rarely write reviews but all the reviews I read helped me make a great decision, so here ya go.

reviews.review_title: Highly Recommend! quality purchase for the price!
reviews.review_description: I am very happy with this purchase! The quality exceeded my expectations, especially for the price. Everything arrived well-packaged, was easy to set up, and worked exactly as described. The materials feel durable, and it's clear that attention was given to the overall design and build quality. I've been using it regularly, and it has performed flawlessly without any issues. If you're looking for a reliable product that offers great value for the money, I would definitely recommend this one. I would happily purchase it again and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to family and friends. Overall, this has been an excellent purchase, and I'm very satisfied!

I was so excited to finally get a new chair for my desk at home. When it arrived, the delivery driver even walked it down the hall to my apartment for me. Once I brought it inside, I saw that the box was kind of badly taped up, but I didn't think much of it at first. Once I opened it, the items inside were haphazardly wrapped in plastic and bubble wrap, but again, it's a cheap chair from Amazon, so not too worried yet. Then I pulled out the little plastic envelope with the toolkit and gloves and that's when I realized that this was not a new chair. The gloves were dirty and had clearly been used before and the toolkit was open in several places. Ugh!

All of the pieces were included and I didn't see any obvious damage on any of the parts. Plus, the thought of trying to send it back was too much, so I decided to move forward. The first step was attaching the legs which went fine. Then I needed to insert the wheels. Four of the wheels snapped in very easily. The 5th wheel, however, would not budge. I tried it several times and on different legs and it wouldn't move. I noticed the other wheels have a little groove on them and the stubborn one does not. It looks like someone might have tried to create a groove, but gave up. Needless to say, I was disappointed and frustrated.

I reached out to Amazon through their chat feature. (I should note hear that the person I dealt with was extremely kind and efficient). After explaining the issue (and pointing out that the chair was an obvious prior return), I was offered the chance to return the item. I didn't really want to do that; I just wanted the wheel I needed. I was then offered a refund of $19.45 and provided a link to purchase new wheels which would cost $11.99 (before taxes and shipping). I explained that wasn't sufficient since after repurchasing the wheels, my actual refund would be about $7.00! I was then sent a new link for wheels that cost $7.99; offered a refund of $25.94; and told I could come back to request a refund for the wheels I after they were delivered. I decided to go with that option instead.

I won't get the new wheels until tomorrow, but I went ahead and assembled the rest of the chair. There were no other problems with the assembly. I did it solo, so it took me about 45 minutes and it was pretty easy.

I really like the chair itself. It looks nice and works well. I like the ability to recline a little and to flip the armrests up. The seat is nice and wide and I appreciate having a headrest.

I'm still annoyed that I was sent a repackaged returned item, but I appreciate the customer service i received from Amazon to resolve the issue.

This chair has been a fantastic purchase! I thought I would have to get a super expensive chair to get the comfort and support I wanted but this one was very reasonably priced and I got it on sale too. It's extremely versatile and very comfortable even for all day gaming. The lumbar pillow is the perfect firmness. The seat width is such a breath of fresh air. I can change how I'm sitting regularly and comfortably with plenty of room. All of its movement is smooth, i.e hinges, support column, wheels. My favourite feature so far is locking the recline in the exact angle I want with a quick push of a lever. It was easy to put together (though it took a bit of hand strength for some spots, like the last screws on the sides, so it may not be very easy for anyone with dexterity concerns.)

It's almost completely noise-free and what noises it does make are quiet. The fabric is holding up well so far (2 months at the time of review). As a seamstress, I had concerns since the faux suede types usually aren't, but it's doing well. And the temperature regulates great. No overheating or sweating. The only thing struggling occasionally are the zippers on the neck and lumbar pillows. Sometimes they slip open since the fabric is so tight over the inserts, but they can be closed again and the zippers aren't technically broken yet. The footrest is a nice addition but doesn't extend far enough out to fully stretch my legs out. An extender that collapses into the main bars for the footrest would be needed since the bars are exactly the depth of the seat when put away. It they were longer they would stick out the back underneath the seat.

All-in-all, a fantastic purchase that my weary body is appreciating when I'm at my computer. I'll try to remember to update this on the durability in a few months!

The only downside I had was the assembly. There wasn't really a clear manual included with the chair, so figuring out exactly how everything was supposed to go together was a little confusing. reviews.review_title: Bad, bad, and also not good.
reviews.review_description:
This chair looks great. I bought it because it had pocket spring construction and the seat wasn't your typical "chunk of foam on a piece of plywood"...and it was red. I hate it. It creaks and wobbles every time you move in it. It took me a solid hour to get one of the arm rest bolts threaded, then the next day, the arm fell off. It's back on, but I have no faith that it will not say goodbye again. The fabric is so slippery that after you sit in it for 15 or 20 minutes, you start to slide forward, out of the chair. Microfiber. Yuck. Warning: Do *not* try to lean back when the chair is in the upright position or you'll end up sitting on the floor (after the seat scrapes your back on the way down.) The headrest is in the right position and is quite comfortable. The lumbar cushion is uncomfortable and, if you do give it a try, it helps in pushing you out of the chair. Sitting on it doesn't help. If you decide to recline, make sure you have a friend there to take a video...so you can post it in the 'funny videos' area of YouTube. It reclines, but the spring isn't adjustable and has so little tension on it that you may end up somewhere you don't want to be. (e.g., the floor)

I don't know who this chair was made for but it certainly wasn't me. Maybe it was you. I'm not a gamer. I just wanted a decent (and fairly comfortable) chair for my desk. Maybe if I was a 16 year old gamer I'd be ecstatic. But I'm not. While I'm at it, how does that tubby guy in the picture get his hugeness on that seat and cross his legs? I'm probably half his size and fairly flexible and I can't do that. I tried. Didn't work. I can easily get one leg up on the foot rest though - two if you cross them.

Finally, on top of all of this, the pneumatic cylinder seems to lose air on a random basis.

As much as I thought I would like this chair I do not. In fact, as much as I hate to say it, this is probably one of the worst chairs that has ever been introduced to my rear end...and back...and arms. I have been in old, wooden office chairs devoid of all padding and/or adjustment that were more comfortable.

Even though it says "FREE RETURNS", I would return this chair in a heartbeat - except that I'd have to disassemble it and get it back in the box in a satisfactory manner. You should buy this chair, but only if you want a nice-looking, fabric covered chair that you will never enjoy sitting in. For me, it's just money wasted.

reviews.review_title: Not a great seat, but the back support is good and the build quality seems quite good honestly.
reviews.review_description:
Disclaimer - this is an initial review - only had this chair a few days

Size: 6'4" ~280lbs

The good:

the materials and build quality overall is pretty good, not sure what more you could want for a <$500 chair. The only thing that worries me is how long the mesh will last. I'd be happy with 3 years to be honest for the price ($180 at time of purchase).

The lumbar/cervical neck support is very good. This is pretty much why I bought it. It will help me force myself into a good posture since my neck is such a mess, both lumbar and cervical.

The head rest is actually quite good. It could be slightly stiffer to stay in place maybe, but it's pretty nice.

The smell - call me weird but the smell of new plastic in a room for a day or two is a pro not a con for me.

It honestly looks pretty nice, not a huge plus for me but it does look sleek.

The bad:

The reviews saying the seat is uncomfortable are right....at least so far as it is a very narrow seat. If it was ~3-4 inches wider, it would be a 10/10 chair for me at least on initial use. The edges are a bit harsh on your hips if you are north of a 38" pants size. If you're sitting pretty straight, not really a problem. The mesh feels fine, it's not as good as a cushion but the tradeoff of breathability is worth it I would say.

What I did right off the bat to help with comfort a bit was get some pipe insulation foam I had laying around in the garage, cut it in half, and lined the front half of the seat underneath with it. Just kinda stuffed it in there up against the edges as much as I could. Does it help? Actually....kinda, ya. I'd say it makes it a good 15-20% more comfortable at the edges. Picture attached (you can kinda see through and see what I did). Edit: I used the other half of the foam for the back half. So I completely lined the edge underneath with pipe insulation. It does actually help. I also figure this will keep the edges of the mesh from fatiguing as quick since it shouldn't pull down on it as harshly over time.

The casters it comes with are pretty bad. If you buy a chair for <$500 though, you should be buying a ~$15-20 set of roller blade casters to swap in. I ran the stock casters for a day as the roller blade ones I got here on Amazon for $16 didn't come until the next day. The stock ones work, but they're quite slow. In my opinion, any reviews saying that the caster input area welds failing were partly due to the stock casters being slow in the first place. This makes you need to push more, and puts more pressure on these spots - making it more prone to failure. The welds to me don't look bad to be honest, and it doesn't worry me - if they failed I'd just reweld them myself.

The arm rests are way too adjustable. They are honestly not bad, but they don't need any more adjustment than literally just going up and down. THIS WAS THE #1 REASON FOR NARROWING MY SEARCH DOWN TO THIS CHAIR - for playing guitar flip-up armrests are a must for me, which narrows down the search dramatically, as anyone reading this knows. But the arm rests aren't bad.

Conclusion: As a big guy, this is a good chair that will help with posture. The seat is too narrow if you are size 38 or greater pants - it's undeniable. Hopefully the mesh holds up - if that is the case I'll be plenty happy for the price. If this chair gets a better version in the future with literally just a wider seat, I will absolutely buy it when this thing is worn out in (hopefully) like 3 years.

NOTE: THE TOP LUMBAR SETTING ISN’T A SETTING IT IS THE RESET. So many people in reviews, including myself thought the lumbar didn’t stay set - it does, just the top most spot is NOT a setting it is meant to unlock it and reset to the bottom.

To be honest. I had high hopes for this chair.

reviews.review_description:
I just received this chair today, so my product review is mostly on the packaging, instructions, and assembly.

The product was well-packaged, and it was obvious when I unboxed it that a lot of care and thought went into packing it in the most efficient way that would also protect the parts. I was positively impressed with the packaging.

I was also incredibly impressed with the instructions and assembly process. I am used to cheaper products where the parts only half fit or important components are missing, or where the instructions were confusing and unclear. This chair's instruction manual was very clear and concise. The diagrams were easy to understand and neat. The screws came labeled and separated and also included the scew types and sizes/lengths, which is handy in case you need to pick up extras at a store somewhere. But they also included one extra of each type of screw, washer, and cover, which I appreciated during assembly. (I didn't find myself worrying what would happen if I dropped a screw, which is something I would normally be distsracted by while working.)

The only things I would take points off for were these:

1. The instructions said the chair came with gloves for assembly, but no gloves were included. That was fine with me, but why mention them if you won't include them? The instructions even later say not to use the chair if not all components were present...but all the important ones were, so I assembled it without gloves (as I probably would have done anyway, since it was for me and not another person).

2. It matters which side of the seat is the front, but the sticker was confusing. The instructions show a sticker placed on the side that is the front, and that is where my sticker was placed. However, the sticker says "FRONT" and has an arrow pointing somewhere. In the instructions this arrow pointed to the front. On my seat, however, the arrow pointed to the back. So am I supposed to believe the sticker placement (it was diagonal, so it looked haphazardly slapped on) or the arrow? On that particular step the piece you are screwing into the seat can fit both ways, but thankfully there is a later step where it becomes obvious which side is the front vs. the back. (The arm rests can only be attached to the back.) So I wish that had been clearer up front, but otherwise it was okay.

Recommendations for assembly:

- To attach the wheels, apply firm, direct, straight-down pressure. I tried screwing them on at first but you just push. Make sure they go in the whole way like the picture shows.

- When they say to tighten the screws to only 60%, it's a helpful tip, because you can't fit the armrests on both the seat and chairback at the same time with the screws completely tightened. Just tighten them enough to fit the pieces on, then later you can tighten up the screws.

So far I find the chair to be very comfortable and I'm exceedingly happy with it. The lumbar support seems like it could potentially be a little chafy or scratchy, but I'll give the chair a chance before deciding if it's problematic or not. Like I said, I only got the chair today, so I can't speak much to its long-term comfort, durability, or longevity. But I was so impressed with how easy and straightforward they made the assembly that I had to write a review to show my appreciation.

reviews.review_title: Bad, bad, and also not good.
reviews.review_description:
This chair looks great. I bought it because it had pocket spring construction and the seat wasn't your typical "chunk of foam on a piece of plywood"...and it was red. I hate it. It creaks and wobbles every time you move in it. It took me a solid hour to get one of the arm rest bolts threaded, then the next day, the arm fell off. It's back on, but I have no faith that it will not say goodbye again. The fabric is so slippery that after you sit in it for 15 or 20 minutes, you start to slide forward, out of the chair. Microfiber. Yuck. Warning: Do *not* try to lean back when the chair is in the upright position or you'll end up sitting on the floor (after the seat scrapes your back on the way down.) The headrest is in the right position and is quite comfortable. The lumbar cushion is uncomfortable and, if you do give it a try, it helps in pushing you out of the chair. Sitting on it doesn't help. If you decide to recline, make sure you have a friend there to take a video...so you can post it in the 'funny videos' area of YouTube. It reclines, but the spring isn't adjustable and has so little tension on it that you may end up somewhere you don't want to be. (e.g., the floor)

I don't know who this chair was made for but it certainly wasn't me. Maybe it was you. I'm not a gamer. I just wanted a decent (and fairly comfortable) chair for my desk. Maybe if I was a 16 year old gamer I'd be ecstatic. But I'm not. While I'm at it, how does that tubby guy in the picture get his hugeness on that seat and cross his legs? I'm probably half his size and fairly flexible and I can't do that. I tried. Didn't work. I can easily get one leg up on the foot rest though - two if you cross them.

Finally, on top of all of this, the pneumatic cylinder seems to lose air on a random basis.

As much as I thought I would like this chair I do not. In fact, as much as I hate to say it, this is probably one of the worst chairs that has ever been introduced to my rear end...and back...and arms. I have been in old, wooden office chairs devoid of all padding and/or adjustment that were more comfortable.

Even though it says "FREE RETURNS", I would return this chair in a heartbeat - except that I'd have to disassemble it and get it back in the box in a satisfactory manner. You should buy this chair, but only if you want a nice-looking, fabric covered chair that you will never enjoy sitting in. For me, it's just money wasted.

reviews.review_title: A good chair for your money
reviews.review_description: Took a while to put together, but it was worth it. It’s a very comfortable chair and as advertised it seems to be exceptional quality so far very pleased.

This office chair looked nice in the listing photos, but it’s even better in person.

I ordered this for my home office space which previously had an armchair that my kids broke by tipping in it. I love the light gray color of this one, since my desk is gray wood, and I love that it is a leather-type material that can be wiped down, since I have messy kids. It has a nice, stylish sleek look to it that elevates my office space.

The chair was easy to assemble, but it does come with some assembly needed. It took about a half hour to get it assembled. My twelve year old did it though, so it might take an experienced adult less time.

The chair is just as comfortable as you would hope for it to be. It has decent cushioning, and the lumbar pump works impressively well. The material is soft and doesn’t stick to your skin or make noise when you move.

This chair is adjustable in height. For reference, I am 5’6”, and at max height my heels are about 3” off the ground. In the middle setting, my heels just touch the ground, with a couple more inches to drop.

As far as width, I would say it’s standard for a full-sized office chair. I am about average in size, but I do think it’s more accommodating for larger adults than many others, due to the fact that the sides are mostly open, and the arms easily lift up. It’s also a pretty deep seat bottom and tall seat back. The build is also very sturdy.

I couldn’t ask for a better office chair. I’m super happy with the overall quality, features, and design of this chair. I can’t imagine that it would disappoint anyone who bought it.

reviews.review_title: Comfortable adjustable-lumbar chair, kind of annoying to assemble
reviews.review_description:
I don't have much experience putting furniture together. This was probably the most challenging piece I've assembled so far. The two armrests were by far the hardest part. Start to finish, it took me about an hour to put the thing together.

First, the instruction manual also has a typo worth knowing about. One step lists screw (11) as M6 x 25 mm, while the parts legend and the screw bag both show M6 x 30 mm. This happened right in the middle of the hardest part. I spent a while convinced I had the wrong screws before realizing it was just an error in the booklet. At least the parts are labeled, with FRONT printed on the seat plate, so orientation wasn't a guess. Still, the typo cost me a lot of wasted time. Not worth deducting a star in the review, but a real annoyance.

Once it's together, though, the chair is really comfortable. I like office chairs with soft arm support. These armrests stay comfortable through long stretches of sitting. The headrest pillow is a nice touch and gives good support when I lean back.

My favorite feature is the inflatable lumbar support. With a pronounced lower back curve, I find pumping up the lumbar makes a real difference. A separate back cushion isn't something I've needed.

The faux leather feels pleasant to the touch. There wasn't any chemical smell when I started using it. Because it's a leather-style surface, it breathes less than a mesh chair. Where I live it gets hot and humid, so that's definitely a tradeoff. Anyone who sweats a lot might want a different material.

The wheels roll smoothly across wood floors without sticking or catching. Moving it around my workspace is pretty easy.

Overall, the assembly could be smoother or better documented, but the comfort, the adjustable lumbar, and how easily it rolls make this a solid office chair... once it's put together.

The Mr. Picky I live with is loving this chair after rejecting many others. It is super comfortable and looks and feels like quality furniture. It is high enough to support his frame of six feet and support his neck which was a problem with other chairs we tried. It was very easy to put together and only took me 40 minutes. I just have a few notes to make it easier for you. There is a QR code to scan for a video or the chair comes with an instruction booklet in the bag with the seat of the chair. I showed in a picture that you may have to move the arm piece a little to see all four holes that will attach the arm to the back and seat cushions. The instructions talk about 25 and 30 mm screws in the instructions book where you attach the arm but there are only 30 mm screws included and only these are needed. One tip not mentioned is you need to lean the back piece on something like the box to make it easy to attach the arm and then the seat cushion also to the arm. These are all minor and I hope will save you time when you put together this chair.

I think it is well worth the cost (and even more) and it is so comfortable to sit on. The wheels were able to easily glide on my low pile carpet. It is an added bonus that the arms lift up to push the chair closer to your desk if needed. It looks good in any office or even a living room.

reviews.review_title: Chair is for little people, but it’s still nice
reviews.review_description:
I guess I misread the size this chair is intended for (description says 54”-62” - but I saw it as 5 foot 4 to 6 foot 2 because of the 300 lbs weight limit) - I mean, I guess that’s really my fault.. but seriously, WHO IS 300lbs and 4 foot 6? So needless to say the lumbar support is in the totally wrong place for me being 6 ft - but I’m sure it’s well placed if you’re a petite person for which it was intended.

Anyway, I’m keeping it because it works for my daughter that is 5’ 6” (she says it’s “super comfy”) and the chair design looks really sharp and modern (we got the Gray on White frame).

The reason I’m not giving it 5 stars is because there’s no way the seat cushion can handle 300lbs, I’m only 210 and my butt fell asleep after 2 hours of sitting in it.. also, the arms flex so much using them to get up out of the seat I’m afraid they will snap under my weight (again, I’m not even close to the 300lb weight limit it’s intended for).

While the lumbar adjustment goes in and out towards or away from your back, it’s good to note that it does NOT adjust up or down.

Props to the mfr for keeping the parts to a minimal and reusing the same screw sizes for most of the build, that was helpful so I didn’t have to worry if I was using the correct screw lengths or washers.. they also include a really nice T Allen wrench instead of the standard L style (which is a super nice touch) - so all this kept the assembly simple and I was done in less than 20 minutes.

Putting my misunderstanding to the side, the reason this gets dinged a star is due to the seat having weak arms, thinner than expected seat padding, and the inability to adjust the lumbar support up/down.. other than that it’s actually a good solid and stylish chair for somebody in the 4 1/2 to 5 1/2 foot, sub 200lb demographic.

reviews.review_title: Decent chair but not for us taller people
reviews.review_description:
I really wanted to like this chair but, while there are things I do like about it, there are too many things I find fault with.

For context, I am 73 years old, am 6’3” and weigh in around 265lbs. My last chair was designed for big and tall people and it fit me to a tee. I worked from home for two years during the apocalypse and that chair was super comfortable and I could spend over 8 hours a day in it with no problems. Unfortunately the faux leather wore off so I needed a replacement. I retired a couple of years ago and now only spend a few hours a week in front of the computer so I really don’t need anything too fancy or expensive.

After researching a bunch of chairs, I settled on the Tralt Mesh Back Ergonomic Computer / Gamer Chair. I’ve never had a mesh chair before so I expected it to feel a lot different from my old all faux leather chair and it does feel a lot different but it’s what I expected.

The good:

1. Price. For $130.00, I think this is a pretty good deal.

2. Assembly. Fairly quick. It took me about 30 minutes to unbox and assemble but I took my time so you could probably do it in 15-20 minutes easy. All parts lined up correctly and all bolts screwed in without any problems.

3. Weight. This chair is at least 50% lighter than my old chair so carrying it fully assembled upstairs was easy for me.

4. Appearance. Very nice.

5. Adjustments. Raising and lowering the chair is smooth and easy. Control lever and hydraulic piston work well. Tilting mechanism is also smooth and easy.

The not so good.

1. IMO, this chair is NOT for anyone over 6’ if you are going to spend any time in it. The Amazon description says this will fit people who are 5’2” - 6’4”. Nope. The measurements shown in the description PHOTOS says 5’3” - 6’2”. Also nope. The front of the seat cushion hits my legs about half way up the thigh. It should hit closer to the knees. This makes me feel like I’m sitting on the edge of the chair. If the seat cushion was 24” in depth instead of 19-1/2” this would solve that problem. Also, if the lumbar support was positioned correctly, it might fit and feel better as well.

2. Lumbar support. As other reviewers have stated, the lumbar is too low and hits your tailbone, not the lumbar area of your back. This setup might be acceptable for someone shorter but for anyone 6’ or taller this is a problem. The lumbar is adjustable but it’s kind of a moot point in my case.

3. Arm rests. They are adjustable and slide forward but for taller people, even if fully adjusted forward, the arm rests still sit too far back and are not comfortable.

4. Stability. When I sit in the chair it doesn’t feel super solid. I don’t know how to explain it but I feel like I am going to tilt off to the side. It’s just a weird feeling. The chair doesn’t actually tip side to side but it’s just this odd feeling I get when I sit and even when rolling forward.

5. Weight capacity. The description says the chair has a weight capacity of 330lbs. This is probably true but, after using the chair for a while, I wonder about the longevity of the chair for someone heavier like me.

Look, as I said earlier, for the price this is a good deal. I only use the chair once or twice a week so decided to keep it as returning it was more of a problem than I wanted to deal with. If the seat cushion was 3-4” longer, it would fit my legs much better and I would be a lot happier.

My advise: if you are big and tall like me, pass on this chair. Spend a little more money and get something that fits you.

The new VIOLET mesh computer chair is extremely comfortable even after spending most of my days and nights sitting in it since i spend many, many hours daily working, communicating and gaming on my desktop computer. the chair may appear to be lightweight; however, it's got a decent amount of weight to it because of the high quality materials used to make it, especially the solid metal parts that make up the strong and stable base.

the arm rests can be moved down at your sides or in an upright position as if there were no arm rests at all. and i have found myself switching back and forth between the two depending on what i am doing and how much movement i require in the chair. they can also be moved forward and backward a short distance, which i did find a little bothersome when the arm rests were down and i bumped them when i happened to move my arm(s) a little. they do not lock in place, but i'm positive that this is just another little concern that i can easily get used to since the old chair's arm rests were not adjustable at all.

did i mention that it's PURPLE!?! not the only reason, but definitely one of the main reasons, that i purchased this chair over every other chair i looked at. and there were a lot of them under consideration. it comes in several different colors, including the traditional, brown, white and black, among others, which i really liked a lot since my room of course has a purple theme going on, and this fashionably attractive and functional chair fits in perfectly with the decor and further brightens up the space!

i am so happy with this purchase even though it took me 3 hours and not 15-20 minutes to assemble. and that was all on me because (1) i am really slow and methodical when i'm doing new things, taking care with every step to do it right, and (2) i am not handy in the least and can barely hammer in a nail these days. as advertised, all tools, primarily the allen wrench, are included. no parts were missing, and nothing was damaged upon delivery. and, best of all, i can say that i assembled it all by myself perfectly on the first try, so it was well worth the time and effort spent.

reviews.review_title: Good chair that's pretty easy to put together with 5 year warranty
reviews.review_description:
Here are my comments and concerns with model YX001 only. The instructions have a few issues imho: black letters/words printed on a dark/darker background, I literally could not read them at times and had to go to another room with a spotlight to make sure I followed directions. A box around the words are fine, but not a colored box. The 6 star gear shims (piece I) on the arms really needs a better way to identify instead of “placed in the direction of the instructions”. I am not having any issues with the arms so I assume I may have gotten it right. There aren't any instructions when to tighten all the screws that you were told to leave untightened, that could lead to an issue if when you finally get the chair finished and see step 8 saying Done and try to sit in it. Not impossible use the included Allen wrench (great it is included!) to tighten the screws from step 4 to Done because the T-handle will not fit in the now put together space. We have a bunch of regular Allen wrenches so I was able to complete the tightening required. Overall assembly was not that difficult and the time to accomplish it was not longer than expected. While the above caused some delay, the chair is still fine after 4 weeks of continuous use.

The chair itself: the lumbar support is very nice and easy to adjust. The arms are attached to the back and the seat seemingly to give more support for them when getting in and out of the chair. The arms lifting up and away is nice. The seat, after a couple of weeks, seems reasonable, not too soft or too hard, the mesh back is nice, and the gas lift feels and sounds solid. The chair would be worth 4.5 Amazon stars, except… I’ve had a lot of office chairs (including work) over my 50+ years of sitting in front of a computer daily: cheap chairs, relatively expensive, and in between. I have a glass floor mat and the chair does not roll freely. There are flat spots on the wheels and it takes effort to get the chair to start to roll anywhere on my mat while sitting in it. The description says they are soft to reduce noise and they do on my mat. When on glass all chairs still make a noise due to the nature of the mat, so that’s not an issue. Compared to the rest of the chair the wheels aren’t up to what I expected and I am concerned about their longevity being soft with a non-circular shape. Perhaps on carpeted floors this might be hidden. Lastly, be aware the description says Lifetime Warranty, however an included index card says 5 years IF you send them an email, which I did, but was ignored for a couple weeks. Only after using Amazon to complain about them were my inquiries finally answered. It is indeed only 5 years (NOT lifetime) which is still a decent amount of years for a chair. I will update this if any issues appear within 5 years.

reviews.review_description: This chair was a lifesaver. I work in an office and sit at a desk all day. The chair I had before had no back support and was uncomfortable. I ordered this one and was very happy with how comfortable it is and how much support it gives. For the privce, you cant beat it. The material is nice, very easy to clean. Looks like an expensive chair but it realistically is pretty affordable. It has held up well over the year I have had it and i see myself getting much longer out of it. The chair was super easy to put together and instructions were clear.

This chair offers good lumbar support and a well-padded seat. It has a very nice and smooth rocking motion, you can loosen the tight/loose knob for reclining, and it is very comfortable to sit in while working on the computer or relaxing to watch TV. The back of the chair hits just above my neck, so the back of my head rests comfortably on the top of the chair. The color, brown, is exactly what I expected and looks professional. The height adjustment works well, it sits higher than my old chair, and I like that. It seems sturdy for the 300-pound weight recommended. I got it on Prime Day, so it was a good value for the money. It came packed well and quicker than expected. The pictures are a comparison to my 20-year-old office chair.

Assembling the chair was easy, however, be sure to attach the bottom part of the chair with the tight/loose knob facing the front of the chair. It's not clearly marked on the instructions. When it came time to put the back of the chair on it would be good to have another person to hold the chair back for you to align the chair arm holes and screw in, then you should be OK but I did discover that if I had attached the arms to the back of the chair first, it would be so much easier to align them for attachment. The wheels glide very easily and will take you across the room after one push. It swivels at 360 degrees easily, almost making me dizzy.

I am writing this review the same day I got the chair so I will update if I run into any issues. Otherwise, I recommend this chair.

reviews.review_title: Comfortable but lack of back support on this chair
reviews.review_description: I give this chair a 4 star not a 5 star review. Reason for that if you look for the first picture I pst you can see from the back of the chair how it reclines. There is no adjustment to make the back rest come up straight so when your working all day at the desk you is an upright right position. I have to put a pillow behind my back for support cause while working leaning back is uncomfortable and who wants to lean back while working. so there is a lack of back support. .Great gaming chair for that reason. Though I really like the looks and the color of the chair. The material was very soft and the quality was made well. The chair you can make go up or down for the height which is nice. The ability to be able to move the char around while sitting is a plus and the wheels move smooth and with ease. I had to put this together which was simple to do and came with everything I needed when open the box. So before buying if the back support and leaning back isnt an issue for you then this would be the perfect chair for you. Please not the first picture with the darker rug is the chair I got , second picture isnt mine but for a review that their chair was up straight. Isnt the way mine should have come. I didnt questioned or return it because it was so heavy and bulky to take back to a UPS store. I just kept it because everything else was great.
Comfortable and easy to put together.

When Covid hit early 2020, I was sent home to work remotely for the first time in my working life. However, my old chair that is pictured on the right is about 25 years old and no longer has any butt cushion. It quickly became painful to work in that chair all day. I have since moved to a new state and found a remote job I will be starting soon so I decided it was time to upgrade the chair. This is a decent chair if you are on a budget like I am and you are not hard on your stuff adding premature wear and tear. For me, it has good lumbar support which I needed, and more cush for the tush! I am a proportionate 5'2" female and about 125 to 130 pounds. The seat has just enough room for my butt but I don't think I would recommend this for larger people. I would look into sizing up to the big and tall chair. Take note of the seat and back size to know what would work best for you but this chair feels small yet good sized for me only because I was able to go by the measurements of my old chair. Might even be best for you to go into an office supply store to test out chair sizes for comfort before making a purchase. Sometimes I like to sit criss-cross applesauce and this chair has a very nice and smooth rocking motion after loosening the tight/loose knob for reclining and is so comfortable for me that I may fall asleep on the job and get fired. The back of the chair hits just above my neck so I am able to tilt my head back a bit to let it rest since my upper back and neck sometimes go numb after sitting for too long. Ugh, it's just so much fun getting older!!

Assembling the chair was easy until I got to step 4 to put the back of the chair on. If you have another person to hold the chair back for you to align with the chair arm holes and screw in, then you should be OK, but since I had no one to help, I had to take the seat off and lay it down. I still struggled to align the back while the arms were attached to the seat so I removed the arms from the seat and attached them to the chair back and then aligned the seat with the arms and screwed them in. Once done, I inserted the completed assembled seat, chair back, and arm attachments back onto the wheels. The wheels glide very easily and will take you across the room after one push.

I am writing this review the same day I got the chair so will update if I run into any issues. Otherwise, I recommend this chair.

reviews.review_title: This review is all over the place but informative!
reviews.review_description:
Initially worried about the reviews I've read about the arm rests and some other things, and the price almost pushing me away from buying this chair. Finally pulling the trigger I can say with confidence they either fixed what people were talking about with the arm rests (made them closer to the chair and more adjustable) or people just expect a love seat or couch. The chair is perfect, not a single problem putting it together, I had it together in 20 mins. The chair is extremely solid and doesn't squeak at all. not only does the back of the chair recline super far like most gaming chairs, it has a separate paddle to set how far the base (place you're butt goes) reclines back to avoid having to sit back against the chair using you're weight to recline which is a massive bonus for me. some chairs require weight to recline but without being locked this chair reclines with ease. The adjustability of this chair is everything you would need. I work from home and this chair keeps me comfortable all day and all night for gaming sessions. Its a stiff chair but not too stiff, Stiff in the best way. when I first sat in it I was concerned it was going to be too stiff but after pulling 6-8 shifts for 2 weeks without standing up during, it has kept me comfortable and with 0 pain compared to my last gtp office gaming chair. after returning my Secret labs titan due to discomfort, I went from a 300$ gtp office chair to this. It has all the features you could need whether you are strict about posture, or you just wanna sit back drink a beer and watch movies or even console game its perfect. I wanted to stick to a gaming chair style but have that lumbar support and some other stuff. and I found it all in this chair. I'm 6,2 at 215-225 pounds. chair fits me perfect. I would 100% recommend trying it out if you want all the features in a gaming chair, while still keeping as much of that ergo you can with the style of chair. the pillow is actually super soft and squishy too. Its actually comfortable to use compared to other brands with really stiff pillows more for look. The chair looks leather in the mock ups, but its far from, its hard to explain, it's sort of a matte leather underarmor t shirt material. smooth and grippy but not sticky like leather. that may sound weird but in my opinion its the perfect material for a computer chair. its almost like a smoother suede material. Only negative I guess I would give them which wont effect anyone using this chair on carpet, is the wheels are pretty stiff if you dont have the weight of the chair on them. they wont freely spin if you flick the wheel with you're hand but they spin just fine. definitely not a hard floor friendly wheel, which I don't know of much other then buying roller blade computer chair wheels for commercial office spaces. all in all doesnt effect me all and the chair moves just as easily as any other on carpet. TO ANSWER SOME QUESTIONS IVE SEEN PEOPLE ASK ONLINE... 1. you cannot feel the diamond stitching at all on your back even after long sitting sessions. 2. the arm rests are more adjustable then secret labs and the gtp office chairs and not too far away from the chair (anymore?). 3. the price is steep until you feel the quality and durability of the materials they use, the weight and thickness of all the bolts, plastics, metals and fabrics show the quality. 4. how does it compare to secret labs? in my opinion the secret labs are super over hyped and over priced, yes they last a long time. but in my opinion they are super uncomfortable. for 150$ less then the titan, this chair takes the cake. All in all this chair is a 10/10 FOR ME. I know chairs fit everyone differently but I found the only chair I'm going to be sitting in until the tc600 or up comes out! sorry for the all over review if you made it this far, I just had all these questions when I was buying and I think this wraps up most of them. 500$ is alot for a chair but this is 500$ well spent in my book. I posted pictures I thought would best explain the chair. there is simply not enough reviews or info on this chair online yet with this model being less then a year old and being expensive I hope this helps you! cheers and good luck on you're chair hunt. p.s I am not sponsored by corsair although I wish I was, I just really like the chair :)

Read more

This is is such an upgrade from my last sub $100 chair. The adjustable back support is worth the cost alone. I was hunching over in my last chair and now my posture is correct. These chairs are made of soft fabric. I am 5’4 and it adjusts to my height. There is a qr code for build instructions on the top of box when you open it. The arm rests can be adjusted multiple ways. There is a tab on each arm that lets you move them up and down. I didn't notice this at first, so I couldn't reach the arm rests till I moved them up. The box is very heavy and very large. You will need 2 people to pick it up or you can turn it on its side and roll it like i did if you don't have help. Cons: The fabric has a break-in period and might feel stiff at first, but it will adjust the more you use it. I recommend getting a memory foam cushion if this bothers you. There is a primer-like new smell but will go away in a few days. You might want to open a window during this period if it bothers you. Since the arm rests move if you pull on them, I recommend grabbing the wings near the top of the chair to move it.

First I want to start off by saying I really wanted to love this chair so badly! I was so excited to buy this and get it into my office setup, but it really fell short of expectations. The 3 star rating is for the $550 price point - I was able to get it on a considerable sale, so for the price of about $300 it’s more worth it and would give it 4 stars but I cannot recommend this chair at full price.

Cons:

- My office does get warm with my gaming computer and this chair absolutely gets hot after sitting for a couple hours compared to my old mesh one, not sweaty but uncomfortable.

- The back has awful padding. The lower portion with the adjustable lumbar feels like a rock pushing into your back if you actually use it so I have to keep it almost all the way depressed. Then right where it transitions from the diamond stitching to the flat part where the wings are, it’s like there’s a metal rod going across (likely the top of the adjustable lumbar thing) but man it’s really not comfortable to lean back into or use that fully reclined position. So overall the lower back is really hard, then there’s this middle that’s extremely plush, and then at the top middle back below your shoulder blades it’s hard as a rock so it’s unfortunate. Not as comfy as most good reviews make it out to be but it’s also not unbearable just being picky due to price point.

- It squeaks!!! I was hoping a few of these reviews were just a couple bad batches but nope. Same thing others have said, right where the metal hinge is on the left side, if your sitting and using the rocking feature it creaks and squeaks every time you rock. Thats something that was just fully unacceptable for a chair at this price.

- The hip bolstering really digs into the sides of my legs if man spreading and hurts after a while.

- Overall the chair just doesn’t seem too sturdy/stable on the base. It has a fair amount of play when moving around but again not the end of the world it’s still fairly solid.

Pros:

- The bottom cushion is actually really comfortable for me sitting in it all day long even though it’s more on the firm side. It’s also big so even at 6’2 with all height in my legs I can kick a leg up.

- While the backing is annoyingly uneven, I think it promotes much better posture than my other chair.

- It looks just so good!! and it is definitely made out of good premium materials, I do see this chair lasting a long time!

- Building it took maybe 15 minutes and you really don’t need any instruction, it’s common sense for anyone who’s ever put something together.

- The pillow is so comfy!

- While the wheels are stiff, and the chair is heavy I was worried about how it rolled on carpet but man it’s a breeze! It rolls really well around the room on carpet.

- For the most part it’s a chair that I can sit in all day and it’s comfortable. The backing is borderline making me want to return it, but I got a great discount so I’m sticking with it.

- Oh and the arm rests! At 6’2 I have longer arms but what… they are perfect for me. They aren’t too far forward or too far back at all. That’s why they have the 180 design if you want to get closer to your desk just flip them around and scoot up!

Overall, again don’t buy this chair at full price you’ll likely be disappointed as the creaking and the back padding are my biggest complaints. If you can get 40%+ off it’s more worth it but be warned if you’re looking into something that’s plushy. It’s very firm. But it’s really pretty to look at!
