reviews.review_title: Great chair for a killer price.
reviews.review_description: I have had a Secret Lab chair that I have been using for work for the past 6 years and have had my share of issues with it (their warranty is a joke). When I had to return to the office and took my Secret Lab back, I needed a chair for home. I refused to pay over $500 for a new chair. I looked into this one and got it around Christmas time for $250. At that price, this chair is a phenomenal value. It is a little smaller than my Titan XL but accommodates my 6-ft 280 Lb frame without complaining. It looks awesome. The green that I have really feels like a master chief OD green. (I'd love to embroider a Chief helmet on the back). The adjustment of the lumbar is great and I was able to make it more comfortable and supportive than my Secret Lab. My only gripe is the armrests don't lock into place. While they are great for their adjustability and range of motion, they can easily move when you are adjusting or really "in the zone." That's really the reason for 4 stars because the armrests are what you interact with the most after the seat itself.

Had this thing almost a year now with about daily use. People are right saying it's stiff. It's well made with nice materials but really lacking in cushioning. The recline and rotating/extending arm rests are nice but it doesn't make up for the low comfort overall. For the price you can definitely find something more comfortable, but if you need something presentable and you're not sitting in it for 8hrs a day it's decent.

Chair was easy to setup. Heads up, there are no instructions in the box, but a QR code to scan to get both a written and video manual. All parts are very sturdy and you can tell that the quality is top notch.

Chair is relatively firm, looks amazing, and has great lumbar support. Wheels seem a little tight, but I'm sure it will break in over time. Many people ask if you feel the "diamond" pattern stitching, I do not notice at all.

A nice bonus is the magnetic head pillow! It is very soft.

I debated between this and the Secret Labs Titan Evo, and tried both out before I bought. The Titan is a bit more firm, this is a bit more cushy. I think for the value (before the occasional discounts), this chair is a better value.

Definitely not worth the price. The seat feels good kind of feels like you’re sitting on a firm bubble. There are side bolsters on the seat with tubular metal so those will hurt your legs if you try to man spread. The quality of the tilt mechanism is absolutely terrible. I only weigh 160 pounds and the tension is maxed out and I still feel if I lean back I’m gonna fly out of the chair. The armrest are cool, but not good. I know a lot of people complain They’re too far forward but that is easily fixed by switching them around, the problem is they’re still not that great even after doing so. The main issue with this chair is the absolute window, licking engineering that went into the back rest. I don’t think these companies genuinely test their products before they release them, but you can 100% feel the support bar that holds the lumbar system at the top of the back rest. It is immediate as soon as you sit in the chair no it is not the lumbar itself it is a brace that holds the mechanism. Also, I am 5 foot 10 and the side bolsters of the back rest make contact with my arms in certain positions and is far from comfortable. Do not let this chair deceive you it does not hold your upper back. You get an uncomfortable bar at the middle of your back and the only other point of contact is the head pillow. Yeah let’s talk about the head pillow you could sneeze in this thing falls off. They use the weakest magnet imaginable, and the pillow feels infinitely cheaper than other companies. Please stop making chairs corsair.

reviews.review_title: Time will tell, but so far it's a solid chair
reviews.review_description:
I own both secret lab titan and this tc500. Titan cushion is softer. With The tc500 the first week I was butt hurt, but it's gradually improving as my body gets used to it. The lumbar support is awesome. I have not been in a chair that promotes a good posture as this one and you can tell as you body will begin to feel different. Much better than the titan in that respect.

Build quality is 5/5. Arm rests are not too far apart as people claim. I am 160lbs 5'11. The material is also awesome. Soft yet I don't really sweat. The casters could be better quality.

I am very happy so far, but time will tell.

reviews.review_title: Its much better than nothing and much cheaper than higher quality chairs
reviews.review_description:
I'm a big believer in "you get what you pay for" and I usually advise to save up, make one purchase, make one investment and don't worry about it for a few years. But something about this chair's value really scales, especially if you can grab it on sale. I got mine in white for $75 including tax and shipping. Many quality gaming chairs cost hundreds of dollars. There a handful of cheap office chairs you can snag for $60. This chair compared to one of those generic office chair is worth the extra $15. If you're looking at this chair for $90 or higher, then the former statement is true (save up). Anyway. I've had this chair for a day now and it isn't perfect. I'll go over what I like and what I don't like.

Appearance: It looks nice. Doesn't look or feel too cheap. The base is metal with plastic feet. Many chairs have plastic base with plastic feet.+1pt

Functionality: This chair has a handful of features--

You can adjust the height. +1pt

But it only has about a 3in range -1pt

It has a lock to let you remain upright and can be unlocked so you can recline back. +1pt

It does NOT have a way to lock in the reclined position. -1pt

Comfort: This chair is pretty comfy. It has a removable/adjustable head pillow and a removable/adjustable lumbar pillow as well. +1pt

It is a little stiff. Some people may like that. It also may break it after a while. I've only had it one day so I will update if something new develops. The chair has a *mostly* comfortable width to me. It measures 19" for arm to arm. But it has this little "cushion" that tries to contour your legs that makes it a little uncomfortable to sit with my legs spread even a little. I have to keep my knees closer together than I normally would to keep the "cushion" from digging into the side of my legs. Because of this, there is really only about 16" of room for your butt or the sides of your thighs. I'm about 5'10" Male 215lbs size 38 pants XL shirt. I think I am at the cusp of being able to comfortably sit in this. It was not made with larger people in mind. It does state a 250lb weight limit while we're on the topic. -1pt

Assembly: I've assembled several office chairs before and this process was similar and just as easy. +1pt

If you aren't experienced or if you struggle with Ikea stuff, you may find it difficult. The hardware that they include is kinda junk. If you have the luxury of using your own hardware (or hand tools at least), I would highly recommend it. I had one bolt that had really junky threads from the factory and I couldn't do much about it, just had to cross thread it and tighten it the best I could. I had another bolt that stripped and the thread never would grab. Luckily there was one extra included in the packaging and I ended up being able to tighten it without cross threading. I think I got lucky. 90% of the assembly was smooth sailing and the few snags that arose, I knew exactly what to do. Again, if you aren't experienced with this, it could easily turn into a headache and a return to amazon over poor quality hardware

Read more
Very comfy

Very easy to put together. I got a black and white one, and it was simple but perfect for use. It’s lasted 3 and a half years, but the bottom now is beginning to rip apart, so we’re getting a new one. We occasionally had to tighten the arms and bottom back up as time went by, but it’s been a great chair.
We have 6 cats and let me just say this chair has been through a LOT! We’ve had it for 3 years and still looks good

At roughly a year-ish of ownership.

It became my main office/computer chair, replacing a pretty standard office chair originally bought at staples/office depot. Work from home so in this chair a pretty consistent amount of time, beyond leisure time/work outside of this.

Pro's - pretty durable. I'd say its gotten its fair share of wear and tear and it's still holding pretty well. No rips that I see, arm supports still holding strong, can lean back and shift the chair up/down with no issues. Head rest isn't half bad, same with the included lower lumbar support.

(Sort of) Con's - It's a little smaller width wise than I'd realize. The previous staples office chair wasn't that expensive, but it had a few extra inches in the seat so it felt a bit more leisurely than this. It's not terrible, but check the width dimensions just to be sure.

The seat cushion you sit on isn't much of a 'cushion' in the sense that it's soft or has any 'give' when you sit, its pretty solid. The good of this means it kept its form over time - the bad is it isn't very comfortable after extended periods; depends what you're expecting. This sturdiness also translates to the occasional bit of not so comfortable sitting with the family jewels.

I bought it the intent to see if this style of chair is worth it, considering some of the competitors want $500 for these. It's good for the price point, but with some shortcomings so to me, it was worth it over spending $500 and having the same complaints.

reviews.review_title: Es war ein Versuch mit dem Stuhl der sich als wirklich gut herausstellt
reviews.review_description:
Mein alter Bürosessel hat es nach 30 Jahren nicht mehr gemacht aber was will man nach dieser Zeit auch verlangen. Ich hab kaputte Bandscheiben und war auf der Suche nach einem Stuhl in dem ich wenigstens eine halbe Stunde oder Stunde verbringen kann und hatte auch schon einen Fehlkauf hinter mir. Selbst wenn einem versprochen wird dass ein Stuhl extra toll ist für die Wirbelsäule bedeutet das nicht gleich automatisch dass ich da noch sitzen kann. Geld war natürlich auch begrenzt zur verfügung also dachte ich mir, dann versuchst mal was, was für einen Bürostuhl nicht so üblich ist und siehe da, ich sitze in diesem Gamerstuhl sehr angenehm. Ich kann ihn fast in eine Liegeposition bringen was mir sehr hilfreich ist und habe auf der Sitzfläche genügend Platz um hin und her zu rutschen. Die Armlehnen sind in verschiedenen Achsen verstellbar was für mich neu war und gleich als positiv zu bewerten war. Die Kippfunktion ist für mich sehr wichtig da sie mir Druck von der Wirbelsäule nimmt. Eigentlich kann ich nach 6 Wochen der Nutzung nichts wirklich negatives finden jedoch möchte ich nur 4 Sterne vergeben weil in der Kippfunktion in der Beweglichen Achse etwas Spiel ist und man das beim Kippen merkt und die Nähte sind an meinem Stuhl an den Rundungen nicht ganz rund genäht. Ich hoffe das der Stuhl sehr lange hält da die unterkonstruktion doch sehr massiv gebaut ist. Der Fuß ist aus Alu-Druckguss und macht wirklich was her. Das Nackenpolster ist klasse und wird von mir gern benutzt. Auf das Polster im Lendenbereich muss ich verzichten, das drückt mir mit meinem Problem zu sehr.

I’m so excited to use this bag! The material seems really durable and hasn’t gotten dirty yet. Seems like you could easily wipe off any dirt or spills. I think it was a great value for the money! I’ll probably order another one to have as a hockey mom travel bag! It would be a perfect weekend bag. And - it has the awesome pocket on the back of the bag that allows you to slip it on top of the handle of a suitcase! That’s a sweet bonus feature that I have to mention!

Overall - I adore this bag. It took 18 years, but I finally found THE perfect teacher bag. Click add to cart now. You will not regret it!

reviews.review_title: Fantastic travel / work backpack at a great price!
reviews.review_description:
I bought this backpack in early August and used it daily as a teacher. Ten months later and at the end of the school year, this backpack is still going strong with little to no signs of wear.

Style: This backpack looks sleek with a touch of vintage appeal. The color is great, which helps if you want to maintain a low profile while using it. There's a small pocket up front, a medium pocket behind that (with a separate zipper pocket inside for safekeeping valuables; and slots to hold several pens), and the main storage area has a separate laptop sleeve. One of the photos has my school-issued 13-inch laptop. It easily fits in the slot with plenty of room to spare. The sides of the backpack have two mesh-like pockets that can hold small items.

Comfort: The handle on top along with the two straps have thick padding. It's comfortable carrying the backpack whether you use one strap or two.

Durability: My backpack is still in great condition after heavy use for the past ten months. This includes tossing it on the rear seat of my car, placing it in my trunk, and having it rest many times on the carpeted classroom floor. The back and bottom of the backpack still look great. I will easily be able to continue using this backpack for at least another full school year.

Cargo capacity: My everyday carry included our school-issued laptops, plus a power cord, an iPad (with protective case), an external hard drive, about half a dozen pens, a pad or two of paper, and other assorted items. Even with all that stuff I can fit more in there if needed.

Overall value: Excellent. This is such a great backpack that I bought one for my wife, and she uses it at her school.

If you're looking to save some money but still want a durable and useful backpack, do not hesitate. Buy this backpack with confidence.

reviews.review_title: What more could you ask for?
reviews.review_description: Absolutely excellent! I have been using this for over a year now at my job, and it is perfect -- of high quality and at a reasonable price. It is stylish and tough with all the right compartments and strong straps that have not shown any fraying yet. In fact, even after almost daily use for over a year, it still looks brand new! I'm absolutely loving this backpack! I used to use a Nordace backpack that was supposed to have 2 laptop pockets, but one of them was very much not meant for laptops, and was disappointed so I looked elsewhere. I am so glad I found this one. It is far more lightweight than my Nordace one, plenty of pockets and zippers for organization, inner pockets and a back pocket for security (I personally keep my wallet in an inner zipper pocket since the back pocket is a wee bit small). It also looks exactly like the picture (which is very exciting to me). Here's a bit of a breakdown:

Pros:

- Large laptop pocket (fits my 16" laptop)

- Lots of pockets

- Against-the-back security pocket

- Very breathable

- Very light

- Feels high quality and durable

- 3 bottle-holder pockets (2 outside, 1 inside)

- USB charging for portable batteries

- Strap for attaching to luggage

- Waterproof

Cons:

- Likely won't hold larger items like textbooks (at least, it doesn't hold my large ones)

- Security pocket is small

- Doesn't have 2 laptop pockets

- VERY tight outer bottle holder pockets

I, personally, got this for both work and school so I can carry both laptops together. It doesn't have 2 laptop pockets, but the one that it does is MASSIVE. The strap is actually loose even after putting both laptops into it so it can easily fit larger laptops. I went on a work trip and it was perfect. Half the time, I forget how much stuff I have in my backpack because of how light it is and how well it disperses the weight. I also appreciate that it's slim. My previous backpacks have always been bulky and I always felt awkward while trying to squeeze down the aisles of a plane to get to my seat, but it wasn't a problem this time. I do wish the outer bottle holder pockets were a little looser and larger so that I can fit my larger water bottle into them, but it isn't too big of a deal for me since I like to carry my bottle for the most part.

Overall, this backpack is AMAZING for the price that it's set at and I hope more people find this. This has honestly been life-changing after having so many poor backpacks. My back thanks you for your product, Volher. Keep making these backpacks to perfection.

reviews.review_title: I packed a whole city and almost got arrested!
reviews.review_description:
I packed a whole city and almost got arrested

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I am a traveller with a problem: too much stuff. I had already checked two suitcases and still had luggage that could fill a small village. So I bought this SHRRADOO Extra Large Travel Laptop Backpack because I needed something that could swallow my belongings without looking suspicious.

When it arrived, I was honestly disappointed. It looked small. I thought, “This thing can barely fit a rat, let alone my entire life.” But then I started packing. And packing. And packing. Different compartments, hidden pockets, secret zip zones, nice color combinations, travel friendly, this bag is like a magician’s hat. I fit clothes, shoes, gadgets, snacks, and maybe a small city and the entire Amazon. I am pretty sure I probably packed a house and a car too.

The zippers are strong. The fabric is tough. And when I put it on my shoulders, the straps were so soft and comfortable I almost cried. I thought I had won. I walked past the airline ground support with confidence, they didn’t suspect a thing. But then came TSA. The scanner lit up like Christmas. They saw the entire city inside my bag. I was flagged. They searched it and found the Mayor tucked in one pocket. Everyone was shocked. How did I pack so much?

Lesson learned: the bag is amazing, but it will make you look like a suspect when you packed a city!

Now for the aftermath. When I arrived home, my shoulders and back were screaming for mercy for three days. I could barely lift my arms as they ache from the weight. But you know what? It was worth it. I carried my whole world on my back and survived to tell the tale.

If you need a backpack that can hold everything and make you feel like a superhero (with back pain), buy this bag. It is a beast.

10/10. Would pack a city again 😂🎒🌆💀

This has become my go to bag for everything. Several times I have thought to buy another one. I don’t have a use for 2 but I enjoy it so much because of its versatility and durable reliability that it might be nice to have a backup.

Friends and family are amazed but how much I fit in this bag. They go to lift it and I say don’t pick it up that’s heavy, I’ve got it. They laugh and go to pick it up and pause to gather their strength and lift and are impressed that I carry it around and then the fact that it holds so much. Outdoor enthusiasts will love this bag. It can carry ski boots, hiking gear, gym gear, sports or sparring gear, picnic supplies, weekend away bag, tailgating gear, you name it. This bag carries it all.

At this point I see it lasting many years to come. If anyone needs a backpack I will buy/recommend this. For the price ($25-30) and durability (1+yr) it’s unbeatable.

reviews.review_title: Great slim bag with a weird laptop holder
reviews.review_description:
I spent more time than I would care to admit looking for a solid backpack, but good ones are expensive and I didn't feel like buying a few to try then return. I wanted a backpack for my office job to carry my tablet, laptop, work binders/folders, blender shaker bottles, and small knick-knacks to and from work and between different offices. These were my requirements:

- Holds my laptop in a sleeve (preferably padded/protected)

- Tablet sleeve big enough to hold my Kindle Scribe Colorsoft

- Stylish and slim with plenty of room

- Good quality without breaking the bank

- Side water bottle cup holders with straps to hold down my insulated blender bottle shakers

- Plenty of pockets for smaller items (gum, chargers, charging blocks, pens, etc.)

- Something I could use for an overnight or couple day trip

I hated it for the first 20 minutes I owned it because I thought it did not have a general large interior compartment area with folder dividers as shown in the product images. However, I quickly realized the zipper track blended in too well with the bag and I simply missed it (it's right in front of the larger top handle).

This backpack nailed it. Even the tablet compartment hold my kindle scribe securely, though I'll likely only use that when traveling as it's a tad too snug. The only thing I don't care for is how the laptop compartment is only a side entrance zip and the "sleeve" is a plush arm that secures the laptop in place with velcro that you have to remove and reattach every time you move your laptop in it. That seems a bit odd and is slightly tedious to do, but I assume it's for easy access; they should really include that in the pictures of the product. Also, I understand that the backpack essentially zips in half to open up 180 degrees for quick airport security laptop checks, but I almost never fly, so that may be useless to me. I've read other reviews that claim the bag opens up on its own because of this feature. I've only had it a week so far but that hasn't happened to me yet and I don't see how it would unless the bag was packed full and only partially zipped shut.

Overall I love this bag, it meets all of my requirements and then some. It also redistributes the weight well due to its longer size, so more weight in the bag somewhat feels like less. Highly recommend.

reviews.review_title: What is your backpack purpose? Repeat customer for Swissgear products
reviews.review_description:
This is my favorite brand of computer backpack. My household has been using this brand for over 20 years. For many years they were used daily. The inner liner on the tiny pocket of my previous 20 year old backpack finally tore so I purchase this one as a replacement. Mainly used for travel and anyplace I have to tote a laptop too. So far, things are going well. I will update if that changes.

Material and workmanship: Sturdy and quality. I understand sometimes there can be defects and I would hope they stand by their warranty. So far all is good.

Size: This is a good size. Small enough to fit under an airline seat, big enough to hold the essentials. I use mainly for all types of travel. I can fit a change of clothes, medications, umbrella, bose headphones, airpods, water bottle, snacks, wipes, tissues, etc. I travel with a macbook air always and sometimes a heavy lenovo laptop. It holds both.

Pockets and design: This is a slightly different design than my last one. I went with this one because it was on sale. For the overall purpose ( to haul all my stuff around,) it serves the purpose. I kinda wish I spent a little more and got the similar model I had before.

-The laptop compartment has a padded velcro adjustable strap. I do not know if this is necessary but it is there. It is removable. Compartment is roomy enough to hold 2 laptops. This compartment only has a "one side" zipper. It does not zip all the way around. I found this a little annoying since my last one had a zip around. I am sure I will adjust to it but I prefer to pull my laptop out of the top instead of out the side. The downfall of one zipper, you can not zip tie or put a lock on the zippers. Depending on where we were traveling, we would zip tie the zippers. It does have a tiny pocket on the top. Not quite sure what I would use that for.

- Next compartment for a tablet. It is padded around the sides and has mesh in the middle. This one unzips all the way around. TSA friendly design. Have not tried this out with two laptops yet so I don't know how that will go with tsa. The tablet pocket is small so maybe ipad mini size? The ipad pro would not fit. They could have designed this to be bigger. I was thinking of getting a laptop sleeve and using this compartment for my macbook air when I travel with 2 laptops.

- main compartment: has a mini pocket for phone but I use for my airpods. Has a divider for books, papers or whatever. I actually use it for wipes. Can fit a change of clothes in a packing cube, medications, headphones, snacks and everything I need. There is a mesh zipper pouch on the top. This is great for cords or whatever.

- top front pocket- I have a love hate relationship with this one. Easy to empty your pockets and phone into when going through tsa but a pain to get stuff back out. You have to dig around a little. I will probably need to separate things in little bags to make this pocket work for my needs. I miss having a small top pocket for things like chapstick and eye drops. Making two pockets, iphone sized and a small one for little things, would have been my ideal solution.

- bottom front pocket: this one is fine. Big enough for epipen, inhaler, key hook, hand sanitizer, tissues, gum, some toiletries, misc stuff. Also has some loops on outer part of pocket.

- side zipper pockets: there are small size zipper pockets on each side that are deep. These are ok. Weird shape. Can fit a small umbrella or a standard plastic water bottle. Space for other things but I don't have that many skinny long things going in a backpack. Pocket is deep so if you wanted to put money or something way down at the bottom of this pocket, this would be hard for anyone to just grab out of your bag. You can not fit a water bottle or similar item in the mesh pockets on the outside of these ones if there is stuff in the pockets.

- mesh stretchy water bottle pockets: The pockets are a little small. These can hold a smaller sized water bottle. There is a strap to help secure. It would be better if there was a loop at the top to hook a carabiner on it, to secure a water bottle. I have lost a water bottle before out of this pocket. Sometimes I use the strap to tie a sweatshirt or raincoat to it.

Backpack Straps: padded, thick work well. Have a few loops for whatever. Back is padded enough. Comfortable enough to carry around for a few hours.

Overall, a good backpack. When shopping for a backpack, think of your purpose and what you want to put in it. Does it have the right sized pockets for your needs? The price was right for this one and I will use it until it breaks.

reviews.review_title: A Masterclass in Design, Capacity, and Comfort
reviews.review_description:
**The "Everything" Backpack: My Go-To for Business Trips, Weekend Adventures, and Everything In Between**

**★★★★★ A Masterclass in Design, Capacity, and Comfort**

As someone who constantly juggles business travel, weekend getaways, and daily commutes, finding a single bag that excels in all scenarios felt like a myth. The AREYTECO 60L Backpack has shattered that myth. This isn't just a bag; it's a meticulously engineered mobile organization system. From a 3-day business conference to a spontaneous weekend hiking trip, this backpack has handled it all with effortless style and remarkable durability.

**Massive, Yet Manageable, Capacity**

The 60-liter capacity is a game-changer, but the real genius is in how it's designed.

* **True "Carry-On" Compliant:** Despite its large volume, the bag is cleverly designed to fit in the overhead bin of every major airline I've flown. This means I can pack for a 4-5 day trip without ever needing to check a bag, saving time, money, and the anxiety of lost luggage.

* **Strategic Expansion:** The main compartment is a cavernous, clamshell-style opening that lays flat like a suitcase, making packing and unpacking a breeze. It easily swallows multiple packing cubes, shoes, and a week's worth of clothing.

* **Dedicated, Padded Laptop Compartment:** The separate, fleece-lined laptop sleeve is a fortress for my 16-inch work laptop and tablet. It's suspended off the bottom of the bag, providing crucial impact protection if I need to set it down roughly. A separate zipper means I can access my tech quickly at security without opening the main compartment.

**Unmatched Organization and Thoughtful Features**

This is where the AREYTECO stands head and shoulders above the competition.

* **A Place for Everything:** The number of well-thought-out pockets is astounding. I can finally stay organized with:

* A discreet **RFID-blocking pocket** for my passport and credit cards.

* A **quick-access top pocket** for sunglasses, keys, and a wallet.

* **Multiple side pockets** for a water bottle and umbrella.

* **Internal mesh organizers** for cables, chargers, and small accessories.

* **Built for the Real World:** The bag is constructed from high-density, water-resistant fabric. I got caught in a sudden downpour, and the beading effect worked perfectly, keeping all my gear completely dry. The zippers are heavy-duty YKK or equivalent, and the stitching is robust throughout.

* **Ergonomic Comfort:** Even when fully loaded, the bag remains comfortable. The **padded, breathable mesh back panel and shoulder straps** distribute the weight evenly. The addition of a **sternum strap and a removable waist belt** provides crucial stability, transforming it from a travel backpack into a capable pack for longer walks.

**Real-World Performance: The Ultimate All-Rounder**

* **The Business Traveler's Dream:** I can fit a suit in a garment folder, my laptop, shoes, and all my toiletries with room to spare. It looks professional and is incredibly functional.

* **The Perfect Weekend Warrior Pack:** For a short camping or hiking trip, the large main compartment handles a sleeping bag, layers, and food with ease.

* **The Overqualified Daily Commuter:** While large for daily use, on days I need to bring gym clothes, lunch, and work files, it has more than enough space without looking overly bulky.

**The Final Verdict**

The AREYTECO 60L Backpack is a triumph of design. It successfully combines the organization of a briefcase, the capacity of a travel suitcase, and the comfort of a hiking pack into one incredibly versatile and well-built package.

**Who is this for?**

* Frequent travelers who want to avoid checking bags.

* Digital nomads and professionals who carry significant tech.

* Students who need to carry books, a laptop, and gym gear.

* Anyone seeking one high-quality bag to replace several specialized ones.

**Who might want to look elsewhere?**

* Someone looking for a minimalist, ultra-lightweight daypack for short excursions.

**Final Thought:**

This backpack has eliminated my "which bag should I take?" dilemma forever. The value for the price is exceptional, offering features and build quality found in bags costing twice as much. **It's a robust, intelligent, and incredibly versatile piece of gear that I cannot recommend highly enough. An absolute five-star product that delivers on every promise.**

reviews.review_title: Item has strap buckle ripped off
reviews.review_description:
*initial review 7/27/25*

When I was researching this item, I saw an offer for a mint return item for less than the listing. The item is damaged. There are straps alone the long edges to help hold the pack together so the zippers are not stressed as much. The item arrived with those straps unbuckled so I almost missed that one of the straps was ripped off entirely. I was testing the bag dimensions for an international flight where I'm expecting the size to be scrutinized exactly so be sure to zip every zipper and buckle every item that is on the unit so you don't miss a defect.

That said, I'm otherwise happy with the bag. I know the item is not sewn together as strongly as it looks or the strap wouldn't be missing. But it is exactly what I think I need for my trip although I can't expect a replacement pack to last as long as most of my luggage.

This same pack has copies under different Brands. All of them are well rated. This one has an additional feature to pass through a battery charge pack cable so you can charge a phone or similar device while traveling. Some of the competition did not.

Otherwise I think all the bags are pretty much the same product rebranded.

The bag has MANY pockets and almost all the larger pockets have smaller pockets sewn into the sides. This will be a great help for organizing. The side near the shoulder straps has a zipper that opens a computer compartment. It has multiple pockets for computers so you can easily take a computer and tablet. Another device would fit outside of the pockets also - but it would side from edge to edge and wouldn't be well protected from the bag being dropped.

One item to be aware is that I chose this bag due to its size and strict carry on requirements of an international flight. This is listed very close to its seams but some of the measurements are a bit questionable on accuracy. It will work for the flight I need it for but the bag is going to bulge when it is full. The long length of 22" seems to be very close to accurate. The next longest width seems to be a bit off at 14". It measures over that even without being stuffed. The back panel is very near that measurement but the side panels fit in a way where they are part of the measurement as well. This is easily 15" when packed. And most of these measurements need the handle to be an additional inch or so.

As long as I don't stuff the bag full, it should fit into a sizer but I could see it causing a couple of issues on airlines that nit pick.

I plan on flying with the bag un-extended so that shouldn't be an issue either. That dimension seems to be about 9" overall and the shoulder straps do zip down into the case.

I do like the design overall. I really like that the main compartment doesn't open right along the middle. The clamshell designs are nice on paper but they are harder to pack bulky items.

The bag holds it shape somewhat but it mostly collapses when empty. As it is filled, the walls hold shape with pressure from the contents. The zippers glide well. I think it mostly functions at its pricepoint. The only item I really think it fails is the lack of reinforcement stitching where the bag gets stressed. I definitely would have concerns checking this bag. But for carryon, I think this is a great bag. I will be returning this defective unit shortly.

reviews.review_title: Great productivity monitors with fantastic value
reviews.review_description:
Never heard of the brand, price too good to be true, so risked buying one, then bought another one. These replaced my dual Samsung 27 inch Viewfinity S80D 4K IPS. My review is from my experience after a few weeks using these as external monitors for my macbook pro.

First, the cons:

1. Noticeable IPS glow, poor viewing angle, bad HDR compared to S8 (although S8 wasn't stellar with its HDR).

2. Poor out of the box colors for both monitors, need calibration.

3. Subpar build quality, not robust, cheap feeling plastic indentations for monitor settings located on the back, screen can bend so must handle with care even when taking it out of the box, whereas S8 was a tank.

4. Basic monitor stand, only horizontal orientation, whereas S8s monitor stand was robust and could rotate to vertical.

5. As other reviewers mentioned, VESA 75 mount is not located in the center of the monitor, but at the lower half, making vertical orientation tricky, but more on that below.

6. S8 brightness could be controlled by macOS keyboard's brightness keys, these cannot.

With those issues you might wonder why I am giving this 5 stars. That will depend on what you are looking for in a monitor. I use these for work, and these are the pros that made me get two and replace my S8s:

1. Increased vertical size due to 3:2 aspect ratio feels significant for me. One in horizontal orientation, the other vertical, feels extremely spacious for reading and coding.

2. Very light weight and very thin, which means easily supported by my VESA monitor arms, and I'm able to adjust these to the back edge of my desk without any fear of it falling or tipping over my monitor arms set up, increasing distance to the screen, significantly reducing eye strain. The default monitor stand, although basic, does not take up any room, has very little depth compared to the S8, so even without monitor arms, you can push these to the very edge of your desk, way further than my S8 with its large monitor stand.

3. Guessing due to its light weight, these do not shake at all when I'm typing. Zero shake with the stand or attached to monitor arms, whereas my S8s shook all the time when I typed on my keyboard with their default robust monitor stands. This is by far the most important factor for me, since I'm typing the whole day.

4. The text is very sharp and crisp, which reduces eye strain for those working with text a lot like I do.

5. I appreciate the minimal, light weight, slim, and bezel-less design. You are just paying for two large and crisp panels, nothing more (just pretend the speakers aren't there). I was eyeing BenQ's 28 inch "programming" monitor before, but didn't buy it because it was too thick, comes loaded with unnecessary software and a ring light, weighs 3x more, and costs 4x more.

Neither pro or con, just notes having used these for two weeks:

1. Factory colors leaning towards red with too much glow, turn black boost in setting to zero, set to RGB, and use software calibration. With macOS screen calibration I got these pretty close to my S8, and fairly close to my macbook pro's screen. It doesn't hold up to a LG OLED for movies, but these beats the LG OLED for work.

2. My initial concern with poor viewing angle becomes almost a non issue as I pushed these to the back edge of my desk with my monitor arms.

3. The matte coating is above average, not as good as my S8, but I work in very bright room and these are perfectly fine for both light and dark modes.

4. Despite the fact that the VESA mount is way off center, these are so lightweight, you won't find any issues rotating these to vertical and keeping it that way provided you have a solid VESA monitor arm. A VESA monitor desk stand probably won't work without an bracket extension.

5. I'm assuming these are not thunderbolt, because I could not enable daisy chaining with my macbook pro despite having 2x DP ports per monitor. I ended up using a DP for one, and HDMI for the other. The DP enables 60hz, HDMI is only 50hz, but I can't tell the difference when I'm working. No noticeable latency.

For the price and my use case, this is a 5/5.

reviews.review_title: Fantastic productivity monitor for the money. One downside: max brightness
reviews.review_description:
This is for the 28-inch 4K+ 3840x2560p monitor.

Raw score: 4 stars

Value for money: 5 stars

Rounding up to 5 stars overall

Setup hint: there is a stupid gamer-oriented setting called "black boost", and by default it is set to 5/10. TURN IT OFF. When on, the colors all look washed out and low contrast. This is NOT a gaming monitor. When "black boost" is turned off (set to zero), contrast is just fine. Not earth-shattering, but perfectly adequate for productivity (I do coding and research on mine).

Note: screen sizes are misleading! This is a 28" 3:2 aspect ratio monitor. It has 18% more area than a conventional 27" 16:9 monitor - same width, 2.4" taller! The display area is even 1/4" taller than a typical 32" monitor (which is usually actually 31.5" diagonally), but 4" narrower. For productivity, I prefer the layout of two of these over two 27" or 32" 16:9 monitors.

I am using a pair of these with a docking station for a MacBook Pro. They don't have USB-C input, don't charge your notebook, and don't daisy chain like $1000+ displays. But they cost a SMALL fraction of the cost too.

I actually replaced my mid-grade LG 4K 27" display with these. The image quality is roughly on par, and the anti-reflective surface is better in my visually noisy environment. I'm actually perfectly happy to use these instead of my 5K LG monitors attached to my other desktop Mac.

There is effectively only one significant downside. They have only a maximum brightness of 270 nits (aka cd/mm^2 or candela per square millimeter). Typical high-quality monitors have maximum brightness of 400-500 nits or more. In practice, 270 nits is enough. In my brightly-lit room, I keep these at 100% brightness. However, in a few years, as the backlight wears, these will definitely get dimmer. Even LED backlights fade over time. Keep that in mind.

Still, for the next few years, I expect to be extremely happy with the quality of these. They will become my roughly 50% daily drivers (my LG 5K the other 50%).

Other minor nits:

The build quality is meh. They have small bezels (about 1/4" top and sides, 5/8" bottom). They have an odd 75mm VESA pattern and it's at the bottom, so they fit oddly on monitor arms. The inputs point down and are so close to the bottom that you essentially can't avoid seeing the cables stick out the bottom of the monitor. They have cheap wall-wart power supplies. The logo on the bezel and during power-up is ugly and looks cheap. But, well, it IS cheap, in a good way. The stand is pretty pathetic, and if you tip it at all, it will scratch your desk.

These advertise HDR capability, but ignore it... it's worse than useless on these monitors. They are physically incapable of emitting enough brightness for HDR.

reviews.review_title: For the money, I don't know how I could be any happier.
reviews.review_description:
28 Inch 3840x2560p display.

Really, this monitor gives you such a great display for such a small amount of money I feel like I stole it! Of course the rest of the package is the cheapest possible plastic and pot metal. Nothing about it feels premium, and apparently there is a speaker, but I don't know why they bothered as it's completely useless.

For this price, the only complaint I have is that my desk isn't big enough for me to buy another one! I'd been complaining that there aren't enough 3:2 monitor options. I guess you really don't need a lot of options when you can get one this good for this cheap!

reviews.review_title: Not as good as the BenQ
reviews.review_description:
I own the BenQ version of this and I was hoping this would be close enough that I could replace all of my monitors with it. It most likely is the same LCD panel as the BenQ, but the backlight is nowhere near as good. The monitor's hue is very warm and it's hard to find a setting that doesn't look muddy. It is much less bright which limits how much you can change the other settings because you don't have much headroom. The matte coating is also much less effective. The BenQ softens reflections and diffuses background light. This is a matte screen too but bright lights are much easier to see and the background light causes a general haze on it that the BenQ doesn't have. That said, the resolution is great. 4K+ at 60hz works fine on display port. The sound is bad, but that's not critical. The build quality is low, I see foam padding sticking out between the bezel and the panel. The input placement is horrible and you'd need to use right angle adapters to not have visible cables since the put the connectors so close to the bottom edge. The VESA mount is also really low, but these are resolvable issues. Every corner was cut to bring this screen down to this price point. I'm unsure who this is targeted at. The BenQ is 5x the price, Gawfolk should have made this a bit nicer than this but still cheaper than the BenQ. They could have sold this for twice the price if it was a real alternative to the BenQ. This screen aspect ratio and resolution is premium, so I don't know why they decided to make a low end budget monitor out of it. If you plan to use this in a bright room I'd skip it. If you plan on coding with this 10 hours a day, I would skip it. If you want to have the color and brightness match your other monitors, I would skip it. If you have a creative need for this aspect ratio and resolution, its a dope monitor at a rock bottom price with no reasonable priced alternative and I would recommend it. But I'm returning it and buying another BenQ, which I consider the best productivity monitor on the market.

reviews.review_title: Great cheap office productivity 4k monitor with extra pixels (x2560 v. x2160)
reviews.review_description:
Bought two of them. They arrived last night. Spent far too much time testing them.

Summary: great cheap office productivity 4k monitor with extra width.

Huge pro: the resolution. Those extra pixels (x2560 v. x2160) are incredible for usability, either in portrait mode or landscape. Even at 200% scaling (to avoid blurry text caused by the rendering that Windows 10/11 has at anything other than 100%/200%/300% because DPI scaling in Windows 10/11 is atrocious. So in landscape mode, I can see two pages, even at 200%. The portrait mode allows me to have very usable, larger text, fitting a page & the header of the next page. Very clear text. Ahhhh.....

Huge Pro: has DC dimming, not PWM. That's critical for my eye strain. I cannot use PWM because my eyes tire quickly. I don't have a physical device, but the app that I use says that the flickering is very low (below 5%). I don't notice anything, in any event.

Pro: supports FreeSync, which means G-Sync worked for me on my ancient 1060 card. YMMV, I guess.

Pro: slightly above average contrast ratio (for an IPS) of 1,200 to 1.

Pro: supports DCR. Probably not a higher end implementation, of course.

Pro: has a blue light mode. I don't use that, because I prefer using software for that.

Con: the stand is perfunctory. I put it on a $30 stand that I previously bought for another monitor. The 75x75 VESA mounting holes are at the bottom of the panel, which means it works well for landscape but do not work for portrait without significant effort (the monitor in portrait mode is also on a custom stand and to offset the sag caused by the mounting hole placement, I have a small shipping box propped under the sagging side, with more cardboard as spacers to level the monitor. Update: I fixed the sagging by buying two VESA adapters (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0741CFJVW), which allows the monitor to be very close to the center of the monitor stand.

Con: although the display is IPS, the panel's viewing angle is not that great. Even looking at it straight on, the right side of the landscape and the right side of the portrait mode monitor are washed out.

Think of this as poor man's BenQ RD280U. I don't know if it's the same panel, btw, just the same resolution, contrast ratio, and both have a matte finish. This has 120% sRGB; the BenQ has 100% sRGB. Perhaps this is a prior iteration of the panel used in the BenQ (the BOE MV282CVB-N11). Perhaps it is uses the BOE MV282CVB-N10. I don't know, though as software does not show the panel manufacturer (other than the Gawfolk model, GF005.

Small Con: HDMI does not run at 60 hz. But the two DP ports are 1.4 and can easily handle 60 hz.

I'm now very tempted to buy another set for my office at work.

reviews.review_title: Budget gaming monitor with a high end feel.
reviews.review_description:
Typically, i like to wait a bit before reviewing anything i buy online. But honestly, this KTC monitor impressed me for being a budget option at this price point so I’m going to go ahead and five my thoughts on it. packinng was what you would expect, nothing too fancy. Included was the mount and and stand for the monitor as well as the power cord, an HDMI cable and a DisplayPort cable.

The Good:

- Picture quality on this monitor is really good. 1440p looks crisp and clear and even downscaling to 1080p, while degrading the image a bit, still doesn’t look overly fuzzy. So if you really wanted to play or use this monitor at 1080p you could. (But being a 1440p monitor, don’t know why you would want to)

- there is very very little ghosting with this monitor at stock settings, i found that setting overdrive to low makes the ghosting pretty much go away without reducing image quality at all so that what I’ve kept mine on. I’ve attached a video to try and show an example of what it looks like.

- Freesync/ G-Sync works well without issues, there was no flickering at all during gaming at 165hz. Gaming felt smooth and i had no issues with stuttering or response time. Just note, 165hz only works with the DP cable. If you decide to use HDMI, you’ll only be able to go up to 144hz.

- Talking about the picture quality, the colors are vibrant without looking overly saturated, the blacks, while not being as dark as you’d see on a VA monitor, are still pretty good. Out of the box, you probably wont need to adjust the settings at all, unless you want really want to.

- Speaking of settings, i thought that using one button to essentially control everything would be annoying, but it’s actually pretty easy. Just press the button once to access the menu, and then move it in the direction you want to change whatever settings you want and then press the button again to turn off the menu.

The Bad:

- the monitor did arrive with some stuck pixels at the bottom right corner of the screen , just above the power button. It wasn’t enough to make me want to return it, as it isn’t noticeable when using the monitor for gaming or when using it for day to day tasks. This is more a QC issue more than anything, so your mileage may vary. I’ve attached a picture of it so you can see it for yourself.

- although it doesn’t affect performance at all, the RGB lights on the back of the monitor only have the option to turn it on or off and no setting to change the color to whatever you want. Out of the box, it just changes colors in this slow wave like effect. But this is just me being nit-picky.

- HDR on thins monitor is pretty bad, it does increase the brightness a bit if that’s what you’re looking for, but it washes out the colors too much and overall just looks too bright imo without manually changing settings in both the monitor and windows. If you’re looking for a monitor for primarily game in HDR, you might want to look at other options.

- this one is me being nit picky again, but the USB port on the back of the monitor doesn’t seem to have functionality, seems its just there to use a USB stick to update firmware or something. I plugged a mouse in there and a USB light strip, the mouse didn’t work at all and only half of the light strip lit up. So while a cool feature, doesn’t seem all that useful. I don’t know, maybe it’s in a firmware update that I haven’t done yet? Ill update this if i’m able to figure out more.

UPDATE: the USB port on the back works, i ended up swapping out old parts for new ones and it suddenly started working. I tried a LED strip and a mouse and both worked fine. I don’t know why or how this would interfere with the monitor, but it is what it is.

Overall, this monitor is really solid for the price, it comes with decent enough features to make it comparable with other options, but keep in mind it is a budget monitor so you won’t get some of the features here like you’d see with higher end models. But if you’re looking to get a gaming monitor with good image quality, good colors, high refresh rate, a 1ms response time and no ghosting, you’d be hard pressed to find a better monitor at this price point.

reviews.review_title: Incredible - especially for the price. I took a gamble and hit the jackpot.
reviews.review_description:
This review is for the KTC Gaming Monitor, 27 Inch 1440p 165Hz 144hz Monitor, 2K QHD 1ms GTG Fast IPS Computer Monitor, HDR, HDMI/USB C/DP Vertical Monitor, FreeSync & G-Sync, Swivel Tilt Height Pivot Adjustable, H27T22.

First off, several reviewers left inaccurate reviews based on some misunderstandings of this specific monitor, monitors in general, operating system settings, GPU control panel settings, or game settings.

I want to correct these inaccuracies so shoppers can make a more informed purchase:

1. The monitor is 27 inches - NOT 24 inches. Monitors are measured diagonally, NOT horizontally. This monitor measures 27 inches diagonally (while it measures 24 inches horizontally).

2. The monitor does have true HDR (not fake HDR), and it has very strong effects, especially when properly configured. Needing to configure HDR is not a limitation of this monitor. It is a fact of life as it relates to HDR. It needs to be configured in the monitor, AND in the Windows operating system (search "Windows HD Color Settings" and turn on "Use HDR" - presumably, if you're using MacOS, it likely also has something similar to this), AND in each specific game which you want to use HDR in.

3. When using HDR, you want to adjust your color, brightness, contrast, black level, gamma, etc. in the GPU control panel (e.g. NVIDIA Control Panel), the Windows OS, search "Color Management" > then click the "Advanced" tab where you'll find a lot of options; and similar in each specific game. I believe a similar function may exist within modern consoles as it relates to turning on HDR, brightness, gamma, etc. in the consoles themselves. This can be adjusted to be easy on the eyes, and even goes far beyond what is needed (i.e. the limitations far exceed the need and therefore do not restrict your ability to adjust it to your liking).

Pros:

1. If IPS panels are supposed to have poor black levels, this monitor completely changes this rule. The blacks are pitch black; like a black hole, they are so black. Again, you have to know what you're doing to properly configure things. So if your blacks don't look black, it is a problem with your configuration, NOT the monitor - unless perhaps you got a lemon, but that isn't likely as this company, while new to consumers, has been producing monitor hardware for decades and isn't as new as they seem.

2. The brightness and contrast are extremely well defined. No complaints whatsoever.

3. The HDR truly puts this monitor in an entirely new class of it's own. The level of detail, the dark blacks, the bright whites (to whatever level you adjust them), the contrast, the color vibrancy/saturation - it all looks so amazing, and it is extremely broad in how it can display images, video, and games. The colors are amazing, and can go far beyond what you need, or dialed back if you prefer.

3. The 1 ms response time, the 165Hz refresh rate, the 1440p (2K) resolution, the G-Sync & FreeSync, the incredible viewing angles of 178° both horizontal AND vertical, and fully adjustable height, swivel, tilt, and pivot, all add up to a monitor without any significant weakness compared to other monitors, and many very solid strengths.

Con:

Only con for me is the bezel is slightly larger than it appears in the pictures, but for a single monitor setup it isn't too noticable.

Summary:

Overall, just as the title says, after a LOT of research into monitors, I still felt like I was taking a gamble buying this one, yet it truly feels like I hit the jackpot. I HIGHLY recommend this monitor, so get it while it's hot.

reviews.review_description:
I saw a video about this monitor being available for $70 on black Friday pricing. By the time I got around to buying it, it was $85. I bought two of them, and I'm very happy, but there's some caveats I think you should know.

This monitor does exactly what it says on the tin... and no more. It has one HDMI and one VGA input (why?) and that's it. It takes in audio via HDMI and has a headphone out jack, and even has volume control on the control nub, but no speakers. It takes 19v power from a barrel jack, but you can swap that for a 20v supply from a USB-C brick with the right adapter (you want the 6.0x4.4mm barrel).

The HDR is rubbish, the VRR works fine. The picture quality is plenty good but not remarkable. The settings are pretty minimal and sane out of the box, you'll tweak one or two of them and then never touch them again.

The stand is a joke. Of the two of these I bought, one of them was missing the 2 required screws to mount the display to the stand. Fortunately, it has a 100x100mm vesa mount on the back, though it doesn't come with screws for that either. I put mine on monitor arms, and threw out the stands.

Basically, if you need a 24" 1080p 120Hz display, and nothing else, of good quality, for as cheap as possible, this is it. For everything else, you'll have to pay more.

There's not much bad to be said about this monitor. It's got great colors with three color adjustment AND six color hue and saturation adjustment. That's crazy to me at this price point. I was able to dial in the colors to where I like them without a problem. I can't get them dead on, but it's very close. It's very green-tinted and over-saturated out of the box, so be prepared for some adjusting. Viewing angles are also good, and it works fine at 120 Hz without any issues on Windows 11.

For build quality and other bits, the whole thing feels solid. The stand is made of metal and requires four screws to assemble, but there's almost no wobble. There's also no height adjustment, but it has a 100x100 VESA mount if you want to get a better stand. Audio output for my external speakers is good too, with no audible noise and plenty of volume. The single knob for menu navigation is the one point I'll put against this monitor, as multiple buttons are always better. Knobs are just finicky and annoying to use.

If you want a large 1080p monitor with good colors and a higher-than-60 Hz refresh rate, you can't go wrong here.
Nice monitors, work great for work!

reviews.review_title: well worth the price for a good budget monitor
reviews.review_description: 8/1/25 been a week so far and satisfied with the quality of this BIG BEAUTIFUL monitor for the great low price. a few bits of advice/insights: for the price I paid for the monitor I got the extra Asurion coverage just in case it stops working after the Amazon return period. take into consideration all monitors can only go to the highest resolution offered IF your computer can go that high. if the monitor box says 4K but your computer can only go up to 1080 then that's what you will see = the better the graphics card and processor the better the resolution. do not touch the front screen at all since it is very delicate and can get damaged easily. adjust the monitor settings from your computer if it turns off to often. the built in speakers are not good so plan on buying great speakers if you want to listen to music at its best. all in all, i would recommend this monitor for those on a budget considering all i have mentioned in this review. i will update this review if there are any changes worth mentioning.

reviews.review_title: Works fine but ghosting really holds it back
reviews.review_description:
I bought this monitor as a secondary display for my setup, and overall the installation was pretty easy. Everything worked right out of the box, and for general use like YouTube, Discord, or multitasking, it does the job without any major issues. The size is good, and for the price it’s definitely usable if you just need an extra screen.

But... there are a few drawbacks I noticed right away. The BIGGEST one is the ghosting. Whenever I drag windows like Discord or scroll through darker content, there’s a visible trail behind moving objects. In games, the motion clarity isn’t very ideal compared to an IPS monitor and darker scenes smear more than I expected. The stand also doesn’t offer much adjustment. The 100Hz refresh rate is nice to have and better than 60Hz and the overall image quality looks okay but just a bit brighter compared to my ASUS monitor.

My recommendation for this monitor: use DP and tweak the monitor settings to reduce ghosting. Just keep in mind that because this is a VA panel and some ghosting will always be there it’s part of the panel technology and can’t be fully fixed

This monitor is fine as a budget secondary screen but if you’re sensitive to motion blur or want better motion clarity you’ll definitely notice the limitations. It works, but it comes with compromises. If you want completely clean motion with no ghosting Id suggest going with an IPS monitor instead.

reviews.review_title: Excellent 1440p IPS panel for the price
reviews.review_description:
I have had no issues with this monitor once everything was dialed in; it works exactly as advertised. I rely on it heavily for both general coding/productivity and gaming, and the Fast IPS panel handles both effortlessly.

At 27 inches, the 1440p resolution provides the perfect pixel density. Text is crisp and easy on the eyes, and the color accuracy is solid right out of the box. I run it at the full 200Hz, and the motion clarity is fantastic with no noticeable ghosting in fast-paced games.

My one minor gripe was during the initial setup: G-Sync was disabled out of the box, which led to some screen tearing when I first booted up a game. However, once I went into the settings and enabled it, the tearing completely disappeared and the adaptive sync has been buttery smooth ever since.

reviews.review_title: Smooth 280Hz, crisp image, and the joystick controls are a win
reviews.review_description:
I've been using this KTC 32" curved monitor for about two weeks now – mostly for FPS gaming and some productivity – and here's my honest breakdown.

**What's great:**

- The 280Hz refresh rate is buttery smooth. Coming from 144Hz, I can actually feel the difference in fast‑paced shooters – less ghosting, snappier response.

- The 240Hz option is solid too, but I keep it at 280Hz for competitive games.

- The curve (1500R) is immersive without distorting spreadsheets or text – sweet spot for a 32‑inch panel.

- Colors are vibrant out of the box; contrast is decent for a VA panel, and blacks are deep.

- The on‑screen menu is controlled by a joystick at the back – it's intuitive and way easier than fumbling with multiple buttons. Navigating settings takes seconds.

- The buttons are placed on the rear right side, so you don't accidentally hit them while adjusting the stand. Easy to reach and tactile.

**Minor trade‑offs:**

- The stand is functional but wobbly if your desk isn't rock‑solid – I'd recommend a VESA mount for stability.

- Viewing angles are typical VA – fine head‑on, but colors shift if you're off‑axis.

- The built‑in speakers are weak – fine for system sounds, but you'll want external ones for gaming.

**Overall:** For the price, this is a killer gaming monitor. The high refresh rate, clear image, and user‑friendly joystick menu make it a pleasure to use. If you're after a big, fast curved screen without breaking the bank, this is a strong contender. Definitely recommend.

reviews.review_title: Excelent Monitor. Exactly what i was looking for
reviews.review_description:
I have been looking for a monitor with some very specific specs for a while, but most that fit were either too expensive or they sacrificed something to achieve one of the specs.

This one finally meets all the specs:

- 400 nits of brightness or more

- 1440p (2K) resolution

- 120 Hz refresh rate or more

- 27 inches

- below 250 USD (i got it for 207 with shipping)

At the beginning there was a bit of fringing on the borders of some elements, but after playing with the refresh rate for a bit, they disappeared. (idk if it was a windows update or due to using HDMI)

when running via HDMI it only reaches 144Hz, so DP is required if you want 180, 200 or 210 (if you enable the overclock. I didn't)

It has 4 ports on the back, so it allowed me to easily connect 3 different PCs to my setup easily (my laptop, my desktop and a mac i have to the side).

Note: the brightness image i couldn't get the measurement in Nits, so i just compared the brightness measured with an iPad Air 3, which is supposed to have a 500 nit display, meaning it might even surpass 500 nits of brightness (many devices limit max brightness if not in a bright environment, i tried faking it by flashing a flashlight on the sensors, but that was the best reading i got).

Read more

It runs at the 120hz advertised. But you will need to enable "Over Clock" in the monitors settings menu. Otherwise it won't go past 100hz. Colors are vibrant and Brightness and Contrast are also good. This monitor supports up to 12bit color as well as HDR. Tho I can't give comment about the built in speakers as I'm using a soundbar. And I have no idea why anybody would be using them in the first place lol

Bought this monitor to replace an older 2K monitor I was using. Assembly couldn't be any easier. Basically you just snap the monitor arm into place, then use a hand screw to secure the base. As far as the graphics go, they're absolutely beautiful. I haven't found any dead/stuck pixels or anything yet. Streaming video, pictures, etc. look great. As some of the other reviews have stated, the "joystick" type control on the back of the monitor could have definitely been handled differently. In my case it really doesn't matter because I only made 2-3 minor adjustments to my monitor settings. It was pretty much set up decently right out of the box. Since I have the monitor attached to a laptop, I never have to mess with the on/off switch on the back. The monitor just powers down whenever my laptop "sleeps" or if I power it off.

Unit looks & feels sturdy and constructed well. Weight is also reasonable (not overly heavy). As some other eviews have stated, the power brick for this monitor is quite large. It's actually larger than my laptops' power brick. Not that it's a show stopper for me, but I found it to be a little strange.

Overall I'm quite pleased with this purchase so far. Granted I just received it several days ago, so if I have any issues I'll definitely come back and edit my review. But, so far, so good!

reviews.review_title: Excellent Budget Monitor for Dedicated Business Use — Know Its Limits
reviews.review_description:
I run multiple monitor setups across my office for different purposes — including writing, business operations, and video production. Not every machine needs a high-end display, and that’s exactly why I picked up this KOORUI 22” monitor.

This one is dedicated strictly to my business correspondence system — email, documents, and general communication tasks — running off an Apple M1 Mini. For that purpose, I wanted something affordable, clean, and easy on the eyes for long sessions.

This monitor fits that role very well.

Text is sharp and easy to read, which is the most important factor for how I’m using it. It’s excellent for writing, reading, and basic graphic placement — but not for critical viewing of those graphics.

Color is where you start to see the difference between this and higher-end monitors. It’s a bit washed out and lacks the vibrancy and precision you’ll get from more premium displays. Brightness is moderate, but in this case, that actually works in its favor — it’s very comfortable for extended use without eye fatigue.

PROS:

* Very affordable for what it delivers

* Sharp, clean text — excellent for email and document work

* Easy on the eyes for long sessions

* Lightweight and simple setup

* HDMI and legacy VGA connectivity

* VESA compatible for flexible mounting

LIMITATIONS:

* Colors are somewhat muted — not ideal for photo or video work

* Brightness is moderate, not high-impact

* Lacks DisplayPort and USB-C connectivity

REAL-WORLD USE:

As a dedicated communication monitor, this is exactly what I wanted. It does its job without distraction and without the need for expensive features that wouldn’t add any value in this role.

However, if your work involves photography, video editing, or anything requiring accurate color and high visual fidelity, this is NOT the monitor for that.

BOTTOM LINE:

For business use, writing, and communication-focused tasks, this is a strong performer at a very attractive price point.

For color-critical work… look elsewhere.

This earns a solid FOUR-STAR rating from me — and would have pushed into five stars with more modern connectivity options like DisplayPort or USB-C.

Recommended for the right use case.

reviews.review_title: Monitor's great! Maybe some of the accessories could use some work.
reviews.review_description:
I really like this monitor. I've been using 1080p as my native resolution since college (back in 2008 at least) so going to 1440p is the first resolution upgrade I've done in over 15 years. I originally had ordered a pair of 1440s from LG but after reading some remarks about the dynamic contrast being locked I bailed on those and ordered these, despite never having ever bought anything from KTC before.

This monitor seems to satisfy everything I wanted to accomplish the jump (a larger screen space over 27" to accommodate the increase in pixels while also supporting the higher refresh rate and VESA AdaptiveSync features of my 27" gaming monitors). The monitor is also brighter than I was expecting. 1440p at 32" has a denser PPI than 1080p at 27", meaning text looks cleaner on this monitor than the 27" displays I was using (I've been told that at 32", 1440p is more comparable to using 1080p on a 24" canvas in terms of PPI). The default color temp is maybe a bit on the cool side but it can be adjusted (the default for "User" seems to suit me). I ordered two of these, one for each of my gaming setups, and neither of them have any dead pixels.

The description says "165 Hz" but in actuality I managed to run this thing at 180 Hz (which means it's a 165 Hz panel overclocked). I notice the thumbnail for the product says "180 Hz" so go by that.

If I had to complain about anything I'd say the accessories leave a little more to be desired. The base is one of those three-point things that looks cool but creates some awkward situations with your keyboard if you have to put the monitor directly onto the desk where your keyboard lives. It takes up less space than I was expecting but I still think I might go for a flatter base. However more importantly the base isn't height-adjustable, which can create issues if you have to set your monitor on a surface where you might want it lower or higher to meet your eye level (it is tilt-adjustable at least, which helps with the desk where I had to put it on a higher ledge). More than the flat base I think this is what would motivate me to get an aftermarket stand solution.

Furthermore the complaints about the short DisplayPort cable in the box are indeed correct. For my setups this isn't an issue, they can reach the port without difficulty, but you definitely may need to consider buying longer cables to handle that if your PC isn't directly below your monitor like mine is. Additionally I'd like to say the cable connecting the power brick to the monitor is also really short. There's a decent chance yours could end up dangling if it can't reach the floor from your desk, even if the cable you run from the plug to the brick isn't short.

reviews.review_description:
I’ll start by saying that my only suggestion is this: when a monitor is purchased, there should be an option to buy a privacy screen that fits it.

However, the KTC 24‑inch curved monitor has met my expectations. Teh Monitors are great, especially for the price range. The 1500R curvature creates a natural, immersive workspace that makes reviewing/creating documents, editing spreadsheets, and creating/watching/reviewing training and/or presentation videos noticeably more efficient and enjoyable. If you’re looking for a monitor that blends style, performance, and affordability, the KTC 24‑inch curved monitor is a standout choice. It’s ideal for gamers, students, home offices, or anyone who wants an immersive display without spending a fortune.

I bought this during a pre-Black Friday sale: an Amazon "Lightening Deal" combined with a KTC coupon that dropped the price well below $200. So, my positive response to the H32S17 is partly based on the big discount I got for my purchase.

The monitor is the advertised 32 inch width. The bezels are very small, about 2 mm; however, the panel has a small, black border, which is never utilized. So the border around the display area extends another 5 mm around the left, right, and top. So, the max viewing area, measured by the diagonal corners is 31.5 inches.

The build quality is solid plastic for the monitor, and the monitor base does use metal. I can't speak to the amount of adjustment the monitor has on its base since I have mine on a 3rd-party VESA mount. The 1500R curvature is very gentle. I use the monitor up close and viewing content from a distance up to 10 feet away, and the curvature isn't annoying. Be aware, since the panel is a VA, the viewing angles aren't as wide as with an IPS or OLED panel. But there is some viewing angle, especially if you are viewing content from a bigger distance. You don't need to be directly dead center in front of the monitor to get a good viewing experience.

The out-of-the-box calibration of H32S17 is not good. You will have to adjust such things like the color hue, saturation, gamma, brightness, and contrast to fit your environment. Some have complained that VA panels aren't very bright. I'm happy with the brightness of this monitor. I never have the brightness maxed out, and I often lower it to 85 - 75% depending on what I'm watching and how dark my office is at any given time. When I finally got it adjusted, the display is vibrant with good color saturation and deep blacks.

This wasn't clear when I researched the monitor, so I will confirm that the H32S17 has an overdrive mode that has 4 different speeds. I currently have it on the highest speed, but all the levels do influence the gray-to-gray response times differently. So, this monitor, like any VA, will have some black smearing, but the overdrive, plus the high refresh rate, will mitigate it some. I'm satisfied with the low level of smearing, but I don't play high-level FPS games where smearing would cause problems.

I do use the monitor for productivity. Text clarity is very good, whether reading black text on white backgrounds or white text on black backgrounds. I was a little concerned about that when I bought the monitor, but it has exceeded my expectations in this aspect.

If you have a decent PC and GPU that can push high frame rates, I recommend connecting the monitor to your GPU with the display port. With a DP connection, the monitor provides a stable 180 frames, which is even higher than the advertised 165-170 hz. I'm extremely happy with that.

Overall, this is a budget-friendly monitor that is good for multiple purposes (viewing content, casual gaming, and productivity). It won't compare to the best IPS and OLED monitors, but, for what I paid, I believe I got a quality product.

The overall design is standard plastic with a fairly thin bevel along the top and sides. It's actually nearly identical to a flat 34" monitor I have from 7 years ago. But it's lightweight. I hardly notice the light from the LED ring on the back of the monitor - it's pretty dim. There seem to be no settings to control the LED light, other than turning it on/off.

When waking up from sleep, the monitor takes a full 3-5 seconds to turn on after my laptop is awake. A few times, the KTC monitor did not turn on at all. I had to manually turn the monitor off, then back on. So that's not so great. This was not an issue with the last 34" UHD wide monitor that is about 7 years old (which I still use), so it's not the laptop causing the long lag time in waking up.

Stand

The stand is sturdy enough to prevent the monitor from being knocked over by accident; however, if the desk shakes, the monitor shakes slightly more than my other 34" that is connected to a desk mount. My main issue with the stand is that it does not lift the monitor very high, only about 6.5 inches between the surface of my desk and the bottom of the stand. So the top 3.5 inches of my laptop obscures the bottom of the KTC monitor. And the laptop covers about half of the length of the monitor. That's quite a lot of monitor being blocked from view, a very annoying situation when working with programs that place controls along the bottom of the screen.

Screen / Image Quality

I did have to adjust the color, brightness and contrast to get a closer match my laptop, which has a very bright, high-end display. Out of the box, the color and contrast of the KTC monitor appear washed out and too gray to me. After increasing brightness, saturation and contrast, I had to bring the black point down quite a lot to get something that does not appear to have a wash of light gray over the colors. As a result, I find my "Custom" color setting way better than any of the pre-installed color modes offered in the settings menu.

Gaming

I don't game off this monitor; however, with a Thunderbolt 4 to DisplayPort cable, I'm getting full resolution at full refresh rates. I don't need the high refresh rate, but the monitor deliveries in these aspects.

Overall Rating

I've had the monitor for less than 2 weeks from the time of writing this review, so perhaps my opinions will change over time.

I think this monitor is fairly good for its price range, so I'm giving it 4 out of 5 Stars. If compared to higher end monitors, this would probably be 3 out of 5 for image quality.

Also, I purchased during a sale of over 30% off. That put it at about half the price of many other monitors at this level, which is pretty good. Knowing the image quality now, I don't think I would buy this monitor at full price. At a discount, totally worth it.

I do a lot of 3D and video editing work, so color and clarity are important, but not essential. This monitor is in no way a monitor that should be used for exact color correcting or color matching. But, for doing things like creating textures for 3D assets, game engine editors, and video editing where perfect color is not so important, then this monitor works well.
