reviews.review_title: Warm, Cozy, and Perfect for Fall!
reviews.review_description:
I bought this spiced pumpkin candle to get into the fall mood, and it has quickly become my favorite seasonal scent. The fragrance is strong enough to fill the room within minutes but not overpowering—it’s the perfect balance of pumpkin, cinnamon, and a hint of vanilla. It makes the whole house feel warm and cozy, almost like fresh pumpkin bread just came out of the oven.

The burn time has been impressive. I’ve been lighting it in the evenings for about two weeks now, and it’s still going strong with an even melt (no tunneling, which is a big plus). The wax burns cleanly, and the wick is easy to trim, so maintenance is minimal.

I also appreciate the design of the jar—it’s simple and seasonal without being overly flashy, so it looks nice on my coffee table and blends well with my other fall décor.

If I had to mention one small drawback, it’s that the scent is so good that I find myself burning it every day—I may run out sooner than planned! My tip: grab two if you want it to last the whole season.

Overall, this candle is a must-have for anyone who loves fall scents. It’s cozy, long-lasting, and makes your home instantly feel festive.

This is by far and away my favorite candle. The smell is both comforting and arousing. When you open the candle for the first time the aroma alone, without burning the candle is enough to fill a room. Commonly that is what I will do. Just open the candle, not light it, and let the fragrance fill the room for a few hours.

Eventually it is time to light it. Both wicks need to be burning for it to evenly burn down. I hate candles that leave wax in the jar as they burn. This one does not do that. All of the wax burns off as it is used up. At the bitter end all that is left is a jar with two burnt up wicks and a very small amount of the wax residue.

This also burns for a very long time. I’d say, end to end, if you light it and just let it burn it would keep burning for about a week total. Maybe 10 days. I have bought many of these and burning it about an hour or two per night I’d say I get roughly 4 to 5 weeks of use out of it. Maybe a little less than that with weekend burning a bit longer sometimes.

It normally comes in a very sturdy package. I like to order it with other goods so as to give it extra protection in shipping. But I have had them deliver it in the original shipping container no problem. That being said I have also gotten one broken like some other reviewers mentioned. What I did was take a small ball peen hammer and carefully broke away the glass outside. Piece by piece. Cut myself doing this but not bad, so follow these instructions with caution. Nevertheless, once I got all of the glass away and carefully removed the bottom glass (which is glued to the candle wicks so use a knife [again carefully] to separate the wick bottoms from the glass) so I could put the candle into a container and light it. It worked. But again that happened once and I have bought MANY of these over the years with no issues.

Let me also say that pumpkin spice is my favorite. And the ladies like it too. Good for getting in the mood if you know what I mean. But I have burned other flavors and they all seem to be top quality. Very fragrant and delicious smelling. Everybody loves the smell of my house when I burn these.

I don’t write reviews unless I truly hate or believe in a product. So just know that I think this product is worth the cost, definitely. Hope you enjoy one as much as I do.

reviews.review_title: One of the most satisfying and best scented candles out there!
reviews.review_description:
Hello everyone, my name is John and this is my honest opinion on this product.

You can buy candles almost anywhere. With so many retailers and brands, it is hard to choose which ones to buy. Maybe you like how one smells but it is too small. Maybe you like how one smells but it is too expensive. Well my fellow candle buyers, look no further than the Vanilla Bean Woodwick Jar Candle by Virginia Candle Company. Now I have to say this was a gift for a friend but I have owned many different Virginia Candle Company Candles in the past and I have loved them all. They are a conversation piece around the holidays and whenever family is over I always hear, "What is that smell? It smells great!" or "What is that crackling sound, is that the candle?" Now, for someone who has never bought one of these candles before, you may not know that these candles actually do make a nice crackling noise as they burn. Nothing dramatic enough to make the in-laws think there is a raging, crackling fire in the other room at thanksgiving, but not quiet enough that you have to tell everyone to quite down so you can admire that satisfying crackling and popping coming from the candle. It is honestly probably my favorite attribute to these candles. I just love that little crackle so much because of how satisfying it is .Anyway, you are probably tired of reading me talking about my obsession of crackling candles so here is what I can tell you about the smell. They have many great scents that are a pure delight to your nostrils. These candles give off a scent that is noticeable, but not too faint. The scent is strong, but not overpowering. Each of these candles smell just perfect. Now the reason I choose to review this specific scent of candle is because it is my favorite. It truly smells like vanilla bean, one of my favorite smells. Another notable attribute to these candles is the duration of burn time you have. Unlike your traditional wick, these candles burn longer and better. Plus they give a pretty little flame which looks a bit different from your generic candle. Anyway, thats all I really have to say.

In conclusion, I would highly recommend this candle or any other candle by Virginia Candle Company. If you ask me how high these candles raise the bar, I would tell you that they are the bar. Nothing can beat them. But in all seriousness, I really do enjoy these candles and have given quite a few of them to my friends and family as gifts after they had asked me about them. These candles really are unique from any other because of the wick they use. If you are considering these candles, I really would encourage you to purchase one because you will not be disappointed with it. I will admit they are a bit pricey compared to your generic candle, (I mean seriously, 18 dollars for a candle) but these truly are a higher quality of candle compared to other brands. Anyway I hope this review was helpful, thanks for reading! ;)

I’m a nocturnal creature, always have been. Naturally I am up until dawn, and only rouse at dusk. Being that I do 12 hour night shifts, I really don’t have a need “flip” my schedule, and can exclusively live the vampire life. I don’t know if it is cause or effect, but I’ve always been photosensitive as well. As a child, I didn’t realize that it wasn’t normal to squint constantly on a sunny day. I ruin every photo from the flash. I even get light-triggered debilitating migraines. I NEED my sunglasses.

So after losing my second pair of Ray-Bans, I couldn’t stomach the cost knowing that I have a tendency to set things down and walk away absent mindedly. Most likely I had dropped them in a parking lot from my purse or hoodie pocket, as I had done in numerous occasions, documented by the scrapes and scuffs on the lenses. It’s just not practical for me to splurge on the item I never prioritized when juggling keys, phone, and bag.

My first lost ones were black and silver Clubmasters which I’ve had a hell of a time replacing in those classic colors, much less the polarized ones. I really missed how stylish they were. Then my classic Wayfarers disappeared. In scoping out to actually buy new Clubmasters, did I come across this package deal with both styles and super affordable. I wouldn’t feel shame about my treatment of sunglasses at this price point.

When I received them I was super impressed. They were a little lighter weight, but overall seemingly sturdy and nice quality. Superb style, I wouldn’t be ashamed of not wearing designer. So I threw them in my bag to leave for work in the evening, to keep one in the car and save one for my purse.

The next morning leaving work, it was nice and bright outside, and after a long shift, it is just the worst to be tired and blinded on a congested commute home. As soon as I hit the exit, I whip out my new glasses, and noticed I still had some eye strain, chalking it up to physical fatigue. Drive home, same thing. The next day I used the other glasses, and it again felt too bright. It only then occurred to me that these are not as dark as I was used to with my Ray Bans.

I gave it a few more days, and realized these just don’t seem to make a difference for me. Feels like I’m wearing nothing at all. (Nothing at all, nothing at all…) Taking them on and off, I feel as if there is barely a difference, like they’re a placebo.

I had focused so much on getting polarized, I forgot how the most crucial part of sunglasses is the darkening effect. They appear to be dark when you look at them, so it’s kind of an odd thing, and why it took me a day or so for it even to click with me with what was wrong.

These are so weak, I feel like the polarized effect didn’t even do much for glare. I can even see clearly LCD displays that I couldn’t see previously even with other discount brands, so I’d say even this feature isn’t as good as it could be.

Perhaps these may be useful in other sporting uses that people wear these glasses for, or could even be tinted enough for some, but absolutely not for me. If you’re truly dependent on eye protection and can’t leave the house without them like me, just keep looking.

I have purchased more than one pair because I like them so much. I also wear them while coaching cheerleading during Saturday morning football games and honestly could not imagine getting through the season without them. These sunglasses make driving easier as someone with a shorter stature.

The fit guidelines are very accurate, which made it easy to choose the right size on the first try. I wear both glasses and contacts and had struggled to find sunglasses that I truly loved until trying these.

I will definitely continue purchasing more pairs and switch over to using these exclusively.

The order said "v2", but I couldn't find much difference. I think there is an upgrade on the material or hinge? I guess it might feel a little more comfy on my face, but I had chalked that up to just being a new pair and not my old worn down pair that I wear daily.

The size of the mediums (OG) is perfect for the average size face. You can even "try on" the glasses on the Goodr website if you aren't sure, but the measurements are a pretty good indicator if you need the regulars or need to change size.

Goodr lenses are quality, and have great sun protection, especially with their reflective lenses. The only Goodrs I haven't liked too much are the more "clear" lenses where you can see your eyes clearly through the lenses from the front, but that is just a preference choice, and they have so many options.

I'll probably look at picking up another color combo soon. I have about 5 pairs of the "OG" glasses, and they have all been great and super durable. The only thing I have noticed is the frames pickup a lot of grease from my face, especially if I wear sunblock, but I just wipe them down before and after use, and they seem to last forever.

title: Ray-Ban RB3025 Classic Aviator Sunglasses for Men for Women
description:
Aviator sunglasses have the timeless look with the unmistakable teardrop shaped lenses. Featuring gold frames and brown polarized lenses, this small metal aviator style in size 55mm allowed the look to quickly spread beyond their utility becoming popular among celebrities, rock stars and citizens of the world alike.

PT. WASHINGTON, NY, 11050 US

reviews.review_description:
My Ray-Ban 3025 Aviator sunglasses arrived today, and I'm completely satisfied. What I received was undoubtably the REAL Ray-Ban product: packaged in a Ray-Ban box with sticker on the end including the 'Made in Italy' statement and including the Ray-Ban sunglasses case, a small 'manufacturer's information note' paper that is written in no less than 24 languages (!!!) - and I'm not joking (I counted). Plus a small marketing brochure 'The Icons' telling the story of Ray-Ban, and finally a lens cleaning cloth with the Ray-Ban logo. The sunglasses themselves have the Ray-Ban logo etched on the right lens prominently, and very subtly etched on the left lens.

So, that's the package. It's as pictured here, and I start with that description because there is always going to be some trepidation at buying something like this online. Will you get The Real Deal, or a cheap knock-off? Well, I purchased mine from Amazon, not from a third-party seller, to reduce that risk, and I am not disappointed.

Now to the sunglasses themselves. I think that there are a few things to know, for someone considering Ray-Ban sunglasses:

- they come in a very wide variety of frame sizes, lens tints and colors, polarized and non-polarized, and with different frame colors and finishes. If you are not already familiar with these sunglasses and know what you want, then my recommendation is that you first go to the Ray-Ban website and familiarize yourself with those variations, especially if you think that you will want something other than the Traditional Gold Frame, Green Lens sunglass. Once at the Ray-Ban website, select 'customize' at the top, and you'll find yourself on a page where you have the full ability to vary the choices I've summarized below. These variations can all be found on Amazon although navigating through all of the sellers and product pages on Amazon that list the different variations of these sunglasses can be very time consuming and confusing.

- For the 3025 Aviator style, the following variations are available:

--- There are no less than 35 choices of lenses - 'classic', 'legends', 'gradient', 'mirrored and flash', and 'polarized'

--- There are 8 variations in frame color - basic colors of gold and matte gold, and 'trendy' colors of black and 5 others

--- There are 5 choices of temple tips (the end of the earpiece) - black or white as basic choices, and brown, beige or transparent also available

--- There are a three different sizes available for the Ray-Ban Large Aviator RB3025. THIS IS IMPORTANT:

----------- 58 14 135: the basic standard size is 58 mm lens diameter, 14 mm bridge width, with temple length 135 mm

----------- 55 14 135: slightly smaller lens size, with same bridge width and temple length

----------- 62 14 140: larger lens size and temple length

--- There are also further variations to the Aviator sunglass:

----------- Large Aviator II RB3026: only available as 62 14 140

----------- Small Aviator RB3044: only available as 52 14 135

----------- Folding Aviator RB3479: available in 55 14 140 and 58 14 145

----------- Outdoorsman II RB3029 (includes 'brow bar' or 'sweat bar'): available in 62 14 140

----------- Outdoorsman RB3030 (includes ''brow bar' or 'sweat bar' plus cable temples): available in 58 14 160

----------- Outdoorsman II Rainbow RB3407 (with 'brow bar' in pink and possibly other color variations): available in 55 14 135 and 58 14 135

----------- Outdoorsman II Craft RB3422Q (with 'brow bar' and temple pads in genuine hand stitched deer leather): available in 58 14 135

----------- Shooter RB3138 (with 'brow bar' or 'sweat bar' and a small circle just below the brow bar. Also the lenses are placed closer together than other Aviator models): available in 58 09 135

- once you have figured out what you want, then the complexity is reduced and it's simply a matter of determining which seller is offering the best price. My own choice was to purchase from Amazon, not from a third-party seller, and I actually ordered two different pairs of sunglasses because I wanted to try both the polarized and non-polarized lenses, and the choices I found also had some variation in frame color that I thought would be worth checking out. I therefore purchased for myself, from Amazon, the following two pairs:

- Ray-Ban Men's Aviator Large Metal Sunglasses, RB3025, 58mm, polarized lens, grey frame, 135 mm temple

- Ray-Ban Men's Aviator Large Metal Non-Polarized Sunglasses, RB3025, 58mm, gold frame, 135 mm temple

The quality of these sunglasses is apparent from the first moment when you remove them from the case. The frames are very high quality, and the gold frame in particular is finished to a high polish and looks absolutely fabulous. The gray frame is less distinctive but equally handsome. I haven't used them in the sunlight for long enough yet to be able to know the difference between the polarized and non-polarized lenses, but my expectation is that the polarized lenses will be my choice for the brightest days and outdoor use, particularly occasions such as on the water. Both glasses provide a good degree of sun protection without darkening my vision overmuch. And both provide the UV protection that my eye doctor told me to get.

I think that some adjustment is going to be necessary, to the nose pieces as well as the temples, to get these to fit exactly right. I'll take them to one of the local optometrist shops and see if I can get them to help with that, so that they are adjusted correctly.

Ray-Ban 3025 Aviator. I'm pleased with my choice.

reviews.review_title: I love the color and style
reviews.review_description: I’m really happy with my glasses! The only thing I wanted to mention is that the box they arrived in was completely damaged, but thankfully the glasses themselves were perfectly fine.

WOW. I am IN LOVE with these fabulous, classic Ray-Ban aviators, by far my favorite sunglass style.

The reason I never owned a real pair is because the original size was too big for my female face and the juniors size was too small. Well, Ray-Ban finally made a middle size, 58mm, that’s absolutely perfect for a woman’s face.

These are so incredibly flattering. The gunmetal frame with dark G15 lenses (they look black to people looking at you) gives these shades a very edgy, cool vibe. I wear black every day, so these are right up my alley.

I really like the darkness and sun-blocking ability of the G15 lenses. I live in Arizona and have chronic migraines that can be triggered simply by exposure to bright sunlight. Having very dark sunglasses is a must for daytime driving, due to glare. These are super comfortable for all-day wear.

The difference in quality is profound between these glasses, made in Italy, and the 6 pairs of $12 aviators in many colors that I bought on Amazon. There is no comparison, whatsoever. The country that made the $12 glasses is known for cheap products and it shows. Every thing I’ve ever purchased that was made it Italy is top notch & lasts forever.

Most definitely, you get what you pay for. The lens quality and construction are superb.

Invest in at least one pair of exceptional sunglasses. It’s worth it. You won’t be disappointed if you choose Ray-Ban.

To fit my slender nose, I very gently adjusted the nose pieces, by bending them slightly inward. I also very gently curved the arms in a smidge so the glasses don’t move if I look straight down. Easy adjustments.

Get these glasses! I got them on sale for about $125 yesterday & they’re $150 today. If you see them for $135 or less, grab them on the spot!

title: Ray-Ban RB3025 Classic Polarized Aviator Sunglasses
description: Designed in 1937 for U.S. military pilots to protect their eyes from the sun's rays at high altitude, the Ray-Ban RB3025 Classic Polarized Aviator sunglasses for men and women has evolved from functional flight gear into one of the world's most iconic eyewear styles — crafted in Italy and made famous by Top Gun. Worn by generals, Hollywood legends, among fashion-conscious individuals and style icons across generations, this original aviator represents timeless design that transcends trends. Today, these Ray-Ban sunglasses for men and women remains the go-to choice for driving, travel, beach sunglasses, and everyday wear for daily activities. These unisex sunglasses combine lightweight comfort with exceptional quality, performance, and superior optics, making them a true staple in men's and women's fashion. Built with Ray-Ban's renowned craftsmanship, these aviator sunglasses feature durable wire metal frames designed for long-lasting wear. These premium classic, timeless sunglasses feature 100% UV protection to shield your eyes from harmful rays, making them perfect for outdoor adventures. These polarized sunglasses for men and women eliminate reflected glare — the ultimate choice for driving glasses, water sports, and outdoor adventures. The go-to aviator sunglasses for men and aviator sunglasses for women who want the clearest vision and shades for men and women built for performance. These mens sunglasses and womens sunglasses make the perfect gift for drivers, travelers, and style icons. Each pair includes a case and cleaning cloth. Click on the Ray-Ban link above the product title to shop the entire Ray-Ban sunglass and eyeglass assortment.

reviews.review_description:
My Ray-Ban 3025 Aviator sunglasses arrived today, and I'm completely satisfied. What I received was undoubtably the REAL Ray-Ban product: packaged in a Ray-Ban box with sticker on the end including the 'Made in Italy' statement and including the Ray-Ban sunglasses case, a small 'manufacturer's information note' paper that is written in no less than 24 languages (!!!) - and I'm not joking (I counted). Plus a small marketing brochure 'The Icons' telling the story of Ray-Ban, and finally a lens cleaning cloth with the Ray-Ban logo. The sunglasses themselves have the Ray-Ban logo etched on the right lens prominently, and very subtly etched on the left lens.

So, that's the package. It's as pictured here, and I start with that description because there is always going to be some trepidation at buying something like this online. Will you get The Real Deal, or a cheap knock-off? Well, I purchased mine from Amazon, not from a third-party seller, to reduce that risk, and I am not disappointed.

Now to the sunglasses themselves. I think that there are a few things to know, for someone considering Ray-Ban sunglasses:

- they come in a very wide variety of frame sizes, lens tints and colors, polarized and non-polarized, and with different frame colors and finishes. If you are not already familiar with these sunglasses and know what you want, then my recommendation is that you first go to the Ray-Ban website and familiarize yourself with those variations, especially if you think that you will want something other than the Traditional Gold Frame, Green Lens sunglass. Once at the Ray-Ban website, select 'customize' at the top, and you'll find yourself on a page where you have the full ability to vary the choices I've summarized below. These variations can all be found on Amazon although navigating through all of the sellers and product pages on Amazon that list the different variations of these sunglasses can be very time consuming and confusing.

- For the 3025 Aviator style, the following variations are available:

--- There are no less than 35 choices of lenses - 'classic', 'legends', 'gradient', 'mirrored and flash', and 'polarized'

--- There are 8 variations in frame color - basic colors of gold and matte gold, and 'trendy' colors of black and 5 others

--- There are 5 choices of temple tips (the end of the earpiece) - black or white as basic choices, and brown, beige or transparent also available

--- There are a three different sizes available for the Ray-Ban Large Aviator RB3025. THIS IS IMPORTANT:

----------- 58 14 135: the basic standard size is 58 mm lens diameter, 14 mm bridge width, with temple length 135 mm

----------- 55 14 135: slightly smaller lens size, with same bridge width and temple length

----------- 62 14 140: larger lens size and temple length

--- There are also further variations to the Aviator sunglass:

----------- Large Aviator II RB3026: only available as 62 14 140

----------- Small Aviator RB3044: only available as 52 14 135

----------- Folding Aviator RB3479: available in 55 14 140 and 58 14 145

----------- Outdoorsman II RB3029 (includes 'brow bar' or 'sweat bar'): available in 62 14 140

----------- Outdoorsman RB3030 (includes ''brow bar' or 'sweat bar' plus cable temples): available in 58 14 160

----------- Outdoorsman II Rainbow RB3407 (with 'brow bar' in pink and possibly other color variations): available in 55 14 135 and 58 14 135

----------- Outdoorsman II Craft RB3422Q (with 'brow bar' and temple pads in genuine hand stitched deer leather): available in 58 14 135

----------- Shooter RB3138 (with 'brow bar' or 'sweat bar' and a small circle just below the brow bar. Also the lenses are placed closer together than other Aviator models): available in 58 09 135

- once you have figured out what you want, then the complexity is reduced and it's simply a matter of determining which seller is offering the best price. My own choice was to purchase from Amazon, not from a third-party seller, and I actually ordered two different pairs of sunglasses because I wanted to try both the polarized and non-polarized lenses, and the choices I found also had some variation in frame color that I thought would be worth checking out. I therefore purchased for myself, from Amazon, the following two pairs:

- Ray-Ban Men's Aviator Large Metal Sunglasses, RB3025, 58mm, polarized lens, grey frame, 135 mm temple

- Ray-Ban Men's Aviator Large Metal Non-Polarized Sunglasses, RB3025, 58mm, gold frame, 135 mm temple

The quality of these sunglasses is apparent from the first moment when you remove them from the case. The frames are very high quality, and the gold frame in particular is finished to a high polish and looks absolutely fabulous. The gray frame is less distinctive but equally handsome. I haven't used them in the sunlight for long enough yet to be able to know the difference between the polarized and non-polarized lenses, but my expectation is that the polarized lenses will be my choice for the brightest days and outdoor use, particularly occasions such as on the water. Both glasses provide a good degree of sun protection without darkening my vision overmuch. And both provide the UV protection that my eye doctor told me to get.

I think that some adjustment is going to be necessary, to the nose pieces as well as the temples, to get these to fit exactly right. I'll take them to one of the local optometrist shops and see if I can get them to help with that, so that they are adjusted correctly.

Ray-Ban 3025 Aviator. I'm pleased with my choice.

reviews.review_title: Order somehow switched and still 10% doubt to the authenticity
reviews.review_description:
I was very concerned about all the counterfit Ray Bans on amazon. I did alot of research on what to look for to spot the fakes. Even people who have said "if the glass is etched on the left lense they are authentic". Well the counterfitters will go to extreme lengths to make them look as real as possable. Nearly every detail is copied. So, after looking at different sellers, watching videos of real and fake glasses I searched for SunglassHut on Amazon. They are the brick and morter authorized sellers. I saved my order to my shopping cart from the Sunglasshut page on Amazon and they were $199.95. When I checked out I noticed it said "sold by and fullfilled by Amazon for $118. This made me a little worried. I wanted to pay the extra money to be sure they were authentic.Why the seller changed I have no idea.

Now my review. I am still not 100 percent they are authentic but about 90 percent sure. All the research I have done and the fakes I have seen have all the same markings on the glasses and the case. The only thing the real ones have that the fake ones do not are that the ends of the plastic ear pieces curve a little bit. all the pictures and videos I have seen show the fakes with straight ear pieces at the very ends. The lenses are indeed polarized as you can tell from looking at different peoples rear windows of their cars in the sun. The glass has an invisable checkerboard pattern with the glasses on and it goes away with them off. The blue mirroring is nice and you cant see your eyes from other peoples perspective unless sunlight is coming in from the sides. The fit is good and I will go to my local Sunglasshut store to have them adjusted.

Overall 4 stars because of placing in my cart from the sunglasshut page and then it being changed to sold and fullfilled through Amazon, and the fact I still have that 10% doubt they could be fakes.

Let's be honest. At a certain point in life, a man has to make a decision.

Do you embrace the full "I buy my sneakers based on orthopedic recommendations" lifestyle, or do you make one last respectable effort to suggest that you may have been cool at some point?

These sunglasses are that effort.

They're comfortable, fit well, and look good without screaming, "Hey everyone, look how hard I'm trying to look young!" Which is important, because nothing ages a dad faster than trying too hard.

I've always admired aviators on other people. Unfortunately, every time I've tried a pair on, I look less like a fighter pilot and more like a guy being questioned by airport security.

These, meanwhile, strike the perfect balance. Modern enough to look good, practical enough for everyday wear, and subtle enough that nobody immediately assumes I'm having a midlife crisis.

I've worn them driving, coaching kids' sports, running errands, and standing in the driveway pretending to understand whatever home improvement project I'm currently avoiding.

Bottom line: Comfortable, stylish, and ideal for dads looking to project the image of a man who still has things under control.

I have owned multiple of the $200 Ray Bans over the years and they always fall apart. Truly "they don't make em like they used to". I remember being a kid wearing Ray Bans in the 80s and 90s and they were dirt cheap and lasted forever. Even as a kid I lost them before I could ever break them. Now my last two made me write off Ray Ban. Just not worth that kind of money when the logo on the arm falls off after a few months or the arms becomes incredibly loose and even Sunglass Hut where you bought them can't fix them and Ray Ban offers virtually zero customer service what's the point of spending that much??

Well, with these sunglasses, I bought a pair as a spare option just in case because I can't go outside without sunglasses due to my eyes being so sensitive to sunlight. I was IMMEDIATELY impressed by the quality. The frames have this matte black color with a sort of soft texture to them. Not rubbery but almost feels soft like that. They feel incredibly nice when pressed against your head or rubbing on your ears. Never feeling uncomfortable no matter now long I wear them.

I loved them so much I now own 5 pairs because even at 5 pairs they cost about as much as a pair of Knockarounds. I paid $40 for my Knockarounds that feel cheap and get loose quickly. I have had a pair of these for I believe about 3+ months now and they are still holding up fantastic. Initially I bought 2 pairs because I wanted a "car pair" but I have only been wearing one pair this whole time and they still look brand new and not a single scratch that I can see despite having dropped them many times. The matte texture does allow for fingerprints but not obvious fingerprints. More like some smudging but I have never noticed it because the matte black hides it well. You really gotta look for it unless maybe you have really oily skin then perhaps it can be an issue then.

They're lightweight but not so light that they feel cheap. Somewhere in-between "heavy luxury" and "Walmart $5 rack light" yet they wear like my old $200 Ray Bans.

These shades are proof that we should not always believe "you get what you pay for". If you disagree go buy a pair of Ray Bans instead and let's see what happens in 3 months if you drop them even once.

The ones in my picture are the ones I've been exclusively wearing for 3 months and I am the kind of person who drops their glasses, puts them in their pocket/bag etc unprotected, wears them to the beach/pool (pool about 3 times a week over the last 3 months jumping in the water with them on too!) etc. These have held up incredibly well for the $8-$9 I paid for them. If they last 6 months to a year I'll be happy but at this rate I feel like they'll last a lot longer than that considering I can't even see signs of wear yet. The arms are still strong and stiff and the lens' look scratch-free.

I love them! Couldn't ask for more from a $9 pair of shades! Hell, if these were $20-$30 I'd still prefer them over my $40 Knockarounds/Goodr/Blenders etc. They look/feel premium and hold up well!

title: Maui Jim Men's and Women's Stingray Polarized Wrap Sunglasses
description: Inspired by encounters with the rare and gentle stingrays of Hawaii, the Stingray wrap sunglasses from Maui Jim are subtle in their magnificence. Made with a durable acetate frame and glare-free, polarized lenses ready to tackle any activity.

reviews.review_description:
I purchased these in July of 2014. I paid $189 for the black frame/netural gray Glass lenses. They have held up very well. No scratches, and the temple springs are as good as they were when new. I take good care of them, keeping them in their case when not in use, and clean them regularly using a bit of dish soap. I love the clarity and weight of the glass lenses, as they are superior to any of the composite lenses I've had a chance to compare them to, including their own brand's plastic lenses. (I spent some time in a Bass Pro Shop comparing these to Costas, Smiths, and Oakleys)

These are my everyday casual and business wear glasses. These are great for driving; the polarization on these lenses is superior to Oakley in my opinion, and I love how well the polarizing lenses cut glare. These also work fantastic for cutting glare on watery surfaces like lakes and rivers, but honestly I am too fearful of losing these in the water to wear them near it!

I would not wear these for any activity requiring a lot of movement, such as playing sports, since they are heavy, and because most of the weight is in the lenses, they are likely to fall off. During every day use though, these are secure enough that them falling off your head is a non-issue (unless you try to "store" them on the top of your head when not in use - DON'T do that!).

My only grip with these is that after wearing them continuously for more than an hour, they do become a bit uncomfortable on the bridge of my nose.. taking them off for a brief period helps with any discomfort, but this is the sacrifice I'm willing to make to wear glass lenses.

I will admit I keep a pair of Oakley flak jackets around for outdoor activities, and for times when I worry about scratching the lens (such as bumming on the beach).

However, the quality of these are fantastic and I am glad I purchased them... I will buy another when the time comes.

Couple of tips:

- In my opinion, I would NOT suggest purchasing these glasses in a composite lens... the glass lenses are so much clearer. In my opinion, these frames are designed to hold a heavy glass lens in place. I would prefer to purchase a composite lens in a "frameless" or "semi-frameless" option to take advantage of the lighter weight of the composite lenses, and the ability to swap lenses on some brands of frames.

- The shiny black frame, on the inside of the frame actually reflects light at some angles, and can be distracting. Wearing a hat eliminates this completely, but if you're looking for a frame that completely blocks the sun due to the way it wraps and fits your face, this probably isn't going to be sufficient.

Read more

After a visit to the eye doc it was presumed that my "fave" sunglasses may not be up to the protection job they might have had when new. I was told that many brands of glasses only lightly "coat" the lenses for UV protection especially the "plastic" lenses. Cheap glasses may not have any UV protection at all despite the claims...who tests them?? Nobody?? What apparently isn't told is that these coatings may/do deteriorate over time AND using alcohol lens cleaners and dish soaps may also remove coatings. My research indicated that the more expensive brands have higher quality and more durable UV coatings (impregnated or baked into the glass) that are important to protect your eyes from sun damage -- not just shading. Although my "Faves" were not inexpensive, they were 4 or 5 years old and apparently had inferior to perhaps zero UV blocking abilities today! Long story short, I researched the MJs and found that these glass lenses have superior harmful UV blocking. my Polycarbonate "faves" lenses...less so and were (only effective when new) likely "coated". I did a side by side comparison between these and my old "faves" and I was blowen away by the superior clarity and color crispness of these Maui Jim glasses. You only have one set of eyes...treat them with respect and invest in quality eye ware...not for fashion but, so you don't lose you vision acuity in later years when it's too late to undo damage. Suffice it to say....these are GREAT sunglasses and even look good...a bonus!!! My eyes deserve the investment. Yours do too!!

There’s also a tradeoff between four little legs at the bottom and stability on uneven ground or in a stiff breeze versus a real tripod with three legs that extend all the way or nearly all the way to where the camera is mounted. But I think the makers of this hit it about right! What is innovative about this product though is, to begin with, that it has a face-tracking feature built into it in the form of a rectangular module with a camera and controls in it that do not require any kind of connection to another device. The face-tracking can even be turned on and off with hand gestures. The face-tracking really does work! And it’s quite impressive! The device that does this has a built in battery and is rechargeable by a USB-C A cable that is included. for which is included. There is also a remote shutter device which of course does need to connect with a phone or other device by means of Bluetooth. There’s a little slot where the remote fits into the tripod as well so this small device can be kept with the tripod and not get lost. This remote pairs very easily with an iphone. I’ve not tried it on other cameras. The main mount works with either a clip or by magnetic means with a suitably equipped MagSafe phone or other phone with a ferrous metal ring attached. One such adhesive metal ring is included with this product. So overall this is a great product. The one downside is that if a phone is attached to the magnetic mount its screen is facing the same direction as the face-tracking detector/camera. And that means one must use the phone’s backward-facing selfie camera rather than the phone’s better quality forward-facing camera. But despite that limitation this is a wonderful product with tremendous functionality while remaining fairly lightweight – a few ounces over a pound – as well as compact and therefore portable and versatile. $55.99 as of this writing is a good value for what you’re getting and in comparison to similar items on offer. Recommended!

I picked up the Oldshark 71" auto face-tracking tripod to film short-form content for TikTok and YouTube, and it's become my goto for solo shoots. No app, no Bluetooth pairing, just set it down, hit record, and it starts following my face. The rotation is smooth and surprisingly accurate. I can walk left to right, stand up or sit down, and it keeps me centered without jerky movements. It handles normal room lighting well, though in very dim settings it can lose me briefly until I step back into the light. At 71 inches fully extended, it's tall enough to get a full body shot without angling the phone awkwardly. The base feels stable and I haven't had it tip over even when I'm moving around. reviews.review_title: Tracking Works Well, But Watch the Height
reviews.review_description:
This tripod has some genuinely useful features, and a couple of things worth knowing before you commit. The single-tap auto-deploy legs are quick and work exactly as advertised. The Bluetooth shutter paired to my phone without any hassle, and the magnetic phone mount is strong enough to hold my 15 Pro Max while in a case. On top of that, it includes spring-loaded clamps for extra security, two cold shoe mounts, and a threaded 1/4-inch mount tucked right into the phone mount assembly, which is a nice touch for anyone wanting to add accessories.

The auto subject tracking does its job well for self-recording and 360-degree walk-around videos. The tracking range is decent for those use cases. That said, the left-to-right motion gets a bit jerky when the subject moves suddenly, so if you're doing anything fast-paced, expect some choppiness in the footage. The bigger issue is stability at full extension. When the tripod is extended too far with auto tracking engaged, the stand flexes and sways noticeably, and you can see it in the recorded video. For the best results, keep the height as short as possible for your shot.

One thing I'd love to see (and as a suggestion, this doesn't reflect in my review), in a future version is the ability to detach the tracking head and mount it onto a sturdier tripod. The tracking unit itself performs well enough that pairing it with a more stable base would make a real difference for taller setups.

Read more

3 stars because the stand tracks your movement fine. However the stand itself is not sturdy enough to accommodate the weight of my phone while turning. The entire stand wobbles side to side as it tracks your movements. Hence creating wobble in video recordings. See my video. I have a Samsung fold 5. Sure it's a heavier phone. But it still should not wobble like that as it tracks you. If you have a small phone, this would probably suit your needs just fine. Not for me.

This AI face tracking tripod has been a really convenient addition to my content setup. The 360° tracking follows movement smoothly without requiring an app or Bluetooth connection for the tracking feature, which makes getting started much easier. The gesture controls are also handy for starting or pausing tracking while recording. I like that it can be used for everything from vlogging and livestreams to workouts, cooking videos, and video calls.

The magnetic phone mount makes setup quick, especially with a MagSafe-compatible iPhone. The included protective clip adds extra security and makes the setup more versatile for other phones. The 71-inch height is useful for getting different perspectives, while the four-leg base provides good stability. The detachable Bluetooth remote is another nice feature for taking photos or starting recordings from a distance.

This is a versatile creator tripod with a lot of useful features in one compact setup. It can function as a selfie stick, handheld grip, desktop tripod, or full-size tracking tripod, and the rotating mount allows both vertical and horizontal filming. The long battery life, quick setup, remote shutter, and broad device compatibility make it a great option for anyone who regularly creates videos or takes photos on the go.

reviews.review_title: Strong, Simple Tripod for Solo Video Work
reviews.review_description:
I bought this for solo phone shoots, tutorials, and quick social clips where I need to stay in frame without asking someone to operate the camera. The build feels much sturdier than I expected for a portable tracking tripod. Most of the body and legs use aluminum, while only the leg-release buttons use plastic.

Setup takes almost no time. I unfold it, attach my iPhone magnetically, and start recording without downloading another app or granting unnecessary phone permissions. The face tracking responds well as I move around the room, and the 360-degree rotation keeps me centered for walk-and-talk clips, product demos, and full-body shots.

The ball head locks down firmly once tightened, so my phone does not slowly drift as it does on cheaper tripods. At full extension, the nearly 71-inch height gives me enough range for standing shots, while the compact folded size fits easily in my production bag.

The magnetic mount makes switching from handheld filming to tripod work fast. I would still use a dedicated heavy tripod for larger cameras or windy outdoor shoots, but this works great for an iPhone and lightweight camera setup. For solo creators, it makes filming more efficient and less frustrating.

reviews.review_title: A Lightweight Inexpensive Tripod That Gets The Job Done!

I was excited to receive the KraftGeek Magnetic Phone Tripod for the MagSafe iPhone yesterday (Nov 10th) to use with my new iPhone 17 Pro Max!

Since I’m an astronomer, I was excited to test the new iPhone’s cameras.

Unfortunately, I was sent a returned and/or defective product not a new one.

When it arrived. I noticed the tripod box was unsealed and the tripod itself was in an opened plastic sleeve. The tripod legs were already open and was unable to close/secure the legs so subsequently the *Tap* to open feature did not work.

I immediately requested a return/replacement with Amazon and received a new tripod today (Nov 11th - Veterans Day)

The new replacement tripod came in a factory sealed box and sleeve so my suspicion on receiving a returned/defective product was verified.

Anyhow, the new tripod works as advertised which is *Great* and the provided USB remote paired easily and quickly to my iPhone 17 Pro Max.

As an astrophotographer, I shoot deep-sky objects like star clusters, galaxies or nebulae and stack the accumulated images, so recommend you shoot on a non-windy day because your camera will easily succumb to the wind on this lightweight tripod. I don’t think it will fall over, but certainly you’ll see movement in your images and for astrophotographers that’s not good thing!

Serious astrophotographers should look for a heavier, more stable tripod. Maybe KraftGeek can make a sturdy MagSafe smartphone tripod for us?

Amazon was *Amazing* (As Always) in the return process, quickly sending me a new replacement product within 24hrs.

Considering the low cost of this tripod, it’s functionally and convenience, I would’ve given 5-Stars but docked them 1-star because of the inconvenience of returning a defective tripod.

A unique mini 6-string nylon guitar that is sized like a baritone ukulele (17" scale) and plays like a standard tune guitar. The guitalele's tuning is pitched up to "A" (or up a 4th) at A/D/G/C/E/A.

reviews.review_title: Great little guitar that can play your favorite Uke songs too!
reviews.review_description:
I've been playing this little gem for a week now as a replacement for my full size acoustic that is in dire need of a neck reset. It sits next to my office chair where I can pick it up and play any time. So far it has done a pretty good job of staying in tune with only the usual nylon string settling in. Tone is interesting with a neat, plucky sound and, being tuned to A, it shares the same finger positions on the 4 treble strings as a ukulele. In fact, it is a good sounding baritone ukulele but could be a little bit challenging for some due to closer string spacing compared to a uke. Action is fine and I am in no hurry to change the setup. factory strings seem OK and i will play on them until they wear out. Yamaha states that low or standard tension classical strings can be used and Savarez, D'Addario and DR are recommended brands. No need for special guilele strings.

The finish is very satin and may not be pleasing for those that enjoy glossy guitars though i think it's OK and seems tough enough. My GL1 came with a small blemish in the wood on the back which is an imperfection in the wood itself and not the finish. I would take 1/2 a star for the blemish but quality control is overall pretty good and the fret ends aren't noticeably sharp.

I would not recommend this instrument for beginners due to the short fret spacing and slightly more difficult fingering for some chords. A 1/2 or 3/4 scale classical or steel string guitar will be a better choice for learning the fundamentals and will have more volume for performances later on when the player gains confidence.

Who is this instrument for? number one, it's for me. I have been playing guitar for decades and have a soft spot for small bodied instruments and recently started playing my wife's ukulele due to my guitar being down for the count. Ukulele players might enjoy this instrument as a way to cross over to six string though the string spacing will take some getting used to. Guitar players who want a sturdy travel guitar will be well served by this instrument but will have to make peace with transposing everything up a fourth. Some players have used high tension strings to allow for standard guitar tuning. I'm not sure I will do so as I like the sound as it is and also play ukulele music.

Overall I think the Yamaha GL-1 is a reasonable value for the money and I'm very happy with it so far.

69 year old guitar hack here. Played electric, and some acoustic guitar in three bands way back in the 1970's. Played acoustic at a wedding. My neighbor bought a Yamaha GL-1 "guitalele" A few years ago, and told me recently that he loves it! A GL-1 is basically a very compact 6 string classical guitar, but, instead of being tuned Eadgbe, it is tuned 5 frets up on each string, so the low and high e's become a's. This means that all the chord shapes I know on a regular guitar can be played in the same positions, but the name of the chord will be different. Example, an e major chord shape on a guitar, will really be an a major on the Yamaha. If I am just playing by myself for myself, there is no problem. If I was to play along with a regular guitar, we would have to work out what key to play in. Also, if I sing and play, then depending on what key I play in, I would have to sing in higher notes.

This thing came quicky to me in Hawaii, and it is in perfect condition! Since it had nylon/classical type strings, it is going to take much longer for the strings to settle down and stop sretching. Way longer than my steel stringers. So, don't write a review after a few days complaining about this. All classical style nylon string guitars do this! Pick it up,tune it, play it, and keep tuning it. The tuners on mine seem just fine. It is a total blast for me to play. It sounds great, especially for the small body size. It has very good volume and sustain too. A bit stingy on the fret markers, both on the fingerboard and side of the neck. If you have big fingers, some chording might be a bit crowded. It doesn't have a truss rod. But, many classical guitars and many other guitaleles don't have them either. I have yet to read a review, or watch a video review, where the owner had a neck warp. In short, I should have bought one of these long ago.

Update after more than a year now. I still love this little 6 stringer! I have been selling some of my amps and ukes etc. I had considered selling my Yamaha, but cannot do it! It is just such a great insrument. Mine is still perfect. Drawbacks? Few. The 17" scale is a bit tight for me. One string started unravelling after not too much playing. I was able to buy the one string and replaced it. I read a review somewhere where the writer returned his due to various flaws. Looking at mine it's hard to believe. I think Yamaha should make an option of the GL-1 that would come with an under saddle pickup with tuner and volume/tone controls. Great price, great instrument, great FUN!!

2/28/2025 update:

Just wanted to say my estimation of this instrument has gone up if anything. I am taking super good care of it. It us holding up great. I had one of the wound strings start to unravel early and replaced it. Zero problems. After break in it holds tune as good or better than my other string instruments. That alone is saying a lot. The climate here in the Puna District on the big island plays he'll with stringed instruments. Most go sharp sitting overnight, and flat sitting during the day. This little guy is built very well. I wish it had come with an active pickup with tuned and equalizer, but it's still a keeper!

reviews.review_title: Perfect little guitar for fun and travel
reviews.review_description:
This little thing is one of my dearest possessions!!

I've played guitar as a hobby off and on for about 18 years and have a couple of full-sized acoustics. About a year ago I started researching smaller instruments because I wanted something easy to travel with. I looked into 1/4 size student guitars and I looked into the Little Martin and its Taylor equivalent. While the Little Martin has great reviews and a great sound, it costs 3-4 times more than this little guy does. It's definitely worth that price, but I didn't have that kind of money to spend. For about $100, the Yamaha Guitalele is excellent.

It has a beautiful sound and it's very easy to pick up and take it with you on trips! (To keep it safer for long trips I bought a hard shell tenor uke case which works really well for it. I also bought one of those little Snark clip-on tuners and have been very satisfied with that as well.)

Two things which take some adjusting to if you are used to playing a full-size guitar:

1) The strings are a lot closer together and your fingers may feel fat and clumsy at first. I got used to this pretty fast though.

2) The guitalele is tuned to A instead of the standard E tuning of a full-sized guitar. Basically this means anything you play on the guitalele is like playing your reg. guitar with a capo on the 5th fret. So when you play a C-shape chord on this guy, you are actually playing a G chord. I was used to playing a lot of songs on my regular guitar and had to figure out how to translate them to continue playing them in the same key. (It's possible to lower the tuning to E if you want, but the strings have a slack, kind of rubbery sound and they don't stay in tune as long.)

I'd recommend checking out the YouTube video reviews for this instrument before you buy it if you have any more questions. You can hear what it sounds like and get some expert input! It really is great. I love mine to the moon and back and have had a blast playing it!

reviews.review_title: Fun instrument for the price, but don't expect perfection.
reviews.review_description:
This guitalele has opened up a bit since I got it.

I started playing ukulele 2 years ago, and started learning guitar almost a year ago. After having Amazon cancel an order I placed on an acoustic guitar from the Amazon Warehouse. (Grr! Btw on that! I feel really cheated considering the same guitar turned up with a seller who refabs and resells damaged instruments, and I was extremely excited about it, until I got the message "they couldn't find it," last minute on delivery day!!! 😠 That's so wrong imo.) I chose this guitalele in it's stead however.

It has issues with frets not being cut long enough in spots but nothing that makes it unplayable. It's cosmetic for the most part. There's a few other purely cosmetic issues. Mine has a couple spots the factory missed applying the wood filler to, on the body to make it smooth. Theres a small spot on the bottom of the neck where the wood chipped before assembly and it wasn't filled with filler or even glue to fill the gap. It's a mass produced instrument at an affordable price. I was expecting small imperfections. The sloppy fret cutting job is the only kind-of annoying one to me. The one I have is actually a replacement for one I exchanged which had a mfg. defect which made it unplayable. The first one wasn't inspected properly and shouldn't have left the factory in the dangerous condition it was in. Amazon took care of me immediately and the exchange was smooth and painless. Hopefully yamaha corrects the quality control issues in their factory.

For my own play style I had the nut filed down so my hand could glide over the nut. The stock nut height stopped my hand down there like a brick wall, and having the nut done cost as much as the guitalele. This probably won't bother most people. I'm just throwing it out there, that the nut sticks up above the string height, and if you like to slide in or out by the nut, it might be something to consider for someone.

The piece of wood that was used on the back of the one I received is unexpectedly pretty. I got lucky. The top has nice strait grain. The neck is ugly. It's constructed in a few pieces and mine doesn't remotely match. One side appears to have had a patch of tear out or something, and Yamaha filled it really nicely with filler, but the filler is darker than the neck wood and adds to the kind of sloppy franken-neck look. Again, not a deal breaker. I can't feel a difference, and they have to keep costs down.

When I got it, it sounded a little "stuffy." After playing it daily since I got it, the wood seems to have opened up a bit on all tones except the low A, which still sounds the same. If it does open up, this instrument is pretty impressive sounding for the money in my opinion.

Someone said in another review the thing is built like a tank. I agree. It's not a delicate feeling instrument. It seems pretty well constructed until the fret wire though.

Overall it's been fun to play. It's the perfect size. I left sheerness blank in the star rating. Not sure how that applies to a guitalele or any stringed instrument? Thickness doesn't really apply either, but I rated it 4 because the wood is thick.

I might update this review in the future if anything changes, but I'd probably get another one if something happens to mine.

reviews.review_title: decent, doesn't need to be tuned up a full 4th to sound OK
reviews.review_description:
Mahalo used to make a similar product for less than half the price, so this guy seems a little overpriced to me – but since the Mahalo seems to be discontinued, there's no real competitor, and this hardly breaks the bank. It has entirely acceptable playability, sound, intontation, etc. I especially like to play it like a mandolin, flat-picking single lines, but of course it can play full-chord accompaniments, sounding just like a ukulele but lower. Travels fine, though one thing to note about the classic camp-singalong use is that the nylon strings are suuuuuper sensitive to temperature changes, so it's a bit frustrating playing it outdoors in chilly air next to a hot campfire

– you might need to invest in a steel-string alternative if you can't abide that.

You *can* tune it to standard guitar tuning (E2, A2, D3, ...), which is useful if you want to use it for, say, composing on the go and not get confused about which key you're in – but down there the strings sound like garbage and don't stay in tune. The recommended tuning is up a 4th, which I find a bit high, since you can't even play G2 (de facto a lot of things you play on guitars tend to be in keys like G, D, C ...). One solution is to use the recommended tuning but with "drop G" (lowest string = G2), which sounds fine. But you also can just tune the whole thing a major 3rd higher than a guitar (major 2nd lower than the recommended tuning), rather than a 4th (so: G2, C3, F3 ....) which IMHO sounds just as good and stays in tune just as well. (I just personally keep getting confused by the mental arithmetic that requires – what you expect to be a G major chord is actually Bb major ... etc.)

I love this thing. I tied a strap to it with some shoe strings, I slap it on my back, get on my bike. I take it with me when I go hiking, to school, to the beach, or anywhere really. The tuning on it is ADGCEA which would be equal to as if you had a capo on a regular guitar's 5th fret, which means that you can play the same chord shapes as a regular guitar, the notes will just be higher.

As far as quality goes, I'm pretty happy with it. Some people said the strings that they got were no good, but I've had mine for about 3 months now and I have no complaints. The strings are very sensitive though. They bend very easily, so sometimes the chords played sound good and other times they might sound a little off. I see as a very delicate instrument.. when I press down my fingers for chords I press them straight down and make sure I'm not bending them. A;so, because they bend easily, it can go out of tune pretty easily too. I tune mine often, to make sure they are good to go. I have always tuned my normal guitars by ear, however I find that it is harder to do with the guitarlele, so I use a tuner usually.

Visually I have no complaints, the wood and finish are nice, the neck has good action and feel, although a small part of me wishes that they had some artwork around the soundhole. As for sound quality, I love it.. the higher strings/notes do stand out more in a way, and definitely have the ukulele sound, but if you play gently enough it creates a nice balance. The resonance is beautiful. It has a very warm, mellow sound. It's pretty loud for it's size too. And it is so versatile, you can play Spanish style chords like Em and Am which sounds awesome (Onda Vaga uses a uke, perfect example, youtube them), .. you can emulate a mandolin to an extent.. I'm not saying it sounds exactly like a mandolin since it obviously can't replicate the resonant-sound of the double layered strings, but it does have the high notes from the strings that at least sound somewhat similar to a mandolin, if you want to cover a song with one. Or you can just play regular songs, normal chord shapes, even powerchords sound good.

It's just like guitar. Just tuned to much higher notes. If you know music theory, you can do a lot with this little guitar. I even have used a capo on mine and it sounds good, although when I put it too high up the fret spaces are so small it's hard to make the chord shapes ;-)

Before I saw the guitarlele I was looking at rogue instruments because they sell cheap mandolins and ukuleles. I checked out reviews of their instruments on youtube and they had some mixed reviews.. they didn't seem like very good quality. I saw someone mention the guitarlele on the comments, and when I looked it up I knew it was the 'travel' instrument I wanted. 100 bucks, for a completely unique Yamaha brand instrument? You can't go wrong. Yamaha aren't the super-high end guitars, but my bigger acoustic is a yamaha and I don't have any complaints about that one either (a friend gave it to me to replace my epiphone acoustic which I need to get a new saddle for).

I hope this review was helpful. If you get one, enjoy it. I know I enjoy mine. I've even started buying other travel instruments like a melodica and a Buffalo Drum.. so yeah. Enjoy!!

reviews.review_title: Here is the "real deal" review on this Guitalele
reviews.review_description:
I've been playing, and writing music since 1984. I play a myriad of instruments and currently, I write and record commercially licensed music under BMI, Inc.

My Wife bought this instrument for me for a holiday gift, but I wanted to check it out before it gets wrapped.. just in case of damage. I am glad that I did. I also know how to setup and do maintenance on both electronic and acoustic instruments.

The good things about this instrument:

This instrument sounds really good, as it seems to be structurally sound. I do not see any cracks in the body or missing glue around the neck joint.

The strings are nice wrapped around to tuning pags.

The open faced tuners and gears seem to be of a higher quality than others that I have seen.

The bad things about this instrument:

The bridge saddle is WAY too high. I have no issues in regards to setting up a bridge saddle, but I expected Yamaha to be a "bit more" on the quality control side of things and at least have the saddle to a more "normal" height.

The fretboard and body of this instrument was "very" dry. I used some Music Nomad f-one oil on the fretboard and some of the body as it needed it "badly".

The thing that was VERY surprising to me, is there were run-offs / rough spots in the back and sides of the instrument. For a more inexpensive instrument from a no-name company.. I could see that. .but for the price and the Yamaha name.. again.. VERY SURPRISING. I'm also having some issues in regards to getting a partial from Amazon for some reason, but I have amplified that further up the chain on the Amazon side.

Other things to think about:

I was able to tune this to a standard guitar tuning, that is very possible.

The neck is "wide" just like a classical guitar. A lot of people think this is a hybrid instrument of an acoustic guitar and a baritone ukulele. It's really a cross between an Classical Guitar and a baritone ukulele.

Conclusion:

I am sure that I will have a really awesome time opening this on Christmas day and setting up the saddle on the bridge. And I can probably buff out the rough spots in the finish.. but buying this really changed my mind in regards to Yamaha quality control.

UPDATE: I was able to take off a lot of material from the saddle, and lowered the strings, so the playability is better, but I still am a bit suprised in regards to the rough spots in the finish. The instrument should be priced in the $50.00 USD mark. Other than that, it does make a nice portable instrument in regards to classical guitar or baritone ukulele. - Tom

reviews.review_title: A Delightful Addition to the Collection!
reviews.review_description: This little guy is so much fun! I love playing the ukulele, but sometimes it can be a little frustrating. With only four strings, uke chords often end up in awkward inversions, having a chord tone other than the tonic as the lowest note. By adding two strings to the bass side, you can always have the inversion you want. For uke players the chords will be a little more complex with two additional strings to deal with. Also, in strumming the "uke sound" you'll need to get the hang of not hitting the bottom two strings. But it's all worth the effort and makes for a more "musically complete" sound. For uke players aspiring to play guitar, this is a great bridge. I think guitarists will find it fun as well. The chords are all familiar but will sound a fourth up. Guitarists who are familiar with using a capo won't have any problem with this. Videos online show how to restring the instrument so it can play down in guitar range, but I think it's more fun as a "super uke!" I like the sunburst style and mahogany back and sides. It has a nice, warm uke-y tone. I'm glad I got it!

reviews.review_description: Good.. appearance looks great.. value of money..

***Update

I am changing my one-star review to five-stars. I wrote my original review complaining of the poor quality, but especially fret placement. The company reached out to me and refunded our money. That is impressive. I appreciate a company that is willing to stand behind their product. Hopefully only our guitar had poor fret placement. Other than that and the poor string quality, the guitar is nice. Again, maybe we just had bad luck.

Original review:

The guitar looks nice upon opening it. It appeared to be of good quality. However, we have only had problems since then.

First, the strings are cheap. They break easily. They did include a replacement set, but we are already through most of those as well. Further, our guitar teacher stated that the frets are off so it will be out of tune the further down you go on the frets. We took it into a guitar repair shop who confirmed the issue. The frets are spaced improperly. They tried to file some parts down to make it the best they could. That was another 50 dollars.

Conclusion, this guitar looks nice but that is about it. If you are seriously looking to learn how to play the guitar then I suggest paying a little more to get a good guitar. We paid almost 100 dollars for this, and more since to replace strings and fix the frets in an attempt to optimize it the best we could. Paying more upfront for a good working guitar with correct fret placement is the best thing to do. I guess we will know better next time. Don't waste your money unless you are looking for a decoration for your room.

reviews.review_title: Would buy again in a second
reviews.review_description: Very nice looking and well put together Fender 3/4 guitar. I am having a little trouble tuning it, but as a newbie to stringed instruments that is probably me. I feel like I got more than what i paid for. Beautiful guitar.

Review – Fender FA-25N Nylon (3/4)

This guitar is very disappointing unless you’re buying it strictly for a small child.

If you have slightly wider fingers, chord shapes are uncomfortable right away. The neck feels narrow, and even basic chords like C major are awkward and frustrating to play.

The biggest issue is the extremely high action. The strings sit very high off the fretboard, making the guitar hard to play and tiring on the fingers. It’s obvious this is done at the factory to avoid fret buzz, but it completely kills playability. The guitar does not feel inviting to play at all.

The instrument is lightweight, and the body doesn’t look poorly assembled, but build quality alone doesn’t make a good musical experience. Comfort and playability matter — and this guitar fails there.

Yes, it’s cheap, but the overall playing experience is bad. If you have any prior musical experience or basic expectations, this guitar is not worth it.

Conclusion:

Only suitable for a young beginner with small hands. Otherwise, I do not recommend it. I’m very disappointed and would not buy this model again.

reviews.review_description:
I was going to try and wait a week or two before writing a review for this, but I just couldn’t help myself. One other thing I’ll add before I start is unlike other reviewers, I haven’t had all the best brand Guitars. I’ve had electric and acoustic guitars, Bass guitars, and Ukuleles of various sizes - all at the $250 or less range. So with that…

I love this instrument. This is the closest thing I’ve ever had to a “deluxe guitar”. I’ve purchased boxes in this range before and thought “yeah, okay, this’ll do.” This is the first time I’ve thought “okay this is what I’m talking about!”

First off, this box keeps in tune. Not only thought but the tuning pegs are tight and seem to snap into tune pretty easily. I walk around the house and sit it up against all kinds of surfaces and don’t have to worry about knocking it out of tune.

Next and just as important, it seems this guitar has raised frets and low action. I saw a few reviews and YouTube comments that made me think this was going to be hard to play and have high action, but this is perfect! I’m not worried about going to get a setup any time soon.

The neck shape does seem to make fretting easier as well. This box was built with a lot of thought and a lot of love. I most recently played baritone ukulele, and even at 6’0 with relatively big hands, a dreadnought style guitar is too cumbersome for me. This thing could be great for a smaller person or kid, but it’s also very comfortable for me.

Lastly but not least, the sound! I will say that when played with a pick or my nails it doesn’t produce a bad sound, but I wouldn’t say that’s the guitars strong suit. It’s kind of high and thin. BUT if you either strum this with your thumb and fingers or (even better) finger style pluck, this thing sounds gorgeous. It’s warm and resonant with lots of emotion. I’ve tried hammer ons, pull offs. Slides, bends, slides into bends, it all sounds clean, full, and resonant. I’m a beginner player, but I can see how I’m really going to be expressing myself with this box soon.

If I had to gripe about anything at all, the bridge is just a little rough and grainy. Like not enough to give me a splinter, but not totally smooth. The rest of the body and guitar feels so nice and high quality to me.

So yeah besides maybe not being the best guitar for pick-exclusive playing, and it might not have any electronics or bells and whistles, I feel like a wizard who found his wand with this guitar. Happy playing y’all!

Ps, the little treats added in the box were a cute touch. 🙂

reviews.review_title: UPDATED 3/6/2022: READ ME! Not as bad as people say! people just love to complain.
reviews.review_description:
READ THIS IF YOU'RE CONSIDERING BUYING THIS GUITAR!!! I bought this used - very good for 45 bucks about a year ago. I probably would not pay full price, as much as I love it. That being said, IT IS NOT JUNK GIVE IT TIME! I swear half the people leaving negative reviews have no idea how guitars work. I am a full grown adult guitar player, and I've been playing since high school. I'm in college now, and I needed something small and light to travel with. I DON'T USE THIS AS MY EVERYDAY GUITAR! I reach for this guy if I'm messing around with chords, my fingers hurt from my metal strings, or I'm just trying to relax. It's great to practice on, but not so much if you're trying to actually play in front of people. Nylons aren't meant to be used like metal stringed acoustics, they're a separate instrument! It still works for that purpose, though, you can play the same exact songs and chords. If you tune it properly it gets the job done. Great for my college dorm or throwing in the car for a camping trip cus it's super light. Great to practice on when I don't feel like lugging my full sized acoustic around. This is a decent product for the price I PAID. Being a nylon string guitar, you have to stretch the strings and tune it quite a bit (2-4 days is recommended for the strings to settle - watch a youtube tutorial on how to do it) Furthermore, the plastic strings that everyone complains about are standard on a nylon. Heck, the C40 from Yamaha, well established nylon, has the same type (but higher quality, I bet) if I recall. They do go out of tune pretty frequently, especially at the start, but it's not even that much - just retune them! The tuner works well for me, but if you don't like it, just get an app like GuitarTuna. Now, for the guitar itself, it's what I expected when I bought it for 45 bucks, barely even damaged since I got a higher quality used (or less damaged I guess) version, and I have to say, it has really grown on me. Guitars are instruments, not toys. You can't give it to a kid and expect them to learn the ins and outs. If you really want them to learn guitar, buy them a cheap acoustic like a rogue or Yamaha, a C40 is a great nylon but you could also get them a metal string, and get them lessons! Find a music store near you, it might be a bit pricey but it's the best way to learn. Originally I recommended swapping the strings, but it's not worth it to be honest. I got it back in 2021 for 45 USD used, and I love it for what I use it for. If you're dead-set on a cheap starter guitar, or you want an affordable spare, grab this but follow my advice. If you really want to learn, shell out the extra money and buy a tried and true brand. For the full price, 80 bucks is not worth it. Get a rogue for that money. Anyway, that's my rant, hope this helps! (I even bumped my review up from 4 to 5 stars - when I first wrote it, it was 1 star because I didn't understand stretching the nylon strings - IT TAKES TIME! but I genuinely love this thing!) Enjoy!

reviews.review_title: 20+ years playing - this is a fine instrument
reviews.review_description:
First off - this does not come set up in any way shape or form. If you are not familiar with guitars and buy this for a child please know that it's not a horrible instrument just because the strings come loose.

The first thing I did is replace the strings - I got the nylon version and nylon strings are notorious for taking forever to stretch out to their final length. Another thing to be aware of - the guitar going out of tune with brand new strings is not the guitar's fault - that's just the nature of classical guitars and since it wasn't setup or tuned from the factory it's going to take a while after you get it for it to stay in tune because the strings are stretching out slowly. I pick the guitar right up by the strings and bounce it a bit to help stretch things out when I change nylon strings.

Second, this is a 70 dollar guitar, manage your expectations.

I have about 10 different stringed instruments in my possession in varying qualities. I've bought cheaper instruments when I was planning on spending a chunk of money because the cheaper instruments can sometimes play and sound much better.

You don't need to spend a massive amount of money for a solid instrument - and frankly the Pyle brand is pretty excellent for the cost. I own a bunch of their microphones and they are pretty epic honestly. I've had people listen to my podcast and tell me how impressed they are with my sound quality and think I'm using 100$+ microphones - and I'm finding the same with the guitar quality.

Good tuners, decent bridge, it's really not bad.

The finish is not great though - if you are purchasing an instrument for aesthetics this probably isn't for you.

They put some weird coating on the fret board that was already flaking off when I got it - though I bought this as a beater guitar so I really don't care. There was also cracking in the finish at the bottom of the guitar. None of this affects playability or sound - so I don't care.

I bought some fun fret marker stickers since this doesn't have any inlays, and the new strings I bought are funky colors. It looks pretty awesome for the 90$ I spent in total with the strings and inlay stickers. It sounds good. It feels great in my hands. I can toss this one in the car or put it on the floor and I couldn't care less if it gets scratched - money well spent.
