I have to say that I am impressed. While I must admit that I'm a beginner at guitar (I'm a former drummer that can no longer play due to health issues), I learned a lot about guitars from an old band mate. This beginner guitar sounds nice, and is of a better size for me to learn on. I have an old acoustic, but the body is far too large for me.

This guitar arrived a little over an hour ago. No nicks, dings, or cracks on it. Checked the screws on the tuning machines, everything was good. Since the headstock is more of a classical style than a regular acoustic, I took off the steel strings that came on the guitar and replaced them with classical strings (nylon - medium tension). While it's going to take at least a few days for the nylon strings to stretch out enough before they stay in tune, I did get it tuned up for a bit and played a few chords. The guitar sounds wonderful, with a good bit of volume. I think I'll enjoy learning on this guitar.

If you decide to get this guitar and go with nylon strings (which you should), unless you go with 'ball end' strings, you might have to look up how to 'tie' the nylon strings onto the guitar, as some nylon strings that you can get will not come with a ball end. I had helped do this on a guitar decades ago, but needed a refresher course, and found the information online easily enough.

The reason I say you should use nylon strings is because they require less tension than the normal steel strings. Since this guitar does *not* have a truss rod, you want to go with strings that do not need as much tension. Using steel strings can cause problems with the bridge piece (breaking or coming off), the neck (warping), and the tuning pegs. You might be able to get away with using light or super light tension steel strings, but that's your choice. I'm sticking with the nylon strings. They bring out the sound that I want from this guitar. They're also easier to learn with as a beginner, as they don't hurt your fingertips as much. Yes, it will take longer to build up the callouses on the fingertips, but hey...less pain when learning can be a good thing.

But again, for an inexpensive guitar, this one is a good deal. As with any instrument, if you're not sure if you, or the person you get it for, are going to maintain interest in learning the instrument...going with an inexpensive instrument like this is always the best idea.

As for the other bits that come in this package...the picks are good, the case is good enough to keep dust off the guitar, the strap is not all that great, and the tuner is pretty much garbage because the battery cover does not want to stay on (I have another one just like it, and it has the same problem), and the pitch pipe is 'meh'. The main thing you want in this package is the guitar. Just get some better strings, a good tuner (I have a 'Snark' that wasn't expensive), and a decent guitar strap...and you're set.

reviews.review_description: I appreciated the price for this guitar. Seems solidly made and electronics are well done - no glitches so far. I like the composition of woods and the resulting sound is clear, can be loud if you want it that way. The imbedded tuner is handy as heck, and the action on the fret board is remarkably low making it fairly easy to play, bend notes, and move quickly. HOWEVER - I do not like the finish on the sounding board. It looks like it is dusty or dirty all the time as a result. Because it comes without a pick guard - the finish is getting scratched. The tuners do not move smoothly and so tuning becomes an issue when needed. And when playing through and amp - it is easy to over power the amp and get some pretty crappy sound as a result. This guitar plays beautifully as an acoustic - just use some caution when plugging in as the sound is easily distorted. Major drawback - comes without a case! description: The AEG Series' slender, single-cutaway bodies deliver powerful and balanced acoustic sound, unplugged or through an amp or PA system. reviews.review_description:
Been playing for 30 years and always wanted a 12 string. With prices this low figured why not. Ordered this and it showed up quickly. Very nice right out the box. The small G string popped on me and took an .010 string from a pile of them I have and tried that, popped that one too. Tried it again and it came right in tune. After that it took a few days for the strings to stop drifting out of tune and are now pretty solid. I play it daily and its a great player. I bought this guitar for my son to replace my twenty year old Takamine 12 string that he had been playing for the last five years.

From my son's point of view, the guitar is easy to play for a 12 string. The onboard tuner is an upgrade from the older guitar because it also shows the battery life. It's also easy to read. The sound quality is bright and has a higher register. It is smaller than the Takamine. He said the fretboard was high quality.

As for looks, it's a beautiful guitar. It's sleek and elegant.

We're both happy with the purchase.

This brings plays very nicely. I bought the Vangoa 12 string from Amazon and was very disappointed so I replaced it with this Ibanez. The Vangoa did have a nice matte black finish but the tuners were garbage. This Ibanez has a satin neck and glossy body finish. Does have some sharp fret ends that can be fixed with some minor sanding. Tuners hold time nicely even though 12 strings are notoriously difficult to keep in tune. The action after was great up to the 12th fret but too high afterwards so I did take out bridge saddle and sand it from the bottom end (approximately 1mm) to lower the overall action. There is a spare saddle included incase you need it. Worked out well afterwards. Overall would highly recommend if you’re looking play Pink Floyd Wish You Were Here or Bon Jovi songs lol at home but if you something more professional for recording then I would recommend something better.

This is a really nice starter guitar for beginners, especially for younger players or anyone wanting something smaller and easier to handle. We got this for our 3 year old grandson and he loves whamming away on it trying to play. The 30-inch size feels more comfortable than a full-size guitar for him. It has a clean look and comes with the basic accessories needed to get started. The sound is really good for a beginner setup and works well for practice. The bundle setup makes it convenient without needing separate purchases. I feel like this is a super good entry-level option to learn on.

The ONLY complaint is that the strings it comes with are very cheap and don't sound good. We swapped them for D'Addario strings and it played so much better. Its okayyy i think i just suck at the guitar but i've learned that its pretty easy to tune. my brother got the hang of it so its good for a beginner. very comfortable to hold and i love the black.

I have to say that I am impressed. While I must admit that I'm a beginner at guitar (I'm a former drummer that can no longer play due to health issues), I learned a lot about guitars from an old band mate. This beginner guitar sounds nice, and is of a better size for me to learn on. I have an old acoustic, but the body is far too large for me.

This guitar arrived a little over an hour ago. No nicks, dings, or cracks on it. Checked the screws on the tuning machines, everything was good. Since the headstock is more of a classical style than a regular acoustic, I took off the steel strings that came on the guitar and replaced them with classical strings (nylon - medium tension). While it's going to take at least a few days for the nylon strings to stretch out enough before they stay in tune, I did get it tuned up for a bit and played a few chords. The guitar sounds wonderful, with a good bit of volume. I think I'll enjoy learning on this guitar.

If you decide to get this guitar and go with nylon strings (which you should), unless you go with 'ball end' strings, you might have to look up how to 'tie' the nylon strings onto the guitar, as some nylon strings that you can get will not come with a ball end. I had helped do this on a guitar decades ago, but needed a refresher course, and found the information online easily enough.

The reason I say you should use nylon strings is because they require less tension than the normal steel strings. Since this guitar does *not* have a truss rod, you want to go with strings that do not need as much tension. Using steel strings can cause problems with the bridge piece (breaking or coming off), the neck (warping), and the tuning pegs. You might be able to get away with using light or super light tension steel strings, but that's your choice. I'm sticking with the nylon strings. They bring out the sound that I want from this guitar. They're also easier to learn with as a beginner, as they don't hurt your fingertips as much. Yes, it will take longer to build up the callouses on the fingertips, but hey...less pain when learning can be a good thing.

But again, for an inexpensive guitar, this one is a good deal. As with any instrument, if you're not sure if you, or the person you get it for, are going to maintain interest in learning the instrument...going with an inexpensive instrument like this is always the best idea.

As for the other bits that come in this package...the picks are good, the case is good enough to keep dust off the guitar, the strap is not all that great, and the tuner is pretty much garbage because the battery cover does not want to stay on (I have another one just like it, and it has the same problem), and the pitch pipe is 'meh'. The main thing you want in this package is the guitar. Just get some better strings, a good tuner (I have a 'Snark' that wasn't expensive), and a decent guitar strap...and you're set.

reviews.review_description:
This guitar is good for deciding if you want to commit to learning guitar. The strings and everything work just fine, so one can learn fingerstyle playing and chords, however, the strings are rather buzzy, and in addition with a high action guitar such as this, it is harder on the fingers to play.

I used this guitar frequently for about 7 months before deciding that I would like to upgrade to an actual name brand guitar (like Fender, Ibanez, or Rogue). When I would put a regular capo on any fret of the guitar, the low E bass note would become flat, however, with no capo, the string would perform just fine. I went to a guitar center to ask about it, and they hadn't even heard of this brand of guitar.

Final Verdict:

Yes, the guitar is good value of money if you are looking to see if a guitar would be the right pursuit for you. Looks-wise, the guitar looks nice with a mix of basic and elegant. However, I'd only recommend buying this guitar if you are looking to see if guitar is the right fit for you. reviews.review_description:
This thing is amazing. It was smaller than

I thought it would be, but that wasn’t the only thing that surprised me. The sound is impressive. For 10 watts, the depth and richness is very impressive. The amp only operates at 5 watts when on battery power but the sound is still great. I love the portability of being able to play on battery power. It’s very fun when using to practice or playing for a few friends. Also the Cubase software it comes with is amazing. This amp does one thing and does it well - it’s the best amp for acoustics and if you want a natural sound that’s just louder, than this is for you.

reviews.review_title: Wonderful when new, but you might need to replace it in about 24 months. This is my second unit
reviews.review_description: Gotta say this unit is UNIQUE, the way it models microphone's for Acoustic play is really 2nd to none. Along with true Mic modeling that is pretty true to the microphones emulated, it also has a great selection of other features like delay, reverb and compression and chorus. I have purchased other "portable amps" for acoustic play. They had larger speakers and might have been a little louder but there they lacked the ability to enhance the tone, they were just louder. Some I purchased for much more money, but wound up in a sound test within 5 minutes returning them. For a portable unit that really gives you the best acoustic modeling and tone, this unit cannot be beat, especially for its size.

I love this Yamaha amp. It sounds great. I use it primarily for practice with my GS mini but I’ve also used it for small get togethers. It has a convenient handle on top making it easy to carry and it just looks really cool. Bonus you can also use batteries to power it.

Quite impressed with this tiny "acoustic" amp! If you simply want to loop tracks you create, for practice, as I do, and amplify your studies with a bit of reverb or delay, this 12" long amp is a great buy! Well made, lovely sound, and with a number of acoustic settings and tone controls. You won't be performing with this, except for a few friends in a quiet context, or just practicing at home, but it is more than adequate for this, and provides sufficient range and a nice variety of tone colors. Haven't used the Cubase software yet, so I won't offer any thoughts there.

reviews.review_title: Super Great Bang for the Buck
reviews.review_description: Remember this is 5 watts. However, its a very clean, sound isn't distorted, it's easy to transport, it has built in features like reverb, chorus etc. that do not require you to carry pedals. Its a parlor practice amp that will allow you to busk on the corner if necessary with it battery power feature. If you have AC power nearby it will work there too. Having it plugged in will not charge your batteries. It's great for travel, in the park, or assisting your writing music. You can also play mp3 music through it with the aux out. If you need to practice in silence use the headphone jack or send music out to a mixer in a bigger environment.
awesome!!!

It's not only for acoustics -- I use the THR5A as a home/practice amp for my electric guitar. Since I play only in a jazz style and hate overdrive distortion, the amp works really well. I don't use the recommended "EG Clean" setting; I use the "Condenser Mic" setting, which gives just the right tone for jazz guitar by helping to preserve the acoustic sonorities of my archtop while at the same time amplifying them. And when I play with a Stratocaster it gives roughly the same effect, creating the illusion that the Strat is a hollow-body -- great for guitaring with headphones while others are sleeping. (When you set it to "EG Clean" the "Blend" knob becomes a gain knob, so you can get a bit of overdrive that way. Works okay; I simply don't play in that style.)

The Hall Reverb is excellent (though you don't get the variability you'd get with a pedal), and the Compression and Chorus effects are serviceable. I don't use the Delay, but it works well enough.

Portability is another boon. I use it with rechargeable AA batteries and carry it to wherever I can find some peace in the house.

My only complaint is that when I put the amp on the wood floor and play with a backing track, it sometimes distorts (perhaps with feedback from the floor vibrations?). Generally, you can't expect great sound from this amp at high volume. But then that's not what it's for.

If you're looking for a case, try the Neewer Large Size SLR DSLR Camera and Video Bag with Shoulder Strap. Perfect fit, and much cheaper than the Yamaha case.

I'm using this primarily for ukulele. And wow *THIS* is it. I'd tried a few before arriving at this little gem of an amp. What I was looking for was a decent acoustic practice amp for home or small groups that was portable and could take batteries. I tried the Blackstar Fly3 but it was just not as clean sounding - I could get close just using my electric guitar Vox 10 amp if I tweaked the settings enough. So I came across the THR series of amps and decided to give the THR10C a try which is geared towards Jazz thinking the cleaner output would lend itself well to nylon. It's a really nice amp but still too electric sounding. That's when I discovered they made a acoustic specific amp, this THR5A. Not only does it have a "nylon" specific setting (which I actually do not play in all of the time), but it has mic models rather than amp models. There is a mixer that blends straight pickup with the mic model. And if you wanna get a little funky, it also has some reverb and hall effect. The compression effect is great to tighten up the sound on strumming so it sounds cleaner. The big thing missing from its THR10 cousins is the ability to memorize settings but I'm ok with that. Also, I understand that the THR5 series puts out the same power as the THR10 series which I was afraid coming from the 10C I would give up some volume but not the case.

Definitely consider the case from Yamaha made for this series of amps. It was designed to fit the longer THR10 series but the extra space with the THR5A just gives you more room for gear. Also grab 2 sets of 8x AA batteries. A single set of 8x AA lasts quite a while actually but its always nice to have a backup because charging them can take a while. I use Eneloop as recommended but I use those batteries for everything anyway (beware of defects being sold on ebay for cheap).

Why the missing star? On BOTH my 10C which I returned for the 5A, NEITHER included this Cubase AI recording software DVD ROM. I thought maybe it was a download but the only thing on the Yamaha site was the editor software (to edit models) and USB drivers.

reviews.review_description: This is so much more than a travel guitar. The looks, feel, playability and sound are superb for this instrument. Worth every penny. Well made and a guitar you don't want to put down. I was pleasantly surprised. I got it for a trip where I didn't want to bring my main guitar and it is a keeper.

Excellent guitar that is easy to play and maintain. The body size makes it much easier to hold than some travel guitars. I like its tone and resonance. The intonation is as close as can get with a standard acoustic design. It stays in tune very well. Considering the price it can’t be beat!

I love to modify many of my instruments; every thing from changing string type to installing pickups, etc.. This guitar will be an excellent platform for modifications. However, I like it the way it is, so I will start with non-permanent mods. First experiment will be to convert it into a jazz box by changing to flat wound strings and adding pickups. (A thin jazz pickup would be ideal if I can find away to fit it but other types can be more easily placed.) This guitar has strong, but nice resonance; however, I might add foam internally to tame the resonance and make it softer.

Don’t forget the great weather resistance, I will definitely take it camping.

What fun!!!

I bought this guitar to take with me on camping trips where I'll be leaving it in a hot car, or possibly exposing it to moisture and the elements. I took it with me on a car camping weekend and it worked very well for my purposes. After the initial tuning it took a few days of adjusting, but it more or less kept in tune after a while. It sat in a car that got well over 100 degrees, sat out in the wood, probably got a little damp at some point, and kept playing as if it hadn't.

All that said, this guitar does not sound very good. It's not awful sounding, but it won't replace even a cheaper wooden guitar. This is a cheap beater instrument that is small, portable, and probably indestructible. I don't recommend it as a first guitar or for performing, but for taking for a hike or sitting around in hot or cold weather it's great.

I’ve been playing guitar for over 15 years and had no idea what to expect since I’ve never played a carbon fiber guitar before (didn’t even know it was a thing till now). What made me try it was the price (terrifyingly reasonable), seeing all the glowing reviews, and because I teach guitar lessons to adults/kids and wanted to see what my students’ experience with it is. The low price made me skeptical primarily about how well this holds its tune which is the problem with most beginner, cheap guitars.

If you’re serious about learning guitar, I fully recommend investing in this guitar as a better beginner guitar. Mind you I really enjoy playing this and I’ve been playing for awhile as I mentioned before. If you go too cheap, like the adm brand for kids (which we have for my 3 year old), you will find they can’t hold their tune past 5 mins of playing which is critical for beginners to develop their ear. That’s because the quality of materials just isn’t there and where they skimp on quality affects playability. Thats not the case here. I can tell this thing is thoughtfully designed. The video I took of me playing is same day it was delivered. It literally was ready to play, all I had to do was tune it a couple times to get the strings used to the tension and then it held its tune which was the real test for me!

This guitar is heavier than I expected for the size but is still lightweight overall. The carbon fiber means this thing is as durable as it gets for a musical instrument, you can feel the this guitar is built solid. I was also hesitant about the sound hole difference with this one as they essentially moved it right next to the player in a side hole and it projects surprisingly well. I was surprised how loud I was able to get this thing. Not the same as a typical guitar but that’s not a knock, it’s just designed differently.

Overall, absolutely worth it for the price. Excellent beginner guitar or if you want something very portable to play out.

This little guitar packs quite the sound for such a small instrument and at an affordable price point. I purchased it as a gift for my son who is quite picky and tends to stick to his expensive Martin. However, he opened up this guitar, quickly tuned it and played for almost an hour. He was surprised at the sound, and his only complaint was that the frets needed to be sanded a bit. It is very well made, sturdy and tuned quickly and held it's tune. He is a pretty extreme traveler, from hiking in Alaska to California road trips and I wanted him to be able to have a sturdy, dependable guitar that would stand up to his travels. It is easy to set up, has a nice fit when holding , and best of all has a beautiful tone. The one piece carbon fiber body is solid and has a super cool design. Highly recommend!!

reviews.review_title: Looks and sounds like a toy guitar.
reviews.review_description: More like a toy thana real guitar. Sounds like the plastic guitar my Dad got me when I was 4 years old. Would be good for a child starting to learn to play perhaps, but there are much better options for less money.(Leo Jaymez)

So, my expectations were not high at this price point, but the reviews made me decide to give it a try. My advice - click the buy button now! This little guitar plays well above its weight. I had tried the guitar version from another company that specializes in outdoor carbon fiber Ukes, and did not keep that instrument - strings broke when you brought them up to tune, and disappointing sound, to say the least. This one - my wife is fighting me to get to play it! It arrived VERY well set up, sounds great, holds tune, a nice well padded case, accessories included, and a very cool little guitar!!

New to trying to learn guitar this guitar feels great in the hands light weight and so far is staying in tune . My guitar teacher said it sounds decent for it’s size was really impressed how well it actually plays . All I did was tune it right out of the box so no paying for setup or tweaking was needed so I highly recommend this guitar .

title: Ibanez AEG70L Left-Handed Acoustic-Electric Guitar - Tiger Burst High Gloss
description: The AEG, a compact body electric acoustic guitar with a slim neck has been well-accepted for its easy playability for more than two decades. Ibanez is proud to announce that the AEG series has been renewed with updated electronics and looks. The changes were based on the concept, “simple and easy control.” The AEG70L starts with a new preamp, an Ibanez AEQ-TTS. The small and simple preamp has only two control knobs, volume and shape. This at-a-glance tone control offers natural acoustic sound in the center position. It allows players to adjust the tone easily and enables them to go from low, fat and powerful tones to a bright and crispy sound while adjusting only one knob. A new easy-to-read onboard tuner with LCD(liquid crystal display) is located on the preamp. The AEG70L comes with a simplified rosette, a binding and ornamentation on the headstock. These finer details add a sharp and stylish atomosphere to the guitar. Other features include a Flamed Maple top and a Sapele back & sides body, an Ibanez T-bar II Undersaddle pickup which equalizes the volume from each string and delivers a well-balanced signal, and special bulb-shaped Ibanez Advantage bridge pins for easy string installation.

reviews.review_description: At 63, I decided to try and teach myself guitar to play in church. Got some lessons and a cheap $150 acoustic. It was difficult going. A friend suggested if I was serious, investing in a quality instrument would keep me from getting discouraged. My Ibanez AEG70L arrived today. I was amazed at the quality of craftsmanship. It is well made and beautiful. To my novice ear it sounds great and the ease of playability is wonderful. Tuned it up fresh out of the box, and was ready to go. Well worth the mild investment. I am enjoying lessons and practice time immensely now!

Beautiful guitar, beautiful sound. I was iffy getting a guitar from Amazon because I couldn't hold it and play it first but this is a good size, the wood on the neck feels really nice, and it has a beautiful sound

reviews.review_title: A good guitar for the price
reviews.review_description: This is a good guitar and would recommend it for a beginner / novice level player but you probably have that figured out if you are looking at this review ;-)
This is a beautiful guitar with a beautiful sound! This guitar is very easy to tune and does not require constant adjustments during use.

reviews.review_title: Amazing sound from a little guitar
reviews.review_description:
Great little guitar! Sounds amazing! It rings like a much more expensive guitar. Very clear plugged in. No static.

On-board tuner is a great feature.

This guitar is beautiful instrument. The action is really nice and the neck is super playable. It is thinner so you do not get deep base tones, definitely on a bit on the "tin" side. But the playability and built in preamp more than make up for it. The built in tuner is really nice too. When you turn on the tuner, it turns off the pickups. A really nice guitar for gigs.

The construction quality and finish were fine, but the sound quality was below expectations. I watched some youtube videos where I was sold on the amplified sound, but as acoustic only it's super tinny. I tried to give it a chance, but I wa so disappointed aftet 5 minutes I put it back in the box and returned it.

Muy buena guitarra electroacústica con excelente sonido. Además, es muy bonita en sus acabados.

Las medidas de la guitarra para comprar una funda o estuche son:

- Lo más ancho del cuerpo: 38cm (15 pulgadas)

Agrego unas fotos, ya que lamentablemente hay pocas fotos en AMAZON.

reviews.review_title: Perfect for what it is intended for
reviews.review_description:
For the price its not a cheap little toy so I do expect this to be fully functional, which it absolutely is, when unplugged its as quiet as an unplugged electric guitar, theres no real "acoustic" unplugged sound to it, so for me its nice for practicing without bothering people.

The reason I got it is for travel, going to the beach, flying to another state, I dont have to worry about taking one of my $1k guitars and something happening to it.

Its definantly more sturdy than a hollow acoustic guitar thats for sure, like im not afraid of accidently smacking It on something and breaking it.

The tuning knobs are OK, could be better but it holds its tune very well, just feels like the strings are a little grippy probably from the acoustic bridge, and the fact that they are being tuned across backwards, pulling the string across the piazo to tune. Intonation and action are set pretty perfectly right out of the box, mine even came perfectly in tune which kinda made me laugh.

I was considering the electric version vs the acoustic version because of the adjustable bridge and ability to set intonation

I originally ally chose this acoustic version thinking it was going to be louder acoustically without any speaker, the video is a bit misleading on that part, in my mind it doesn't sound anywhere near as loud as in the video.

The input jack does in fact need to be opened up and tightened , its loose from the start and ive experienced this before as a beginner that even 1 twist to tighten without gripping the nut under the plastic plate can break the wires inside.

Plugged in using my small rock on amp it sounds good, theres definantly some minor "fuzz" id guess you'd call.it, not feedback but almost like if a pickup was trying to read 2 strings ar the same time and kinda blending them when chords are played

And the output from the low e seems to be lower than the other strings so its a touch quiter.

The leg rest at first confused me because theres a notch on the end of the first bat which slides into the body of the guitar so I figured it must like "pop" into some kind of locking mechanism that would prevent it from sliding out but theres definantly no "locking" feeling when its put all the way it

BUT I do think it has something to do with holding it in because once its in you can hold the guitar without supporting it and it doesn't just slide out but when intentionally pulling it out there zero resistance so kinda nice.

Neck plays like a low actioned acoustic, it has the thickness of an acoustic guitar neck but the strings are easier to press than my personal acoustic guitar yet haven't had any buzzing problems on 3rd fret buzz test

The case is a simple over the shoulder/ handle case

I will say the handle needs to be about 2 inches further forward for the weight to be correctly distributed and carried properly, as it is the weight it forward and makes the neck hang down which is awkward and the reason I will never carry it this way but it comes with a cross shoulder strap which fits perfectly comfortably across my back.

All in all I only gave 4/5 stars on value for money, because I really feel this should be more around $200-$230 , vs the $300+ i paid for it

BUT

That said, I'd easily purchase this again seeing as theres nothing that is quite like it and theres nothing about it that stands out as a blaring issue, looking forward to having it wherever I go!

Read more

Being an airline pilot I have been on a quest to find the perfect travel guitar and my quest has ended here, this thing is fantastic! For traveling it really doesn’t get any better. Since I spend lots of time in hotel rooms it’s important that it’s not too loud. With the headphone amp and headphones or my Bose bluetooth speaker I can customize the sound as to not bother whoever is in the next room (some hotel walls are better than others!) and being it full scale and just a high quality instrument the sound quality is way better than any of the mini travel guitars I’ve owned. It’s also nice at home to be able to play and not bother my wife or kids if they’re still sleeping.

I know other reviews have mentioned the quality and action being really good and that is definitely true. I made no adjustments to this out of the box and the action is really low, it’s really easy to play. It would be great to learn on for that reason.

With the lap rest on it’s easy to balance it on your left leg so it’s not neck heavy like a lot of reviews have said. I like using a strap because it’s easy to position it right where you want it. I know it’s closer in to your body than a full size guitar but I actually kind of prefer the way this plays.

I have tried both the acoustic and electric headphone amps by traveler. The electric one is fun to play with but the acoustic definitely sounds the best. The only negative I’ve encountered so far is that sometimes the headphone amp can have some sort of internal vibration that’s kind of annoying. It happens with both my headphone amps so I don’t think it’s a defective unit. It only happens sometimes and seems to correct itself if I rotate the headphone amp a bit. I know some sort of plug in extension cord would take care of this too but I haven’t tried that yet.

It also holds its tune really well, even with all the traveling it seems like I very rarely need to touch the tuners.

Overall this thing is great I highly recommend it.

………

A few years in. This thing is still great. I was given a traveler pro series and I still tend to play this one more. A while ago I decided to modify it to fit in my roll aboard suitcase. I cut off the top four frets (so like it’s capo’d on 5). I just cut the truss rod too and re-installed the headstock piece and tuned it only two steps up from standard. It still sounds and works great. I’m glad I did it.

Read more

So, despite the title I LOVE this guitar. It’s not loud but very light and super small. It’s the perfect practice instrument.

However, the tuners are straight up garbage. Holds tune for a practice session but absolutely terrible holding tune longer than that. But the real issue is that dialing it back in is not smooth. Pretty standard tuners and, believe it or not, you can buy their $60 locking tuners. Standard replacement for the tuners so you can use another brand.

Overall though, I’d absolutely buy it again.

reviews.review_title: A well designed highly portable travel/practice guitar.
reviews.review_description: This will fit in an airline overhead. Mine fits (without the gig bag) diagonally in my 25” roller suitcase. It is quiet enough for a hotel room. I can play it in the den while my wife watches TV. It is full scale (on the long side) so it is good for practice. It sounds great with my Vox amped headset. The quality is good. It buzzed at first but I cured that with a truss rod adjustment (included wrench). The action is good. If your goal is a practice guitar on the road or if others are nearby, it’s a great choice. I wouldn’t use it as a performance guitar though it might work with a small speaker/amp but it doesn’t have the resonance of a “real” guitar. For the reason I bought it - quiet practice and portability - I’d totally buy it again. I think the price is reasonable given the quality.

Caveat, I might be writing too soon as I just got the guitar a few hours ago, but I am so happy with it I'll write a review now and edit later if any issues come up.

I bought it with the idea of traveling, but honestly I probably never will take it camping or whatever, that possibility is certainly there if you want.

It feels quite sturdy, it is tiny, it comes with a nice little case already stringed up. Everything about it is ingenious from inverting the tuners to putting the jack into the peg that holds the strap. With the little extension bars it really doesn't feel that different. My father also plays guitar and said he "cant get used to it, feels weird to hold" but I didn't feel that at all. You honestly only ever touch the fretboard and the bottom side of a guitar anyway so it feels fine in the lap, feels fine on a strap. Action on the strings is very nice for me, very easy to play. I re-strung it although the factory D'Addario strings are fine, I just wanted to see how easy it is and it's honestly just as if not a little easier than a standard guitar, sounds absolutely fine. I play-tested w my strat and this thing, and I can't notice any difference in sound quality at all from my $1400 guitar. Other people might as some people get very into the weeds with that sort of thing, but honestly who is buying a traveler guitar to record an album?

Anyway, love it.

Read more

If you're considering this guitar, it has to be solely because you want something that doesn't take up a lot of space. In that respect it is ideal. Full size scale (24-3/4" nut to bridge), but still the most compact guitar ever.

You do have to realize, though, that there are some compromises you have to make. So here they are:

1) Like most compacts, it is neck heavy. Even using a strap on the buttons provided, it will point down. I manage this by tying the top end of the strap above the nut. You can also use the thigh rest, but again, it will tend to tilt down.

2) There is no place to rest your right arm. You can kind of rest your forearm on the corner, right above the output jack, but it's not as comfortable as most full size guitars. If you strum, his will probably cramp your style a bit.

3) There is no sound box, so to play you need a small amp. You can practice with just the sound the strings make (which is kind of a feature, since you can practice very quietly, if you are concerned about bothering others), but you're not going to want anyone else to hear it without an amp.

And that is literally ALL. Everything else is perfect. It is very nicely built and finished, and I can't wait to pick it up every day to practice. The strings are extra light D'Addario EJ15s, which are perfect for me. My last guitar, long ago, was a Squier Strat, and this guitar is superior to it in every way. My best Amazon purchase ever.

Read more

Bought specifically for international air travel in my checked duffle. It is actually a pretty nice guitar with good tuners and the intonation is fine. It takes some getting used to (tuners in the back - restringing is very different) but it is functional. I play sitting mostly and the lap piece attachment works well for me. I could gig with it in a pinch.

I’ve have owned this guitar for 2 years now, this guitar has zigzagged across the country as a carry on without any issues. I always look forward to playing in the hotel room or quiet mornings. Although I do have a headphone but prefer just acoustically. No, it’s not loud, looking at it is not going to be. It’s nice just hearing the strings resonate and you can feel the guitar vibrate. I have a handful of acoustics, certainly not a replacement, but sometimes you second guess, should I have gotten the rosewood body, spruce top, should I change the saddle material or string type, etc.., with this, those thoughts vanish, and allow me to focus solely on playing. I think it’s a great design, body and neck are a single piece of wood, attached fretboard, level frets, intonation decent, stays in tune. Great solution for easy travel.

reviews.review_title: My take on this 30" classical guitar
reviews.review_description:
I have been playing the heck out of this 1/4 size classical nylon guitar and it's time for my review. I am no beginner. I call myself a guitar hack, as my technical knowledge of music theory is um, spotty. I am a full sized 71 year old adult 5'8" with average sized hands. I enjoy playing the smaller sized guitars and never expected this little guy to boom out like a 41" dreadnot guitar. It has a 20" scale and is 30" end to end.

It arrived quickly and I saw no visible damage. As for tuning it? I need to say we live on the big island Puna District. We leave our windows open always. The climate, humidity, etc make it impossible for any hollow body acoustic to stay in tune overnight. Ever. Tune it in the early day, and it will go sharp overnight. Having said that, the tuners are just okay. They do the job. The guitar has a decent finish. I am going to add fret markers on the side of the neck just like on my steel string acoustics. Classical guitars have few fret markers, and I need the full set. It comes with a bare minimum gig bag with no real padding and a storage pocket. Spare set of strings, A capo, and a strap. Has a strap pin in the end of the body and none at the top, but the strap has a string to tie that end onto the neck. No tuner came with it. Too bad because I have bought four Pyle acoustics and they came with great rechargeable tuners that I love. The neck seems straight and does not have a truss rod. Many classical guitars, even full sized ones like Yamaha do not have truss rods. This one has no "kerfing" inside. My Pyle 34" steel string acoustic has full kerfing. This 30" is tuned to standard guitar tuning, EADGBE. I'm quite sure, with the right strings, one could tune it down five frets to A and call it a guitelele, like my Yamaha GL-1. I plan to leave it standard tuning. It developed a bit of a fret buzz caused by the 3rd fret. When pressing down the D string the second fret it would buzz. The harder you picked that string, the worse it was. I agonized whether I should send it back or not for a couple weeks. Then, after a particularly hot dry spell here, the buzzing quite. I have played this every day. I like to grab my guitar whenever I want and I may pick it up and play 10-15 times a day. I have grown to really love this handy little classical and enjoy the nylon strings and sound it gives me is very nice! I am going to install a piezo pickup inside the body and will have to drill a small hole for the input jack. I could see myself playing one or two of my original songs at an open mic night using one of my amps. I'm a blues oriented player. I like I play slide, and I often use a slide with this guitar. I tune the high E sting down 2 frets to a D, as it really gives a fuller sound with a slide. I love this little bugger and would buy it again. My kitty liked it too!

Read more
My son loved it. Easy to follow instructions.

We bought this for the grandkids who have yet to play It. I've been playing guitar for 50 years and it's not bad for a beginner guitar. It has a pretty good sound. This is for nylon strings only!! Do not put steel strings on this or you will pop the bridge right off the body. It took a bit of time to stretch the strings to keep them from going out of tune. You just have to be patient play it and stretch the strings and retune.

Action is about an inch high (string height). Intonation is about an inch off (cannot be tuned). Frets are painted. Coming from a past instructor, this is closer to a toy than an actual "beginners instrument" as the description claims. Not worth its price.

reviews.review_title: Small guitar great for a beginner teen or child
reviews.review_description: Very nice guitar it is smaller than a regular guitar easily handled by 18 or child plays nice comes with all the stuff you would need basically it’s really pretty guitar
Seems well built for the cost. Great starter for my 6 yr old

This guitar is amazing! My son is just starting out learning guitar and this was perfect for him. The black color is super shiny and looks great, plus it comes with everything you need. Extra strings, a capo, picks, even a strap and a case so he can carry it around. We didn’t have to buy anything else. It sounds really good for a beginner guitar too, wasn’t expecting that.

Honestly, couldn’t have found a better deal for the price. My son loves it and plays everyday. It’s a great size for him to handle and he’s learning fast. I would recommend this guitar to anyone looking to start out, especially for kids. Can’t go wrong with this one.

title: Traveler Guitar Escape Mark III Mahogany Acoustic Guitar | Portable Acoustic with Built-in Headphone Amp | Full 25.5" Scale Headless Guitar | Custom Gig Bag Included
description: The Escape Mark III is a full-scale acoustic/electric travel guitar with advanced features for the discriminating player on-the-go. The Escape Mark III is a full 25 1/2" scale guitar with a headphone amp built in. The proprietary In-Body tuning system uses standard tuning machines relocated into the body, eliminating the need for a headstock. As a result, you’ll have the same full-scale playing experience you’re used to on an instrument that’s 26% shorter and 47% thinner than a typical, full-sized acoustic. The built-in headphone amplifier produces a crisp, clean signal through headphones for private practice sessions. A Shadow Nano Flex pickup under the saddle senses the vibrations of the strings and body for an acoustic-style sound without the bulk of a resonant body. The control plate includes volume, treble and bass controls, a built-in chromatic Tuner as well as a headphone output and aux-in for jamming along with your favorite tracks. A standard ¼" output jack allows you to plug into your favorite amp. Features include a Mahogany body with cutaway for high fret access, and a bolt-on Mahogany neck with black walnut fingerboard. It has standard tuning machines and uses standard acoustic strings, measures only 29 1/2" Long, and is ready to play right out of the gig bag. The escape mark III is a perfect solution for traveling acoustic players unwilling to compromise on scale length, and looking for a compact yet comfortable guitar. Fits easily in airline overhead compartments in the included deluxe gig bag.

reviews.review_title: You won't be disappointed the quality of the guitar!
reviews.review_description:
Amazing quality and performance! I played around with one of these Escape Mark III guitars a while back but didn't have the need for a travel guitar at that time. Now that I have retired, I like to travel a bit more. This guitar fits perfectly into that lifestyle. Well-built with great sound whether you are using the headphone jack for silent playing or through an amp. The two-stage built in amp adjusts the sound to your ears and offers a nice tuner that lines up perfectly with other tuners I have tried. You can also add your phone or tablet for backing tracks, music, etc. No Bluetooth but I like the simpler way anyway. Bluetooth tends to have latency issues, and I have none with this set-up.

I use some pretty good headphones, but I have also used the older style Apple earbuds and they sound great. I travel with these in the case but use the better headphones at home.

The neck is solid and very comfortable. It's hard to believe you are playing a travel size guitar! I do use a strap for my personal comfort, but the larger body does well in other positions.

I have yet to fly with this guitar, but this is really no bigger than my baritone ukulele that has thousands of miles on it. The silent feature is good for me when we are in a hotel and my wife sleeps in. I can still practice without disturbing her. The ukulele was not good for that...

reviews.review_title: Ultimate Practice Guitar - it will make you better
reviews.review_description:
This is the ultimate practice guitar. At first, I overlooked this guitar because the neck didn't detach and fold like other travel guitars. Then I realized how perfect this design is and how it doesn't need that feature, which I now think is gimmicky. I'm shocked this isn't way more popular.

1) it's tiny. My wife and mother-in-law watched me open it and they had to each ask me twice "THAT's a guitar?!?!" You will most definitely have no traveling issues and certainly fit in a carry on, overhead, flight bag. in fact, it's the same length as my Baritone Ukulele (and hence fit in their cases). I carry it everywhere: in my bed, in my car, at the park, on a hike, in a boat, with a goat, in a box, with a fox, in a house, with a mouse, here and there, I carry it anywhere! I do so like this guitar! Thank you! Thank you, Traveler!

2) despite it's size, it is a 100% full sized 25.5" scale. This was very important for me because, as a beginner, I did not want to train on a short scale just to suffer when I picked up a full scale. Trust me, you want to get used to a full scale and then if you pick up a smaller guitar, it will be easy. It kind of makes me wonder, why aren't all solid body electric guitars this size?? Seriously, why do they need to be any bigger??

3) it's a solid body. I like this because it's QUIET. If you want to get better at guitar, you have to practice a lot, but nobody wants to hear a noob practice on a dreadnought all day. Also, the solid body makes it smaller and more durable for traveling.

4) it's an "acoustic" style. This means it uses acoustic strings, which are thicker (including a wound G-string) and at a higher tension than electric strings. Read: harder to play. I liked this from a practice perspective. Again, I think it's important I get accustomed to acoustic strings, so when I play an electric, it's like child's play and a confidence booster. If you disagree with my theory here, well Traveler also makes electric (EG-1 and EC-1), and nylon classical, versions of this guitar, so the choice is yours. Note, it uses completely standard guitar strings, so you can replace them with whatever is your favorite.

5) it has a built in tuner. nobody ever talks about this, but I love built in tuners. One less thing to carry around - especially important when we're talking about travel guitars. The electric version EG-1 has one too, but not the EC-1.

6) it has a built in headphone amp. Sounds good unplugged, but if you want to jam a little harder by yourself, just plug headphones directly in. Of course, it has a standard amp output too.

7) some have expressed concern about the in-body tuners. I think they are fabulous and have great tuning stability. In fact, I think it's even better than headstock tuners that are prone to getting shifted when it brushes up against a wall, your body, or you have young curious kids who turn them when you're not looking. Why aren't all guitars headless these days?? The tuners are nicely protected in the body. I find there is ample space to fit your fingers to tune them and the holes do not get in my way, even when I'm playing fingerstyle. It's slightly awkward crossing your arms to pick a string and tune at the same time, but really not an issue. The actual tuners seem pretty standard, so I'm sure you can replace with one of your choice, and I noticed Traveler sells a locking tuners upgrade, but I don't think they need them.

8) I think the mahogany version looks amazing. The tales are true that if you are attracted to your guitar, you will want to pick it up and play more.

Conclusion: This guitar will make you play more than any other guitar = will make you better. IMO, as a beginner, you should be less concerned about tone nuances and more concerned about getting your hours in. I would definitely consider the EG-1 or EC-1 electric versions in the future.

Some minor criticisms:

1) now the sound sucks. But what do you expect with a solid body "acoustic"? You're not going to be gigging in front of a huge audience with this thing. The sound is solely created from a piezo pickup under the saddle. From what I've read, piezo pickups on normal acoustic guitars are one of the least desirable ways to record your instrument. So this is piezo without any acoustic sound to help out. It sounds weird plugged in (headphones or amp), fake sounding acoustic sound, and it's got some gain/sustain, which is weird for an "acoustic". But sound quality is not why you should be buying this. Again, if this turns you off, check out their humbucked electric versions, which I assume sound like normal electric guitars.

2) the top edge of the body is razor sharp and very uncomfortable on the forearm. Also note, the black "binding" I believe is just a strip of paint for looks. The back has a rounder edge, so they should really round the top for the next generation.

3) there's no pick guard, and it definitely needs it. I was very light on it in the beginning and it already has tiny scratch marks. I've seen this happen to others too. I made my own pick guard with clear packing tape, which works very well. I highly recommend everyone make a pick guard before they start playing.

reviews.review_title: Great guitar for my van travels and is fun and educational at home too. Pretty guitar!
reviews.review_description: This is a great guitar (my first travel electric). It plays nice. The body is big enough to rest my forearm on it. Its not neck-heavy, yet light and balanced. Only 4 stars on "thickness category" because the neck could be a little thinner but no complaints here. A sales point for me was that I could plug my phone into it and play Ultimate Guitar app, YouTube or whatever to play through the amp. The 3 dot tuner doesn't compare to a Snark (which clamps nicely on the stubby head). I coupled this with a Blackstar 3W amp. Everything fits nicely in my van.

reviews.review_title: Must have for acoustic guitar players
reviews.review_description: I don’t write a lot of reviews, but I am so impressed with this guitar I feel I owe it to Traveler to comment on it. You really need to buy this guitar if you are an acoustic guitar player. It has a full size acoustic neck, but sounds like a non-amplified electric, so it doesn’t annoy others when practicing the same licks over and over again. I find I practice so much more because of this. Of course you can plug it into an amp or plug in earbuds if you want to hear a full sound. I bought it for travel because I am always short on cargo space in my vehicle. This takes up about a 1/4 of the space my other acoustics take up with a hardshell case. Didn’t expect the quality of this guitar. Very solid and well crafted. The engineering to make it compact is genius.
This is a well crafted guitar. Light, great action, built in tuner, very light and portable.

I'm a beginner/intermediate guitar player and wanted a low profile guitar for traveling. I was a bit skeptical and watched a lot of YouTube and read a lot of reviews and finally decided on this guitar. I have to say that I was pleasantly surprised and 100% satisfied when I received it. For it's small size, it's a heavy instrument. But this is a solid body, beautiful work of art and engineering. It's not much of an acoustic guitar, but with the built-in tuner, electronics, and headphone jack, it makes a great electric sound. With the treble and base adjustments, and phase shifting, there's so much sounds to play with. The neck and the body are ascetically perfect and clean. I love to hold it in my hands, even if I'm not playing. And that's saying a lot. This is a beautiful instrument, very functional, and a lot of fun. If I had to complain, I would say it's a bit heavy, but that solid wood body is a great trade off. I'll take the extra weight and still give it five stars. Weather you're looking for a traveling guitar or just an enthusiasist, you need one of these. Highly recommend. And 100 percent real deal.

I have owned many piezo pickup acoustics and this one sounded really thin and bad even after working with an EQ pedal for a while. It looks great and like it is well made. It was almost perfectly in tunes out of the box, I just thought it sounded week especially with single note flatpicking. It might work pretty well if all you are looking to use it for is strumming chords.

I am planning a trip and I have my guitar, as I will be playing for a family gathering outside. So, I need to travel on an airplane with it. I need portability to the outside venue and I need a good sound. After reading so many reviews, and looking at options for several hours, I finally decided on the Mark III. I received it yesterday. I have been playing it for several hours and I have to say, I love this guitar. If you plug into a decent amp, the sound is great. It does not have the full sound of my Fender. It's a solid body, and it's better than I expected. Also, it feels the same. With headphones, it is very quiet. I highly recommend the Mark III. I am also using the Donner Mini Guitar Amp for portability.

reviews.review_title: BP40: A Powerful, Portable Amp with Incredible Sound
reviews.review_description:
The BP40 is an outstanding amplifier that delivers exceptional sound quality in a compact, thoughtfully designed package. Despite its affordable price, this amp is incredibly reliable and built to last. The clarity and projection it offers are impressive, especially considering its small size. Plus, the fact that it runs on a battery makes it incredibly convenient for gigs, rehearsals, and remote locations.

User-friendly and versatile, the BP40 features Bluetooth connectivity, allowing seamless playback of backing tracks or house music during setup. With three inputs, we typically run a violin through input 2 and a cello through input 3, leaving input 1 available for a microphone or piano. The built-in inlet on the side allows for easy mounting on a universal speaker pole, ensuring optimal sound projection.

Battery life is another highlight. We regularly run multiple instruments at high volume for 2–3 hours, and after more than a year of use, our BP40 still performs flawlessly. Its rugged casing, made of thick leather/cloth material with a sturdy metal grill, protects the speaker while adding a sleek, professional look. This amp is built tough and can handle heavy use without missing a beat.

Despite its durability, the BP40 remains highly portable—it fits in a suitcase, on a dolly, or can be carried short distances with ease. Most importantly, the sound is loud, rich, and full of depth. In fact, it outperforms some traditional PA systems we’ve used that require an electrical hookup.

If you’re looking for a powerful, portable, and dependable amplifier, the BP40 is an excellent choice.

reviews.review_title: A Great Addition, & Must-Have For A Musician's Gear Collection!
reviews.review_description:
You'll be so happy you purchased this and will love all the features! I know I am! CoolMusic has really outdone themselves with making this speaker/amp so versital!

I originally purchased Coolmusic's BP-Mini for practicing & hoped to use it as a light-weight monitor for gigs. I decided that for gigs, I should get a speaker/amp that was a little more robust than the BP-Mini (which I love!). After checking out what was available for small battery operated & highly portable speakers/amps, I decided to give this BP40 a try.

I am so impressed! I've used it at a gig as a monitor, & my band loves its crisp sound. It handles treble, mids & even bass great! We can hear our sound clearly! Though I haven't used it on a speaker stand, it has a hole that accepts universal tripod speaker stands... which makes this BP40 more versital in a performance setting.

I've hooked instruments up to the BP40 with cables and wireless, and the sound is very faithful to the instrument without any problems. I've plugged in an acoustic guitar, an acoustic/electric violin and a kalimba (with an instrument jack) and they all sound faithful to the instruments. I've plugged instruments in and played along with pre-recorded tracks from my Android phone and also from my iPad which were connected via Bluetooth on separate occasions. Recording to a separate device (phone, iPad or multi-track recorder) comes in clean from the D.I. Out Port.

The first two inputs are basic with separate gains & a shared reverb. The third input has more controls with gain, bass, treble & reverb. The reverb is nice. It's not overdone, and sounds like you're in a bigger space.

I've not used the speaker more than 6 hours at a time, so I haven't experienced its maximum run time. The 9-volt port for charging is a very secure connection. The 9-volt port out is also a secure connection and a thoughtful addition for power pedals.

I also play gigs & impromptu music outdoors... I can't wait to use it outside! I will update this review once I'm able to get outside to use it.

For the price, I don't think there's a rival for the quality & features you get with this speaker/amp! This was a great purchase for me! Thank you CoolMusic!

UPDATE: This speaker/amp is such a pleasure to use outdoors. It's light, and easy to setup. The sound is very clear and true to acoustic instruments. Every musician I've let use it has remarked about this speaker's big sound from a small battery-powered unit! Check out my video!

Very nice product. Light and easy enough to handle. Play back through phone is true and clear. Plenty of inputs and amazing power at a very good price.

reviews.review_title: Light, sturdy, speaker has great sound and is an awesome value!
reviews.review_description:
The speaker arrived quickly and the packaging was very professional and safe. There was no damage at all when opened. And it was even charged and ready to go! (not sure if that is always the case but definitely a pleasant surprise)

The sound coming from the speaker of my guitar sounded great. There are settings for reverb, gain, high and low, and I could dial in my Gretsch really well. The tone was very clear and crisp. My friend used it with a violin and again, very clear and crisp. I imagine that the tone with an electric acoustic is also excellent. Overall, the excellent tone for the price point is a total win. You could probably spend 10x as much and get something a little purer, but it probably wouldn't be noticeable except by the most trained ear.

I also really liked how the 3 inputs work. 2 have a shared reverb and individual gains, while a 3rd has its own reverb, gain, high and low settings. This could allow for some really cool use of synth, vocals, and a guitar.

The speaker itself was surprisingly light and small for the sound it produces. I read the dimensions and saw the weight before purchase, but once I held it, I was really surprised by how light and small it was. It feels really sturdy too.

One surprise:

For me, when I plugged in the vocals, my dynamic mic (beta sm58a) was very quiet. I was able to crank to gain for that channel to near max and it wasn't a problem, but it seemed very strange. It likely has to do with the fact that the 3 inputs are all 1/4" jacks, and none are xlr. I needed to use a transformer in order to plug my mic in. However, once the gain was set appropriately, I was able to get the speaker to produce plenty of volume for both my guitar and vocals and they sounded level and clear.

So the only 2 things I would change

1. Have a multi-input or just xlr instead of one of the 1/4" (maybe one of the shared reverb with individual gain). This was not a deal breaker at all, because the transformer is 20 bucks, is small, and most musicians will need one down the road anyway. So for the price, 1/4" is fine. A multi-input would be great though.

2. My second change would be to indicate the battery life somehow. The battery may change eventually to red when it is almost dead, but it is just on or off.

Overall, this speaker deserves a 5-star rating. Especially the tone. Even for tone snobs, this is a really good speaker, and for the price you can't go wrong. Light and sturdy, with great sound.

Read more

I've had it one day. Play almost exclusively acoustic and I'm a clean tone guy, want it to sound like my guitar only loader. Plugged in several guitars, Martin's, Recording King and Vintage, dialed them in and was pleasantly surprised. Obviously it didn't rival my higher end amps but for impromptu playing at the beach is more than ample and the battery is missing on plug-in amps. It's plenty load and will distort if too high but it's not designed for that. The electronics even beat out some of my more expensive amps with 3 inputs and just about everything you need considering the cost? Obviously the speaker is sub-par, after warranty I may upgrade to a better? Ran mike, piezo pickup and a combo mike/mag pickup and it handled all of them nicely. Miked Harmonica really stood out, SM58 also sounded quite acceptable. Not too heavy, purty easy to pack around and it's built darn tough. Price was right! The ultimate question is: how long will it last? Stick around, I'll update if it takes a dump. Not sure about negative reviews? Everything works perf, maybe they were looking for a Marshall stack for a buck and half?

I liked the portability of this amp.

I liked the sound and power of this amp.

It was great with a mic and acoustic guitar,

and then...... after a year of moderate use, it died at a gig. It was plugged in and it died. YangYang77, the seller offered me a new battery or even a new amp, pretty impressive. But Amazon authorized a full refund and free return shipping. I decided to get the refund and buy a higher quality amp from a different manufacturer.

I have used this for close to a year now, especially on my bass guitar, but also for my dulcimer. I wish it had a little more volume, but the tone is clean, and you have several sound options, such as chorus and reverb. I think the volume problem is the weakness of the signal I put in it, because if I use some sort of external pre-amp on my guitar, it is plenty loud enough. I like that it is rechargeable. One complaint was that it didn't have a carrying handle on the top, so I had to use one from another source. I also had to drill another hole to mount a pin to hold the strap. Other than that, it works well, and I use it all the time.

First off I must say I didn't expect it to be all that great and I am pleasantly surprised. This amp seems real well built and the sound is much better then I expected.. Sure it isn't a modeling amp and better suited to acoustic guitar (I'm using it for electric guitar) but it sounds pretty damn good. Has plenty of volume and you can crank it real loud before it loses tone quality. For practice or to haul with you camping or whatever it is great. I've played through it quite a bit and still haven't had to charge the battery. I tried running through a overdrive pedal but the sound wasn't great but I probably was pushing it to much as I didn't change my overdrive setting from what I use on my big stack amp. I'll have to play around with that. Bottom line for the price I recommend this amp. I'm very happy with it..

Just don't expect the quality of a 500 dollar amp, but you could use it for a gig in a small bar or restaurant and not having to plug it in is fantastic !

Follow up after a very long time ( maybe over a year) I still find it to be a great item ...

Buy one and you won't be disappointed

Very fine

reviews.review_title: Zager Easy Play Strings are easy on your fingers and sound great
reviews.review_description: Wonderful playing experience using Zager Easy Play Acoustic Guitar Strings! That I’ve ever used…. Especially for my arthritis fingers on my left hand. I had nearly given up playing steel strings but now find I can still play with steel strings

I have 2 Zager guitars and they are both fantastic. I only put the Zager coated strings on them because they sound and feel incredible. The service that the Zager family provides is excellent and they are responsive right away. The strings they sent to me were damaged in transit and they sent me replacement strings immediately. I fully endorse purchasing a guitar and accessories from them.

Not happy with these strings. They don't sound good at all. Broke the G string before it was in tune while installing it. Broke the low E string while tuning it on the 3ed tuning. There not worth the $19. I paid for them. Will be going back to my DAddrio strings

Other reviews gave these strings high marks for being easy on the fingers and having superior tone. For me, they were slightly easier to play, but the tone wasn't outstanding and they wouldn't stay in tune, even after 3 weeks on the guitar. I gave them 3 stars because they might be appropriate for other players, but they did not work that well for me.

description:

Acoustic-electric Guitar with Spruce Top Sapele Back Sides

reviews.review_description: Great and beautiful starter guitar for people who just want to strum and learn. Pickups are clean, works great with amps and effects pedals, exactly what I’ve come to expect from Ibanez.

I was never a great guitar player but I used to be good at improving melodies and finishes to existing songs. That was in my youth, when I played. Now that I am retiring in January, I want to relearn guitar and take a swing at composition. I am medium statured with not so big hands, so I require a quality slimline, left handed guitar, which many know are nearly impossible to find. I originally considered a Godin A6 Ultra, but the humidity here in Wyoming gets down to 0%, and I didn't want a $2,000 guitar to crack in a few months. I was going to split the difference with a Fender Acoustasonic, but they no longer make that for lefties. This Ibanez is perfect! It is slim profile, light weight, and it has a thin neck but enough frets to do the job. I don't need for it to produce performance level sound. I just want to be able to pick it up and compose without plugging it into an amp. Of course, having the ability to plug it into an amp is a plus for when I want to record. It's not the best guitar, but the sound quality is there, it is for lefties, and the price point can't be beat!

Great guitar. Exactly what I ordered and the runner had me playing in 15 minutes. The resonance is clean and full. It's not a full deep sound like a dreadnought but pretty close for its size and weight.

Thinner body than my first Ibenez. Changes the tone quite a bit. Easier to play with my big belly though! Electronics work well, tuners feel sturdy. Needs a good set up. Action is good but intonation is off. I guess I'm happy with it but it is a step down from the model I had until my gtandkids broke it. I'm also not crazy about the 2 tone black front and wood tone side and back

This was my first guitar purchase, so I have very little expertise in this... but I can tell this guitar is well-built and sounds great! I've tried out a few other brands over the past few months – mainly via trying out friends' guitars, and in local stores – and this one was the one I kept coming back to. The neck seems to be a bit thinner than other models, which just feels better to me... and I like the instrument's overall lower profile (thickness), too. The built-in tuner works perfectly... and the simple sound control knobs are all I need. And most importantly: It sounds fantastic whether I'm plugged in or not.

reviews.review_title: This is a 40 inch dream of a machine.
reviews.review_description: I am currently learning to play guitar and I found the hardest thing to find is a decent left-handed guitar. I could not find one in my area due to it being such a small town. So I decided to see what Amazon had for sale. I returned my first guitar purchase from another company, it wouldn't stay in tune, and man am I glad I did. This one has a great tone and is a huge upgrade from my last guitar. The sound is wonderful, not too deep, and not too high pitched. It is a gorgeous Guitar. Even the husband was impressed by the sound and look. This girl is a keeper. It also fits perfectly into my small hands. There is a bit of a stretch on the 4th, but not enough that I can't reach.

reviews.review_title: Good quality. Look good. Sounds good.
reviews.review_description: I bought this for my son almost a year ago. We both think it's an excellent guitar. He loves it. It sounds great when he plays. Quality is very good. No issues or complaints at all. I am going to buy an acoustic soon and plan on getting another one.

reviews.review_title: First act has one up on this guitar
reviews.review_description: I have played hundreds of guitars never have I ever played one so terrible from the factory ever. 14 out of 22 frets buzz on every string it wasn't setup whatsoever I've played busted old beauty's with 1000 times the sound quality. They expect me to pay for shipping back to the factory to remedy the situation. That's not acceptable when you purchase a precision instrument and its broken they should make it right. Thanks for cementing the idea of never buying ibanez ever again.

title: Fender CD-60SCE All-Mahogany Dreadnought Cutaway Acoustic Electric Guitar, with 2-Year Warranty, Fishman Pickup and Preamp System, Natural
description:
Product Description

Combining powerful onboard electronics—including a built-in tuner—with great tone and easy playability, the CD-60SCE is ideal for beginning to intermediate level players who are ready to plug in. The single-cutaway body provides easy access to the upper frets, while the solid spruce top and mahogany back and sides offer increased volume and crisp sound. These features along with Fender’s signature easy-to-play neck make the CD-60SCE the perfect choice for the coffeehouse, beach, or patio.

From the Manufacturer

Combining powerful onboard electronics—including a built-in tuner—with great tone and easy playability, the CD-60SCE is ideal for beginning to intermediate level players who are ready to plug in. Featuring a single-cutaway body for easy upper-fret access, warm-sounding solid mahogany top, easy-to-play neck and mahogany back and sides, the CD-60SCE is perfect for the couch, the beach or the coffeehouse—anywhere you want classic Fender playability and sound.

reviews.review_title: Fender makes a great affordable guitar!
reviews.review_description: Awesome guitar! Easy to play, has a built in tuner is beautifully finished and sounds amazing through a matched Fender Acoustisonic amp. Was priced like it was stolen!

I ordered this model Fender Guitar for my 86 year old husband as his Christmas present. Giving him this beautiful surprise present at Christmas brought joy to our family. My husband had admired our son's guitar that is this same model and said how much he would love to have one just like it. At Christmas when my husband first received the guitar I wrote an "outstanding rave" review about the guitar. Less than 2 months later I am back with very bad news. My husband complained to our son that he was having difficulty tuning his guitar. Our son checked it out and discovered the problem! The 6th string (E), 2nd, 3rd and 4th frets have sunk into the keyboard there by making the guitar untunable. The guitar sounds horrible! My husband is very disappointed and his Christmas gift has turned into a joyless, sad and expensive mistake. Fender Company can you help us?

July 16, 2023- Since I wrote my original evaluation about the guitar I bought my Husband, the Fender Guitar Company has come to my rescue. They have made everything right. I found them very responsive to my problem and more than willing to help. My husband now loves playing his beautiful guitar with the fabulous tone.

reviews.review_title: Great Guitar - Set it up properly.
reviews.review_description:
I was not disappointed in any way with this guitar. It's my northern guitar for when we're home in Massachusetts. I leave the Gibson in Florida. The fended is way less expensive, but the quality is there, and the sound is excellent - after a couple of tweaks.

When the guitar arrived, I knew it'd need SOME work, so I was ready. I'd ordered a set of BONE pins, nut, and saddle. When I immediately replaced the strings upon the guitar's arrival, I fitted the bone components. If you have an inexpensive guitar, it's likely that these pieces are composite. Replace them with bone! Replace them with bone! Replace them with bone. This (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07CQSZQZL/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1) is the one I used. I can guarantee (from other guitars I've owned) the proper nut and saddle increase both volume and sustain.

If you don't feel up to the job, take it somewhere and have it done. The neck guitar that I received needed no adjustment, and the new saddle matched the original one perfectly.

By the way, the built-in tuner and pickups are worth the extra expense.

reviews.review_title: Fender CD60SCE Mahogany electric acoustic guitar
reviews.review_description:
This is my 3rd Fender in my collection. I originally played a Les Paul Jr in the 60s. I loved that one, the stratocaster is my choice now. The other is a 3/4 Fender Acoustic guitar, nylon strings. Great practice one for me.

The CD 60 is farthest in the photo, the built in tuner works great. After initial tuning, the guitar stayed tuned first couple days. Seems to have a good setup, the tonal quality is excellent and with amp really nice. Kinda warm, not twangy.

A significant improvement over my beater, Hohner acoustic. Easy on the hands. Seems to be settling in after practicing on it for about a half hour. Strings definitely were not pre-stretched. Nice sound projection and the body resonates nicely. Sustains a note/chord for long time. It rewards you well sonically when you hit the chords and notes just right.

I can't say much regarding the "setup" because I am not skilled enough to determine if the neck needs adjustment or anything like that. Looks fine to me when I hold it up closely and look down the neck/frets. The saddle and nut also seem fine, but I will likely replace the saddle and nut as well as the pins with those made of bone for both tone and cool factor. Head stock and tuning knobs all seem fine on close inspection and operation.

Sorry to report not much useful info from me on the electronics because I don't have an amp. But one thing of note... Be aware that the built in tuner will not work unless you have it plugged into an amp. I confirmed this with the included Fishman instructions. I thought the tuner would come on anytime I wanted so I could tune it. Nope. Must be plugged in to an amp. Thinking back, it makes sense, because the sound is transduced into an electric signal by the Fishman pickup on its way to the amp.

Docked one star in craftsmanship for the sloppy application of stain you see in the pic as well as some minor finish aberrations. The builder(s) just let the stain run down into the sound hole; they didn't actually put it there with intent. It would have only taken 3 seconds to correct this during the staining process. I will fix it with one of those stain pens you can get at any DIY store because my eye automatically goes directly to that spot when I pick it up. Leaving it raw wood would have even looked better. Also noticed some aberrations on the body if I hold it at specific angles. You can detect them as distortions of the glare, but not when looking at it "normally." I cannot feel them when I run my finger over those areas though. Maybe just the clearcoat.

All told, this seems like a decent guitar for the price. I am not disappointed, even with the small cosmetic flaws. Hopefully one day I will be able to play good enough to get all the potential out of this guitar.

Good luck to everyone learning. Anything worth learning requires effort. At least, that is what I keep telling myself.
